entry.summary: Introduces BLiMPPI, a multilingual suite of over 12,000 minimal pairs for negative polarity items across 33 languages, built automatically from Universal Dependencies treebanks with licensing-environment labels and perturbations. Evaluating 14 models shows multilingual models struggle most with cross-linguistically variable NPI licensing. A rigorous linguistically grounded benchmark that extends grammatical evaluation beyond English.

entry.title: Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence

author.name: Han Luo, Zhan Zhuang, Xu He, Jujia Zhao, Yu Li, Suqin Yuan, Dong Li, Lei Feng

entry.summary: Proposes improving memory retrieval for assistants by matching queries to contextual token-level representations already computed by embedding models, using sparse token matching combined with whole-memory similarity, without additional training. An optional low-rank query adapter enables supervised refinement.

entry.title: Faithfulness Without Anchors: A Position Paper on the Structural Misalignments of Explainable AI Faithfulness Metrics for Feature Importance

author.name: Marco Zullich, Emily Schiller, Ivan Gentile, David Dembinsky, Adriano Lucieri, Kilian G\"oller, Steffen Seitz

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that explainable AI (XAI) has largely failed its promise of building trust, instead encouraging overreliance or algorithmic aversion, and that XAI is better understood as a debugging tool. It examines structural misalignments between feature-importance explanations and the models they describe, critiquing existing faithfulness metrics. This matters because it challenges foundational evaluation practices in the XAI field.

entry.title: AI-Mediation in Retail Markets: Revenue Effects and Assortment Optimization

author.name: Omar El Housni, Marouane Ibn Brahim

entry.summary: This paper models retail assortment planning when an AI shopping intermediary, rather than the retailer, determines which products customers actually see, using multinomial logit demand with both deterministic and Plackett-Luce stochastic mediation. The authors build a dataset of real product rankings from leading AI models, estimate ranking models on it, and show that accounting for AI mediation changes retailer revenue outcomes and optimal catalog choices. It matters because AI assistants are becoming a major gatekeeper in e-commerce, and this is one of the first formal treatments of how that shifts market power and optimization problems.

entry.title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Finite-Beam Reachability and Continuous-Query Generation in Generative Recommendation

author.name: Yu Sun, Renkai Xiang, Zuodong Xiang, Junwei Zhou, Yike Zhang, Jianxin Zhang, Zhihao Zhu, Xiaoyu Cao, Hailu Xu

entry.summary: Analyzes how finite-width beam search over discrete Semantic IDs constrains whether target items can appear in generative recommendation outputs, distinguishing scoreability from empirical top-K support. Proposes two continuous-query paradigms (CQG-Single and CQG-AR) that remove SID vocabularies and discrete beam expansion.

entry.title: Does Location Matter? A Black-Box Causal Audit Reveals Model-Dependent Audio Grounding in LALM Hallucination

author.name: Mohammad Khalooei, Mohammad Sabokrou

entry.summary: This paper introduces a black-box causal testing method for auditing how large audio-language models (LALMs) ground their hallucination judgments in actual audio content. By localizing claimed evidence regions using CLAP similarity, removing them via spectral gating, and comparing against controls in a 2x2x2 experimental grid, the authors show that the popular Audio-Aware Decoding (AAD) mitigation suffers from a duration confound: its blank-waveform baseline removes the whole clip rather than the relevant evidence, and results vary by model (e.g., Qwen2-Audio-7B).

entry.title: AdaC-GRPO: Towards Mastering Long-Horizon Visual Sudoku Puzzles via Adaptive Curriculum Learning

author.name: Sida Li, Yuanxin Liu, Linli Yao, Shicheng Li, Xu Sun, Haoli Bai, Xiaohui Li

entry.summary: Introduces FG-Sudoku, a fine-grained visual sudoku benchmark by grid size and deduction depth, showing frontier multimodal LLMs fail on long-range dependencies like 9x9 puzzles, causing reward sparsity that stalls standard RLVR. AdaC-GRPO adds adaptive curriculum group relative policy optimization to overcome sparsity during post-training.

entry.title: SWE-Critix: Post-Training Generalist Verifiers for Assessing Coding-Agent Trajectories

author.name: Jiajun Hu, Chun Yong Chong

entry.summary: SWE-Critix addresses the lack of oracle evaluators for coding agents by post-training generalist verifiers that can judge and explain full agent trajectories on long-horizon software engineering tasks. It moves beyond general-purpose LLM judging and scalar-reward critics toward verifiers that handle hundreds of iterative repository and tool interactions.

entry.title: Causal Effect Identifiability in Causal Abstractions: A Strict Hierarchy of Criteria

author.name: Cl\'ement Yvernes, Marianne Clausel, Emilie Devijver, Eric Gaussier

entry.summary: This theory paper formalizes causal effect identifiability at the level of causal abstractions, collections of graphs compatible with partial causal knowledge, rather than single fully specified diagrams. It organizes identifiability notions into a strict hierarchy and shows effects can be identified over graph collections even when not identifiable in any individual diagram. This relaxes the unrealistic requirement of a fully known causal graph.

entry.title: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack

author.name: Vagner Figueredo de Santana, Diogo Cortiz

entry.summary: Introduces MASTIF, a testing framework for evaluating combinations of LLMs, protocols, and agent frameworks that make up the Agentic Web, benchmarking 3 LLMs, 3 protocols, and 4 frameworks against 300 tasks. It matters because the agentic ecosystem is fragmenting across many interoperability standards and developers lack systematic guidance on which stacks work together.

entry.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?

author.name: Alexander Hickey, Joanna Knight, James Bishop

entry.summary: This paper uses the Wikipedia Game, where players must navigate from one article to a target using only hyperlinks, as a benchmark for evaluating information retrieval over very large unindexed document collections. The authors build large local graphs of Wikipedia pages across five languages and citation networks from OpenAlex, then compare sentence embedding models and LLMs on navigation tasks without third-party APIs. This provides a reproducible, self-contained testbed for studying how well language models traverse large-scale knowledge structures.

entry.title: Semantic Views: Certified Reuse of LLM Labels Across Semantic Queries

author.name: Oktie Hassanzadeh, Dharmashankar Subramanian

entry.summary: Presents SemViews, a certified semantic query filter that reuses LLM labels from earlier queries as semantic views, combined with embeddings and helper-model scores, then certifies answers with stratified oracle samples to meet precision/recall targets. Tackles the cost dilemma of LLM-as-oracle query engines with provable guarantees.

entry.title: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training

author.name: Yuxuan Gu, Kequan Niu, Xiaocheng Feng, Yun Li, Yiqiao Yang, Bing Qin

entry.summary: The paper argues that model-compatibility signals used in dynamic supervised fine-tuning (token probability, prior support) conflate compatibility with learning value, and that forcing imitation can interfere with behaviors already supported by pretraining. It proposes conditional information gain as a token-weighting criterion for SFT that better targets generalizable post-training. This refines a growing line of work on selective token-level supervision.

entry.title: PRIME: Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling Enhancement for Structured Document Retrieval-Real

author.name: Cheuk Hei Chung, Li Liu

entry.summary: PRIME is an index-side optimization framework for retrieval-augmented LLM agents that complements the usual query-side focus. It combines an LLM-driven semantic restructuring track that converts long documents into information-dense sections with deterministic metadata synthesis and hierarchical retrieval to create semantic anchors. This addresses an underexplored lever in RAG pipelines: corpus/index quality rather than retriever or generator improvements.

entry.title: When Edge Independence Fails: Joint Graph Diffusion with Latent Sociability Priors

author.name: Adarsh Jamadandi, Nicolas Keriven, Aline Roumy

entry.summary: This paper proves that discrete graph diffusion models with independent edge updates have an Erdos-Renyi terminal prior, which in the large-graph limit makes GNN denoisers ineffective at recovering node heterogeneity and higher-order structure without node features. The authors propose a joint graph diffusion approach with latent sociability priors to address this fundamental limitation. The work provides theoretical grounding for why unconditional featureless graph generation has struggled in practice.

entry.title: A Categorical Atlas of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: Cones, Orbits, and Gauges

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Zhizhou Sha, Chiwun Yang, Dai Shi

entry.summary: The paper reframes parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods categorically: a pretrained checkpoint is a base point in weight space and each method is a smooth map from a small parameter space, forming a slice category with the frozen model as initial and full fine-tuning as terminal objects. Three invariants of these maps (local image, fibers, base change) organize expressivity, training dynamics, and common PEFT design moves.

entry.title: Controlled-Minimax: Stabilizing Adversarial Optimization via Control Theory

author.name: Tianjiao Luo, Jianfei Chen, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes instabilities in adversarial (minimax) training by modeling training dynamics as a second-order ODE, attributing non-convergence to the Hessian's eigenstructure near equilibria. It proposes Controlled-Minimax, which treats the optimization trajectory as a controllable physical system and applies derived feedback control rather than heuristic regularization. This offers a principled remedy for limit cycles and divergence in adversarial learning.

entry.title: CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jingru Yang, Jinhang Wu, Minjing Shi, Shengfeng He, Xuyan Li, Man Tan, Biye Li

entry.summary: CAST tackles credit assignment in cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation: chunk-level decoded-text alignment specifies how much a span should change but not how the signal distributes across student tokens, leaving unaligned tokens unconstrained. The shift-or-stay framework redistributes chunk advantages using predictive uncertainty and teacher-signal smoothness while anchoring selective tokens. This resolves a concrete technical gap in distilling across tokenizer boundaries.

entry.title: CopRoute: Dependence-Aware Conformal Routing for Language Models

author.name: Siva Rajesh Kasa, Santhosh Kumar Kasa, Karan Gupta

entry.summary: Introduces a conformal routing method for set-based LLM routing that accounts for the dependence structure of model failures, unlike prior risk-controlled policies that score models in isolation with a single threshold. By exploiting complementarity between models, it can control all-miss risk while reducing redundant inference calls. Relevant to cost-efficient multi-model serving.

entry.title: SBNO : Schr\"odinger Bridge Neural Operator for the Forward and Inverse Problems under Missing Information

author.name: Jaehyeon Park, Inhyeok Jeong, Noseong Park

entry.summary: This paper introduces SBNO, a diffusion Schrodinger bridge matching framework for PDE surrogate modeling that handles both forward and inverse problems when observations are sparse or the governing physics is only partially known. It learns a pair of time-dependent drifts from a mask-aware endpoint coupling, preserving input-solution pairing during training and supporting both task directions within one equation-free model. This matters because practical scientific applications often lack the dense data or fully specified equations that conventional neural operators require.

entry.title: Studying the Effects of Task Diversity Using Small Mathematical Worlds

author.name: Emily Xia Meng, Xuanyu Yang, Junaid Hasan, Michael Ruofan Zeng, Henry Kvinge

entry.summary: The authors introduce IntWorld and PermWorld, procedurally generated ecosystems of distinct but related mathematical tasks that permit precise control of task diversity. These small worlds serve as tractable testbeds for studying how task diversity during training shapes neural network behavior, mimicking the multi-task exposure of language models.

entry.title: Prediction Is Not a Sufficient Memory State

author.name: Robert Jenkinson Alvarez

entry.summary: This theory paper characterizes when a fixed-dimension recurrent state can support exact cumulative learning, proving that for smooth convex residual losses such a state exists exactly when the loss is polynomial, with precise coordinate requirements growing combinatorially in degree. Non-polynomial losses yield unbounded memory requirements even among histories with identical current predictions.

entry.title: MolP2SBench: Do LLMs Really Reason from Molecular Properties to Structure?

author.name: Yuhang Xie, Zhiyi Shi, Zeyi Zhang, Zhisheng Qi, Yushun Dong, Yu Wang, Xiongye Xiao

entry.summary: The paper introduces MolP2SBench, a benchmark testing whether LLMs genuinely reason from molecular properties to structure by presenting masked scaffolds with given properties and asking models to select the missing structure among plausible candidates. By shuffling or replacing properties, it tests whether predictions rely on correct property-structure pairing and respond to counterfactual property changes, with a Property-Gap-based channel-wise leaderboard.

entry.title: Two-way Guidance: Simultaneous Learning of Summary Statistics for Generative Bayes

author.name: Percy S. Zhai, Max Pachman, Peverel D. Shipley, Jungeum Kim

entry.summary: Proposes learning sufficient summary statistics jointly with the posterior in simulation-based inference, using structural restrictions on how the posterior learner depends on the learned summary. The identified two-way guidance mechanism helps scalable SBI recover concentrated posteriors as observation size grows.

entry.title: Sonic-AMG: Streaming Human Motion Generation from Spatial Audio

author.name: Jingcheng Ni, Zekun Li, Zhiyang Dou, Xiaoyan Cong, Ziyao Zeng, Hongyang Du, Randall Balestriero, Taku Komura, Srinath Sridhar

entry.summary: Sonic-AMG is presented as the first framework for streaming human motion generation conditioned on spatial audio, encoding acoustic content and body-relative source geometry as separate tokens for a causal transformer with a flow head. Unlike prior offline approaches, the model reacts to sounds as they arrive, mimicking human reactive behavior. This enables applications in VR, avatars, and interactive agents.

entry.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Discrete-Time Self-Attention Dynamics in Transformers

author.name: Claudio Altafini

entry.summary: The paper provides a thorough discrete-time analysis of self-attention dynamics, giving a complete classification of equilibria and their stability in single-head and multihead cases, in contrast to prior continuous-time treatments. It shows the main attractor is a consensus equilibrium aligned with the principal eigenvector of the value matrix. This deepens theoretical understanding of how transformers' attention layers evolve when layer index is treated as time.

entry.title: Scalable Sparse Autoregressive Variational Inference for Non-Gaussian Spatial Fields

author.name: Paul F. V. Wiemann, Matthias Katzfuss

entry.summary: This work introduces a scalable variational inference framework for latent Gaussian process models with non-Gaussian likelihoods, mirroring the sparse nearest-neighbor autoregressive structure of the prior in the variational family. It uses normalizing-flow conditionals and a shared neural conditioner to amortize parameters, achieving polylogarithmic per-iteration complexity on large spatial datasets.

entry.title: Activating the Annotator: Operationalising Lived Experience in Data Annotation

author.name: Sheza Munir, Ramaravind Kommiya Mothilal, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed

entry.summary: Proposes AXLE, a pre-annotation stage where scenario vignettes prime annotators via axis-guided conversations synthesized into first-person micro-narratives before labeling, moving beyond static demographic forms for capturing positionality. This operationalizes perspectivist NLP insights about how annotator identity shapes subjective labels.

entry.title: Evo$^2$: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution

author.name: Chejian Xu, Shujian Zhang, Wenxuan Zhou, John Lambert, Beck Chen, Bo Li, Andrew Hard, Rajiv Mathews

entry.summary: Proposes Evo2, a self-evolution framework that jointly updates model weights and the agent harness via a dual-role pipeline where one policy acts as both Proposer and Executor, connecting two previously separate self-improvement approaches. Targets improving language model systems without human intervention.

entry.title: A Better Metric Will Not Save You: What You Compare Beats How You Compare It

author.name: Noureddine Khaous (LLF - UMR7110, UPCit\'e), Guillaume Wisniewski (LLF - UMR7110, UPCit\'e)

entry.summary: Argues that representational similarity measures (RSA, CKA, Procrustes) are dominated by upstream decisions about which input conditions are compared and how they are grouped, rather than by the choice of metric. Using vowel acoustic organization across fifteen languages and twenty-seven representations, changing the compared categories moved the measured gap more than twice the effect being measured. A sharp methodological critique for interpretability and representational analysis.

entry.title: MVGraph: Benchmarking LVLMs on Evidence Composition across Multi-View Visual Graph

author.name: Yingjie Zhu, Han Cheng, Xuefeng Bai, Youcheng Pan, Yang Xiang, Kehai Chen

entry.summary: Introduces MVGraph, a benchmark of 8k programmatically constructed instances across 8 graph-theoretic tasks that tests whether large vision-language models can align and compose evidence distributed across multiple interrelated visual graph views. It fills a gap left by single-structure graph reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Multimodal Image-based Robotic Assistance and Guidance Environment (MIRAGE): A Novel Unified Framework for Surgical Navigation and Visualization

author.name: Ehsan Nasiri, Yi Zheng, Michael A. Kokko, Xiaoyao Fan, William R. Warner, Keith D. Paulsen, Ryan J. Halter

entry.summary: MIRAGE is a multimodal image-guided robotic surgery framework integrating stereovision reconstruction, AR video overlay, heads-up display navigation, and intraoperative ultrasound into the da Vinci console. It includes calibration, registration, and 3D point-cloud reconstruction modules with quantitative preclinical evaluation. This provides a unified open architecture for surgical navigation research on a clinical platform.

entry.title: PATACON: GPU-Parallel Tangent-Bundle RRT-Connect for Constrained Motion Planning

author.name: Gahyun Oh, Junho An, Suhyun Jeon, Suhan Park

entry.summary: PATACON is a GPU-parallel bidirectional planner that steers directly on the tangent bundle of constraint manifolds rather than in the ambient configuration space, reducing the overhead of repeated constraint projection in highly constrained, high-dimensional planning. It targets fast whole-body motion planning for humanoids that must continuously replan in dynamic environments.

entry.title: Gaussian BROJA Partial Information Decomposition in Closed Form

author.name: Ohad Sheelo, Tal Golan, Ari Pakman

entry.summary: The paper derives a closed-form solution to the BROJA partial information decomposition optimization for jointly Gaussian variables, enabling direct computation of unique, redundant, and synergistic information components in the general multivariate Gaussian setting. This yields speedups exceeding two orders of magnitude over prior numerical optimization approaches.

entry.title: Representation Alignment from a Few Paired Data via Distilled Optimal Transport

author.name: Julien Kordes, Reuben Dorent

entry.summary: The method aligns two independently pretrained unimodal encoders using only 100-500 paired examples by expressing representations via similarities to paired anchors, matching modalities with entropic optimal transport whose marginals counteract hubness, and distilling the plan into lightweight inductive encoders. This drastically reduces the paired-data requirement compared to millions of examples. Valuable for data-scarce multimodal alignment, e.g., medical imaging.

entry.title: SWEAR: Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning via Self-Rated Difficulty

author.name: Yixuan Li, Minghao Lv, Xuenan Xu, Zihao Zheng, Mengyue Wu

entry.summary: Proposes SWEAR, a difficulty-aware adaptive reasoning framework for large audio-language models that derives five-dimensional difficulty scores and compressed reasoning traces, learns difficulty signals during SFT, and uses RL to allocate reasoning effort across stages. It improves accuracy on MMAU-test-mini and MMAR while substantially reducing generation length.

entry.title: A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO

author.name: Ronghan Li, Fei Chen, Mingyu Lu

entry.summary: This paper studies whether GRPO training should persistently select medium-difficulty samples or progress toward harder ones, re-estimating sample difficulty under the current policy as it evolves. It provides an analysis of where curriculum difficulty progression helps and where it does not, refining the popular easy-to-hard heuristic for RL fine-tuning of reasoning models. The findings inform practical data selection in GRPO pipelines.

entry.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics

author.name: Weiliang Chen, Song Liao

entry.summary: Proposes RATED, a tool retrieval framework combining a frozen contrastive dual-encoder with a lightweight contextual bandit that re-ranks tools based on real-time execution feedback, enabling rapid adaptation to runtime tool failures. Also introduces EcoAgent, a benchmark of 5,172 real-world tools for evaluating retrieval under execution dynamics.

entry.title: Don't Guess, Just Ask: Evaluating Interactive Requirement Clarification for Repository-Level Software Development

author.name: Mingyu Chen, Zhiqing Zhong, Manyi Wang, Linxi Liang, Rouyu Chen, Pinjia He

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates whether LLMs can transform vague user intent into clear requirements through interactive clarification before coding at the repository level, a stage most coding benchmarks skip. It measures how clarification capability affects subsequent code generation and rework costs. The work fills a real evaluation gap between underspecified requests and full specifications.

entry.title: AudioTETRIS: Token Elimination via Transitional Importance Signals for Efficient Audio LLMs

author.name: Shreya Sajid, Anna Vettoruzzo, Joaquin Vanschoren

entry.summary: AudioTETRIS is a training-free token compression method for large audio language models that exploits the structured temporal patterns of speech, pruning based on importance peaks at acoustic transitions rather than generic attention or feature similarity. By preserving fine-grained phonetic transitions that coarse similarity-based methods destroy, it reduces the quadratic self-attention cost of audio token sequences without retraining.

entry.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents

author.name: Jingwei Song, Zhisheng Chen, Bingfan Zeng, Jing Tang, Yubo Hou, Jinhao Jing, Zhengwei Xie, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: MC-EvoBench is a controlled Minecraft benchmark with 19 registered evolution chains and paired probe families designed to audit whether embodied agents genuinely acquire reusable capabilities from interaction history. It explicitly separates capability change from confounds like carried-over resources, unequal source exposure, and early execution failures. It targets evaluation of recursive self-improvement claims in embodied agents.

entry.title: Primal-Dual Flow Matching for Sample-Wise Constrained Generation

author.name: Zhengyan Huan, Peter Y. Lu, Shuchin Aeron

entry.summary: PDFM extends flow matching to generation under sample-wise constraints with a user-specified probability of satisfaction, deriving theoretical guarantees for a primal-dual optimization algorithm. The practical implementation requires only binary membership oracle feedback and offers direct control over the constraint satisfaction rate.

entry.title: Cross-Behavior Policy Optimization: Unified Learning from Offline Demonstrations and On- and Off-Policy Rollouts via a Shared Regression Target

author.name: Du Cheng, Junyu Lu, Jingfan Zhang, Yuzhuo Zhang, Haoxuan Jia, Shichao Weng

entry.summary: CBPO unifies supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for reasoning post-training through a single regression loss with a fixed-reference target that is independent of the generating policy. This lets offline demonstrations, reference responses, and current and historical rollouts share a common reward-labeled replay buffer, enabling continued reuse of collected responses without coordinating separate objectives.

entry.title: Double-Take: Improving Capacity, Binding, and Selectivity In Long-Context Within Bidirectional Memory

author.name: Vakul Raghavan, Utkarsh Grover, Mingyang Mao, Chengwen Wang, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: The paper studies why fixed-size memories fail to keep distant information usable as context grows, examining large-chunk test-time training (TTT) and identifying failures in single-step writes that accumulate interference. Double-Take proposes improvements to capacity, binding, and selectivity as distinct requirements for usable long-context memory. This contributes to the architectural frontier of sub-quadratic long-context models.

entry.title: PDE-PFN: Prior-Data Fitted Neural PDE Solver

author.name: Jaehyeon Park, Mingu Kang, Dongseok Lee, Woojin Cho, Kookjin Lee, Anthony Gruber, Youngjoon Hong, Noseong Park

entry.summary: Proposes a prior-data fitted network for in-context prediction of PDE solution fields, pre-trained on noisy approximate solutions from physics-informed neural networks. Inspired by LLM robustness to noisy pre-training data, it approximates the posterior predictive mean of PDE solutions via transformer-based self- and cross-attention. This allows solving PDEs without exact simulation data.

entry.title: Randomized Momentum Transport with Cheap Predictors

author.name: El Mahdi Chayti, Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: This paper randomizes the transport correction in momentum methods like STORM, evaluating it only with probability q and otherwise using a cheap prediction with importance weighting. Under stated assumptions, linear minimization oracle updates including normalized, sign, and Muon-style spectral directions retain O(T^-1/3) stationarity bounds with reduced per-iteration cost.

entry.title: Golden Anchor for Video Generation

author.name: Jinyuan Xu, Shitong Shao, Lichen Bai, Zikai Zhou, Guoxi Huang, Nantheera Anantrasirichai, Zeke Xie

entry.summary: Investigates whether text-to-image generated anchor images are truly suitable for image-to-video generation pipelines, finding that anchor aesthetic and quality scores correlate only weakly with downstream video quality and that some structure-and-texture scores correlate negatively. Proposes improvements to anchor selection for video generation.

entry.title: From 2.1M Hours of Raw Broadcast Audio to Finnish Speech SSL: Confidence Filtering and Architectural Analysis at Scale

author.name: Yaroslav Getman, Tam\'as Gr\'osz, Tommi Lehtonen, Mikko Kurimo

entry.summary: A large-scale Finnish speech SSL study starting from 2.1M hours of broadcast audio, proposing ASR confidence as a data-quality filter that yields 3-7% relative WER improvements over LID-based filtering despite a smaller training set. Also contributes controlled architectural analysis for non-English SSL.

entry.title: OGPO: Offline Goal-conditioned Policy Optimization for Recoverable Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Xule Gao, Xi Wang, Zehua Zang, Rui Wang, Changwen Zheng, Chuxiong Sun

entry.summary: OGPO reformulates VLA post-training as offline goal-conditioned policy optimization, relabeling demonstrations as goal-conditioned transitions rather than step-wise action labels, to teach recovery toward task-progress states when execution deviates from demonstrated paths. It addresses a real weakness of imitation-trained robot policies. Relevant to making robot manipulation policies robust and recoverable.

entry.title: VETR: Execution-Grounded Self-Improving Agent for Symbolic Graphics Reasoning

author.name: Yingbo Ma, Kuangshi Ai, Gordon Dai, Chenglong Yu, Chaoli Wang, Hua Shen

entry.summary: Proposes VETR, a framework for agentic recursive self-improvement over executable world representations in symbolic graphics reasoning, extracting actionable evidence from execution traces such as which proposed edits survived, disappeared, or interfered. It retains aligned program/render records with bounded runtime observations to provide less ambiguous supervision than final renders alone.

entry.title: Competence-Aware Orchestration for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Songmiao Wang, Yuchen Wang, Chenglin Yu, Hongxia Yang, Ming Li

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage competence-aware orchestration framework for LLM multi-agent systems that models the backbone's task-conditioned competence and uses it to adapt role activation and the communication graph, avoiding collaboration overhead on easy queries. Across six benchmarks it achieves average gains (abstract truncated before full numbers).

entry.title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC

author.name: Donatella Genovese, Philip Ploner, Simone Scardapane, Stefano Giagu, Thea Klaeboe Aarrestad

entry.summary: This paper addresses the interpretability gap in using learned neural embeddings for anomaly detection at the LHC, where flagged events must be diagnosed to separate new physics from detector mismodeling. It evaluates supervised and self-supervised embedding strategies and provides local diagnostics to recover physical observables from learned representations. This work supports deploying anomaly detection into actual discovery pipelines at HL-LHC.

entry.title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Shi-Yu Tian, Yong Liu, Ximan Liu, Tianrui Zhu, Sule Bai, Xinwei Yang, Ruiqi Liu, Kun-Yang Yu, Ming Yang, Zhi Zhou, Yu-Feng Li, Yipeng Sun, Gu Simiu

entry.summary: Road MOPD identifies gradient conflicts in multi-teacher on-policy distillation when diverse teachers supervise shared student parameters, even with domain routing. It introduces non-routed teachers as auxiliary cross-domain guards during joint optimization to prevent capability degradation. This addresses a real obstacle to scaling multi-teacher distillation.

entry.title: Cancerous Backdoor Attack: Gradual Activation via Invisible Tokens and A Stage Controller

author.name: Tahmid Imtiaz Imu, Emama Nahid, Prodipta Sen Amartya, Ahsanul Jobayer, Yutong Song, Jiang Wu, Pengfei Zhang, Honghui Xu

entry.summary: Presents a novel LLM backdoor attack where malicious behavior develops gradually across multi-turn interactions using invisible tokens hidden from the user and a stage controller tracking attack progression. This advances understanding of stealthy, staged threats against deployed language models.

entry.title: An all-transistor physical-learning transformer can be trained to perform in-context learning

author.name: Michael C. Abbott, Benjamin B. Machta

entry.summary: The authors extend physical learning frameworks (equilibrium propagation, coupled learning) to an attention mechanism by introducing circuit elements that restore bidirectional information flow through nonlinear multiply-capable circuits, built with an all-transistor design exploiting exponential current-voltage characteristics. The resulting physical transformer can be trained to perform in-context learning. This is a step toward transformers implemented and trained directly in analog hardware.

entry.title: Neural expectation-maximization and meta-models

author.name: Zhuolin Fu

entry.summary: This theoretical paper interprets Transformers as learned approximations to a hybrid probabilistic inference procedure combining max-product loopy belief propagation with expectation-maximization on partially observed Markov random fields. Self-attention is shown to implement a differentiable LBP approximation, and depth corresponds to EM-style updates of latent representations and transition parameters.

entry.title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics

author.name: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou

entry.summary: The paper shows that random data splits in ML benchmarks for perovskite solar cells leak information because nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another. The authors map institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database, propose a hierarchy of grouped splits isolating duplicates, publications, and institutions, and benchmark thirteen models, revealing a regime shift where tree ensembles lose their advantage.

entry.title: Gaussian-Width Bounds for Offline-to-Online Linear Bandits

author.name: Kushagra Chandak, Volodymyr Tkachuk, Xiaoqi Tan, Csaba Szepesv\'ari

entry.summary: This theory paper tightens regret analysis for linear bandits with partially covered offline data, showing prior sqrt(dkT) bounds stem from loose control of reward prediction error. Using concentration of Lipschitz functions of Gaussian vectors, it derives a phased elimination algorithm with regret order k-sqrt(T) and proves matching lower bounds for the unit Euclidean ball. Notable authorship including Csaba Szepesvari lends credibility.

entry.title: Rethinking Relative Policy Differences Transfer of On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Rong Wu, Daocheng Fu, Yu Yang, Xuemeng Yang, Siqi Li, Shu Zou, Yao Zhu, Botian Shi, Bo Zhang, Cong Zhang, Pinlong Cai, Jianbiao Mei

entry.summary: This paper develops a unified view of on-policy distillation where the log-probability ratio between a proxy expert and proxy reference acts as an implicit reward for KL-regularized policy optimization. It clarifies which relative differences provide useful supervision and which target policies can benefit, recovering conventional OPD as a special case. This relaxes the requirement that the teacher be substantially stronger than the student.

entry.title: Recovering Irreducible Three-Body Interactions with Lagrangian Neural Networks

author.name: Sena Kalabalik, Sukru Caglar, Abdullah Umut Hamzaogullari, Arkadas Ozakin

entry.summary: Extends Lagrangian Neural Networks beyond pairwise-additive interactions by showing they can recover the Axilrod-Teller three-body dispersion term, an irreducible many-body interaction, from trajectory data alone. Kinetic energy is prescribed exactly while only the potential is learned. This answers an open question about the expressivity of variational-structure-biased learning of mechanics.

entry.title: Returning to Development States: When Full Sandbox Snapshots Help Coding Agents

author.name: Daniel Thi Graviet, Tanmay Shah

entry.summary: This work applies Go-Explore-style search over full virtual-machine snapshots to coding-agent failure recovery, restoring and branching from intermediate environment states instead of restarting from scratch. It finds gains come mainly from progress outside the repository, such as databases and runtime service state.

entry.title: Partially Informed Stochastic Optimization via Zeroth-Order Residual Tracking

author.name: El Mahdi Chayti, Alireza Mirrokni, Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: PISO addresses settings where only part of the gradient is directly accessible, combining the available component with a running zeroth-order estimate of the residual. By centering probes on this estimate, the variance due to random probing depends on tracking error rather than residual magnitude, yielding a contraction mechanism and a principled view of momentum.

entry.title: Bridging Human and Model Attention: Explainability Analysis of CNN, Mamba, and ViT Architectures with Gaze-Based Validation

author.name: Marco Stefani, Edoardo Parpaiola, Matteo Bino, Gianluca Caregnato, Francesco Roncolato, Daniel Fusaro, Loris Nanni, Alberto Pretto

entry.summary: This systematic study quantifies alignment between post-hoc attribution maps from CNNs, Vision Transformers, and Vision Mamba models and human gaze, using eye-tracking ground truth and a standardized normalization pipeline that maps both onto spatial probability distributions. Alignment is measured via Jensen-Shannon similarity across fine-grained classification, medical imaging, and emotion recognition tasks.

entry.title: Lower Bounds for Randomized Linear-Oracle Optimization over Strongly Convex Sets

author.name: Sebastian Pokutta

entry.summary: The paper strengthens recent worst-case lower bounds of order 1/T^2 for linear minimization oracle (Frank-Wolfe style) optimization over strongly convex sets by extending them to randomized algorithms. It also shows the prior deterministic bound's constructions are brittle, with prescribed trajectories amplifying initialization errors exponentially. This resolves robustness concerns around a recently settled open question in first-order oracle complexity.

entry.title: Hitting-Time Bounds for Asynchronous Q-Learning

author.name: Yang Peng

entry.summary: This paper proves last-iterate high-probability sup-norm error bounds for standard asynchronous Q-learning from a single trajectory, allowing periodic behavior-policy chains and characterizing sample complexity via the effective horizon and hitting times of the reverse chain. Zero-initialized Q-learning with constant step sizes achieves epsilon error in order H^4 transitions plus a hitting-time term.

entry.title: Fear Is Not Always Fear: Variation in Emotion Label Equivalence Across Datasets

author.name: Emily \"Ohman, Anna Koufakou

entry.summary: Tests whether same-named emotion labels mean the same thing across GoEmotions, XED, and BRIGHTER, finding dramatic scale mismatches (one fear classifier flags 71% of texts, another 8%) that training-label prevalence largely explains. Cross-corpus transfer loses 55% of native discrimination, and simple recalibration cannot repair it.

entry.title: PreSTO: Predictive Subtree Prefetching for Fast LLM Power Sampling

author.name: Nan Jiang, Panagiotis Theodoropoulos, Wei Deng

entry.summary: Proposes PreSTO, which accelerates PowerMH (the sampler behind power sampling for test-time LLM reasoning) by prefetching future Metropolis-Hastings proposals as a tree of accept/reject decisions, provably leaving the MH transition kernel unchanged. Avoids changing the sampler or model unlike prior speedups.

entry.title: Structural Automata for Neural Semantic Parsing

author.name: Xiao Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates structural automata at decoding, post-processing, and training stages of semantic parsing to DRS and AMR, introducing accepting-path decoding which guarantees well-formed outputs within a length limit by tracking verified completions without token retraction. This goes beyond constrained decoding, which only prevents locally invalid tokens. A rigorous formal-methods-flavored contribution to structured generation.

entry.title: Knowing Is Not Telling: Identity Ossification in LLM Representations of Trans-border Communities

author.name: Minglu Sun, Lan Chen, Hang Jiang

entry.summary: Studies how LLMs represent nine transborder ethnic communities along China's southwestern border, defining identity ossification—the collapsing of fluid cross-border identities into single nation-state identities—and introducing the Transborder Identity Ossification benchmark. This surfaces a novel representational failure mode with real social consequences for marginalized groups. A distinctive contribution at the intersection of LLM bias and area studies.

entry.title: PriMoRetarget: Humanoid Motion Transfer Through Prioritized Motion Retargeting

author.name: Nicholas Ioannidis, Dun Yang, Max Smith, Tue Vu, Ziyu Zhang, Shayegan Omidshafiei, Xue Bin Peng

entry.summary: Introduces PriMoRetarget, a motion-retargeting framework that replaces weighted multi-objective optimization with an explicit priority hierarchy, constraining lower-priority updates to preserve higher-priority motion characteristics. Particularly useful for multi-character and object interactions where contacts and spatial relationships must be preserved.

entry.title: Tactile Sensing-based Secure and Gentle Grasping of Unknown Objects

author.name: Feng Han

entry.summary: This work presents an online data-driven predictive control framework for grasping unknown objects safely, enforcing both slip avoidance and gentle contact force constraints. Compact single-channel tactile sensors characterize gripper-object dynamics in real time without prior knowledge or offline training, with a finite-state-machine mechanism for grasping force probing. It addresses a practical gap in reliable manipulation of novel objects.

entry.title: PartiGen: Part-Aware Representations for Language-Conditioned Humanoid Motion Generation

author.name: Chuxuan Huang, Zhanxiang Cao, Tianyue Zhan, Haoyang Li, Yang Zhang, Liyun Yan, Chenlin Ming, Keqi Zhu, Yizhi Chen, Shengcheng Fu, Zihao Zhou, Xinyi Peng, Kaixuan Zhang, Boyang Xing, Jiawei Bao, Yang Yang, Yue Gao

entry.summary: PartiGen is a part-aware latent diffusion framework for language-conditioned humanoid motion generation that embeds anatomical structure into a whole-body latent representation using part-specific attention over masked frame features. It generates motion primitives autoregressively with forward-kinematics supervision and a learned end-of-sequence predictor to select motion duration.

entry.title: ManeuverFlow: Maneuver Hypothesis Generation with Future Evidence for Trajectory Evaluation and Refinement in End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuhao Wei, Yong Chen, Chen Yang, Yingchen Wang, Delin Ouyang, Lingfeng Qi, Qi Lan, Zhanhua Zhang, Jie Li, Guofa Li

entry.summary: ManeuverFlow generates trajectories for distinct driving intentions in one step by selecting maneuver modes and drawing from a Gaussian mixture prior via a maneuver-oriented flow model, then evaluates and refines candidates using current and future evidence. It targets the scaling bottleneck of candidate-based planners where small sets miss maneuvers and large sets are costly.

entry.title: Mapless, Stabilizing, and Anti-Stuck Flipper Control for Articulated Tracked Robots

author.name: Valent\'yn \v{C}\'ihala, Pavel Sarga, Martin Pecka, Tom\'a\v{s} Svoboda, Karel Zimmermann

entry.summary: SAS is a mapless flipper controller for articulated tracked robots that combines a body roll/pitch stabilization term with an anti-stuck term, using only IMU, flipper joint angles, and a short-window motion cue that avoids odometry drift corrupting remembered terrain maps. It is deployed on a real tracked robot, targeting rescue and rough-terrain scenarios where elevation maps are unreliable.

entry.title: Spatial Prediction with Guided Diffusion

author.name: Andrew Zammit-Mangion, Lachlan Astfalck, Rapha\"el Huser, Christopher Nemeth, Henry B. Moss

entry.summary: The authors show how guided diffusion models from machine learning can be used for spatial and spatio-temporal prediction in geostatistics, sampling from predictive distributions that are rarely available in closed form under hierarchical models. This bridges modern generative modeling with classical spatial statistics where the likelihood is difficult to handle.

entry.title: VIGOR: Verifiable Industrial Geometry Optimization and Repair in Scene Programs

author.name: Fuqiang Wang, Zheng Guo, Xiaoming Wu, Hanlin Kong, Nayu Liu, Chuanting Zhang, Daojun Liang, Jingxuan Wei

entry.summary: Identifies the executability-engineering-feasibility gap in LLM-generated industrial scene programs, where code runs but violates coupled boundary, collision, clearance, or structural constraints. It contributes an execution-grounded dataset of 1,749 constructible scenarios with executable verification to make this gap measurable and support repair research.

entry.title: MAGMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Embodied Agents under Dynamic Tasks and Execution Failures

author.name: Loan Bernat (LAAS-GEPETTO), Matthieu Grard (LAAS-RAP), Ariane Herbulot (LAAS-RAP), Florent Lamiraux (LAAS-GEPETTO)

entry.summary: MAGMA-Bench is an architecture-agnostic benchmark evaluating persistent task reasoning in dynamic multi-robot environments, covering task horizons, execution failures, interruptions, mission updates, and heterogeneous robot coordination. A structured skill-level interface separates task-level reasoning from low-level control. It fills a gap at the intersection of dynamic task execution and multi-agent embodied coordination.

entry.title: Realism VS Accuracy: Event Sequence Forecasting from a Generative Modeling Perspective

author.name: Dmitry Osin, Egor Surkov, Petr Mokrov, Igor Udovichenko, Ivan Karpukhin, Evgeny Burnaev, Egor Shvetsov, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: The paper studies multi-horizon event sequence forecasting as conditional generative modeling, presenting a benchmark with metrics for both prediction accuracy and distributional realism, strong statistical baselines, adapted models from adjacent fields, and curated real-world datasets. Evaluation reveals no method excels at both, exposing a fundamental accuracy-realism trade-off. Applications span finance, healthcare, and business process intelligence.

entry.title: Rationally Linearized MLPs

author.name: Arijit Sehanobish, Byeongchan Kim, Avinava Dubey, Min-hwan Oh, Krzysztof Choromanski

entry.summary: Introduces RaLiMPs, a method for efficiently linearizing MLPs via low-degree rational approximations of activation functions, constructing kernel representations with narrow bottlenecks that compose across layers. The paper provides approximation guarantees and evaluates on applications from implicit 3D models to LLMs, showing favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs. Extends polynomial-linearization ideas with better approximation efficiency.

entry.title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire

author.name: Scott C. Lowe, Sander W. Keemink

entry.summary: SpireBench uses the full commercial deck-builder Slay the Spire to evaluate long-horizon strategic reasoning in LLM agents. Across 20 models at maximum difficulty, frontier models beat heuristics and match average humans but fall far behind experts, with the gap widening as runs lengthen. The benchmark helps disentangle knowledge, reasoning, and luck in long-horizon agentic performance.

entry.title: SmartSalesBench: A Resistance-Aware Multi-Turn Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Sales Agents

author.name: P N Bhargav Teja, Velpula Lokesh Reddy, Madhu Basumata, Susen Sarkar, Rajasekhara Reddy Duvvuru Muni

entry.summary: Presents the first multi-turn benchmark testing LLM sales agents against psychologically grounded buyer personas programmed to resist, inverting the cooperative-user assumption of typical task-oriented dialogue benchmarks. It includes 13,680 sessions across agent profiles, personas, and price tiers, grounded via retrieval-augmented generation.

entry.title: Looking Ahead and Back: Anticipatory Generative Modeling for Road-Network Trajectories

author.name: Zhenhao Huang, Li Sun, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Recasts road-network trajectory generation as generative route choice modeling over intersections rather than location simulation, targeting the critical decision points where multiple outgoing paths look plausible. The anticipatory approach considers downstream consequences of transitions, addressing off-network drift in diffusion-based methods.

entry.title: RoleWorld: Knowledge Transfer in World Modeling with Functional Role Abstractions

author.name: Boyuan Xiao, Pu Wang, Ji Feng, Yao-Xiang Ding

entry.summary: RoleWorld is a symbolic world modeling framework that helps LLM agents transfer world knowledge across environments with similar interaction structures. Instead of organizing dynamics around environment-specific objects, it uses reusable prototypes and environment-specific parameter values as functional role abstractions, learned from interaction trajectories. This enables more efficient generalization of world models to novel environments.

entry.title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy

author.name: Naji Alazhar, Wassel Alazhar

entry.summary: Extends the HiSparse KV-cache hierarchy so that speculative decoding methods (DSpark, DFlash2) work over host-memory sparse KV storage, adapting cache residency to GPU load. This improves long-context inference throughput by keeping the working set in limited GPU memory while retrieving history on demand.

entry.title: KITE: A Knowledge-Injected Temporal Encoder for Time-Series Event Forecasting

author.name: Jonas Petersen, Pratik Jawahar, Riccardo Maggioni, Gian-Alessandro Lombardi, Matteo Cozzi, Marek Gajewski, Federico Martelli, Camilla Mazzoleni, Philipp Christian Petersen

entry.summary: Proposes KITE, which injects expert knowledge (semantic priors) about rare-event precursors into a self-supervised time-series forecaster via switchable covariate and attention-bias mechanisms, each identity at its null setting so one architecture serves all prior types. Addresses the core problem that rare high-cost events leave too little data to learn from.

entry.title: COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering

author.name: Kavinda Kehelella, Sanghamitra Dutta

entry.summary: This work studies few-shot distillation of LLMs for open-book question answering and shows that choosing uncertain samples near the teacher decision boundary can substantially hurt distillation performance. It proposes a counterfactual-guided sample selection method to pick better training examples for the student model. The finding that harder-is-not-better in sample selection is a useful practical insight for efficient distillation.

entry.title: Collective Autonomous Vehicle Routing Needs Social Awareness for Coexistence with Human Drivers

author.name: Anastasia Psarou, Mikolaj Rams, Blazej Torbus, Rafal Kucharski

entry.summary: Using multi-agent reinforcement learning on real-world traffic networks (Ingolstadt, Provins), the authors show selfish AV route choices create negative externalities for human drivers. They add a marginal-cost social term to the AV reward, capturing each AV's impact on others via counterfactual simulation. The result argues that social awareness is necessary for mixed-autonomy traffic coexistence.

entry.title: FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems

author.name: Vishnu Arun, Adam Obeng, Tianyou Wang, Zilin Ren, Mukuntha Narayanan Sundararaman, Han Wang, Shivin Thukral, Zhixiang Wang, Saurabh Vishwas Joshi, Darren Reger

entry.summary: FORTE is a model-agnostic production framework from a large industrial team for discovering, validating, and safely removing features in recommender systems, tackling the lifecycle asymmetry where feature addition must show gains but removal must cause no regressions. It uses efficient perturbation for daily evaluation and addresses real constraints like A/B test contention and multi-model coordination. It offers rare documentation of feature-deprecation practice at industrial scale.

entry.title: Sample-Adaptive Zeroth-Order Post-Training

author.name: Haiyuan Wan, Yanyi Li, Weicheng Lin, Cong Fang

entry.summary: SAZO improves zeroth-order fine-tuning of LLMs by learning sample importance online from gradient-norm information extractable from directional differences, then adaptively allocating queries via per-example exponential moving averages. This reduces estimation variance and accelerates convergence versus uniform sampling of training examples. It targets memory-efficient post-training without backpropagation.

entry.title: Critical Mass: Structure-Disjoint Splits Drift With the Libraries They Are Built On

author.name: Tomo Oga, Devesh Shah, Cailum M. K. Stienstra, Gabriel Asher, Antonio H. de O. Fonseca, Niall O'Connor, Michael Widrich

entry.summary: This paper shows that the standard structure-disjoint evaluation convention in molecular machine learning, single-linkage clustering under MCES distance at a threshold set on 29,000 molecules, no longer reflects current libraries of over 227,000 molecules. The authors propose an optimized version of the criterion to make the split computationally feasible at scale and study how evaluation splits drift as databases grow.

entry.title: HART: Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time series Foundation Model

author.name: Qingwen Lin, Boyan Xu, Shifeng Xie, Zhifeng Hao, Keli Zhang, Ruichu Cai

entry.summary: HART is a time-series foundation model combining attention and RWKV-7 layers for non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting. The authors identify a mechanism called Placeholder Idling Decay that explains RWKV-7's long-horizon degradation when future patches are missing inputs, and design a hybrid architecture and gating adjustments to compensate.

entry.title: GIST: Generator-state-Informed Supervision for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Zhangyang Peng, Jingze Shi, Tongyi Zhang, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: This paper targets tabular foundation models built on prior-data fitted networks, arguing that sampling hard query labels during pretraining introduces avoidable variability. GIST exploits intermediate generator states to average query losses over conditional label distributions, yielding tractable, input-consistent supervision targets. The authors show the averaging preserves the population objective and controls gradient covariance.

entry.title: CB-Orchestrator: Adaptive Workflow Optimization for LLM Agents via Contextual Bandits

author.name: Jiahang Sun, Zhiwei Shang, Zhipiao Liu, Hongwei Yang, Guoqing Xie, Shuang Qiu, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: CB-Orchestrator decouples workflow generation from selection for LLM agents: an evolutionary stage builds a diverse candidate workflow pool, while contextual bandits adaptively select and reuse high-quality workflows per query. This reduces the expensive API feedback costs that plague prior automated workflow optimization methods. It addresses cost-effectiveness and adaptivity gaps in agentic workflow design.

entry.title: MHR-Router: Multimodal Heterogeneous Retrieval-Enhanced Adaptive Routing for VLM Inference

author.name: Wenjuan Zhu, Zheming Yang, Yunqing Hu, Qi Guo

entry.summary: Presents MHR-Router, a two-stage framework that routes multimodal image-question queries to the most suitable vision-language model expert using retrieval-based local evidence rather than text-only cues or static model profiles. It fuses frozen multimodal features into routing representations that capture expert-specific failure patterns. Aimed at efficient VLM inference across heterogeneous model pools.

entry.title: PPG-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for PPG Foundation Models

author.name: Arvasu Kulkarni, Mahir Jain, Aditya Ray Mishra, Sandeep Singh, Siddharth Panwar

entry.summary: Presents PPG-Bench, an open-source benchmark unifying evaluation of five public photoplethysmography foundation models across nine datasets and 26 tasks covering cardiovascular state estimation, activity, sleep, screening, and identification. It standardizes preprocessing, downstream heads, and tuning under four adaptability regimes from linear probing to fine-tuning. Addresses the incomparability of prior PPG model evaluations.

entry.title: $L_0$ Feature Selection via Monte Carlo Tree Search in High-Dimensional Financial Regression

author.name: Cameron Mouangue, Tristan Cazenave

entry.summary: This paper applies Monte Carlo Tree Search with Generalized Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation (GNRPA) to L0-sparse feature selection in high-dimensional financial regression. It avoids the shrinkage bias of Lasso while sidestepping the full cost of exact combinatorial sparse regression, targeting out-of-sample performance.

entry.title: PANDA: Prior-guided Attentional Dual-path Architecture

author.name: Rishabh Jain, Federico Belotti, Stefano Coniglio, Pietro Lio, Stefano Fiorini

entry.summary: This paper introduces PANDA, a plug-in module for hypergraph neural networks that addresses weaknesses of fixed structural weights and normalized attention in higher-order message passing. Its dual-path design interpolates between receiver-normalized learned attention and prior-guided components, and works in both undirected and directed hypergraph settings, targeting improved robustness in heterophilic data.

entry.title: SeoulMMOD: A Large-Scale Multimodal Origin-Destination Flow Benchmark

author.name: Taeyoung Yu, Seonbin Jo, Jiwon Kim, Junyoung Byun

entry.summary: SeoulMMOD is a large-scale public benchmark of citywide multimodal origin-destination flows in Seoul, providing three years of hourly OD flows for six travel modes across 25 districts and 426 sub-districts with covariates like travel time, rainfall, and points of interest. It enables full-coverage mobility forecasting that can disentangle mode shifts from total demand changes.

entry.title: Acoustic Biomarkers for Alzheimer's Disease Detection from Spontaneous Speech

author.name: Anh L Tran, Arjee Javellana Restar, Bereket Kindo

entry.summary: The study evaluates whether low-level acoustic descriptors spanning prosodic, spectral, and temporal domains, extracted from spontaneous speech in the Cookie Theft picture-description task, can distinguish individuals with Alzheimer's disease from healthy controls. Multiple machine learning classifiers are compared, with results indicating promise for speech-based digital biomarkers of cognitive decline.

entry.title: A Distributional Framework for Behavioral Characterization and Risk Management of Large Language Models

author.name: David Garc\'ia-Lorite, Raul Merino

entry.summary: The authors propose a framework treating LLM outputs as stochastic response distributions estimated via Monte Carlo simulation, applicable across the model lifecycle from task design to continuous monitoring. Semantic interventions quantify how distributions change, illustrated on borrower classification and music recommendation tasks, and the framework connects to model risk management and governance by measuring robustness and control effectiveness.

entry.title: Sparse Dictionary Learning for Measure-Valued Data via Linearized Optimal Transport: Efficient Algorithms and Sample Complexity

author.name: Brendan Mallery, Shuchin Aeron, James Murphy

entry.summary: Learns data-adapted dictionaries for probability-measure-valued data by embedding measures into Hilbert spaces via optimal transport geometry, using sparse autoencoder parameterizations. Demonstrated on hyperspectral images, point clouds, and LLM latent document embeddings, with generalization bounds proven.

entry.title: Fast Gradient-Based Approximation of Continuous Dynamic Time Warping

author.name: Pierre Houedry, Romain Tavenard, Nicolas Courty, Romaric Gaudel

entry.summary: Revisits Continuous-DTW by establishing its differentiability under mild conditions and introducing FastCDTW, a fast gradient-based approximation that substantially reduces the computational cost of CDTW and Soft-DTW for large-scale ML pipelines involving time series.

entry.title: Decoding Register Tokens Preserves Global Scene Details

author.name: David Jacob Drexlin, Julius Hense, Jonas Dippel

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether non-spatial register tokens in vision transformers, known to encode global scene properties like illumination and style, improve image decoding in representation autoencoders when patch tokens are already available. By feeding register tokens jointly with patch tokens through a self-attention decoder, the authors show global appearance details are better preserved. This informs how structured ViT representations can be leveraged for reconstruction and generative pipelines.

entry.title: Model-free Bayesian Clustering and Multimodal Posterior Summarisation

author.name: Qing Li, Sara Wade

entry.summary: The authors develop a noise-aware Bayesian clustering framework that builds a martingale posterior over clusterings from a predictive Bayesian viewpoint, avoiding explicit likelihood-prior specification, costly MCMC, and mode-seeking variational approximations. To make high-dimensional posterior distributions interpretable, they propose a Wasserstein-type summarization method that compresses posterior draws into a small set of weighted representatives capturing distinct cluster structures and noise assignments.

entry.title: Learning by Compression: Risk Estimates Attain the Law-of-Large-Numbers Rate

author.name: Simone Garatti, Marco C. Campi

entry.summary: The paper improves generalization bounds for learning via preferential compression schemes, proving that the previously logarithmic margin over the sample-dependent complexity term is not intrinsic. For any fixed confidence level, the risk is bounded by the complexity ratio plus an order 1/sqrt(N) term, matching the law-of-large-numbers rate. This tightens a foundational result in compression-based risk bounds.

entry.title: Adaptive Variance Reduction without Knowing Oracle Smoothness

author.name: Wei Jiang, Yibo Wang, Zechao Li

entry.summary: This paper develops a two-phase algorithm for stochastic nonconvex optimization that adapts variance reduction across average smoothness, standard smoothness, and noiseless settings without knowing smoothness constants or variance bounds. The first phase compares independent gradients and switches to normalized momentum when their difference exceeds a threshold, yielding parameter-free guarantees.

entry.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness

author.name: Daniel Szelogowski

entry.summary: This paper introduces DyssomniaNN, a biophysical computational framework that combines established sleep regulation models (Borbely's two-process model and Saper's flip-flop circuit) with a recurrent corticothalamic spiking neural network to simulate human sleep disorders. It simulates five clinical cohorts over a 72-hour photoperiod, aiming to explain the gap between objective sleep measures and subjective restedness in conditions like paradoxical insomnia and narcolepsy type 1.

entry.title: perturber: A Stateless Service for Semantics-Preserving Text Perturbations

author.name: Khoi-Nguyen Tran

entry.summary: Introduces perturber, a stateless service and Python library applying single semantics-preserving text perturbations from a catalog of 68 perturbations across 11 families, designed for reproducible robustness evaluation decoupled from any benchmarking stack. Its one-perturbation-per-call primitive makes perturbation studies composable and portable across environments.

entry.title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models

author.name: Ke Wan, Chen Chen

entry.summary: Analyzes how quantization errors propagate across recurrent depth in recurrent-depth language models and proposes RAMP, a recurrent adaptive mixed-precision scheme for efficient long-context prefill. Exploits the finding that early-introduced quantization errors are attenuated along the recurrent trajectory.

entry.title: Multi-Stream Attention Residuals

author.name: Xiaohan Qin, Xiangdong Zhang, Tuo Dai, Sunan Zou, Huaijin Wu, Yebin Yang, Zhuo Xia, Lin Yao, Yuliang Liu, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Proposes MSAR, generalizing single-stream attention residuals along network depth to multi-head depth attention, with stream diversity derived from multi-scale causal convolutions and lightweight stream combination. Reports substantial performance gains with minimal overhead. An architecture-level contribution relevant to efficient deep-network design for sequence models.

entry.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection

author.name: Juan Terven, Diana-Margarita C\'ordova-Esparza, Ruben Gomez, Carlos Miranda Rocha, Julio-Alejandro Romero-Gonz\'alez, Edgar Chavez-Urbiola

entry.summary: Studies whether abstention behavior on factual QA improves by training the model itself versus training a separate answer selector, using a utility score rewarding correctness and permitting abstention, on Qwen3-14B (an existing released model). A learned selector improves coverage (20.2% to 30.9% on TriviaQA) and reduces error among scored answers, while tested RL approaches do not establish clear gains. A careful, honest negative-ish result on RL for calibrated abstention.

entry.title: What Do Audio-Language Judges of Generated Music Listen For? Four Probes with Controls from Expert Ratings

author.name: Mateusz Modrzejewski, Tomasz Radzikowski

entry.summary: Proposes four controlled probes to determine whether audio-language model judges of generated music actually respond to the audio, the text prompt, or instruction phrasing, validated against expert ratings. Applied to five open judges on MusicEval and SongEval, revealing that judges degrade substantially without audio.

entry.title: Selectively Actuated Fiberbots for High-precision Minimally Invasive Surgery

author.name: Jinshi Zhao, Libaihe Tian, Alex Ranne, Qindong Zheng, Yue Li, Xiaotong Guo, Ziqi Yang, Ali Anil Demircali, Mohamed E. M. K. Abdelaziz, Bruno Gil Rosa, Ferdinando Rodriguez y Baena, Burak Temelkuran

entry.summary: Presents an electrothermally actuated, thermally drawn fiber robot (1.9 mm diameter, 1.2 m length) that concentrates Joule heating in a distal active segment, enabling sub-100-micron positioning precision for surgical laser fibers. Its compact size allows passage through flexible endoscope working channels.

entry.title: FallGown: A Soft Pneumatic Wearable Device for Fall Prevention

author.name: Megan C. Coram, Haoran Lei, Steven H. Collins, Steve B. Cousins, Michelle Baldonado, Cynthia Sung, Allison M. Okamura

entry.summary: Presents FallGown, a soft wearable with pressurized pneumatic pouches in a fabric shell that can support a user's full body weight to prevent falls in older adults, offering a less bulky and stigmatizing alternative to walkers and rigid exoskeletons. The device is portable at 6.9 kg and shows low drag force with an optional rolling base.

entry.title: Adaptive Whole-Body MPC with Optimal Posture Planning for Humanoid Robots under Unknown Payloads

author.name: Manh Cuong Nguyen, Duc Cuong Vu, Viet Anh Vu, Duc Tuan Pham, Toan Nguyen, Minh Hiep Phung, Ngo Anh Vien, Minh Nhat Vu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a humanoid control architecture combining a centroidal MPC for dynamically feasible reference motions, an adaptive fuzzy balance controller that compensates for payload-induced model mismatch, and a waypoint-based optimal posture planner for smooth sit-to-stand transitions. The system targets lifting and material handling with unknown and varying payloads. It addresses a practical robustness gap for humanoids in logistics-like tasks.

entry.title: When LiDAR Fades, Radar Takes Over: LiDAR Reliability-Aware Adaptive Localization Under Airborne Obscurants

author.name: Moumita Mukherjee, Avijit Banerjee, Anton Koval, George Nikolakopoulo

entry.summary: This work presents a one-class temporal learning framework for detecting LiDAR degradation in subterranean environments with smoke and dust, using an LSTM autoencoder trained only on nominal operation to model the evolution of degradation-sensitive spatial, cross-modal, geometric, intensity, and recency features. Detected degradation triggers reliability-aware fusion that leans on radar, which is more robust to obscurants.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust Adaptive Iterative Covariance Steering for Small-Body Proximity Operations

author.name: Vivek Khatana, Aditya Gahlawat, Naira Hovakimyan, Petros Voulgaris

entry.summary: This paper combines iterative covariance steering with L1 distributionally robust adaptive control to provide risk-aware collision avoidance for continuous-thrust spacecraft proximity operations under uncertain gravity, solar-radiation pressure, and stochastic disturbances. The planner enforces distributionally robust conditional value-at-risk keep-out constraints while the adaptive controller bounds residual model mismatch via a Wasserstein radius, validated in 1,000 paired Monte Carlo trials.

entry.title: Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection

author.name: Yiming Yang, Jeremy P. Bos

entry.summary: This paper reports a counter-intuitive finding: LiDAR object detection accuracy consistently improves with increasing snow intensity on WADS-3D and CADC datasets. Through ablations and meta-information analysis, the authors show that snow accumulation boosts object point counts (a geometric enhancement from changed vehicle surfaces), outweighing the noise effect of falling snow.

entry.title: Markov Chain Convergence in Kernel-Induced Geometry

author.name: Oleksii Kachaiev, Luc Brogat-Motte, Silvia Villa, Lorenzo Rosasco

entry.summary: The paper establishes non-asymptotic high-probability bounds for convergence of empirical occupation measures to invariant measures in MMD geometry, under kernel contraction and spectral gap assumptions. As an application, it derives fast learning rates for one-step prediction of dynamical systems from a single trajectory, with credible authorship including Lorenzo Rosasco.

entry.title: CLEAT: Learning Value-Guided Clarification for Interactive Agents

author.name: Jiatan Huang, Zheyuan Zhang, Ziming Li, Tianyi Ma, Mingchen Li, Yanfang Ye, Chuxu Zhang

entry.summary: CLEAT co-trains a clarification-value controller with a task policy, using a residual query value formulation to decide when asking the user a clarifying question will actually improve task decisions. It frames interactive intent alignment as a value-of-information problem that changes as training progresses. This targets a practical weakness: agents that guess at unstated user constraints.

entry.title: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows

author.name: Yuchen Ling, Shengcheng Yu, Zhenyu Chen, Chunrong Fang

entry.summary: Empirically examines whether swapping LLM agents' decision maker to the faster, cheaper Jev model transfers local savings into efficient, reliable task completion, across five agents in ALFWorld and AndroidWorld over 4,500 executions. Results show substantial decision-level savings but mixed or degraded task-level outcomes.

entry.title: A Local Agentic AI Framework to Generate Edge Case Scenarios for Safety Assurance

author.name: Victoria J. Hodge, Colin Paterson, Rob Alexander

entry.summary: This work uses locally deployed LLM agents to autonomously generate diverse edge-case scenarios for safety assurance of autonomous systems, avoiding human-in-the-loop and rule-based constraints that limit coverage of the long tail. The approach targets training, testing, and safety-case construction for systems operating at the boundaries of their operational design domain. Local deployment addresses privacy and certification constraints.

entry.title: Surfing the Activation Wave: Analyzing the Information and Geometry of LLM Hidden States for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Raghavv Goel, Sudhanshu Agrawal, Mukul Gagrani, Risheek Garrepalli, Mingu Lee

entry.summary: This paper provides a principled framework for selecting which LLM layers' hidden states to use for speculative decoding, replacing fixed position-based heuristics. It uses matrix-entropy analysis for informativeness and centered kernel alignment for diversity to navigate the combinatorial layer-selection space. Better layer selection can improve speculative decoding efficiency without exhaustive search.

entry.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models

author.name: Bhanu Tokas, Rahul Nair, Rockwell Jackson, Hannah Kerner

entry.summary: Hide and Seek is a concept-level attribution method for black-box vision models that requires neither model weights nor concept-annotated datasets. It retrieves concept-aligned images with a vision-language model, localizes concepts, and hides them to measure causal effects, extending concept attribution beyond classification to a wide range of vision models with image-level attribution. This broadens accessibility of concept-based explanations.

entry.title: GlucoPRISM: Protocol-Supervised Pretraining for Cross-Cohort Glucose Transfer

author.name: Adinath Madhavrao Dukre, Abdullah Mohammad, Yifan Lu, Eran Segal, Ahmed Metwally, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: GlucoPRISM trains a continuous glucose monitoring foundation model with response contracts that partition the representation into trait, state, and sensor bands with specified invariance properties, so that harmful measurement components can be dropped via a fixed projection at deployment without target data. This addresses sensor-induced confounds that hurt cross-cohort transfer of CGM foundation models. The approach is a structured disentanglement recipe for wearable time-series transfer.

entry.title: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Large Language Model via Hypergraph Message Passing

author.name: Kai Li, Hanlin Cai, Zihao Liu, Yichen Li, Jose Alcaraz Calero, Wei Ni, Falko Dressler, \"Ozg\"ur B. Akan

entry.summary: The paper formulates a defense against Byzantine attacks in federated LLM training that jointly maximizes global accuracy and suppresses malicious updates without accessing private data. It introduces HMP-GAE, a hypergraph message passing graph autoencoder over low-rank model updates, to prevent semantically corrupted knowledge from propagating during aggregation.

entry.title: Personalized Federated Direct Preference Optimization via LoRA Adapters

author.name: Zhanhong Jiang, Soumik Sarkar

entry.summary: The paper proposes pFedDPO, in which each federated client maintains a private LoRA adapter for client-specific preferences atop a shared global base model synchronized via FedAvg. The authors prove this decomposition replaces the gradient diversity term in the FedDPO convergence bound, addressing the mismatch between single-shared-policy assumptions and heterogeneous client preferences.

entry.title: Low-Rank Kolmogorov-Arnold Generator Flows for Interpretable Operator Learning

author.name: Minjong Cheon

entry.summary: This paper observes that dense pseudo-differential symbols learned by Kolmogorov-Arnold neural operators are unnecessarily high-rank, since finite-order variable-coefficient differential operators have separation rank bounded by their coefficient functions. It introduces a low-rank variant reducing resolution-dependent cost and yielding closed-form learned operators that need not be read out by hand. This improves both efficiency and interpretability of operator learning for physical dynamics.

entry.title: BLOKS: Scaling Kernel Solvers with Sketched Block Preconditioning

author.name: Giordano Vitale, Giacomo Meanti, Marco Rando, Blanca Ayuso de Dios, Lorenzo Rosasco

entry.summary: Proposes BLOKS, a solver for kernel ridge regression that combines sketching, batching, and a sketched block preconditioner to accelerate convergence while managing preconditioner memory costs. This mitigates the tradeoff between preconditioner expressivity and memory that limits approximate KRR solvers on large datasets. Authored by a team including established researchers in kernel methods.

entry.title: Scan-Parallel Variational Inference for event-driven Latent Jump Models

author.name: Vansh Bansal, Min Chen, James G. Scott

entry.summary: Introduces latent jump models for irregularly observed time series, where the latent state follows deterministic dynamics between Poisson-driven event times with learned instantaneous jumps, better encoding discrete unobserved shocks than ODE/SDE models. Provides scan-parallel variational inference for scalability.

entry.title: JitterVLA: A Replay Benchmark for Motion Quality in VLA-Driven Human-Robot Manipulation

author.name: Faith Ogunwoye, Didar Seyidov, Konstantin Gubernatorov, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: JitterVLA is a replay benchmark that pushes identical VLA commands and arrival-time traces through alternative robot controllers to isolate the controller's effect on motion quality near humans, evaluated on synthetic reaches, hand trajectories from 20 people, three open VLA pipelines (838 episodes), and a physical UR3. It shows interpolation lowers p99 jerk substantially (e.g., 83% on human motion with 200 ms delay) at a small tracking cost. The benchmark addresses safety-critical motion smoothness for VLA policies operating around people.

entry.title: KV-Repurpose: A Testbed for Evaluating Non-Prefix KV-Cache Reuse

author.name: Taiga Ikeda, Daisuke Miyashita, Jun Deguchi

entry.summary: Introduces KV-Repurpose, an open-source vLLM-based testbed for segment-wise KV-cache reuse beyond exact prompt prefixes, with cache-aware scheduling, capacity management, and workload generation. Experiments show naive reuse preserves quality for single-document tasks but struggles with cross-document reasoning under realistic RAG workloads.

entry.title: Verifiable Retrieval for Legal Reasoning through Structure-driven Knowledge Graph

author.name: Ibrahim Siddig, Sviatoslav Tugeev, Munir Georges

entry.summary: Builds a structure-driven knowledge graph over the German Legal Code to enable verifiable retrieval-augmented legal reasoning, addressing the failure of naive retrieval as source corpora grow and the opacity of LLM systems in reliability-critical domains. The structured representation aims to make generated answers checkable against the code's hierarchy. Useful work at the intersection of RAG, knowledge graphs, and trustworthy legal AI.

entry.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation

author.name: Fu-An Chao, Bi-Cheng Yan, Berlin Chen

entry.summary: Presents OpenPA, a pronunciation assessment framework that uses Whisper cross-attention to jointly predict word- and utterance-level scores without forced alignment, handling both closed- and open-response settings via mixed-transcript adaptation. Trained only on speechocean762, it achieves state-of-the-art results.

entry.title: Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training
