author.name: Suorong Yang, Jiaxin Wang, Jiaming Su, Chentao Yue, Furao Shen, Peng Ye, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: The framework concentrates reasoning post-training supervision on the most valuable trajectories by building Monte Carlo reasoning trees around intermediate reasoning steps to profile uncertainty, then progressively contracting the supervision set. It asks how far reasoning supervision can be compressed without capability loss. Directly addresses the rising cost of reasoning-focused post-training.

entry.title: Model-agnostic Knowledge Augmented Machine Learning for Weakly Annotated Bioimaging Data

author.name: Jayanie Bogahawatte, Sachith Seneviratne, Simon Maksour, Dzung Do-Ha, Elizabeth Qian, Samuel Brennan, Matthew Keon, Lezanne Ooi, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: The authors propose a model-agnostic knowledge augmentation method that lets ML models inject domain knowledge beyond what automated feature extraction captures, targeting weakly annotated bioimaging data like microscopy and cytomorphology. The approach improves classification across seven architectures and is strongest when combined with masked-autoencoder self-supervised learning, improving precision by 2.9 percent over the next-best baseline.

entry.title: CacheScope: Exact-Compute Allocation for Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration

author.name: Qinhan Lyu, Jusheng Zhang, Zhixing Zhang, Hao Liu, Zijie Liang, Jin Jiang, Keze Wang

entry.summary: CacheScope improves training-free diffusion transformer acceleration by showing that once a stable first-order feature reconstructor is used, where to place exact-computation steps matters more than improving reconstruction of skipped steps. It introduces a displacement-normalized probe metric to better estimate cache risk, decoupling it from input-trajectory displacement confounds. This yields better fidelity at the same compute budget.

entry.title: Spatial Context or Memory? Sizing the Inputs of Neural Surrogates for Partially Observed Fields

author.name: Ruige Kong

entry.summary: This work studies how neural surrogates for forecasting physical fields from sparse noisy sensors should trade off spatial window size versus history length, benchmarking against exact Bayes-optimal error computed via Gaussian analysis. Experiments on linear fields, Burgers flow, and chaotic Kuramoto-Sivashinsky dynamics quantify when additional spatial context or memory actually helps.

entry.title: Robust Langevin Sampling under State-Dependent Heavy-Tailed Noise with Applications to LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: M. Berk Sahin, Ege C. Kaya, Arda Fazla, Behzad Sharif, Abolfazl Hashemi

entry.summary: The authors relax standard assumptions for SG-Langevin Monte Carlo convergence, replacing globally Lipschitz gradients and bounded noise with generalized smoothness and a state-dependent heavy-tailed noise oracle with finite p-th moments. They propose three methods, including robust LMC under geometric decay and extensions relaxing smoothness, motivated by Bayesian fine-tuning of LLMs.

entry.title: PlacePulse: Learning Transferable Place Representations from Structural Geographic Data

author.name: Luc\'ia Garc\'ia-Duarte, Miguel \'Alvarez, Diego Vicente, Javier P\'erez Trufero, Javier de la Torre

entry.summary: Introduces PlacePulse, a geospatial foundation model that compresses 572 static structural attributes (demographics, businesses, risks), expanded to 2,288 inputs via H3 neighborhood aggregates, into 256-dimensional transferable place embeddings at fine spatial resolution. Unlike prior geospatial models based on mobility, search, or satellite imagery, it captures the static structural composition of places. Targets replacement of task-specific feature engineering in geospatial ML.

entry.title: Generalized Determinantal Point Processes for Attraction and Repulsion with Distinct Interaction Kernels

author.name: Hideaki Ishibashi, Takahiro Kawashima, Hideitsu Hino

entry.summary: Proposes the determinant-ratio point process (DRPP), which models both repulsion and attraction as a ratio of determinants of two symmetric positive-definite kernels, preserving DPP interpretability. An auxiliary-variable representation enables efficient MCMC sampling and tractable expectations.

entry.title: CLUE: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Unsupervised Event Type Induction and Annotation

author.name: Pratik Maitra, Lauren Kwon, Qi Li

entry.summary: CLUE is an unsupervised framework for event type induction, naming, and annotation that replaces costly, bias-prone manual ontology creation. It combines a joint embedding capturing verb-centric and semantic views of events with contrastive-loss-guided clustering and automated event naming and refinement.

entry.title: Temporal Evidence Forests for Long-Horizon Multi-Party Conversational Memory

author.name: Junyou Guo, Chongyang Tao, Yan He, Yong Wang, Shuai Ma

entry.summary: Proposes Temporal Evidence Forests, a memory framework for long-horizon multi-party LLM agent interactions that uses temporal structure both to recover locally dense evidence and to anchor state transitions, rather than storing time as mere metadata. Targets decisions that evolve across participants and stages.

entry.title: Not Just an Evaluation: A Case Study of Discourse Particle Sensitivity in Language Models

author.name: William Sheffield, Jiahui Chen, Amy Zhang, Alex Warstadt, Junyi Jessy Li, Kanishka Misra

entry.summary: Investigates LLM sensitivity to the discourse particles just and only using combined behavioral and mechanistic analyses in natural conversations, finding that models and humans similarly prefer these particles and are more sensitive to certain contextual factors. The study connects subtle pragmatics with internal representation analysis. A careful bridging of theoretical linguistics and interpretability.

entry.title: Non-Prehensile Multi-Object Placement with Mobile Robots via Diffusion-Based Trajectory Planning

author.name: Lance Pharand, Megnath Ramesh, Mark Chiu, Yash Vardhan Pant, Stephen L. Smith

entry.summary: Formalizes multi-object pushing with a mobile robot as a multi-target assignment problem at tight placement tolerances, proposing a diffusion planner with causal factorization where each robot denoising step is followed by an object step conditioned on the clean robot estimate. This enables sampling multiple object outcomes per robot rollout for efficient replanning.

entry.title: Collaborative Theory of Mind: Learning to Self-Revise by Anticipating User Responses

author.name: Fanzhi Zeng, Anubrata Das, Maytal Saar-Tsechansky, Liu Leqi

entry.summary: Collaborative Theory of Mind (CToM) trains LLMs to draft responses, predict how the user will respond, and use that prediction to internally revise before answering, with the user's actual reply serving as the training target. It targets multi-turn collaboration failures like acting before understanding user needs. A thoughtful human-AI interaction contribution with a concrete training signal.

entry.title: RegulaTutor: A Theory-Informed Framework for Long-Term Personalized Learning

author.name: Yonggang Li, Boqian Han, Rui Sheng, Yushi Sun, Zixin Chen

entry.summary: RegulaTutor is a theory-informed framework for long-term personalized LLM tutoring that explicitly links a learner's evolving history to instructional strategies, grounded in self-regulated learning research via a cognitive-affective-metacognitive-motivational (CAMM) framework. It operationalizes evidence-supported learner interpretations and teaching policies, making pedagogical rationale explicit rather than implicit in memory and retrieval mechanisms.

entry.title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga

author.name: Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: Proposes PAGE, an AI framework for large-scale comics scholarship that parses scans into panels and text, annotates pages with VLMs following a written codebook, and grounds readings in human annotation, demonstrated across American comics and Japanese manga. It represents a substantive application of multimodal AI to digital humanities at corpus scale.

entry.title: Localized Generative Design of Ship Hulls with Diffusion Models and High-Fidelity Assessment

author.name: Hadi Keramati, Mohammed A. Hannan, Patrick Kirchen, Sina Tousi, Joonas Riekkinen, Jim Pyra, Rajeev K. Jaiman

entry.summary: The paper presents a reward-directed diffusion framework for localized ship hull optimization, using parametric masking to restrict geometric changes to components like the bulbous bow while preserving hull continuity. Surrogate-assisted sequential Monte Carlo sampling targets reduced resistance, with an automated CFD pipeline validated against benchmark container ships for assessment. It demonstrates domain-specific generative design with rigorous physical verification.

entry.title: Does Learning Recurrent Networks Matter in Partially Observable RL?

author.name: Zekang Wang, Zhe He, Gaojie Jin

entry.summary: This paper asks whether the recurrent networks used for memory in partially observable RL actually need to be trained, studying a frozen recurrent module combined with a trainable nonlinear output layer, motivated by reservoir computing theory. Evaluation across tasks with varying memory demands tests whether learned recurrence is necessary for POMDPs. A negative or nuanced answer would simplify common RL practice.

entry.title: Algebraic Integer Quantization for Machine Learning Applications

author.name: Anthony Kostal-Vazquez, Vassil Dimitrov, Branden Butler

entry.summary: The paper proposes algebraic integer number formats (AINF) as a compressed computation framework reducible to pure integer arithmetic, enabling error-free multiply-accumulate operations. The authors build a matrix multiplication engine with performance within a predictable factor of efficient numerical baselines on modern accelerators, and highlight the freedom to select algebraic integers tailored to a use case. This explores an alternative to floating-point and fixed-point numerics for ML.

entry.title: Enriched Holomorphic Neural Networks for 2D and 3D Laplace Problems

author.name: Kalp Shah, Andrei Vlad Nicula, Mihnea Andrei B\^arsan, Robert-Stefan Sofroni, Agneya Bhardwaj, Jan Jel\'inek, Alejandro Valverde Mahou

entry.summary: The paper combines holomorphic neural networks with geometry-derived singular enrichment functions for Laplace boundary-value problems, giving a representation that is harmonic by construction so only boundary data is fitted. Trainable singular exponents let it handle unknown local expansions, and a 3D extension uses networks along complex null directions. It reports the highest accuracy among tested methods on these problems.

entry.title: Kernelized Parameter Sensitivity Atlases for Amortized Conditional Interpretability

author.name: Davide Wiest, Ahanaf Hasan Ariq, Abdul Monaf Chowdhury

entry.summary: KPSA derives normalized parameter-group sensitivities from a block decomposition of the empirical neural tangent kernel and uses a lightweight kernel to amortize sensitivity estimates to unseen inputs, avoiding per-sample backpropagation. The authors provide error bounds and demonstrate applications including identifying parameter groups susceptible to forgetting and analyzing LoRA update dynamics.

entry.title: The Expressive Power of Random-Feature MPNNs Across Graph Sizes

author.name: Robert R. Nerem, Mitchell Black, Antonis Vasileiou, Christopher Morris, Yusu Wang

entry.summary: The paper develops a population-level size-uniform approximation framework for message-passing neural networks with continuous random node features. It shows that under graph-size-independent Lipschitz bounds, random features can be quantized to finitely many colors with arbitrarily small uniform error, transferring finite-color distinguishability limits to limitations of random-feature MPNNs across graph sizes.

entry.title: Scaling RNA Foundation Models through Iterative Refinement

author.name: Pengan Chen, Liang Hong, Xinyuan Liu, Han Huang, Ziqian Lin, Jiayang Chen, Yimin Fan, Jiyue Jiang, Yu Li

entry.summary: Eco-RNA is an 80M-parameter RNA foundation model whose inference depth is adjustable via learned iterative refinement: a shared, input-conditioned Transformer core is applied repeatedly, with iteration count chosen after training to control effective depth. Training spans recurrent depths using masked reconstruction, state regularization, and a one-sided auxiliary loss. This decouples parameter capacity from inference depth, letting the model scale computation per input.

entry.title: DAG Structure Learning with Node-Varying Heavy-Tailed Disturbances

author.name: Robin Francis, Sundeep Prabhakar Chepuri

entry.summary: Proposes a node-varying Student-t extension of DAGMA for causal DAG structure learning that jointly estimates graph structure, node-specific disturbance scales, and degrees-of-freedom parameters. An iteratively reweighted formulation from a Gaussian scale-mixture representation down-weights large residuals, improving robustness to heavy-tailed noise. Extends causal discovery beyond Gaussian assumptions.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Numerical Stabilization for Half-Precision Proximal Policy Optimization

author.name: Linxuan Wu, Liang Chen

entry.summary: Studies FP16 training of PPO, showing naive conversion is unreliable because numerical errors propagate through policy updates and data collection. It proposes three structure-aware protection modules covering shared statistics, policy-change residuals, and persistent training state. Targets efficient RL on resource-constrained platforms such as commodity GPUs.

entry.title: Private and Distributionally Robust Federated Multiclass Classification

author.name: Andrea P. Hernandez, Michael Ibrahim, Nagi Gebraeel

entry.summary: The authors develop a differentially private, distributionally robust framework for federated multiclass classification with sample-level privacy at each client, built on a Wasserstein DRO objective with the Crammer-Singer loss and solved via ADMM. It targets fault diagnosis on noisy, sensitive industrial data.

entry.title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Alexander Kreusel, Maximilian Beichter, Alexandra Nikoltchovska, Benjamin Sch\"afer, Ralf Mikut, Frederik Zahn, Veit Hagenmeyer

entry.summary: This study systematically examines how calendar feature encoding choices affect the forecast accuracy of covariate-informed time series foundation models, comparing seven encodings including ordinal, one-hot, cyclic, and target-based representations. It shows that encoding, often treated as an implementation detail, substantially changes model performance and is one of the few design levers available at inference time for pretrained models.

entry.title: Machine Unlearning for Federated Socially Fair k-Means Clustering

author.name: Aravind Reddy, Deeraj S K, Mohd Wasif Raza, Saurav Prakash

entry.summary: The paper studies exact machine unlearning for federated socially fair k-means clustering, where deletion requests interact with fairness constraints across demographic groups. By maintaining separate per-group local summaries, unaffected institutions' summaries remain valid while fairness is preserved during exact deletion.

entry.title: KL Before and After Mixing: A Round-Complexity Separation in Parallel Sampling

author.name: Tianyi Wu

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes a round-complexity separation between two notions of divergence in parallel sampling: the schedule-averaged KL divergence versus the KL divergence of the averaged output law. Using the uniform distribution on balanced binary strings, it proves that the least expected number of sampling rounds at a fixed tolerance scales as Theta((log n)^2) under one regime, giving a provable gap between the two divergence measures.

entry.title: Minimax Rates for Estimating Powered Sliced Wasserstein Functionals

author.name: Binh Thuan Tran

entry.summary: This paper establishes minimax estimation rates for powered Sliced Wasserstein functionals under projected moment assumptions, showing the plug-in estimator is rate-optimal with risk N^{-(r-p)/r} when r < 2p and N^{-1/2} when r > 2p. At the endpoint r = p, uniform consistency is impossible, while at the critical order r = 2p a logarithmic gap remains between lower and upper bounds.

entry.title: Trainable Quantum-Native Language Models: Dissipative Memory, Capacity Limits, and Hardware Validation

author.name: Deniz Yunus G\"o\u{g}\"u\c{s}

entry.summary: This paper studies byte-level autoregressive language models with quantum register hidden states and learned token-conditioned quantum channels, with next-byte predictions from Born-rule measurements rather than a classical softmax. It finds that unitary dynamics cannot retain useful memory, while learned dissipative gating improves test loss by about 0.20 nats/byte over parameter-matched one-token controls, with hardware validation included.

entry.title: When Solvers Get Moody: Quantifying and Predicting Performance Variability in Mixed Integer Programming

author.name: Mourchid Adegbindin, Brenda Dietrich, Jamol Pender, Andrea Lodi

entry.summary: Introduces the Weighted Variability Score (WVS) to quantify MIP solver performance variability across repeated runs, using a large MIPLIB 2017 study with 100 randomized four-hour runs per instance. Finds right-skewed variability distributions where some instances are highly unstable for reasons not explained by basic properties.

entry.title: Neurograf v1: An End-to-End Romanian-First Language Model Family

author.name: Ionut Adrian Rotaru

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end Romanian-first language model pipeline including a 635 GB corpus, an 80k BPE tokenizer, five decoder-only models from 160M to 6B parameters trained on 131 billion tokens, plus instruction-tuned and embedding models. Shows consistent scaling behavior and growing Romanian factual and cultural knowledge.

entry.title: One Thing Leads to Another: The Essentials of Time Series Causal Discovery

author.name: Kurt Butler, Damian Machlanski, Michael P. J. Camilleri, Zhihua Liu, Panagiotis Dimitrakopoulos, Feng Chen, Ricardo Silva, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris

entry.summary: This tutorial provides a unified overview of time series causal discovery across statistics, dynamical systems, and machine learning communities, covering core principles, assumptions, limitations, evaluation practices, and downstream applications of discovered causal structure. It serves as an entry point into a fragmented field with roots in signal processing from over fifty years ago. Tutorials of this kind can meaningfully shape how new researchers approach the area.

entry.title: A Scalable Learned Iterative Solver for Nonlinear MPC via Temporal Decomposition

author.name: Lukas L\"uken, Sergio Lucia

entry.summary: The paper extends LISCO, a self-supervised learned iterative solver that predicts primal-dual steps toward KKT satisfaction, to large nonlinear model predictive control problems via temporal decomposition, avoiding the dense monolithic architecture that scales poorly. This enables real-time application of NMPC to systems with fast dynamics or many states without precomputed training solutions. It bridges learning-based optimization and constrained control at scale.

entry.title: X-AVDD: Cross-Attentive Audio-Visual Dataset Distillation

author.name: Saumyaranjan Mohanty, Aravind Reddy, Konda Reddy Mopuri

entry.summary: X-AVDD is a cross-attention-based dataset distillation method for paired audio-visual data that explicitly captures inter-modal relationships during synthesis. By decoupling cross-modal alignment from joint optimization, it substantially reduces memory usage compared to prior methods like DM and AVDD while better preserving cross-modal semantic correspondence.

entry.title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks

author.name: Kosio Beshkov

entry.summary: The paper proposes measuring neural network topological expressivity via Betti numbers of the network output rather than only the decision boundary, extending the framework beyond binary classification to regression. It provides constructive architecture bounds showing ReLU networks can express spaces with homology prescribed by given Betti number sequences.

entry.title: Time Delay System for Sequence Modeling

author.name: Youshan Zhang, Jialu Li

entry.summary: Proposes a sequence modeling framework based on nonlinear time-delay systems with a differentiable semantic lag estimator that dynamically sets content-aware temporal recall delays, addressing limits of LSTMs, Transformers, and state-space models. Aims for explicit, interpretable, content-addressable memory of past events.

entry.title: Towards the Roof of the World: NLP Progress in Tibetan Languages

author.name: Xi Cao, Yijie Li, Yuan Sun, Shiwei Dong, Zeguang Huang, Nuo Qun

entry.summary: Presents a systematic bibliometric survey of Tibetan NLP, covering 140 publications from 2004 to 2026 and annotating venues, research areas, affiliations, and resource release. It documents rapid growth since 2018 and bottom-up expansion along the NLP pipeline toward LLMs, while highlighting underrepresentation of a language spoken by about seven million people. Valuable for low-resource language research planning and resource equity.

entry.title: Large Language Models, Machine-Assisted Cultural Analytics, and the Agentic Turn

author.name: Andres Karjus

entry.summary: A book chapter examining how LLMs and agentic systems transform cultural analytics by converting cultural material into analyzable variables and delegating parts of the research workflow. The author argues these tools expand scale and methodological range, but the underlying logic connecting measurements to cultural claims remains largely unchanged.

entry.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion

author.name: Amit Kumar Jaiswal, Sagar Uprety, Prayag Tiwari

entry.summary: Proposes SAFE-QE, a training-free, retriever-agnostic method for query expansion that scores candidate terms via a subsequence-association account of hallucination, filtering off-topic or nonexistent entities. Also provides a principled criterion for how many expansion terms to keep.

entry.title: Cooperative Aerial Transportation of a Payload with a Sliding Cable Attachment

author.name: Sebastian Tilaguy Lezama, Diego S D'Antonio

entry.summary: This paper studies a dual-quadrotor system transporting a payload suspended by a single cable that slides through a frictionless hook, introducing a cable-distribution variable that couples quadrotor motion, cable geometry, and payload dynamics. The authors formulate a feasible reference-generation framework respecting cable-length constraints and elliptical workspaces, with quadrotors tracking the generated trajectories.

entry.title: HorizonNav: Geometry-Guided Video Diffusion for Anticipatory 3D Robot Navigation

author.name: Hajira Amjad, Valerii Serpiva, Viacheslav Liubimov, Didar Seyidov, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: HorizonNav uses a vision-language model to convert a single RGB image and text prompt into structured prompts for a video diffusion model, generating plausible future observations that are then processed with ORB-SLAM3 and monocular depth estimation for anticipatory 3D navigation. Its central contribution is a geometry-guided depth alignment stage to make the imagined video geometrically usable.

entry.title: Beyond Discrepancy: Oracle Drift in Nonstationary Weighted Risk Minimization

author.name: Tobias Brock, Thomas Nagler

entry.summary: The authors analyze distribution drift in nonstationary weighted risk minimization by bounding drift error via the movement of the best in-class predictor (oracle drift) rather than discrepancy-type quantities. They show discrepancy bounds can be overly conservative, scaling at a larger order than the actual excess-risk contribution, and instantiate the analysis for linear regression.

entry.title: Minimum required pacing: finish aligning it before you train the next one

author.name: orthonormal

entry.summary: The author proposes a minimum governance standard for frontier AI pacing: a lab should not train the next capabilities generation until it has adequately resolved significant alignment issues in the current generation, analogized to not launching a faster jet before fixing crash causes. The post argues this proposal creates incentives for labs to advance alignment and interpretability research, and is attractive to both prosaic-alignment optimists and pessimists.

entry.title: Benchmarking Embedding Geometries and Clustering Algorithms for Unsupervised Patent Claim Classification

author.name: Sujith Subramanian, P N Bhargav Teja, Susen Sarkar, Rajasekhara Reddy Duvvuru Muni

entry.summary: Trains matched hyperbolic and Euclidean variational autoencoders on 45,000 US patents and shows the hyperbolic model retrieves genuinely cross-category prior art 52% more often (18.76% vs 12.34% of top-10 results). The authors explain the reduced agreement with official classification codes geometrically as a feature of hyperbolic organization.

entry.title: Incremental Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Human-in-the-Loop Decision Support

author.name: Federico Mazzoni, Andrea Failla

entry.summary: Introduces iRAG, a decision-support system where the knowledge base starts empty and grows from stored human decisions used as retrievable precedents, progressing from observation to evidence-grounded contestation to autonomous handling with abstention. Shows robustness under knowledge drift, including a retrieval-decay mechanism.

entry.title: Market Impact Estimation via Causal Foundation Models

author.name: Dennis Thumm, Ying Chen

entry.summary: The authors frame market impact as a causal counterfactual question and train a continuous-time causal prior-data fitted network (PFN) on a synthetic market prior with a hidden informational confounder built in. They derive and empirically confirm a closed form for the naive estimator's bias and show the PFN-based simulator can correct it. It is a proof-of-concept causal market simulator applying in-context-learning-style amortization to quantitative finance.

entry.title: Static Gradient Attribution Underperforms a Density-Matched Random Mask on Loss-Based Forgetting Within LoRA B-Matrix

author.name: Yu Sun, Junwei Zhou, Zuodong Xiang, Yike Zhang, Pengcheng Xu, Xinyu Guan, Ruoyun Ma, Hailu Xu

entry.summary: The authors identify a parameter-pool confound in continual learning comparisons between gradient-attribution masks and random masks under zero-initialized LoRA: because the gradient with respect to A is identically zero, gradient masks select only from the B matrix while random masks draw from both. With density-matched random masks restricted to the B matrix, static gradient attribution actually underperforms on loss-based forgetting.

entry.title: Neural Surrogate Modeling of Ultrasonic Wave Propagation in Heterogeneous Media

author.name: Burla Nur Korkmaz, Petro Moilanen, Ari Salmi, Harsha Vardhan Tetali, Arto Klami

entry.summary: The paper shows Fourier Neural Operator surrogates fail to capture essential ultrasonic signal features like reflections, while U-Net methods learn wave fields well but transfer poorly across spatial scales. It proposes a hybrid surrogate integrating FNOs with local-integral resampling inside a U-Net architecture for high-frequency wave propagation in heterogeneous media. This enables fast auto-regressive modeling and inverse solutions for ultrasonic sensing.

entry.title: Accelerating Linear Bandits with Persistent Candidate Sets

author.name: Bingkui Tong, Daria Korovaitceva, Marina Sheshukova, Sergey Samsonov, Junpei Komiyama

entry.summary: Proposes PC-LinUCB, which maintains k active actions and samples q challengers per round, reducing optimistic scoring cost from O(K) to O(k+q) in linear bandits with many actions. The paper establishes problem-independent and problem-dependent regret bounds including an additive discovery cost, and shows this cost is unavoidable under their sampling scheme. A theory-driven efficiency improvement for large-action-space bandits.

entry.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code

author.name: Meriem Terki, Nouhaila Innan, Minghao Shao, Muhammad Kashif, Alberto Marchisio, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: QTestBench is a framework for evaluating whether LLM-generated test suites for quantum programs can distinguish correct implementations from faulty ones, judged against independent benchmark checkers rather than treating tests as ground truth. It targets the unique challenges of probabilistic quantum code and domain-specific tolerances.

entry.title: Structural and Representational Agency in LLM-Driven Timbre Generation and Interpolation

author.name: Joseph Cameron, Alan Blackwell

entry.summary: This measurement study of an LLM-driven timbre interface shows that what a user can actually cause is separable from what the interface reports: the reachable set is exactly characterizable as a zonotope whose dimension grows with each sound placed, while the model's self-reported positions in the possibility space diverge from this structure. It leverages audio's unique property of admitting agreed measurement to check model self-reports that most creative domains cannot verify.

entry.title: Beyond Second-Order Information: Paid Logistic Regression with Noisy Features

author.name: Sanghwa Kim, Kyoungseok Jang, Se-Young Yun

entry.summary: Studies online binary prediction where a learner pays to obtain less noisy feature observations, motivated by medical testing. Shows that unlike paid linear regression, covariance information alone is insufficient for logistic models, and develops algorithms balancing prediction loss and acquisition cost.

entry.title: CorrFlow: Exact and Permutation-Equivariant Flow Matching on the Correlation Elliptope

author.name: Gautier Marti

entry.summary: CorrFlow generates correlation matrices by separating validity from distribution learning: a generalized Fisher transform maps full-rank correlation matrices bijectively to unconstrained coordinates, while a graph-based flow matching model with permutation equivariance learns the empirical distribution. This guarantees outputs on the correlation elliptope without post-hoc projection and respects row-column permutation symmetry. It improves on financial matrix generators that mix these two problems.

entry.title: Error Rate is Not Enough: Costs of Augmentation in Low-Resource ASR

author.name: Katsumi Ibaraki, David Chiang

entry.summary: Analyzes phoneme-level error effects of four augmentation methods for low-resource ASR across four languages and five data sizes, finding complementary failure modes: SpecAugment increases tone and palatalization errors while text-to-speech-based methods introduce consonant insertions, each offsetting the other in combination. Argues aggregate error rates obscure when and why augmentation helps. Valuable for low-resource speech practitioners.

entry.title: Mind the Spatial Gap: A Benchmark for Geospatial Reasoning and Constrained Spatial Editing

author.name: Zheng Ren, Yanning Wang, Ziheng Huang, Fei Huang, Shiqi Wang, Ziqian Ye, Yang Yue

entry.summary: GeoSpatialBench evaluates multimodal LLMs on an escalating ladder of spatial cognition, from relation understanding and geometric reasoning to constrained spatial editing, grounded in real urban data from six geographically diverse cities. It moves beyond static QA on synthetic scenes toward modifying spatial configurations under explicit constraints. Useful for assessing grounded world-model capabilities in MLLMs.

entry.title: Simultaneous Competitive and Regret Guarantees for TCP Acknowledgment

author.name: Tsubasa Harada, Yasushi Kawase, Hanna Sumita

entry.summary: Constructs a randomized online algorithm for the TCP acknowledgment problem that simultaneously achieves a (2+epsilon)-competitive ratio versus the offline optimum and near-optimal regret O(sqrt(OPT log(k+1)) + log(1/epsilon)) against the best of k randomized experts, without knowing the packet count or OPT in advance. Combines competitive analysis and learning-augmented guarantees for a classic online problem. Theoretical contribution to online algorithms.

entry.title: Kernel-based External Validity of Experimental Studies

author.name: Federico Matteucci, Gerhard Neumann

entry.summary: The paper formalizes external validity of experimental studies as the probability that two independent same-sized replications produce results within a maximum mean discrepancy tolerance, using reproducing kernels over a space of results. It establishes an asymptotic power-law relation between study size and MMD quantiles, enabling estimation of how findings generalize to unseen conditions such as new datasets. This offers a flexible statistical framework relevant to reproducibility and meta-research.

entry.title: Equal-Budget Monte Carlo Tree Search versus Randomized-Restart List Scheduling for DAG Workflows: A Controlled Equal-Budget Computational Study

author.name: Yuyu Zhang

entry.summary: A rigorously controlled study comparing MCTS for DAG workflow scheduling against a much simpler randomized-restart list scheduler under identical computational budgets. The analysis plan was preregistered and independently validated across 768 confirmation-stage schedules. It addresses a common methodological failure: not giving simple baselines equal search effort when claiming MCTS superiority.

entry.title: Mitigating Capability Degradation in LLM Self-Improvement via Representation Geometry Regularization

author.name: Jiaqi Tian, Ting Long

entry.summary: The paper shows that on-policy self-distillation can progressively degrade previously correct capabilities, coinciding with deterioration of hidden-representation geometry (reduced cluster compactness and separation). It proposes a representation-geometry regularization to mitigate this. A focused diagnosis-and-fix contribution to the self-improvement literature.

entry.title: JoyInside-VLM-Agent: Product-Conditioned Multimodal Policy Learning for Embodied Agents

author.name: Gangyi Li, LuYao Wang, Jingfu Sun, Jingyi Yuan, Hang Liu, Hao Zong, Yujia Hu, Tingting Gao, Jianyong Wang, Xu Yang

entry.summary: JoyInside-VLM-Agent is a ReAct-style multimodal embodied agent trained through product-conditioned trajectory generation in a closed-loop sandbox, followed by SFT, multi-teacher on-policy distillation, and a novel RL method called DPER with token-level evidence routing. It targets robotic platforms and smart hardware where agents must adapt to product constraints, goal changes, and execution feedback. The staged training pipeline is the main technical contribution.

entry.title: Data-driven Optimal Sensor Placement for Aerosol Monitoring in the UK

author.name: Talha Ansar (University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore, Pakistan), Waqar Muhammad Ashraf (The Alan Turing Institute, London, UK), Alejandro Coca-Castro (The Alan Turing Institute, London, UK), Manvendra Janmaijaya (The Alan Turing Institute, London, UK), Ramit Debnath (University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK), J. Scott Hosking (The Alan Turing Institute, London, UK)

entry.summary: The authors embed a convolutional Gaussian neural process in the DeepSensor framework and use genetic optimization with lazy evaluation and caching to place aerosol monitoring stations across the UK. The approach cuts computation time by roughly 60 percent while achieving placement quality comparable to a greedy solver and improving oracle-benchmark joint NLL by about 22 percent.

entry.title: Monarch-MoE: Structured Experts for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Xi Zhang, Boyu Diao, Zesen Chen, Ruiqi Liu, Hangda Liu, Yongjun Xu

entry.summary: Monarch-MoE combats catastrophic forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning by replacing dense low-rank LoRA expert factors with block-diagonal factors connected by fixed permutations. This yields blockwise gradient isolation so individual updates affect only one output block while retaining full input-output connectivity. The authors add batched computation and fused operators for memory-limited hardware.

entry.title: AgentTune: A Unified Training Lifecycle for Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: R E Zera Marveen Lyngkhoi, Abhivansh Gupta, Vidushee Vats, Ram Mohan Rao Kadiyala, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu, Pratinav Seth

entry.summary: Presents AgentTune, a source-available Python library unifying building, training, evaluation, distillation, and maintenance of tool-using LLM agents around a two-tier EventLog trajectory representation. It bundles a shared runtime, tool-calling RL, agentic distillation, RAG, workflows, and evaluation utilities. Addresses the fragmentation of tooling across the agent development lifecycle.

entry.title: Scalable Learning of Determinantal Point Processes with Kernel-Structured Interactions

author.name: Takahiro Kawashima, Hideitsu Hino

entry.summary: The paper addresses the expressive-power versus scalability trade-off in learning determinantal point processes by modeling full-rank kernel interactions through a nonlinear kernel function with latent features. It designs a surrogate objective for maximum likelihood estimation and uses stochastic optimization with random kernel features, enabling DPP learning at scales that previously required restrictive low-rank-plus-diagonal assumptions.

entry.title: BLEND: Balancing Personalization vs. Generalization in Federated Vision-Language Models

author.name: Payam Abdisarabshali, Fardis Nadimi, Kasra Borazjani, Naji Khosravan, Richeng Jin, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour

entry.summary: Presents BLEND, a federated fine-tuning framework for vision-language models combining shared global vision and text adapters with a per-client personalized vision projection adapter, plus a loss blending global and personalized outputs. Aims to jointly improve personalization and generalization in FedVLMs.

entry.title: EmoGavel: Grounding-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards for Multimodal Emotion Preference Learning

author.name: Zilong Huang, Kong Aik Lee, Zezhong Jin, Man-Wai Mak, Tatsuya Kawahara

entry.summary: EmoGavel is a reinforcement learning framework for multimodal emotion preference learning that adds grounding-aware supervision for error localization and repair rather than only optimizing the final pairwise preference decision. It uses grounded supervised fine-tuning with controlled-error construction, then applies RL with verifiable rewards over preference prediction, error localization, repair, and missing-evidence recovery. This improves the interpretability and correctness of emotion-description preference models.

entry.title: Diversity-Aware Ensemble of Quantum-Classical Models via Combinatorial Fusion

author.name: Jingyan Xu, Yuanhong Wu, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Sean Patten, Christina Schweikert, D. Frank Hsu

entry.summary: This work applies Combinatorial Fusion Analysis to fuse predictions from a pool of 29 architecturally diverse variational quantum circuits and classical models, using rank-score functions and cognitive diversity for diversity-aware model selection. The results show that exploiting structural diversity across quantum circuit search spaces yields stronger predictions than selecting a single best circuit.

entry.title: CliQ-RRG: Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Chandravardhan Singh Raghaw, Shahid Shafi Dar, Arnav Nishith Sharma, Shrey Modi, Nagendra Kumar

entry.summary: Presents CliQ-RRG, a two-stage framework for radiology report generation using disease-aware visual-textual alignment and prior-guided attention to produce interpretable, QA-style clinically grounded reports instead of lengthy unstructured narratives. Aims to incorporate diagnostic cues and multi-view information.

entry.title: REFLECT: Role-Aware Detection of Sentiment, Emotion, Politeness, and Formality

author.name: Sangpil Youm, Annabel Stocks Natalias, Hayden Heninger, Leah Jones, Xiaoyang Jin, Xiaoya Zhang, Bonnie Dorr

entry.summary: Introduces a role-aware transformer architecture that maps sentiment, emotion, politeness, and formality to Semantic Role Labeling configurations integrated into self-attention, distinguishing non-directional internal states from directional initiator-to-recipient relations. This grounds pragmatic-semantic detection in theory-grounded role structure rather than purely contextual embeddings. A thoughtful architecture for dialogue understanding.

entry.title: Graph-Based Heuristics for Minimum Constraint Removal in Cluttered Robot Motion Planning

author.name: Antony Thomas, Fulvio Mastrogiovanni, Marco Baglietto

entry.summary: Proposes a graph-based heuristic pipeline for the NP-hard Minimum Constraint Removal problem, combining bidirectional feasible-set generation with fixed-length searches over reduced MCR graphs, plus an extended generator for hard instances. Targets humanoid and service robots in cluttered environments where some obstacles are movable.

entry.title: Towards Safer Cities: A Design Process for Perception Datasets in Urban Driving Scenarios

author.name: Alexander Kroth, Cristian Martinez, Steven Peters

entry.summary: This paper proposes a guided dataset-creation methodology for urban automated-driving perception, emphasizing underrepresented transport modalities such as heavy-duty trucks, buses, and trams beyond passenger cars. It analyzes operational and geographic constraints unique to these platforms, including pedestrian-zone traversal and tasks like trailer movement or winter service. The work highlights a coverage gap in existing automotive perception datasets.

entry.title: Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion

author.name: Yiming Yang, Jeremy P. Bos

entry.summary: The authors propose a low-cost, self-supervised method to detect wheel tracks on snow-covered roads using fused RGB and long-wave infrared imagery, generating training labels automatically from projected GNSS wheel trajectories. Following wheel tracks improves traction and path stability where general traversability estimation falls short, with applications in autonomous driving in winter conditions.

entry.title: Learning Size Independent Constraint Models from Input Data and Positive and Negative Example Solutions

author.name: Helmut Simonis

entry.summary: This paper describes a constraint acquisition tool that learns size-independent MiniZinc constraint models from input data plus positive and negative example solutions across multiple problem instances. The system finds size-specific models from typical constraint patterns, then generalizes them to run on unseen inputs. Evaluated on PTHG21 Challenge problems, it sits at the intersection of program synthesis and constraint programming.

entry.title: Trajectory Prediction for Autonomous Driving in Road Construction Zones Using Human-in-the-Loop Driving Data

author.name: Shuo Zhang, Aman Sunesh, Semiha Ergan, Kaan Ozbay

entry.summary: Collects WZDrive-Data, a multimodal dataset of 1,183 work-zone driving segments from 33 drivers in a simulator with VR-controlled workers, capturing driver gaze and control signals alongside trajectories, to study ego-trajectory prediction in construction zones. Targets an underexplored, safety-critical autonomous driving scenario with temporary road geometry changes.

entry.title: How Reliable are AMR Parser Outputs? Uncertainty Estimation for AMR Parsing

author.name: Anuj Kumar, Shintaro Ozaki, Yamuna Prasad, Katsuhiko Hayashi, Hidetaka Kamigaito, Taro Watanabe

entry.summary: This is the first study of uncertainty estimation for AMR parsers in a black-box setting, using top-k beam-search candidates and pairwise candidate similarities evaluated with the Prediction Rejection Ratio. It characterizes the relationship between parsing performance and uncertainty and identifies parsers with the best performance-reliability balance. The work brings much-needed reliability analysis to structured semantic parsing.

entry.title: Behind-the-Meter Photovoltaic Visibility from Net Smart Meters: Deployment Regimes and Operational Insights

author.name: Jack Zheng, Hao Wang

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks deep-learning PV disaggregation from net smart-meter data across four deployment regimes separating household transfer from temporal extrapolation, using Ausgrid data with cross-dataset adaptation to Pecan Street. It quantifies how the operational value of behind-the-meter PV visibility depends on whether models serve known customers, new customers, future periods, or new regions. It provides regime-matched evaluation for an energy-domain ML problem.

entry.title: Evidential Multimodal Transformers with Dempster-Shafer Fusion for Emotion Recognition

author.name: Muhammad Usama, Yeoreum Jung

entry.summary: EMT-DS addresses overconfidence in multimodal emotion recognition when modalities conflict, modeling predictions as Dirichlet-based Subjective Opinions that separate epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty. Modality-specific transformer encoders produce belief masses fused via Dempster's Rule with conflict normalization. This brings formal uncertainty quantification to a task where softmax models fail under corrupted sensor data.

entry.title: How Much Computation Does Every Forecast Need? Structured Block Skipping in Two Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Max Bourgeat

entry.summary: This single-author study tests whether whole Transformer blocks can be skipped at inference in two pretrained time-series foundation models, Chronos-Bolt and TimesFM 2.5, using masks selected only on calibration windows. At moderate sparsity it reduces median A100 batch-1 latency by 11.2% and 13.4% with little change in forecast quality, with more aggressive settings trading accuracy. The bypasses preserve the dense model exactly when all blocks are enabled.

entry.title: Why Linear Models Can Still Work in a Complex and Changing World

author.name: Fangzhou Lin, Dengzhe Hou, Yinxing Li, Kazunori D Yamada

entry.summary: Argues a position paper explaining why linear models can outperform flexible nonlinear models under distribution shift: when world complexity exceeds what finite, partially observed data can reliably learn, nonlinear components fit idiosyncrasies that fail to transfer, and omitting them can lower prediction error in new environments. Connects the claim to bias-variance, best linear prediction, invariance, Rashomon sets, and underspecification literature. Primarily conceptual with synthesis of existing theory.

entry.title: EarLog: Opportunistic Ear Physiology Sensing toward Personalized Hearing Risk Awareness

author.name: Yongzhi Huang, Jiayi Zhao, Kaishun Wu

entry.summary: EarLog turns ordinary headphone playback into an opportunistic probe for measuring the acoustic reflex, an involuntary ear-protective response, introducing content-conditioned residual sensing to suppress interference from nonstationary audio content plus individual ear acoustics modeling. This enables continuous, personalized hearing-risk monitoring during everyday listening rather than after-the-fact detection of damage.

entry.title: PVBRF-ID: Private, Verifiable and Byzantine-Robust Federated Intrusion Detection for Oilfield Enterprise Networks

author.name: Mustafa S. Aljumaily, Ali Ataeemh Allami, Mustafa N. Mnati, Nawar S. Alseelawi, Shahab Abdulla

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-server federated learning protocol for oilfield intrusion detection in which sites secret-share updates so servers can jointly test update norms and cosine similarity against a clean reference while revealing only one accept bit per site, reconciling Byzantine robustness with secure aggregation. Commitments, Merkle roots, and homomorphic auditing make acceptance publicly verifiable, evaluated on a 15-class Edge-IIoTset task across ten sites.

entry.title: From Imbalance to Evidence: Deep Nonparametric Testing for Complex Data under Severe Sample Imbalance

author.name: Guanhao Zhou, Xiufan Yu

entry.summary: Studies classifier two-sample tests under severe sample imbalance, showing that extreme imbalance can substantially degrade testing performance for complex non-Euclidean data like graphs. Proposes a deep nonparametric testing procedure that leverages majority observations while retaining sensitivity to minority-sample differences.

entry.title: Verifiable Sampling for Delegated Generative Quantum Machine Learning

author.name: Matteo Inajetovic, Anna Pappa, Petros Wallden

entry.summary: Proposes a blind and verifiable protocol for delegating the sampling/inference phase of quantum generative models to a remote quantum server, inheriting blindness from Universal Blind Quantum Computing and verifiability from trapification schemes, with accompanying training delegation.

entry.title: Harmonic analysis and circuit approximation of Sobolev functions on quantum input spaces

author.name: Philipp Schmocker

entry.summary: The paper derives approximation rates for Sobolev functions defined on quantum state spaces and unitary groups using harmonic analysis on compact homogeneous spaces, characterizing Peter-Weyl decompositions and Sobolev spaces via irreducible representations. Combining spectral truncation with finite-depth quantum circuit approximation via Solovay-Kitaev, it establishes quantitative rates separating truncation and circuit approximation errors. This provides rigorous function-approximation foundations for quantum machine learning.

entry.title: Probabilistic Forecasting of Electric Vehicle Charging in a Time-varying Hierarchical Infrastructure

author.name: Guillaume Principato, Yvenn Amara-Ouali, Yannig Goude, Bachir Hamrouche, Jean-Michel Poggi

entry.summary: The paper studies probabilistic forecasting of EV charging demand on a large Scottish public charging network, where demand has a hierarchical structure and the infrastructure itself evolves as stations are added or removed. It combines hierarchical forecasting with conformal prediction methods tailored to this changing structure. The work supports using EV demand uncertainty as a flexibility resource for power systems.

entry.title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sajjad Baghaeea, Aimin Lib, Shanmugarajan Balasubramanian, Elif Uysal

entry.summary: The paper presents a closed-loop reinforcement learning framework for relay-side bundle scheduling and dropping decisions in deep-space communications under the Bundle Protocol, optimizing allocation toward downstream mission utility rather than FIFO fairness. It addresses intermittent connectivity, long delays, and relay storage constraints in store-carry-forward networks.

entry.title: Retractions Revisited: A Replication, Extension, and Mechanistic Evaluation of Linguistic Obfuscation Effects in Fraudulent Science

author.name: David M. Markowitz

entry.summary: Replicates and extends prior findings that fraudulent scientific papers show higher linguistic obfuscation, comparing 800 fraudulent and 800 genuine papers from 2013-2025 and evaluating three competing psychological mechanisms via parallel mediation. Finds support for obfuscation with reality monitoring as the operative mechanism. Relevant to research integrity and forensic linguistics.

entry.title: Image-Based Path-Planning for Navigation of Soft-Growing Robots in the Spinal Sub-Arachnoid Space

author.name: George Dimas, Panagiotis G. Kalozoumis, Panagiotis Vartholomeos, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: Proposes an image-based 3D A*-extension path-planning algorithm for navigating a soft-growing robot inside the spinal subarachnoid space, aiming to protect delicate tissue during minimally invasive procedures or drug delivery. The method ensures safe pathways to target locations under medical imaging constraints.

entry.title: EliteTable: Self-Improving Program Search for Executable Control Policies

author.name: Stuart Farmer

entry.summary: EliteTable is an LLM-guided program-search algorithm that maintains a fixed-capacity table of top-scoring solutions to steer new proposals, edits, and remixes. Evaluated on six Gymnasium control tasks over ten generations, candidate scores improved consistently, with CartPole-v1 winners hitting the score ceiling immediately. It offers a simple, cheap mechanism for LLM-driven self-improvement in executable policy synthesis.

entry.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models

author.name: Ivan Moloshnikov, Dmitry Kunitsyn, Alexander Sboev, Maksim Skorokhodov, Roman Rybka, Yuanchao Liu

entry.summary: This system uses a three-role multi-agent LLM framework (analyst, coder, recorder) with a sandboxed environment and experiment log to automatically tune key components of specialized neural networks. Rather than optimizing whole scripts or searching architectures, agents generate code only for specified components within an open but semantically narrow space. The framework is designed to transfer across models of different natures.

entry.title: UkrMeme: Multimodal Explainable Persuasion Detection in Ukrainian Memes

author.name: Nazar Andrushko, Vera Schmitt, Veronika Solopova

entry.summary: Presents UkrMeme, a 200-item dataset of Ukrainian wartime memes annotated for persuasion techniques, plus a Ukrainian translation of a Propaganda 950 subset, and evaluates VLMs zero-shot on multimodal persuasion detection with explainability comparisons (LRP vs token attributions). It contributes a culturally specific resource for studying political influence operations.

entry.title: Kairos: Toward a Byte-Level Foundation Model for Every Modality

author.name: Fabien Furfaro

entry.summary: Kairos is a single-author technical report proposing a byte-level foundation model combining bidirectional gated-DeltaNet linear attention, sliding-window attention, block-wise attention-residual aggregation, sparse mixture-of-experts layers, and a multi-scale byte codec trained with a denoising objective across text, image, audio, video, lidar, and control data. The report focuses on whether this ambitious combination can converge and optimize at all, providing code-derived algorithms and convergence sanity checks such as overfitting tests. It is an early-stage feasibility study for a universal byte-space modality model, trainable on a single machine.

entry.title: Efficient Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement via Reinforcement Learning-Based Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Khubaib Ahmed, Ahsan Adeel, Nasir Saleem, Kia Dashtipour, Ahsan Ulhaq, Amir Hussain

entry.summary: This paper uses reinforcement learning-driven neural architecture search with proximal policy optimization and constraint-aware action masking to find compact audio-visual speech enhancement models for edge devices. The reward jointly optimizes SI-SNR improvement and model size, evaluating only 35 candidate architectures and producing a 2.9M-parameter model. It is relevant for deploying speech enhancement on resource-constrained hardware.

entry.title: Agent4Spec: An LLM-based Agentic System to Optimize API Specifications through Automated Validation and Market Analysis

author.name: Yongjian Tang, Costel Moraru, Doruk Tuncel, Hanya Elhashemy, Steffen Klepke, Thomas Runkler

entry.summary: Agent4Spec is a multi-agent framework with two pipelines: one detecting and self-correcting OpenAPI specification errors, and another doing market analysis to identify functional gaps and drive specification evolution. It reframes API spec generation as a continuous validation and maintenance process rather than a one-time event. This targets a practical software engineering workflow where spec quality affects integration and code generation.

entry.title: CNN-Transformer with Sigmoid Label for High-Resolution Sub-Degree DOA Estimation

author.name: Lifeng Wang, Xintong Li, Aifei Liu

entry.summary: This signal processing paper tackles grid quantization error in deep-learning direction-of-arrival estimation by encoding source angles as sums of angle-shifted monotonic sigmoid functions. Differentiating the CNN-Transformer output yields sharp spectral peaks, achieving sub-degree accuracy with a modest 0.25-degree grid. It is a focused engineering contribution to radar/array processing.

entry.title: An Input-Dependent Readout Phase for Resonant Sequence Models

author.name: Shivesh Rane

entry.summary: The paper modifies ResonatorLM, a fixed-transition resonator sequence model, by making its per-head readout phase a function of the current token, adding input dependence to the read path while preserving the exact O(T log T) convolutional training route at a cost of only 0.2% more parameters. The analysis also examines what the untrained oscillator bank encodes, finding phase tracks elapsed time but tokens fall below background levels. It is a focused architectural refinement.

entry.title: NV-Tesseract-AD: Curriculum-Enhanced Conditional Diffusion for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Aditi Gautam, Manikandan Ravikiran, Saira Qureshi, Sena Fatma Ekiz, Charan Jagwani, Mahmoud Elhadidy, Sanjeev Roka

entry.summary: NV-Tesseract-AD combines a Transformer-based conditional diffusion backbone with a three-stage dual curriculum over masking severity and diffusion noise levels for multivariate time-series anomaly detection. The hypothesis is that structuring reconstruction difficulty from easy to hard along both axes stabilizes optimization and improves residual discriminability, evaluated across two regimes.

entry.title: FedPCD: Priority-Constrained Federated Aggregation

author.name: Yousef Irshaid, Dara Varam, Mohamed I. AlHajri

entry.summary: Proposes a priority-constrained federated optimization framework that keeps the conventional federated aggregate as the primary objective while adding client protections as constraints, rather than re-weighting clients or symmetrically treating objectives. This preserves the global optimization direction under statistical heterogeneity while improving fairness for priority clients. Targets fairness gaps in federated learning.

entry.title: VQIL: Visible Quantum Interference Learning for Perturbation Response Ranking on Graphs

author.name: Seokjun Lee, Sergio A. Ortega, Daniel K. Park, Namshik Han

entry.summary: VQIL formulates seed-conditioned perturbation response ranking on graphs as learning a trainable Szegedy quantum walk, with edge weights, link phases, and node phase rotations optimized end-to-end by backpropagation while preserving unitarity. Node scores derive from a geometric quantity related to the walk.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Satellite Intelligence: A Formal Framework for Event-Driven Architectures, Spike-Based Algorithms, and Quantitative Energy-Accuracy Trade-offs

author.name: Suresh Kumar TP, Vikas Agnihotri

entry.summary: This paper develops a formal mathematical model of spiking neural computation for satellite onboard workloads, deriving closed-form energy expressions as functions of sparsity, firing rate, and synaptic fan-out. It proposes three algorithms - a Spiking Kalman-Complementary Filter, a Temporal Contrast Anomaly Detector, and a Spike-Based Adaptive Modulation and Coding scheme - targeting the tension between growing mission intelligence demands and fixed power, mass, and radiation budgets.

entry.title: Polyconvex neural-network surrogates with learned paired directional features for anisotropic hyperelastic homogenization

author.name: S. Ares de Parga, A. Cornejo, J. A. Hern\'andez, R. Rossi

entry.summary: The work develops physics-augmented neural network surrogates for anisotropic hyperelastic material response, using paired directional features with learned orientations and exponents composed with input-convex cores (ICNN or input-convex Kolmogorov-Arnold networks). The constructions guarantee objectivity, exact stress-free reference, 2D polyconvexity, and prescribed growth conditions by design.

entry.title: Desertification Forecasting in Semi-Arid Regions: Using Deep Learning to Probe the Observability Limits of Land Degradation Dynamics

author.name: Filipe Moura Da Silva, Cl\'aubio Landney Lima Bandeira

entry.summary: The paper trains a convolutional LSTM on ten annual Earth observation variables over Ceara, Brazil, to forecast a MapBiomas-derived land degradation index, explicitly probing how much year-to-year degradation change is predictable from satellite data. It uses a two-stage training regime and contiguous spatiotemporal holdouts, finding state-wide trends but cell-level dynamics dominated by year-to-year noise. The work shifts attention from mapping desertification to forecasting it and honestly quantifies observability limits.

entry.title: BenCoDiC: A Large-Scale Contextual Cyberbullying Corpus for Bengali Political News Discourse FULL VERSION

author.name: Md. Nesarul Hoque, Rudra Pratap Deb Nath, Umme Salma, Shima Chakraborty, Md. Hanif Seddiqui

entry.summary: Introduces BenCoDiC, a publicly available Bengali cyberbullying corpus of 50,250 instances from 100 YouTube political news discussions, preserving caption-comment-reply structure with a nine-dimensional annotation schema. Enables contextual detection and study of harasser behaviors in a low-resource language.

entry.title: MoPrO-SD: Modular Prompt Optimization for Stance Detection

author.name: Meysam Sabbaghan, Nikesh Gyawali, Arman Zareian Jahromi, Sebastian Loera-Lozano, Doina Caragea, Cornelia Caragea

entry.summary: Introduces MoPrO-SD, a prompt optimization framework tailored to stance detection that decomposes prompts into functional semantic modules refined sequentially via LLM feedback, with three refinement strategies compared. It targets class-specific ambiguities like sarcasm and implicit stance that generic prompt optimizers ignore. A solid application-level contribution for a specific NLP task.

entry.title: Distributed Harmonic-Covariance Feedback for Hole Closure in Planar Robot Swarms

author.name: Jitian Liu, Subhrajit Bhattacharya

entry.summary: Proposes a distributed harmonic-covariance feedback law for closing holes in planar robot swarms, using harmonic edge signals over a time-varying Cech complex converted into agent forces via a fixed-degree polynomial of the regularized Hodge Laplacian. Provides global convergence guarantees with explicit approximation error bounds.

entry.title: Large to Small Model Stitching Destroys What You Built It to Carry Along the Fit

author.name: ppriyadarshini

entry.summary: An early-stage independent research post extending model stitching work on transferring linear features between language models, reporting that feature transfer from large to small models peaks early in training and then declines, while geometric similarity metrics keep rising and miss this trend. The finding holds across three bridge objectives and multiple hook points, with implications for AI safety techniques that reuse SAEs, probes, and steering vectors across models.

entry.title: GeoFitBench-LLM: A Benchmark for Assessing Large Language Models' Capabilities in Geospatial Data Requirements Elicitation for Geo-Analytic Tasks

author.name: Amirhossein Vahdat, Thierry Badard, Luc Lamontagne

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark testing whether LLMs can infer the datasets, resources, and constraints needed to fulfill natural-language geo-analytic requests, structured around Spatio-Temporal Relational and Semantic Grounding reasoning dimensions. Fills an evaluation gap for LLMs in GeoAI planning before retrieval can even occur.

entry.title: Evolving Creatives with Clicks: CTR-Driven Advertising image Editing via Attribute Disentanglement and Preference Alignment

author.name: Xu Zhang, Haohan Wang, Zheng Zhang, Yingjie Xia, Wei Feng, Honghe Zhu, Jingjing Lv, Changping Peng, Xuheng Qin, Zehua Zhang, Zheng Luo, Qicheng Li

entry.summary: ECC reformulates e-commerce advertising creative optimization as fine-grained editing rather than generation from scratch, disentangling image attributes so that only CTR-hurting attributes are refined while beneficial ones are preserved. It uses CTR-derived reward signals with preference alignment for the editing policy. This reflects a shift in industry objectives from aesthetics toward measurable business metrics.

entry.title: Prediction-Informed Landing Window Planning for UAV Landing on USV in High Sea States

author.name: Kaizhen Li, Xi Zhou, Dan Zhang, Xiaowei Li

entry.summary: Proposes a prediction-informed hierarchical control framework for autonomous UAV landing on unmanned surface vehicles, using a pretrained model to explicitly predict USV attitude and identify suitable landing windows, combined with a low-level flight controller. Evaluated under realistic sea-state disturbances.

entry.title: Vocal Intensity Conversion with Continuous SPL Control via Adversarial Training

author.name: Quentin Le Tellier, Albert Rilliard, Olivier Perrotin, Marc Evrard

entry.summary: The paper presents a lightweight conditional cycle-consistent GAN that converts recorded speech to any target sound pressure level on a continuous dB scale, preserving content and speaker identity rather than merely scaling amplitude. It operates on features of a frozen speech encoder with a pretrained vocoder for resynthesis and compares log-mel, WavLM, and SpeechTokenizer representations under an objective protocol measuring achieved intensity change. This extends voice conversion with continuous, physically grounded control.

entry.title: SharP: Soft and Hard Prompt-Guided Augmentation with LLM for Low Resource Fake News Detection

author.name: Ziyu Luo, Wei Li, Haoping Huang, Kecheng Liu, Min Gao

entry.summary: Proposes SharP, combining soft and hard prompt-guided LLM augmentation to produce task-relevant synthetic examples for low-resource fake news detection under a fixed evaluation protocol. Motivated by generic LLM-generated augmentation lacking deceptive-pattern specificity.

entry.title: Enhancing Legal Reasoning in Pre-trained Language Models via Knowledge Graph-Guided Multi-Task Pre-training

author.name: Ibrahim Siddig, Munir Georges

entry.summary: Presents a multi-task pre-training approach for German traffic law combining NSP, KG-guided clustering, and KG-aware paragraph classification to encode hierarchical statutory structure into model weights, addressing the flatness of standard masked-language pre-training. A companion effort to the authors' verifiable-retrieval work on legal reasoning. Solid domain-specific pre-training contribution.

entry.title: Faithful and Complete LLM-Assisted Automated Construction of Hierarchical Hardware Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Haotian Qiao, Robert P. Dick

entry.summary: An LLM-driven pipeline converts hardware datasheets into hierarchical knowledge graphs via chunk-based property extraction, hierarchical routing, and iterative refinement, addressing the omissions of naive one-shot processing. It targets engineering workflows like component selection and compatibility verification. Useful applied work demonstrating structured extraction beyond single-pass LLM reading.

entry.title: Agentic Large Language Models

author.name: Max van Duijn, Michiel van der Meer, Aske Plaat, Niki van Stein

entry.summary: This is a book-length educational treatment of agentic LLMs covering how they work, act, and interact with each other and the world, and what that means for users. From an established academic group (van Stein, Plaat et al.), it appears aimed at students and practitioners entering the area. It consolidates a fast-moving field into an accessible reference rather than presenting new research.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient Spiking Neural Networks for Sensing-Aided Beam Prediction

author.name: Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Phuong Nam Tran, Mengyuan Ma, Huy T. Nguyen, Ahmed Alkhateeb, Markku Juntti

entry.summary: Develops spiking neural network architectures for millimeter-wave beam prediction using vision, position, and multimodal sensing, comparing them against compact ANNs. SNNs win on vision and multimodal sensing while ANNs are better for position-only input, informing energy-efficient 6G-era wireless design.

entry.title: MotionCoach: Constructing Multimodal Guidance for Video Professional Motion Editing

author.name: Siyi Qian, Hanqing Yang, Weihuang Lin, Zihao Yang, Yichen Lu, Yuanhong Zheng, Sheng Li

entry.summary: MotionCoach is a trained multimodal agent that uses multi-turn tool use and self-verification to generate grounded prompts and reference media for professional motion editing in video, covering domains like sports, performance, and martial arts. It targets cases where editing models fail on fine-grained motion instructions such as a Stoppie maneuver. The agentic guidance-construction approach addresses a real gap in instruction-following for specialized motion.

entry.title: Inverse Synthesis of Shock Time Series from Shock Response Spectra Using Ensembles of Conditional Variational Autoencoders

author.name: Adam Watts, Charles Young, Ryan Bowering, Andrew Jeon, Destry Newton

entry.summary: The paper extends a conditional variational autoencoder with a recurrent decoder predicting multiscale wavelet coefficients to synthesize acceleration waveforms consistent with a prescribed shock response spectrum. Because individual models show limited variability, the authors use ensembles across mother wavelets and decomposition levels to generate diverse candidate waveforms for engineering design.

entry.title: WaSA: Wavelet Scattering Autoencoders for Unsupervised Offline Detection of Malicious Clients in Federated Learning

author.name: Alessandro Licciardi

entry.summary: WaSA provides unsupervised, offline detection of malicious clients in federated learning: each client sends a privacy-preserving spectral summary of its data before training, and a denoising autoencoder trained on clean auxiliary data scores deviations from the benign manifold. Unlike reactive or supervised defenses, it identifies corruption regardless of attack type, suiting open-ended IoT deployments. Single-authored work with a clear defensive use case.

entry.title: A Sampling Complexity-aware Framework for Discrete-time Fractional-Order Dynamical System Identification

author.name: Xiaole Zhang, Vijay Gupta, Paul Bogdan

entry.summary: This paper proposes an algorithm for identifying discrete-time fractional-order dynamical systems, which model non-Markovian dynamics in biological and man-made systems, and provides a detailed sample complexity analysis under noisy data. The method avoids solving higher-order polynomial equations that produce multiple candidate fractional orders by reformulating the identification problem.

entry.title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion

author.name: Zeru Zhu, Marco Gamarra, Ji Liu

entry.summary: The paper tackles the open problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed vertex and edge counts via a two-stage approach: a density-dependent structural backbone using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in sparse regimes, followed by reinforcement learning to refine remaining edges. Numerical results show favorable runtime scalability versus existing methods.

entry.title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels

author.name: Efstathios Chatziloizos, Konstantinos Vandikas, Aneta Vulgarakis Feljan, Zheng Chen, Nikolaos Pappas

entry.summary: The paper combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict channel state information in time-varying multi-antenna wireless channels from noisy observations. A residual correction configuration relative to the latest latent state outperforms baselines at moderate and high signal-to-noise ratios. This applies self-supervised representation learning ideas to a practical telecommunications problem.

entry.title: Does Financial Speech Need Continual Learning Regularization? A Study of EWC and mini-KFAC on Earnings Call ASR

author.name: Thai Quoc On, Homayoon Beigi

entry.summary: The study examines continual learning regularization (EWC and mini-KFAC) for adapting Whisper-small to earnings call transcription, finding that adaptation improves held-out same-domain financial speech rather than causing catastrophic forgetting, making regularization counterproductive. When regularization is warranted, a layer-wise mini-KFAC approximation achieves lower word error rates and more stable optimization. It is a useful negative-result-driven analysis of when continual learning machinery is actually needed.

entry.title: U4RASD at KnowledgeGraphEval-2026: Ontology-Constrained Encoder and LLM Systems for Arabic Relation Extraction

author.name: Ahmad Abbas, Hussein Mazeh, Chadi Abou Chakra, Aya Jouni, Mohammad Ballout, Fadi A. Zaraket

entry.summary: A shared-task submission for Arabic directed relation extraction combining encoder models with typed entity markers and QLoRA fine-tuned LLMs (including a Qwen3.5 variant, an established model family) with ontology-constrained prediction. The best ensemble achieved 94.06 micro-F1, ranking first in Subtask 2.

entry.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis

author.name: Natapong Nitarach, Phume Ngampornsukswadi, Pittawat Taveekitworachai, Surapon Nonesung, Warit Sirichotedumrong, Kunat Pipatanakul

entry.summary: Introduces AMLworld-Compact, a compact evaluation set for the anti-money-laundering graph benchmark that keeps every illicit transaction and samples benign ones from score strata, using Horvitz-Thompson weights to give unbiased full-test confusion-count estimates. It cuts evaluation targets by 271x to 611x while preserving estimate validity. A niche but methodologically careful contribution to evaluation cost reduction.

entry.title: Robust and Scalable UAV-UGV Planning for Aerial Monitoring under Energy and Precedence Constraints

author.name: Cahit Ikbal Er, Yasin Yazicioglu

entry.summary: Formalizes planning for multi-UAV-UGV teams in aerial monitoring with ordering constraints, where UGVs act as mobile charging stations transporting UAVs between tours. The objective is minimizing mission completion time under UAV endurance limits, with a scalable and robust solution approach.

entry.title: Towards a Unified Taxonomy of Agricultural Harvesting Technologies: Linking Physical Interaction, Automation, and Selectivity

author.name: Renato Cristiano Torres, Fabiano Mariath D Oliveira, Claudio Gottschalg Duque

entry.summary: This position/survey paper proposes a unified taxonomy for agricultural harvesting technologies organized along two axes: the physical principle governing plant-machine interaction and the level of automation, with selectivity treated as a derived property. It aims to resolve the current fragmented classification by crop type, mechanism, sensing, or robot architecture that hinders comparison.

entry.title: MARGoS: A Configuration-Driven Platform for Reproducible MARL Experiments in ARGoS

author.name: Tom Philipp Backert, Mohammad D. Soorati, Javad Ghofrani

entry.summary: MARGoS is a lightweight, configuration-driven platform that standardizes experiment definitions for multi-agent reinforcement learning in the ARGoS swarm robotics simulator, treating simulator files, training scripts, seeds, and configurations as first-class reproducible artifacts. It addresses the fragility of manually assembled MARL experiment setups.

entry.title: CoGameReg: Cooperative-Game-Based Collaborative Semi-Supervised Regression for Seismic Reservoir Property Prediction

author.name: Zhiyu Guo, Jiwei Jia, Lei Li

entry.summary: CoGameReg is a semi-supervised regression framework for predicting reservoir properties from seismic data with sparse well-log labels. It uses a Tri-Game Shapley mechanism combining a rank-MSE performance game and a pairwise consistency game to compute nonnegative weights over heterogeneous regressors, which then generate contribution-weighted pseudo-labels for unlabeled seismic samples.

entry.title: Target-Constrained Pooling for Trajectory Extrapolation

author.name: Ning Wang, Claire Cardie, Sainyam Galhotra

entry.summary: TCP addresses trajectory extrapolation from partial trajectories by separating finite-horizon endpoint estimation from continuation shape, pooling information from completed related trajectories. It combines uniform pooling of final response levels with matched-increment pooling after state alignment, projecting estimates onto a target-consistent region with calibrated weighting. This is a general method for completing underdetermined sequential forecasts.

entry.title: Probabilistic Ship Trajectory Forecasting using Transformer Models on AIS Data

author.name: Frederik E. T. Sch\"oller

entry.summary: Applies Transformer and Performer models to probabilistic vessel trajectory prediction in confined waters using AIS data, encoding local vessel movement history as KDE-generated positional heat maps. The work supports collision avoidance for human navigators and autonomous surface vessels. An applied sequence-modeling study in the maritime domain.

entry.title: Learning Schwarzschild Geodesic Motion with Lagrangian Neural Networks

author.name: Sukru Caglar, Sena Kalabalik, Abdullah Umut Hamzaogullari, Arkadas Ozakin

entry.summary: This paper extends Lagrangian Neural Networks to the previously open challenge of Schwarzschild geodesics in general relativity, tackling training difficulties from diverse dynamics, numerical instability, and orbital regime sampling. It introduces a decoupled position-velocity normalization scheme and a coordinated second improvement to make learning stable. The result demonstrates variational inductive biases generalizing to strongly relativistic settings.

entry.title: Towards Defining, Measuring, and Leveraging Creativity in AI Applications

author.name: Jingyi Yang, Alexander Tuzhilin

entry.summary: The paper proposes formal postulates of creativity grounded in psychological theory, particularly Boden's categories, aiming for definitions that are both conceptually sound and empirically applicable across art, science, and games. It seeks to bridge informal creativity definitions and purely formal ones. Relevant to the growing area of AI creativity evaluation but largely conceptual.

entry.title: DataCupid: Stable Matching Repair for Training Data Acquisition with Delayed Feedback

author.name: He Sun, Junyuan Mao, Wenhao Jiang, Mingjun Xiao, Shinan Liu

entry.summary: This work studies how to repair matching allocations during training data acquisition when utilities change and evaluations return with bounded, possibly reward-dependent delays. The proposed Residual Load Repair (RLR) combines outcome certificates with batched matching schedules, achieving a sharp issue-round bound (coefficient below 1.607) plus separate delay and evidence-lifetime guarantees.
