Exploration traces drive co-evolution of the system's knowledge, skills, and multi-agent orchestration, improving both the produced models and the system's modeling ability.

entry.title: From Chain-of-Thought to Loops: Non-Autoregressive Latent Reasoning via Looped Transformers

author.name: Gerard Grau Garc\'ia, Arnau Padr\'es Masdemont, Niccol\`o Grillo, Jordi Ros-Giralt, Arash Behboodi, Victor Conchello Vendrell

entry.summary: LLoCoT replaces autoregressive chain-of-thought tokens with iterative refinement of a compact latent workspace, reapplying a shared transformer to jointly update latent slots based on the prompt and evolving workspace. This removes the left-to-right dependency that constrains most latent-reasoning methods.

entry.title: AgentEvolver: System-Wide Self-Evolution Through Task Execution

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Fuchao Yang, Yilei Zhao, Xinrun Wang, Bo An

entry.summary: AgentEvolver is a system in which an agent's surrounding capabilities (operations, methods, control flow, interfaces, state) evolve through task execution while the foundation model stays frozen, with eight entity families under a versioned lifecycle and a shared runtime. It reports strong results on SWE-bench Pro Public plus six application case studies.

entry.title: Safe Actions Alone Do Not Ensure Safe Agents: Identifying Unfulfilled Obligations with Guard Models

author.name: Youwei Feng, Yitong Zhang, Yuetong Liu, Jia Li

entry.summary: Argues that guard models for LLM agents should detect not only forbidden actions but required safety-critical actions that were omitted, which the authors call obligations. On a popular safety benchmark, 56.92% of trajectories contained unfulfilled obligations versus only 30.00% containing forbidden actions, and the paper builds evaluation infrastructure for obligation-aware guards.

entry.title: Learning to Plan by Looking Back: Hindsight Hierarchies for Training Reasoning Models

author.name: Lars Simon, Holger Eble, Manuel Radons

entry.summary: This work proposes a self-improvement loop for reasoning models in which the model reverse-engineers solution ideas from problems with supplied solutions, then uses those ideas as supervision alongside idea prediction and idea-conditioned solving. The formal framework turns hindsight on unsolved problems into a training signal for self-improvement.

entry.title: Verdict Without the Rule: Diagnosing and Auditing Regulatory Rule Sensitivity in LLM Compliance Systems

author.name: Saisab Sadhu, Aadit Sengupta, Vinay kumar Sankarapu, Pratinav Seth

entry.summary: The authors test whether LLM compliance verdicts actually depend on the regulatory rule provided, by deleting, swapping, or negating governing rules across five models and 20 policy domains. Verdicts are often invariant to substantial rule perturbations, and a dedicated guard model is the least rule-sensitive and least accurate (51% versus 90-92% for general models).

entry.title: Strategic Governance of AI Models in Earth Science

author.name: Makoto Kelp, Amirhossein Arzani, Patricia Castellanos, Paul Griffiths, Ivan Higuera-Mendieta, Manuel Perez-Carrasco, Viral Shah, Patrick Obin Sturm, James Weber

entry.summary: Argues that AI foundation models for weather and climate are being adopted faster than the scientific community can evaluate them, and that benchmark forecast skill does not establish physical reliability, especially under nonstationary climate conditions. The authors propose five priorities for physically grounding the evaluation of Earth-science AI models.

entry.title: Optimizing Large Language Models with Chained LMOs

author.name: Sungyoon Kim, Kaan Ozkara, Youngsuk Park

entry.summary: The paper unifies Muon-style optimizers as compositions of chained linear minimization oracles, showing that many chains fall outside the standard LMO framework and can diverge on smooth convex objectives, while linear associative memory analysis explains when chaining helps under anisotropic embeddings. It proposes TensorChain, a new optimizer that stacks and normalizes weight matrices across layers.

entry.title: SFT-as-Context Mitigates Forgetting in Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Kenan Tang, Andong Hua, Chengxuan Qian, Saket Tiwari, Yao Qin

entry.summary: SFT-as-context is a training-free method where the parent pretrained model consumes the SFT model's response as context, acquiring specialized capabilities through in-context learning while preserving its general abilities. Across 19 parent-SFT model pairs and 11 benchmarks it stays close to SFT performance on fine-tuned tasks while mitigating forgetting. The idea is simple, broadly applicable, and directly addresses a ubiquitous problem in LLM deployment.

entry.title: Large Language Model Turnover Undermines Screening for Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Scientific Writing

author.name: Kazuki Nakajima, Takayuki Mizuno

entry.summary: The authors quantify how the rapid turnover of LLM versions undermines detectors used by journals to screen for AI-assisted writing. Using 4,000 PNAS abstracts rewritten by 23 LLM versions from three vendors between 2023 and 2026, they evaluate detectors under maintenance scenarios from full retraining to never updating, showing that detectors trained on past versions degrade as models change.

entry.title: All Verdicts are Not Equal: Rethinking LLM Judge Reliability

author.name: Vineet Kumar, Darshita Rathore, Anindya Moitra

entry.summary: This comprehensive audit stress-tests six frontier models as LLM judges across four benchmarks, five prompt formats, two presentation orders, three temperatures, and ten repetitions, finding severe reliability failures: verdicts flip at temperature zero on identical replications, position swaps flip majorities, and the most consistent judge is only 51% accurate despite perfect self-consistency. The paper proposes formal metrics to characterize these failure modes.

entry.title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants

author.name: Pratik Dutta, Matthew B. Obusan, Max Chao, Rekha Sathian, Nimisha Papineni, Ramana V. Davuluri

entry.summary: ARGUS is an agentic framework for interpreting noncoding genetic variants that strictly separates deterministic biological computation (458 DNABERT-based TF binding models) from LLM-mediated reasoning, in a hypothesis-directed investigation loop with uncertainty awareness. It directly addresses LLM hallucination of transcription factor binding changes and fabricated experimental support in genomic medicine.

entry.title: RH-Detect: A Unified Benchmark for Reward Hacking Detection

author.name: Junwei Quan, Evgenii Opryshko, Rohan Subramani, Igor Gilitschenski

entry.summary: RH-Detect aggregates reward-hacking-relevant subsets from eleven public datasets into a common schema of 92,761 rows spanning six behavior categories, providing 5,021 open-ended evaluation units including multi-turn tool-use trajectories. The benchmark evaluates six off-the-shelf language models from five families as zero-shot reward-hacking detectors, enabling comparable detector assessment for the first time.

entry.title: Read What Matters: Query-Adaptive Quantization for KV Caches

author.name: Siddharth Bhandari, Lucas Gretta, Krishna Balasubramanian, Shiva Kasiviswanathan

entry.summary: ReadKV stores KV-cache entries in progressive codes whose prefixes support multiple reconstruction precisions, then allocates key-channel and value-token prefixes adaptively per decoding query under separate budgets for stored and fetched bits. The method optimizes a calibrated distortion objective with provable exact allocation under diminishing refinement gains, relating the objectives to attention-output error. This query-aware approach addresses the mismatch between pre-stored precision and per-query needs.

entry.title: PRAXIS: Learning Dynamics of Self-Improving Models with Symbolic Archives

author.name: Venkat Margapuri, Mustafa Teber

entry.summary: PRAXIS is a co-evolutionary framework modeling self-improving systems as interacting generator, learner, and symbolic archive processes. The authors prove theoretical guarantees bounding one-step objective drift, archive suppression of comparators under sub-Gaussian noise, and an average-stationarity guarantee for SGD whose degradation is governed by cumulative objective drift, supported by experiments.

entry.title: A Unified Bellman Operator for Safety-Critical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nishanth Arun Rao, Royina Karegoudra Jayanth, Benjamin Eysenbach, Jaime Fern\'andez Fisac

entry.summary: The paper proposes a novel Bellman operator unifying task performance and safety constraints into a joint value function, aiming to escape the usual safe-RL trade-off between strict a priori guarantees (safety filters) and average-case constraint satisfaction. It proves convergence of temporal difference learning under a two-timescale stochastic approximation framework. Authors include Benjamin Eysenbach and Jaime Fisac, both prominent in safe RL and control.

entry.title: Beyond Distributional Fidelity: Causal-Penalized Diffusion for Synthetic Tabular Data

author.name: Lan Tao, Yongxian He, Shirong Xu, Yidong Ouyang, Guang Cheng

entry.summary: This paper shows theoretically that high statistical fidelity in synthetic tabular data does not imply preservation of causal effects, and proposes a causal-fidelity-aware training framework adding a causal discrepancy penalty to a generative objective, instantiated as causal-penalized TabDDPM. The goal is to make synthetic data reliable for downstream causal inference.

entry.title: $\sigma$Transfer: Uncertainty Transfer from Small to Large Networks under $\mu\mathrm{P}$

author.name: Richard Bergna (University of Cambridge, Spotify), Fernando Ruiz Mazo (University of Cambridge), Nicol\`o Felicioni (Spotify), Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato (University of Cambridge), Kamil Ciosek (Spotify)

entry.summary: This work derives a rescaling of the prior covariance under Maximal Update Parametrization so that the prior precision selected for a Laplace approximation on a small model transfers zero-shot to much larger models. The authors prove convergence of prior kernels, posterior covariances, and downstream decisions, avoiding prohibitively expensive hyperparameter sweeps at billion-parameter scale. This makes Bayesian uncertainty quantification for large networks far more practical.

entry.title: SAIL: Scientific Agentic Intelligence via a Science-Aware Loop

author.name: SAIL Model Team, Boyuan Sun, Bryan Dai, Che Liu, Chi Liu, Derek Li, Hongming Piao, Mengzhuo Chen, Xidong Wang, Yan Shu, Yinda Chen, Ziyang Zeng

entry.summary: SAIL is an open 35B-total/3B-active parameter model for literature research, scientific coding, and multi-step research workflows, developed through a self-improving loop where agents built on frontier models diagnose its task failures and construct targeted training tasks, trajectories, and executable environments. The loop is repeated over multiple development cycles.

entry.title: A persistent accuracy ceiling in automated verbal deception detection

author.name: Riccardo Loconte, Jonas Festor, Zane Fatjanova, Mariam Bolkvadze, Bennett Kleinberg

entry.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis covers 25 years of verbal deception detection research, pooling 3,653 models across 97 datasets, finding a stubborn 74.4% accuracy ceiling. Accuracy is driven more by methodological quality than model complexity, and LLMs have not improved performance, while only about 12% of reports used verifiable ground truth.

entry.title: Velocity Scaling in Flow Matching

author.name: Youssef Saied, Fran\c{c}ois Fleuret

entry.summary: This paper corrects the theoretical account of velocity scaling in flow matching, showing that MSE training does not actually create a velocity-magnitude deficit as previously argued; instead, scaling reduces a population time lag where sampled states at model time t resemble earlier training states. Measuring this lag and selecting the gain accordingly improves generation quality across architectures and model sizes. This is a valuable mechanistic insight for the widely used flow matching framework.

entry.title: Stop My Dancing! Understanding, Detecting and Attributing Motion-Aware Deepfake Videos

author.name: Fazhong Liu, Yan Meng, Tian Dong, Guoxing Chen, Haojin Zhu

entry.summary: Constructs the first benchmark and measurement framework for motion-aware deepfakes (MAD) generated by pose-guided diffusion models, with over 1.5 million frames mixing 1,363 real and 30,122 synthetic videos from six generators under realistic perturbations. The work identifies faint but reliable motion-boundary artifacts enabling detection and attribution of this emerging threat.

entry.title: Connected Self Forcing: Beyond Local Learning in Video Autoregression

author.name: Dongbin Zhang, Chaoda Zheng, Kangjie Chen, Xiangyu Li, Shijia Chen, Jinhao Deng, Yuqi Zhang, Guangfeng Jiang, Hongbin Lin, Choo Sin Wai, Minqi Wang, Puyi Wang, Jingye Zhang, Yu Zhang, Xianming Liu, Boyang Wang

entry.summary: The authors extend Self Forcing, a training method for streaming video autoregression, by reconnecting gradient paths across autoregressive chunks so that later predictions can influence how earlier context is generated. This addresses the memory-motivated detachment of historical KV caches, enabling end-to-end credit assignment in long video generation.

entry.title: SepGen: Multi-Stem Audio-Video Separation and Generation in a Single Model

author.name: Aviad Dahan, Rajaei Khatib, Yonatan Bitton, Idan Szpektor, Lior Wolf, Raja Giryes

entry.summary: SepGen extends a pretrained audio-video generator so a single joint sampling run produces video, a mixed soundtrack, and an individual waveform for each captioned sound source. This enables novel-viewpoint rendering of 4D audio-visual scenes where each source can be spatially localized and propagated before mixing.

entry.title: PathTime-VLA: Path-Time Decoupling for Factorized Post-Training of Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Qing Huang, Yifei Yang, Ziqing Zou, Anzhe Chen, Zhenjie Zhu, Yufei Wei, Rong Xiong, Yue Wang

entry.summary: PathTime-VLA decouples geometric path from execution timing in VLA policies by representing motion as a progress-indexed interaction path plus a monotone time profile, importing path-time parameterization from classical motion planning into learned action representations. This enables post-training factorization so teleoperation data's timing artifacts can be separated from useful geometric guidance.

entry.title: DivMoE: Fine-Grained MoE Upcycling via Cross-Domain Expert Composition

author.name: Yuxuan Lou, Kai Yang, Geng Zhang, Yong Liu, Yang You

entry.summary: The paper identifies a structural pathology in fine-grained MoE upcycling from dense models: naive routing collapses and accuracy drops to near-random (e.g., 23.2% on Qwen3-1.7B versus 50.2% for coarse-grained upcycling). DivMoE addresses this via cross-domain expert composition, making sparse upcycling from pre-trained dense checkpoints viable at fine granularity.

entry.title: Estimating great expectations under autoregressive language models with potentials

author.name: Francesco I. Re, Shubhangi Ghosh, Tim Vieira, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: This paper shows how to efficiently estimate expectations of test functionals under autoregressive LMs by exploiting next-token conditional probabilities obtained as a by-product of sampling. Using additive prefix-decomposed potentials, the authors construct estimators with controllable variance, derive variance-reduction conditions, and demonstrate substantial variance reductions across applications.

entry.title: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin

author.name: Yuan Tian, Bing Hu, Hao Wang, Binghang Lu, Fang Wu

entry.summary: The paper empirically separates gains from harness evolution (around a frozen model) versus weight training by crossing seed and evolved harnesses with base and trained weights, and classifies failures as process failures (repairable by the harness) or content failures (requiring weight training). This failure composition indicates when harness evolution has hit its ceiling and weight training should begin.

entry.title: Cited but Not Consulted: A Counterfactual Audit of Legal Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness

author.name: Saisab Sadhu, Shreeyans Arora, Pratinav Seth

entry.summary: Holding case facts fixed, the authors substitute named legal authorities with unrelated ones and decode verdicts from hidden states to test whether legal citations actually cause LLM verdicts. Across seven open-weight models, models name the correct authority 66.7-100% of the time, but verdicts change only 0-50% depending on the benchmark, revealing shallow citation faithfulness.

entry.title: NavGPT-3: Harnessing Context in a Hierarchical Navigation Runtime

author.name: Gengze Zhou, Yicong Hong, Jiazhao Zhang, Xunyi Zhao, Jian Zhou, Zixing Lei, Zun Wang, Chongyang Zhao, Xionghui Chen, Stephen Gould, Anton van den Hengel, Qi Wu

entry.summary: NavGPT-3 connects LLM-based long-horizon agentic reasoning with low-latency action policies through an OS-like runtime where reasoning, acting, and monitoring run as scheduled threads with their own context, tools, and permissions. This allows the robot to react to sudden real-world events via interruption and thread switching while the LLM handles high-level goals.

entry.title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Haixuan Liu, Xingjian Su, Yong Liu, Zhi Chen, Yuxuan Wang, Jianmin Wang, Mingsheng Long

entry.summary: Timer-M1 is a pretrained multivariate time series foundation model built on the idea that time series share elementary temporal and relational primitives across domains. It uses a primitive-based data synthesis and pretraining pipeline combining generated and real series to improve zero-shot forecasting generalization in complex real-world scenarios.

entry.title: Optimally Pacing Budget Spending and Learning

author.name: Mark Braverman, Jingyi Liu, Jieming Mao, Jon Schneider, Eric Xue

entry.summary: The paper establishes near-optimal regret bounds for budget-constrained online learning against arbitrary classes of budget-pacing experts in the adversarial setting, giving a full-information algorithm with regret O(D sqrt(log F) + sqrt(T log F)) matching known lower bounds. The techniques extend to online resource allocation problems where the learner observes rewards and costs of available options, achieving O(D sqrt(log F)) bounds with fractional allocations.

entry.title: When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization

author.name: Fei Ding

entry.summary: This analysis identifies seven failure modes in interactions between reference-policy KL regularization and rewards in group policy optimization (as used in GRPO-style LLM post-training), including residual KL updates after reward clipping and KL concentration on few tokens. It proposes Zero-Sum Calibrated Policy Optimization (ZCPO), which uses conditional-KL-measured relative drift to calibrate within-group reward coefficients.

entry.title: HAND: A Biologically-Inspired Activation Function that Improves Generalisation and Sample Efficiency in Image Classification

author.name: Michael W. Spratling, Heiko H. Sch\"utt

entry.summary: HAND is a new activation function incorporating homeostasis, accelerating nonlinearity, and divisive normalisation as biologically-inspired inductive biases. On ImageNet1k, a ConvNeXt-tiny with HAND reached in 25 epochs the accuracy the unmodified model achieved in 200 epochs, indicating substantial sample and compute efficiency gains.

entry.title: VersaCamVLA: Camera-Configurable VLA Policies for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Boyao Han, Chen Shi, Jingjing Qian, ZhuoTan Tian, Li Jiang

entry.summary: VersaCamVLA addresses brittleness of vision-language-action models to camera configuration changes by decoupling camera-set representation from action learning. It learns a unified scene-token interface mapping arbitrary sets of posed RGB views into fixed-size latents, using multi-signal target-view prediction and Wrist-Augmented Pose Sampling that exploits wrist-camera motion for free pose diversity.

entry.title: DreamTrue: Action-Faithful Robot World Model with Counterfactual Post-Training

author.name: Junyan Li, Ruizhi Li, Yu Liu, Xiangshuo Liu, Mingchao Sun, Hongyu Pan, Mu Xu, Lue Fan, Zhaoxiang Zhang

entry.summary: DreamTrue is a multi-view, cross-embodiment robot world model for action-faithful, physically plausible video prediction. It tackles imprecise calibration via offline geometric alignment of rendered action conditions, and combats success bias in training data through counterfactual post-training that modifies recorded trajectories and generates videos under a wider range of actions and contacts.

entry.title: Reading the Room: Foundations, Design, and Challenges of Normative Competence in LLMs

author.name: Andrea Wynn (Nathan), Harsh Satija (Nathan), Seokhyun (Nathan), Baek, Anqi Liu, Eric Nalisnick, Gillian K. Hadfield

entry.summary: The paper introduces normative competence, the ability to discern a community's enforced norms from interaction alone without static pretraining knowledge, as a central alignment challenge. It presents a multi-agent community debate setting with synthetic norms to study this capability in isolation, including how agents detect and respond to community sanctioning.

entry.title: When Lower Reconstruction Loss Hurts: Distributionally Robust Refinement for Low-Bit LLM Quantization

author.name: Yanlong Zhao, Xiaoyuan Cheng, Huihang Liu, Baihua He, Xinyu Zhang, Harrison Bo Hua Zhu, Wenlong Chen, Li Zeng, Zhuo Sun

entry.summary: This paper challenges the standard assumption in weight-only post-training quantization that minimizing reconstruction loss on calibration data preserves model quality, showing lower reconstruction loss can even degrade performance when input activation distributions shift. It proposes Distributionally Robust Quantization (DRQ), a post-hoc refinement that minimizes worst-case reconstruction loss over a constrained set of distributions.

entry.title: SynCo: Data Synthesis Co-Training for Self-Evolving LLMs via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wei Yang, Shawn Li, Yuehan Qin, Yawei Wang, Mingxi Wang, Shixuan Li, Tiankai Yang, Jiate Li, Jesse Thomason, Xuezhe Ma, Yue Zhao

entry.summary: SynCo tackles the mismatch between a self-evolving LLM agent's changing capabilities and its static training data by co-training a data synthesis model alongside the agent via multi-agent reinforcement learning. This lets the training curriculum evolve with the agent, replacing trivial tasks and rescaling overly difficult ones to sustain self-improvement.

entry.title: Tracing the Thoughts of a Coding Agent Playing ARC-AGI-3: Lessons for Continual Learning

author.name: Chen Wu, Josh Passenger, Yin Song

entry.summary: The authors study continual learning by having a coding agent built on a frozen foundation model play ARC-AGI-3 interactive reasoning games, where all learning is externalized as Python scripts and text notes. Because the agent retains no hidden state, every belief revision leaves a traceable artifact, enabling a detailed analysis of how strategies form, fail, and transfer across levels.

entry.title: Where to Adapt Matters: Layer-Selective Fine-Tuning for Capability Retention

author.name: Zhiqiang Pang, Zihong Sun, Qi Xie, Jun Shu, Deyu Meng, Zongben Xu

entry.summary: Instead of mitigating fine-tuning-induced capability loss with data replay or regularization, the paper asks where adaptation should be applied, showing different transformer layers yield different target-task gains and capability degradation. It uses layer-wise empirical Fisher information to select layers, retaining general capabilities while fine-tuning.

entry.title: Where Draft Trees Lose Target Mass: Exit-Guided Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shijing Hu, Xuancheng Ren, Zhihui Lu, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: Analyzes tree-based speculative decoding through a target-flow view, proving an exit law showing that one plus target coverage bounds the expected output-block length of any exact path verifier, and showing all optimal verifiers share the same law. Builds on this to introduce Tree Exit Verification, an exact, level-parallel procedure that uses target feedback to improve both verification and tree construction.

entry.title: Structure Tax: How Structured Output affects LLMs Performance

author.name: Vineet Kumar, Kanishka, Bhuvanesh Mandora

entry.summary: Re-examines the assumed accuracy cost of constraining LLM outputs to JSON or XML, finding the structure tax depends on schema design rather than structure itself: reasoning-first field ordering matches or exceeds free-form accuracy while answer-first ordering causes steep drops, especially in smaller models. Schemas preserving reasoning order also improve calibration, with hidden-state geometry evidence via CKA.

entry.title: An Investigation of Model Coherence: Narrow Finetunes Contradict Themselves Under Resampling

author.name: Robert Graham, Yariv Barsheshat, Phil Blandfort, Sabri Alouache

entry.summary: This paper introduces a high-specificity coherence metric based on contradictions when resampling answers to the same question, using a curated set of 175 questions designed to exclude ambiguity or indifference as alternative explanations. It finds that narrowly finetuned models score poorly, exhibiting identity conflation, introspection failures, and rationalization in model organisms from the literature.

entry.title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot

author.name: Drew T. Nguyen, William Fithian

entry.summary: The authors recompute METR's 50% time-horizon estimates across 228 tasks and 26 AIs using splines and item-response theory, relaxing the assumption that AI task difficulty scales linearly with log human time. They find the human-time-to-difficulty conversion is nearly flat between 2-30 minutes and near-linear elsewhere, implying time-horizon jumps of equal multiplier differ greatly in difficulty.

entry.title: SpectralCache: Accelerating Diffusion-Based World Models via Spectral Feature Caching

author.name: Zhendong Mi, Pu Zhao, Ziyu Hu, Xiaodong Yu, Yanzhi Wang, Grace Li Zhang, Shaoyi Huang

entry.summary: Proposes SpectralCache, a training-free acceleration framework for diffusion-based world models that exploits stable singular subspaces and predictable singular-value evolution across adjacent denoising steps. By reusing subspaces and estimating only low-dimensional singular values, it reduces the heavy overhead of repeated Transformer evaluations during interactive environment generation.

entry.title: TestJack: Should you trust the results in coding benchmarks? Agentic Coding Benchmarks Auditing via Evaluator Evolution

author.name: Shuangjie Yao, Hao Wang, Koushik Sen, Simin Chen, Baishakhi Ray, Dawn Song

entry.summary: Presents TestJack, an auditing framework showing that coding benchmarks relying on fixed unit tests can be reward-hacked and can silently miss required behavior, so rising scores may reflect adaptation to the evaluator rather than better problem solving. Unlike static test augmentation, it models how real agent trials fail and evolves the evaluator to audit benchmark validity.

entry.title: MemoWM: How World Models Change What Agents Need to Remember

author.name: Bingfan Zeng, Zhisheng Chen, Chenbo Sang, Zhengwei Xie, Jinpeng Wang, Xiangchen Guan, Rui Qian, Zheng Lu, Jingwei Song

entry.summary: MemoWM formulates memory allocation conditioned on a world model, using shared predictions to compress retained experience and reconstruct omitted content, with a task-aware rule balancing reconstruction error against storage cost. Across five long-term agent-memory benchmarks it achieves 42.42% average accuracy, beating the strongest baseline by 2.62 points while reducing stored experience size.

entry.title: Stochastic Teacher Intervention for Agentic On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Junnan Liu, Linhao Luo, Zhijun Chen, Qianren Mao, Thuy-Trang Vu, Gholamreza Haffari

entry.summary: STI-OPD addresses a failure mode of on-policy distillation in multi-turn agentic tasks: student errors compound across turns, drifting trajectories away from the teacher's distribution and making token-level teacher supervision unreliable. The framework introduces stochastic teacher interventions during multi-turn interaction to keep supervision on-distribution.

entry.title: Language Modeling is Monotone Compression

author.name: Noam Mazor, Andrew Morgan, Rafael Pass

entry.summary: This work initiates a theoretical study of the empirical connection between LLM capability and compression ability, building on prior experimental results showing LLMs act as powerful compressors and that compression correlates with reasoning benchmark performance. The title suggests a provable result that language modeling corresponds to monotone compression, grounding the intelligence-as-compression hypothesis in formal theory. It is notable for bridging learning theory, information theory, and modern LLM behavior.

entry.title: From Geometry to Generalization: Why Row Normalization Can Beat Adam and Muon

author.name: Jihwan Kim, Dogyoon Song, Chulhee Yun

entry.summary: This theoretical optimization paper proves that row-wise normalization can achieve strictly higher population accuracy than full-batch Adam and exact-SVD Muon in high-dimensional multiclass classification, using an isotropic Gaussian-cloud data model. The key insight is that row normalization preserves population decision-boundary directions while Adam's coordinate-wise and Muon's spectral geometries introduce nonvanishing distortions. It offers a rare provable link between optimizer-induced classifier geometry and generalization.

entry.title: LTBD: Learnable Trust-Boundary Delimiters for Prompt Injection Defense

author.name: Luman Zhao, Minghui Xu, Yue Zhang, Yijun Yang

entry.summary: LTBD is a lightweight prompt injection defense that encodes trust boundaries via a small set of learnable delimiter tokens distinguishing trusted user instructions from untrusted external data, without changing LLM parameters. It targets the root cause identified as the absence of explicit trust-provenance representation, avoiding brittle handcrafted markers and full fine-tuning.

entry.title: Agentic-TTT: Training test-time policy for test-time training

author.name: Jiahao Lu, Mohan Kankanhalli

entry.summary: Agentic-TTT trains a policy that decides when test-time training is warranted, which TTT algorithm to invoke, and whether existing skills can be reused, since misapplied TTT can waste compute or degrade performance. This introduces agency into parameter-level self-improvement, letting models gate their own adaptation at deployment.

entry.title: Predicting Alignment Generalization with Value Representations

author.name: Andy Liu, Mehar Bhatia, Karolina Stanczak, Mona Diab, Vered Shwartz, Daniel Fried

entry.summary: The paper establishes the task of alignment generalization prediction: forecasting how fine-tuning a model toward one value changes behavior across many held-out values. The authors analyze 66 values from modern alignment targets and benchmark representational techniques for predicting these spillover effects.

entry.title: NEMORA: Neural Equivariant Multipole Operators for Long-Range Atomistic Learning

author.name: Jay L. Kaplan, Samuel Varner, Rebecca Willett, Juan J. de Pablo

entry.summary: Proposes NEMORA, an equivariant graph neural network for interatomic potentials that combines learnable long-range equivariant transport with multiscale many-body expressivity and linear cost. It addresses over-smoothing, over-squashing, and truncation limitations of cutoff-based message passing while preserving exact equivariance.

entry.title: Barron Optimal Transport I: Generative Modeling

author.name: Evan Dogariu, Joan Bruna

entry.summary: The authors introduce a framework for optimal measure transport where the transport cost captures neural network complexity, motivated by generative models that map a reference distribution to a target along ODEs or SDEs implemented as deep residual networks. Building on the kinetic formulation of optimal transport, the work asks for the most efficient neural representation implementing the transport. This connects optimal transport theory with practical generative modeling efficiency.

entry.title: Bridging KV-Cache Quantization and Linear Attention: From Theory to Pretrained Weight Migration

author.name: Kaicheng Xiao, Liran Dong, Haotian Li, Guoliang Xing

entry.summary: The paper identifies RAM-Net as a bridge between KV-cache quantization (per-entry compression retaining all entries) and linear attention (recurrent aggregation into a fixed-size state) via soft assignments over a discrete address space that drive recurrent updates to per-address slot states. This unified view of per-KV compression and multi-KV aggregation includes a path for migrating pretrained Transformer weights. It is conceptually relevant to efficient attention as models scale to longer contexts.

entry.title: SpatialOPSD: Self-Distilling Spatial Intelligence from Verified Coding Agent Traces

author.name: Rongxue Li, Meng Yang, Yiru Mao, Yongliang Tao, Lulu Hu, Bin Yang, Zhao Xu, Weihua Luo, Bowen Xu

entry.summary: SpatialOPSD is an on-policy self-distillation framework that internalizes a spatial coding agent's tool-verified reasoning into a standalone MLLM, enabling tool-free spatial intelligence. The key observation is that prompting an MLLM with summarized execution traces unlocks internal spatial chain-of-thought, which the framework then distills from verified agent traces. This removes prohibitive inference-time overhead and external tool dependencies of agentic spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Test-Time Compute for Tabular Foundation Models: Mechanisms, Gains, and Limits

author.name: Kanghui Ning, Marin Bilo\v{s}, James T. Wilson, Yilang Zhang, Kashif Rasul, Dongjin Song, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka

entry.summary: A systematic study of which forms of test-time compute improve pretrained tabular foundation models across adaptation, aggregation, and context construction, evaluated on TabArena and OpenML. It introduces DiagScale, a diagonal query-key similarity update training only 0.003-0.03% of parameters that matches full fine-tuning gains across three independently pretrained backbones.

entry.title: SplitJEPA: Learning Invariant and Variant Latent Worlds without Reconstruction

author.name: Ruijin Hua, Zichuan Liu, Zhuokai Zhao, Yujia Zheng

entry.summary: SplitJEPA extends joint-embedding predictive architectures to explicitly decompose latent states into invariant factors (shared across related observations) and variant factors, without any reconstruction objective. This addresses representation disentanglement in dynamical settings, e.g., a robot acting consistently under camera or lighting changes. It is the first result recovering invariant/variant structure within a reconstruction-free JEPA framework.

entry.title: Omni-Diffusion-Distill: Few-Step Distillation of Unified Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Hong Huang, Chenhongyi Yang, Junzhe Sun, Animesh Sinha, Wuyang Chen, Yifan Jiang

entry.summary: This work presents the first unified two-stage distillation framework for multimodal diffusion LLMs, compressing models that need tens to hundreds of decoding passes into efficient few-step students preserving both image generation and multimodal understanding. It aligns distillation of generation and understanding rather than treating them separately.

entry.title: Selective Listening: Mechanism-Guided Control of Audio Influence in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Yulin Sun, Kele Xu, Yong Dou

entry.summary: This paper studies how task-irrelevant audio can distort text reasoning in large audio-language models, introducing a paired drift analysis that reveals accuracy metrics can mask opposing audio-induced errors. The authors identify intervention-sensitive late audio pathways and propose ICAP-Gate, a mechanism-guided, task-conditioned control method that reduces influence rate and answer flips across four LALMs and multiple interference conditions.

entry.title: Minimax Gaussian Mechanisms for Continual Machine Unlearning

author.name: Qi Kuang, Yin Xia

entry.summary: This paper develops Gaussian noise mechanisms for Newton-update machine unlearning under sequential deletion requests, using Gaussian differential privacy and its adaptive composition to show released models are statistically hard to distinguish from exact retraining. It also derives error bounds for Newton approximations relative to full retraining to calibrate noise per release. This addresses a practically important privacy problem as deletion rights (e.g., GDPR) become routine.

entry.title: Sparse Attention Is Matrix Approximation, Not Choosing from a Bag of Values

author.name: Fang Wan, Xufeng Liu, Fan Li, Yi Liu

entry.summary: This paper argues that sparse attention methods for LLMs rest on a mathematically flawed view: keeping large scalar entries or high-mass regions treats the attention matrix as a bag of values, ignoring that entries jointly determine output through multiplication with value vectors. The authors reformulate sparse attention as structured matrix approximation. This conceptual reframing could improve the design of efficient attention methods for long prompts.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Machine Translation Quality Annotation: Humans and Models Are Both Challenged

author.name: Hala Almaghout, Christian Federmann, Qin Gao

entry.summary: This paper from Meta-affiliated researchers (Federmann, Gao) evaluates LLMs as alternatives to human judgment for machine translation quality evaluation using MQM and Error Span Annotation schemes. It tests agreement with human annotators across a long-context test set of 70 language pairs plus WMT23/WMT25 data, finding both humans and models struggle with the task.

entry.title: TRACE: Diagnosing Verifier Brittleness in Agentic Evaluation

author.name: Radhika Gaonkar

entry.summary: TRACE is a protocol that treats score changes in LLM agent evaluations as hypotheses to diagnose rather than verdicts: it perturbs one part of an evaluation, compares paired runs, and rescores unchanged trajectories to test whether the scoring rule itself caused the change. Controlled experiments show brittle effects, such as tool renaming lowering a scripted agent's score by 0.250 despite identical behavior.

entry.title: SAGE: Sink-Aware Guided Emphasis for Visual Grounding in Vision-Language Decoders

author.name: Jeonghyo Song, YoungJoon Yoo

entry.summary: SAGE investigates attention sinks in large vision-language model decoders and identifies a layer-dependent structure: early and late layers show prompt-invariant attention collapse onto the same image regions (Prompt-Invariant Sinks), while mid layers are prompt-conditioned and drive alignment. Building on this, the paper proposes a sink-aware guidance method to improve visual grounding and reduce hallucination. This contributes to the interpretability-driven reliability improvement of VLMs.

entry.title: LVSPM: Long Sequence View Synthesis and Pose Estimation Model

author.name: Xi Chen, Yachi Zhang, Linghao Chen, Minghua Liu, Hao Su, Zexiang Xu, Xiaoshuai Zhang

entry.summary: LVSPM jointly estimates camera poses and synthesizes novel views from uncalibrated image collections using test-time training layers to scale to hundreds of input views, trained with only RGB images and pose supervision without dense 3D ground truth. It surpasses VGGT in pose estimation across 16-256 views and achieves state-of-the-art pose-free novel view synthesis, even exceeding pose-dependent models in PSNR while remaining stable as scene scale grows. This advances practical large-scale 3D reconstruction from casual captures.

entry.title: BudgetPix: Compute-Adaptive Tokenization for Pixel-Space Image Diffusion

author.name: Ozgur Kara, Yujia Chen, Daniel Watson, David Forsyth, James Matthew Rehg, Wen-Sheng Chu, Du Tran

entry.summary: BudgetPix replaces uniform tokenization in pixel-space diffusion with an adaptive framework that allocates compute based on visual complexity, using an entropy-guided quadtree encoder producing variable-length token sequences with multi-scale patch embedding. This enables flexible inference-time compute budgets and better quality-cost trade-offs between plain backgrounds and intricate details.

entry.title: OneSearch-VL: Unified Multimodal Deep Research Agent for Image and Video

author.name: Hongyu Li, Manyuan Zhang, Kaituo Feng, Shu Chen, Dian Zheng, Hao Li, Hao Yu, Zhangquan Chen, Zoey Guo, Ray Zhang, Shaofei Huang, Tianrui Hui, Linjiang Huang, Si Liu

entry.summary: OneSearch-VL is a unified agent for image and video deep research built around a Visually Grounded Evidence Graph that encodes dependencies among visual anchors, entity relations, and source-supported facts for data construction, process supervision, and evaluation. The VGEG-based data engine yields SFT datasets (110K) and additional trajectory data for training the agent.

entry.title: Dex-One2Many: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Human Demonstration

author.name: Jusuk Lee, Sungha Kim, Yeonsoo Park, Jonguk Cheon, Yoonkyo Jung, Yongjun You, H. Jin Kim, Jia-Bin Huang, Furong Huang, Youngseok Jang, Seungjae Lee

entry.summary: Dex-One2Many is a real-to-sim-to-real framework that learns generalizable dexterous manipulation policies from a single human video, combining RL-based exploration with guidance from the demonstration. The key insight is to extract goals and constraints from the video rather than strictly matching demonstrated motions, enabling generalization to unseen object poses, goal poses, and grasps.

entry.title: USDCraft: Geometrically Grounded Programmatic Modeling of Articulated 3D Assets for Simulation

author.name: Chuanrui Zhang, Zaijia Yang, Duomin Wang, Lu Shi, Daquan Zhou, Ruihua Zhang, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: USDCraft formulates articulated 3D asset reconstruction as programmatic modeling, using a pretrained LLM to write and revise executable programs that produce simulation-ready articulated assets from partial geometric evidence. This targets real-to-sim transfer for manipulation when real-world meshes are incomplete or out-of-distribution.

entry.title: Tell Robot What Not to Do: A Negation Understanding Perspective

author.name: Fazeng Li, Gan Sun, Hao Cheng, Weihong Ren, Yang Cong

entry.summary: NegaAlign is a parameter-efficient, plug-and-play framework enabling pretrained VLAs to follow negated instructions - accomplishing goals while respecting explicit exclusions - using image-language supervision alone. It inserts Negation Transformation Layers into the vision-language backbone to reshape intermediate representations.

entry.title: OpenProblemBench: Benchmarking AI on Open Problems in the Foundational Theoretical Sciences

author.name: Zhiyi Li, Sihan Hu, Tianning Xiao, Xiansheng Cai, Xiaojun Tan, Youjin Deng, Kun Chen

entry.summary: OpenProblemBench comprises 82 unresolved problems from mathematics and theoretical physics with research context and prior progress, evaluated by four independent models assessing correctness, completeness, and progress without reference solutions. Across seven configurations, GPT-6-Astra achieved the strongest results among evaluated frontier models.

entry.title: Open-ended Scientific Discovery with Possibilistic Reasoning

author.name: Anita Yang, Siu Lun Chau, Tomoya Wakayama, Krikamol Muandet, Masaki Adachi

entry.summary: This work formalizes open-ended autonomous scientific discovery as Abductive Autonomous Scientific Discovery (AASD) using possibility theory, addressing the problem that the best found hypothesis may be the best of a bad lot while even background knowledge like physical laws may need revision. It introduces abductive utility as a computable progress measure and possibility frontier search as the first algorithm for AASD.

entry.title: Safe, Persistent, and Evolving Agent Harness for Understanding Partially Observable Worlds

author.name: Yisen Gao, Yue Guo, Qing Zong, Yiwen Guo, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: E-Ledger is a multi-agent harness combining a code approval layer that checks every proposed action against organizational policy with a world ledger of verified hidden rules and evidence-backed dynamic state. It also proposes WorldAbduct, an abductive method for inferring hidden rules under partial observability, targeting enterprise workflow requirements.

entry.title: Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks

author.name: Haoyu Zhao, Zhengxu Yu, Zhiyuan He, Meng Fang, Rasul Tutunov, Haitham Bou-Ammar, Weilin Luo, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Presents Memento 3, a framework where frozen LLM agents continually learn explicit world models by maintaining a natural-language rulebook of revisable hypotheses about environment dynamics, compiled into executable code for prediction and planning. A continual loop of observation, reflection, and rule revision lets the agent improve in unfamiliar environments while leaving unknowns underspecified.

entry.title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark

author.name: Christopher M. Stewart, Preston Botter, Natalie Sarabosing, Muye Zhang, Rachel Phinnemore, Shalini Ghosh, Hong Shen, Hoda Heidari

entry.summary: Using a construct-validity framework, the authors examine whether harmful refusal constitutes a single measurable attribute within HELM Safety's datasets and attribute structure. The work tests whether safety benchmark scores actually isolate the attributes they purport to measure, given that similar overall scores can hide very different attribute profiles.

entry.title: From Investigation Failures to Reliable SOC Agents: Understanding and Improving LLM-Based Alert Triage

author.name: Saimon Amanuel Tsegai (Daphne), Alex Kantchelian (Daphne), Danfeng (Daphne), Yao, Peng Gao

entry.summary: Studies why tool-using LLM agents fail at security operations center alert triage, comparing five reasoning strategies from single-pass tool use to explicit verification. The authors build ALERT-BENCH, an interactive benchmark replaying enterprise telemetry through a live SIEM, and find systematic investigation failures across 1,247 alerts in a multi-stage attack scenario.

entry.title: Can Jev be Your Q or Policy in Reinforcement Learning?

author.name: Yi Ma, Tianpei Yang, Yaodong Yang, Weixun Wang, Hongyao Tang

entry.summary: This paper examines whether Jev, a recently released decision model that returns calibrated typed answers in a single forward pass without generation, can serve as a Q-function or policy component in reinforcement learning. It analyzes fit requirements and evaluates how such a non-generative decision model improves RL sample efficiency and transfer, filling a gap between foundation-model-as-trainee and foundation-model-as-generator framings.

entry.title: When Routing Reveals Membership: Privacy Leakage from MoE Router Telemetry

author.name: Yixin Tan, Jiayang Liu, Lu Sun, Yuke Hu, Zheng Li, Rui Wen

entry.summary: Shows that router telemetry from Mixture-of-Experts language models, often logged for monitoring and debugging, enables membership inference attacks revealing whether an example was used for fine-tuning. A router-augmented attack combining output-side signals with aggregated routing features consistently outperforms conventional attacks across three MoE architectures and three data domains.

entry.title: Measuring and Mitigating Solution Mode Collapse in RLVR

author.name: Liv G. d'Aliberti, Marwa Abdulhai, Sofiia Druchyna, Peter Henderson, Manoel Horta Ribeiro

entry.summary: This work studies solution mode collapse in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR): because RLVR rewards only correctness, training can drive models to produce many copies of one correct answer while losing diverse alternative solutions. The authors introduce ModeBench, a benchmark of multi-solution tasks where verifiers report both correctness and solution mode, and use it to measure and mitigate how RLVR training erodes solution diversity, which matters for user choice and problem-solving capability.

entry.title: Memorization and Malign Generalization in Conditional Diffusion Models with Random Features

author.name: Gwangho Kim, Sungyoon Lee

entry.summary: The authors analyze a random-feature conditional score model in the high-dimensional proportional limit, deriving asymptotic training and test loss expressions for conditional diffusion models. They show that in the overparameterized regime, increasing width improves prediction of the condition-dependent mean while reducing within-condition variance, a phenomenon termed malign generalization, and characterize memorization via training loss decomposition. This extends memorization theory from unconditional to conditional diffusion settings.

entry.title: DataSense-Bench: The First Step Toward an AI Scientist

author.name: Yudi Zhang, Mingyu Cao, Lu Yin, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: DataSense-Bench evaluates whether frontier AI agents possess data sense: selecting and ranking training subsets to fine-tune a small LLM, with agents allowed to inspect data, write analysis code, and run forward passes but not train or see evaluation tasks. The benchmark measures data selection and performance forecasting as a component of AI-scientist and recursive-self-improvement claims.

entry.title: Safe at One Loop, Risky at Another: Aligning Safety Across Recurrent Depths in Looped Language Models

author.name: Yi Wang, Xiuyuan Qi, Dongqi Han, Dongsheng Li, Wenjie Wang

entry.summary: This paper evaluates the safety of Looped Language Models, which reuse shared parameters across recurrent inference steps, under jailbreak attacks targeting different recurrent depths. The authors find that attack success can increase at deeper inference depths, so the same query may behave differently depending on the readout depth. This exposes a novel safety alignment challenge specific to recurrent-depth architectures.

entry.title: PlanWAM: Planning-Shaped Future Representations for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jinchang Xu, Hongda Yu, Fengwei Dong, Wenhui Huang, Xi Wei, Yongzhi Liu, Sunan Zhang, Jirao Wang, Chen Lv, Bingbing Li, Guodong Yin, Weichao Zhuang

entry.summary: PlanWAM reframes world models for end-to-end autonomous driving by letting the planning task shape which future-state representation the latent world model predicts, using a Temporal Register Pyramid to compress history. The result is foresighted planning driven by future representations filtered for planning-relevant information.

entry.title: Language-Specific Effects of Tokenizer Choice in Multilingual Language Models

author.name: Clara Meister, G\"ul Sena Alt{\i}nta\c{s}, Antoine Bosselut

entry.summary: Training 123 language models spanning 54 tokenizers under controlled conditions, the authors show tokenizer choice matters more for languages with less language-model training data, with tokenizer effects on bits-per-byte varying substantially across languages. This quantifies trade-offs in finite multilingual vocabulary allocation.

entry.title: SpaceCast-Bench: Evaluating Predictive Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hongxing Li, Jinyue Su, Dingming Li, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: SpaceCast-Bench is the first benchmark targeting predictive spatial reasoning in VLMs, distinguishing it from static spatial perception via an observe-transform-infer framework with 3,862 questions from 182 real-world scenes across 16 task types at three difficulty levels. Evaluation reveals how models handle anticipating interventions and reasoning about unobserved outcomes. This addresses an important blind spot, since most spatial benchmarks test only perception of visible relations.

entry.title: Parametric Trajectory Distillation for Few-Step Video Generation

author.name: Lan Feng, Peter Karkus, Maximilian Igl, Julius Berner, Yuxiao Chen, Shuhan Tan, Alexandre Alahi, Boris Ivanovic, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: Introduces PTD, a few-step distillation method for video diffusion and flow models where the student parameterizes teacher trajectory segments as polynomials and learns from teacher guidance along its own predicted path, adapting learned curvature to the student's capacity. Strong author team from EPFL, NVIDIA, and other institutions.

entry.title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents

author.name: Jiawei Chi, Shangchen Miao, Zhiyuan Shi, Kailu Wu, Hanyang Wang, Weiliang Chen, Qiyu Dai, Jinshan Ren, Jun Gao, Mingsheng Long, Yueqi Duan, Jiangran Lyu, Jialong Wu, Fangfu Liu

entry.summary: AgentGarten couples simulators and game engines with a shared neural renderer to create faithful, realistic real-time interactive environments for agent training. Simulation backends maintain persistent world state and program-defined rules, while a neural renderer produces visual observations from structured conditions through a common interface, addressing the bottleneck of building diverse yet consistent worlds.

entry.title: CoCam4D: Geometry-Aware Cooperative 4D Perception for Camera-Only Autonomous Driving

author.name: Soham Pahari, Sudip Das, Arindam Das, Ujjwal Bhattacharya

entry.summary: CoCam4D is a Bayesian collaborative perception framework for camera-only autonomous driving that explicitly models monocular depth uncertainty. It uses a VGGT-based feedforward network to produce 3D Gaussian scene representations with uncertainty estimates, allowing multiple vehicles to fuse information coherently despite occlusions and blind spots.

entry.title: Acting from Belief, Looking When Needed: A Bayesian Spatial World Model for Navigation under Intermittent Perception

author.name: Feihong Yang, Xiang Long, Jincheng Yu, Jianfei Zhang, Guangjun Ge, Chao Wang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: ALONE is a Bayesian spatial world model enabling navigation under intermittent perception: the robot acts from an internal belief and re-observes only when needed, freeing a shared sensor for other tasks. Learned priors over common geometric structures let it infer unobserved structure from sparse observations.

entry.title: How Narrative Wrapping Affects LLM Refusal: A Cross-Language Benchmark and Defense

author.name: Zhankai Ye, Yanning Wang, Yukai Jin, Bo Mei, Fangyi Li, Wei Wang, Shangqian Gao, Xin Liu

entry.summary: The paper quantifies how narrative and role-play wrappers bypass safety training across languages, finding attack success rates up to 95.7 percent on Qwen3-1.7B with Classical Chinese wrappers. It introduces GUISE, a benchmark with parallel English, modern Chinese, and Classical Chinese requests and stricter success criteria, and shows harmful-request representations move little across languages.

entry.title: RaReCache: Bridging the Gap in Cross-Model KV Cache Reuse via Rank disagreement-based Selective Recomputation

author.name: Sreetama Sarkar, Saptarshi Mitra, Sitao Huang, Souvik Kundu, Peter A. Beerel

entry.summary: RaReCache enables KV-cache reuse across different models in LLM serving, addressing the problem that cache transfers degrade as the model-size gap widens. The key insight is that transfer failures concentrate in a small subset of information-dense tokens, which the system identifies via rank disagreement and selectively recomputes, avoiding full prefill after model switches.

entry.title: Fed-GRPO: Reward-Signal-Driven Federated Group Relative Policy Optimization

author.name: Pengxin Guo, Shuang Zeng, Zonggen Li, Weiying Zheng, Mengting Liu, Liangqiong Qu

entry.summary: Fed-GRPO extends GRPO-based reinforcement learning of LLMs to federated settings where raw training data cannot be shared, using reward statistics naturally produced during GRPO training as zero-cost signals to guide aggregation, local training, and communication. It targets privacy-constrained collaborative reasoning fine-tuning.

entry.title: Error-Propagation Modeling for Failure Attribution in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jiaqi Liao, Yuanzhao Zhai, Huanxi Liu, Xu Zhang, Zheming Zhuang, Dawei Feng, Bo Ding, Huaimin Wang

entry.summary: The paper defines the failure attribution target as the decisive error - the agent-step pair whose correction would recover the failed execution - and models how errors propagate across interactions in multi-agent LLM systems. Its approach distinguishes decisive errors from downstream symptoms, where prior suspicious-step methods fall short.

entry.title: What Output-Only Review Cannot Verify: Study Contracts for Research Agents

author.name: Eitan Waks, Ben Glocker

entry.summary: Proposes study contracts that bind declared experimental choices, run obligations, and claim scope to recorded execution evidence, distinguishing contract-relative verification from scientific truth. A diagnostic with clean/mutated study pairs shows a deterministic checker with registry access detects all registered mutations while LLM judges reviewing outputs alone miss most of them.

entry.title: RouterInterp: Understanding Superposed Specialisation in Mixture of Experts Routing

author.name: Ilya Lasy, Nora Yinuo Cai, Kola Ayonrinde

entry.summary: Challenges the hypothesis that MoE experts specialize in single coherent domains, proposing instead the Superposed Specialisation Hypothesis: experts specialize in disjoint unions of fine-grained features. RouterInterp uses sparse autoencoder features to interpret routing decisions, providing a more successful interpretability approach for MoE models than domain-based assumptions.

entry.title: When Should Agents Think? Adaptive Reasoning via Cross-Turn Estimation

author.name: Yiruo Cheng, Shen Huang, Xiaoshuai Song, Jiejun Tan, Guanting Dong, Pengjun Xie, Ji-Rong Wen, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Tackles when LLM agents need new reasoning versus when earlier reasoning suffices, showing that the drop in likelihood of subsequent reference actions after removing additional reasoning tracks action recoverability. This yields a lightweight, generation-free signal for deciding across turns whether a new reasoning step is needed, cutting unnecessary computation.

entry.title: Accurate but Not Humble: Evaluating Epistemic Humility in LLM Agents under Knowledge Conflict

author.name: Kaiser Sun, Bernal Jimenez Gutierrez, Hongjun Liu, Jingyu Zhang, Jie Gao, Mark Dredze, Daniel Khashabi

entry.summary: The paper proposes evaluating LLM agents on epistemic humility, operationalized through Identify, Solve, and Escalate behavioral dimensions, in knowledge-conflict situations where retrieved evidence contradicts parametric knowledge or where contextual sources disagree. It tests whether agents revise answers, acknowledge uncertainty, or persist incorrectly.

entry.title: Certified Corruption Budgets: Anytime-Valid Leaderboard Claims under Adaptive Rigging

author.name: Hamed Khosravi, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: Introduces certified corruption budgets, a statistical framework that publishes a tolerance alongside each pairwise leaderboard claim so that, with probability at least 1-alpha, the claim is simultaneously correct at all times or more records were corrupted than the budget. The guarantees hold against adaptive attackers who observe every published certificate with an unbounded corruption budget.

entry.title: RFChipAgent: Multi-Agentic AI Flow for Analog/RF Chip Design

author.name: Awani Khodkumbhe, Yunfei Feng, Raj Rangarajan, Kevin Wang, Kamal Sahota

entry.summary: RFChipAgent is a multi-agent LLM flow for end-to-end analog/RF circuit design automation, combining multimodal RAG over engineering documentation, task orchestration across specialized agents, and human supervision. It targets a labor-intensive chip design domain facing pressure from Wi-Fi 7 and 6G standards.

entry.title: REMORY: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction

author.name: Hanchen Xia, Baoyou Chen, Yutang Ge, Naihao Deng, Senqiao Yang, Zilong Dong, Weihao Yuan, Siyu Zhu

entry.summary: REMORY is a neural memory network that supplements textual history summaries with a bounded sequence of learned soft memory tokens, trained to help a frozen LLM approximate its full-context continuation; the tokens act like a residual connection along the sequence dimension. On SummHay it approaches full-context joint scores using only 5.2% of input positions while improving source attribution. This is a promising direction for long-horizon agents operating under finite context windows.

entry.title: Zatom-2: Multitask Pretraining on Atomistic Data for Generative Modeling across Domains

author.name: Miruna Cretu, Alex Abrudan, Antonia Panescu, Tynan Perez, Rishabh Anand, N. Benjamin Erichson, Michael W. Mahoney, Samuel Blau, Joseph Jacobson, Rafael G\'omez-Bombarelli, Rex Ying, Tuomas Knowles, Pietro Li\`o, Alex Morehead

entry.summary: Zatom-2 is an atomistic generative model pretrained on roughly five million structures from the OMol25 and OMat24 electronic-structure datasets, aiming to unify chemistry, materials science, and biology modeling. It pairs a multiscale Transformer with conditional flow matching and supports force conditioning, bridging data-rich chemical domains and data-scarce biological contexts. The work targets general-purpose pretraining across organic and inorganic data, which prior specialized generative approaches lacked.

entry.title: One Skill Too Many: How Co-Installed Skills Conflict in Coding Agents

author.name: Chaoliang Yan, Zihao Xu, Yuekang Li, Shangzhi Xu, Yi Liu, Gelei Deng, Siqi Ma

entry.summary: This is the first empirical study of conflicts between co-installed agent skills, where similar skills from independent sources cause models to lose core functions like git-safety restrictions because a similarly named skill runs instead. Mining 20,947 repositories yielded 822,109 candidate similar-skill pairs, and the paper shows task-completion benchmarks miss these silent failures.

entry.title: Humanoid World Action Model With Joint State--Action Generation

author.name: Yan Yang, Jikun Rong, Minzhao Zhu, Zheyi Zhao, Qirui Hu, Zihan Lan, Weixin Mao, Yinhao Li, Zhen Fu, Hua Chen

entry.summary: The paper addresses the action-execution gap in hierarchical humanoid systems, where VLA or World Action Model reference actions diverge from motions realized through whole-body control and dynamics. It jointly models realized body state alongside future visual prediction so that the policy can account for the discrepancy between commanded and executed motion.

entry.title: Distilling Routed 3D Privilege for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hongxing Li, Yixin Li, Dingming Li, Zixuan Wang, Yuchen Yan, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: GPD improves spatial reasoning in vision-language models via geometry-privileged on-policy self-distillation, rendering depth, semantic, and bird's-eye-view cues as compact text privileges during training while requiring none at inference. It targets perception-stage spatial errors rather than supervising only final answers with outcome rewards.

entry.title: LeWAM: A JEPA World Action Model with Diffusion-Steering-Based MPC

author.name: Shashank Hegde, Alexander Popov, Elie Aljalbout, Nikolai Smolyanskiy

entry.summary: LeWAM is a bidirectional transformer trained end-to-end on forward, backward, inverse dynamics, and policy prediction over a decoder-free JEPA latent, combined with diffusion-steering-based MPC for control. Benefits include latents that better encode robot and object state while ignoring visual distractors compared to reconstruction-based world action models.

entry.title: Learning infinite context windows in recurrent architectures via spatial neural computing

author.name: Aleix Salvador-Pomarol, Arthur N. Montanari, Earl K. Miller, Adilson E. Motter, Jorge Cort\'es

entry.summary: Introduces a second-order recurrent model replacing neuron-to-neuron communication with a spatially evolving field governed by discretized PDEs, inspired by cortical waves in the brain. The model is equivalent to a structured infinite-order RNN, using spatiotemporal field patterns as implicit high-capacity memory for long-range dependencies while retaining constant memory.

entry.title: Spectrally Targeted Muon

author.name: Vishrut Goyal, Rohan Ramkumar

entry.summary: The Muon optimizer orthogonalizes update matrices by setting all singular values to one, but it is unclear whether its success stems from amplifying small singular directions or suppressing large degenerate ones. Spectrally Targeted Muon orthogonalizes only singular values above or below a threshold tau, interpolating between normalized SGD and Muon without requiring SVD, using Newton-Schulz iteration on a shifted Gram matrix. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and NanoGPT isolate which spectral mechanism drives Muon's effectiveness.

entry.title: Do Flatter Minima Drive Better Generalization? An Algorithmic Separation in Grokking

author.name: Mohnish Harwani

entry.summary: Using grokking as a testbed, this work examines whether flat loss landscapes causally drive generalization rather than merely correlating with it. The author finds that biasing training toward flatter solutions with sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) is insufficient to reliably induce the transition to generalization, providing an algorithmic separation between flatness and generalization. This challenges recent claims that flatness is a necessary geometric condition for grokking.

entry.title: Sample-Efficient Generative Conformal Prediction

author.name: Minxing Zheng, Shixiang Zhu

entry.summary: CASA improves generative conformal prediction by adaptively allocating a sampling budget across inputs: it characterizes the marginal value of an additional sample and distributes samples to minimize expected set size while maintaining coverage. This addresses the waste of uniform per-input sampling, where simple response distributions are oversampled and complex ones under-covered. The method matters where samples are expensive, such as diffusion models and scientific simulators.

entry.title: Early Signatures of Memorization in Diffusion Models via Basin Geometry and Cyclic Denoising

author.name: Nikhil Verma, Siddharthan Dileep, Anoop Singh, Srikanth Sastry, Ramya Hebbalaguppe, Sayan Ranu, N. M. Anoop Krishnan

entry.summary: Shows that memorization in diffusion models is encoded in the geometry of the learned energy landscape before any near-copies are generated, introducing the notion of latent memorization detected via score divergence, basin volume, and cyclic denoising probes. Basin onset follows the same O(n) scaling as memorization time. This enables auditing a released diffusion model before its outputs visibly reproduce training data.

entry.title: Training on the Future: A Delay-Aware Audit of Test-Time Adaptation for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Mohamed Readh Fentazi, Mazene Ameur, Adlen Ksentini

entry.summary: The authors build a leakage-free harness enforcing that H-step forecast labels are only available H steps (plus pipeline delay) later, then re-evaluate four recent test-time adaptation methods (TAFAS, COSA, PETSA, DynaTTA) on their own backbones across five benchmarks. They also introduce closed-form correctors, including recursive least squares filter banks, as strong references.

entry.title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization

author.name: Hanyang Li, Shao Tang, Daniel Thomas Braithwaite, Gregory Dexter, Leonardo Neves, Aman Gupta, Hiroto Udagawa, Abhishek Shivanna, Daniel Silva, Rohan Ramanath

entry.summary: This work redesigns 4-bit quantization of AdamW optimizer states by changing the rounding space: quantizing in preconditioner space rather than state space. The authors show analytically that small state-space error does not imply small preconditioner error near zero, motivating a Zero-Inclusive Preconditioner-space rounding scheme. Since optimizer states dominate persistent memory in large-scale training, this directly reduces training storage/communication cost.

entry.title: V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention

author.name: Hao Jiang, Yiru Mao, Tianpeng Bu, Hao Zhou, Hongtao Duan, Wang Jing, Bowen Xu, Xin Chen, Lulu Hu, Bin Yang, Yongliang Tao, Minying Zhang

entry.summary: V-CoLA is a training-free vision token compression framework designed for vision-language models with hybrid linear attention architectures, such as Qwen3.5-style models, where prior softmax-attention compression methods degrade. The paper analyzes why attention- and similarity-based compression fails in the linear attention regime and proposes a tailored alternative.

entry.title: CAPABLE: Capability-Aware Policy Adaptation via Behavioral Latent Encoding

author.name: Mohammad Khoshnazar, Mohammad Dehghani Tezerjani, Deyuan Qu, Zhiyuan Gao, Yanxiang Zhan, Jeroen Schafer, Andrew Melnik, Qing Yang, Michael Beetz

entry.summary: CAPABLE enables frozen vision-language-action policies to adapt when joint faults change how commanded actions are physically executed, without task-specific retraining, fault labels, or privileged embodiment information. It infers capability online from command-response history and kinematics using a temporal encoder and Jacobian-based analysis, combined with residual reinforcement learning. This targets a real robustness gap in deployed VLA systems.

entry.title: WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Zheyu Fan, Yue Zhang, Mingkai Deng, Kangrui Wang, Qineng Wang, Canyu Chen, Jie Hao, Xing Fan, Chenlei Guo, Eric P. Xing, Mohit Bansal, Manling Li

entry.summary: WOVEN hypothesizes that MLLM failures in spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal reasoning share a root deficit in visual transition reasoning, and provides both a training data source and benchmark organizing transition supervision by scene, action, and reasoning type. It tests whether this capability is a reusable training primitive learnable from heterogeneous supervision. This matters as a systematic attempt to improve world modeling in multimodal LLMs rather than patching tasks one by one.

entry.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing

author.name: Tianyu Fu, Tengxuan Liu, Ruoxi Wang, Yixin Dong, Yi Ge, Yichen You, Yu Wang

entry.summary: TokenRouter is a serving system for token-level LLM routing that addresses step desynchronization, batch admission delays, and developer complexity in existing single-LLM-assumption systems. It aims to realize the efficiency and quality gains that algorithmic work has shown fine-grained token routing can deliver over query-level routing.

entry.title: Chronos Enables Code Agents to Reason over Software Evolution

author.name: Xin Yin, Yiang Zhang, Zhiyuan Peng, Chao Ni, Zhe Cui, Xiaohua Xin

entry.summary: Chronos is a test-time memory framework for LLM-based code agents that distills merged pull requests into structured experience cards connected through a typed graph of code-level, developer-intent, and organizational relations, with semantic search and weighted multi-hop expansion for retrieval. This lets agents exploit repository history when generating and selecting patches. It addresses a real gap: most coding agents ignore the design decisions encoded in historical changes.

entry.title: Learning to Retrieve: Internalizing Memory Retrieval for Video World Models

author.name: JiaKui Hu, Tailai Chen, Yuqi Pan, Xuerui Qiu, Jialun Liu, Xiao Cao, Zhenxin Zhu, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Bing Wang, Yanye Lu

entry.summary: Proposes internalizing memory retrieval into the generative dynamics of video world models, so that the model intrinsically learns when and what historical information to retrieve, instead of relying on external memory systems bolted on to reduce scene drift during long-horizon camera-trajectory-conditioned generation. This addresses 3D-consistent long video generation.

entry.title: Reasoning-Informed Visual Editing

author.name: Xue Yang, Peiyuan Zhang, Yilun Zhu, Qihao Yang, Mingxin Liu, Xiangyu Zhao, Ziqian Fan, Zhaokai Wang, Yan Li, Yifan Yang, Xu Yang, Xiaosong Jia, Yue Zhou, Zhihang Zhong, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: The authors present RISEBench and its extended version RISEBench++, the first benchmarks for evaluating reasoning-informed visual editing, with a hierarchical taxonomy spanning temporal, causal, spatial, logical, counterfactual, and hybrid reasoning across multi-turn edits. This targets documented weaknesses of large multimodal models in complex instruction editing and appearance consistency.

entry.title: WorldCast: Distributed Multiplayer World Models

author.name: Ziyang Ye, Junchao Huang, Evelyn Zhang, Zhihao Xie, Ruicheng Zhang, Boyao Han, Litao Ban, Ziye Wang, Xinting Hu, Shaoshuai Shi, Zhuotao Tian, Li Jiang

entry.summary: WorldCast presents a distributed architecture for multiplayer world models where each player runs a local video generator and state model, exchanging player states projected into camera-aligned state fields that guide rendering of other players. This avoids the cost scaling of joint multi-view generation while maintaining consistent shared-environment representations.

entry.title: OmniDex: Scaling Dexterous Hand Grasping to Diverse Cluttered Scenes

author.name: Naiyu Fang, Zhongjin Luo, Yuxin Mo, Siyuan Huang, Jianbo Liu, Yufei Liu, Zheyuan Zhou, Chenkai Jin, Xiaogang Wang, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: OmniDex delivers a large-scale simulation benchmark for dexterous grasping in cluttered scenes, using a scalable seed-and-filter strategy to curate over 2.6 million scenes with 0.4 billion scene-specific grasp ground truths plus semantic and geometric observations. This tackles the data scarcity bottleneck for learning robust grasping in realistic clutter.

entry.title: SuperNav: An Agentic Navigation System for Any Task in Any Scene

author.name: Jinkai Zhang, Jingyi Xu, Yuanhong Yu, Jiarui Guo, Ruizhen Hu, Hujun Bao, Xiaowei Zhou, Sida Peng

entry.summary: SuperNav is an agentic robot navigation system that lets a pretrained multimodal LLM handle request interpretation, scene understanding, and decision-making while delegating motion execution to specialized navigation tools via an agent harness. This design preserves the MLLM's general capabilities instead of overfitting them to navigation training data.

entry.title: RAGNAROK: Radar-Aided Gravity-Normalized Alignment for Robust Open Keyframe-based Radar-Visual-Kinematic-Inertial SLAM

author.name: Hanjun Kim, Chiyun Noh, Sangwoo Jung, Jaehyung Jung, Simon Boche, Cedric Le Gentil, Stefan Leutenegger, Ayoung Kim

entry.summary: RAGNAROK is presented as the first radar-visual-kinematic-inertial SLAM system designed for legged robots in challenging environments, combining slip- and rolling-contact-aware leg velocity estimation, a kinematics-aware radar factor, degradation-aware image enhancement, and B-spline trajectory representation. It targets robust state estimation where proprioceptive-only estimators drift in rough terrain.

entry.title: PLaW-VLA: Predictive Latent World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Yu Liu, Hetian Guo, Tianlv Huang, Ziyi Cai, Wudi Chen, Hantang Wang, Qiutong Liu, Yingzhi Peng, Wei Han, Peijun Tang, Jianan Wang, Zipei Fan, Zhiyuan Zha, Xuan Song

entry.summary: PLaW-VLA augments vision-language-action policies with predictive latent world modeling: it predicts task-relevant future states in a pretrained prediction-oriented representation space and conditions action generation on observation history, task semantics, and predicted futures via structured causal attention in a Mixture-of-Transformers. It reports large gains, including +11.8 percentage points over reactive policies on RoboTwin Hard Horizon III.

entry.title: Reviewing failure modes in science as we prepare for AI researchers

author.name: Jason Fantl

entry.summary: Jason Fantl catalogs roughly 50 documented failure modes in science, from p-hacking and the file drawer problem to shallow peer review, and predicts how each will change with fully autonomous AI researchers. Most failures worsen, since AI enables more experiments (more statistically lucky results), correlated errors across model copies, and higher reward-hacking-driven misconduct, while tedious-work failures like citation-checking improve. The author argues for replication requirements and preparation before the wave of AI-driven research arrives.

entry.title: StoreBench: A Live-Commerce Environment for Evaluating and Training Autonomous Operator Agents

author.name: Daksh Raghuvanshi, Ved Vedere, Yifan Wang

entry.summary: StoreBench is a live-commerce RL environment where an agent runs an online apparel store on a production-grade commerce backend, contending with continuous customer orders, supplier repricing, and market shocks through 29 merchant tools. It tests long-horizon planning and economic judgment under a windowed operation budget.

entry.title: Workerville: Towards an Organizational Behavior Account of Agent Safety

author.name: Hanjun Luo, Junting Mao, Yuhan Lu, Haobo Zhang, Zhimu Huang, Yankai Chen, Hanan Salam, Xue Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes organizational behavior (OB) theory as a framework for studying LLM agent safety, unifying influences such as user instructions, peer messages, and long-term memory into a single relational structure. It formalizes counterproductive work behavior (CWB) for agents, a safety-relevant construct from organizational psychology.

entry.title: Probability-Signature Dynamics: Unpacking Modular Addition Learning Within Two-Layer Networks

author.name: Yunji Wang, Junjie Yao, Linyu Liu, Pinyan Lu, Zhi-Qin John Xu

entry.summary: Explains why networks trained on modular addition develop Fourier-structured circuits by introducing probability signatures — leading gradient interactions expressed through conditional statistics of the training distribution. These signatures are diagonalized by the discrete Fourier transform, yielding approximately decoupled Fourier-mode dynamics that explain frequency matching, phase alignment, and Fourier sparsity.

entry.title: OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport

author.name: Babak Barazandeh, Connor Swanson, Chinmay Kulkarni, Nikhil Mungel

entry.summary: OnTrack is a streaming monitoring mechanism that compares an agent's steps and dependencies against recorded successful runs using structure-aware optimal transport, alerting users or blocking the agent in about a millisecond per step. It avoids the cost and latency of a safeguard agent per step and the post-hoc nature of log evaluation.

entry.title: SWE-Journey: Towards More Realistic Evaluation of Coding Assistants through Long-Horizon, Multi-Turn Interaction
