author.name: Hexuan Deng, Yue Wang, Wenyu Jiang, Cheng Yang, Haolin Yang, Zhaohua Zhang, Chenchen Zhao, Beiduo Chen, Muxi Chen, Sa Zhu, Geyuan Zhu, Jianhuan Zhuo, Qiuyong Xiao, Tianwen Jiang, Jihong Zhang, Xuebo Liu

entry.summary: SWE-Journey is a benchmark for evaluating coding assistants like Claude Code and Codex under more realistic conditions: a weak-to-strong synthesis pipeline automatically constructs long-horizon coding tasks, and four user personas mined from real interactions address the multi-turn clarification and adaptation gap. This targets the mismatch between existing short-horizon, single-turn benchmarks and actual assistant use in evolving repositories.

entry.title: Same Outcome, Different Evidence: Intent Recovery in LLM Safety Evaluation

author.name: Haitong Jiang, Chunlin Liu, Sihan Tang, Chan Wu, Xiaoqing Su, Yuhong Feng

entry.summary: This paper argues that attack success rate alone obscures why a model avoids harm, and pairs ASR with an operative understanding rate measuring whether a response identifies and engages the evaluated task. The paired view reveals substantial hidden variation across interfaces, especially under intent-obscuring prompts where low ASR may reflect failure to recover the task rather than safety.

entry.title: VINCIE-NExT: Unlocking Video Editing from Images via In-Context Modeling

author.name: Leigang Qu, Feng Cheng, Ziyan Yang, Bangbang Yang, Zhaoyang Huang, Wei Chow, Yicong Li, Wenjie Wang, Tat-Seng Chua, Yan Zeng

entry.summary: VINCIE-NExT transfers video editing capability from mature image editing by decomposing video editing into a composable chain of sub-tasks (Video to Image to Image to Video) routed through in-context visual demonstrations. This avoids the need for expensive paired video-editing triplets by leveraging abundant image-editing pairs for scalable joint training.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Egocentric World Model with Fine-Grained Embodied Interaction

author.name: Dahyun Chung, Siyoon Jin, Hyunwook Choi, Honggyu An, Junyoung Seo, Hyunsung Kim, Seung Wook Kim, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: This work formulates multi-agent egocentric world modeling, where multiple agents interact through fine-grained embodied actions in a shared environment, requiring cross-view action consistency and consistent propagation of interaction-induced state updates. It extends prior single-agent or coarse-command world models toward realistic multi-agent embodied settings.

entry.title: Amortized Off-Policy Evaluation for LLMs

author.name: Younwoo Choi, Leo Feng, Vincent Liu, Haanvid Lee

entry.summary: Proposes PFN-OPE, a prior-data fitted network for amortized off-policy evaluation of LLMs that handles both policy shift from post-training and reward definition shift under continual deployment. Unlike classical per-task OPE, it reuses learning across new logged datasets and reward definitions without fitting from scratch.

entry.title: QUILT: Rethinking Sparse-Attention Prefill through Shared Query Execution

author.name: Zhenduo Zhao, Qihui Zhou, Mingcong Song, Zhiyi Chen, Chuangguan Ye, Fengfan Hou, Zequn Gong, Jing Li, Hongjie Si, Guoping Long

entry.summary: QUILT is a workload-aware sparse-attention execution mechanism that exploits substantial overlap in KV entries selected by neighboring queries, jointly processing queries and reusing shared KV entries to cut redundant memory traffic and computation during long-context prefill. Its Shift-and-Compare Set Decomposition transforms irregular set operations into regular data-parallel primitives and is pipelined with attention computation, targeting modern accelerators.

entry.title: NP-Hardness of Minimizing Neurons in Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Neural Networks

author.name: Sangrock Lee

entry.summary: This paper proves that computing the minimum number of hidden neurons needed for a two-hidden-layer ReLU network to approximate a target function within Lp tolerance is NP-hard, for all fixed dimensions and 1 <= p < infinity. The result holds even for rational ReLU network targets that are nonnegative, compactly supported, Lipschitz, and piecewise affine, via a 3-SAT reduction that produces an architecture gap. This resolves a fundamental complexity question in neural architecture optimization.

entry.title: What can linear attention learn from nonlinear teachers in-context?

author.name: Mary Letey, Arman Rysmakhanov, Yue M. Lu, Cengiz Pehlevan, Jacob Zavatone-Veth

entry.summary: The paper extends theory of in-context learning in linear attention from linear regression to nonlinear single-index targets, proving a nonlinearity-noise equivalence: linear attention extracts only the linear Hermite component of the target function, with remaining nonlinear structure acting as effective noise. This lets linear-attention theory transfer to nonlinear tasks and illuminates finite-pretraining-data behavior. Strong theory team including Pehlevan, Zavatone-Veth, and Lu.

entry.title: Smoothing the Top-k Exposure Boundary for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Yunkai Chai, Tong Zhu, Xiaoye Qu, Xuyang Hu, Guanjie Chen, Qipeng Guo, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: The paper identifies the brittle boundary created by static top-k expert routing in sparse MoE models, where competitive experts are arbitrarily split between supervision and zero-feedback zones. Elastic Expert Routing stochastically samples the active expert budget around k, softening the hard threshold into a gradual distribution over training.

entry.title: FastBench: Can Streaming VLMs Perceive High-Dynamic Real-World Streams?

author.name: Yuxuan Hu, Weikang Shi, Yang Bo, Xudong Lu, Xintong Guo, Shuhan Li, Yuyang He, Huankang Guan, Peiwen Sun, Yunqiao Yang, Wenbo Li, Rui Liu, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: FastBench evaluates high-dynamic perception in streaming video LLMs, where models with bounded context must trade off temporal history, spatial resolution, and temporal granularity, and 1-2 FPS sampling misses fast events. The benchmark uses a rigorous trajectory-grounded pipeline including SAM3 and CoTracker3 answer verification and three rounds of human inspection, producing 306 carefully validated QA pairs across eight domains and three temporal scopes. It exposes weaknesses of current streaming VLMs on fast real-world events.

entry.title: WorldAlign: Decoupled 4D Reward for World-Consistent Video Generation

author.name: Jing He, Kaixin Ding, Xingye Tian, Guibao Shen, Wenhang Ge, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan, Ying-Cong Chen

entry.summary: WorldAlign introduces a decoupled 4D reward framework for post-training video generation models toward world consistency, separately assessing static consistency (coherent 3D structure across viewpoints) and dynamic consistency (plausible subject motion and appearance over time). This addresses the static-scene assumption and unreliable feedback in existing geometry-aware post-training methods.

entry.title: WARP-VLA: Wrist-Camera Adaptation for View-Robust Policy Execution in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Junmyeong Lee, Dongmin Shin, Min-Gyu Park, Wooseok Jeon, Inho Chang, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: WARP-VLA makes vision-language-action models robust to variation in wrist-camera mounting configurations, which typically disrupt fine-grained geometric cues at deployment. It uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture where experts learn view-specific feature transformations and a router combines them based on the observed camera setup.

entry.title: From Solo to Ensemble: A Hierarchical Framework for Composable Multi-Agent Human-Object Interaction

author.name: Zekai Deng, Kangyi Chen, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang

entry.summary: This work converts single-agent physics-based human-object interaction policies into reusable Object-oriented Motion Skills via a hierarchical framework, distilling task-specific teachers into low-level skills and enabling multi-agent cooperative manipulation across object geometries, interaction types, and team sizes without task-specific fine-tuning.

entry.title: Control-Ready Uncertainty for Trajectory Diffusion

author.name: Zhiwei Xue, Jia Yue Kam, Jinhang Qiu, Yifeng Cheng, Ege Gursoy, Jiaming Wang, Vincent Bonnet, Harold Soh

entry.summary: SCOPE augments diffusion trajectory models with cheap, calibrated uncertainty: it distills score-curvature information into a structured precision matrix around each nominal trajectory, producing per-timestep Gaussian covariance tubes without Monte Carlo sampling. These uncertainty tubes support real-time risk assessment, collision avoidance, and control integration.

entry.title: Plan-and-Patch: Diffusion Language Models for Agentic Planning

author.name: Syamantak Kumar, Jiang Guo, Hassan Hamad, Hideo Kobayashi, Yi Xiang, Yezhou Yang, Yanjun Qi, Daniele Bonadiman, Jiarong Jiang

entry.summary: Plan-and-Patch is a plan-and-act framework where a diffusion language model generates plans and repairs only the affected regions of invalidated plans, conditioned on preserved prefix and suffix structure, rather than regenerating the whole plan. This enables targeted plan revision for long-horizon agentic tasks.

entry.title: Harness Compilation: Which Decisions Should a Small Vision-Language Model Keep?

author.name: Minhao Fan, Yinyi Liu, Jiayu Zhao, Zihan Teng, Song Chen, Weichen Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Harness Compilation, an offline procedure that optimizes how work is divided between a frozen small vision-language model and its external orchestration harness, using a large teacher to revise content and control based on student execution traces. Across seven visual question-answering settings with students up to 9B parameters, it improves scores by 9.9-23.9 points without weight updates or teacher calls at deployment.

entry.title: Finsler Flow Matching: Dynamics-Aware Geodesic Interpolation for Single-Snapshot Trajectory Inference

author.name: Niklas Canova, Jonas Simon Fleck

entry.summary: Finsler Flow Matching learns continuous stochastic dynamics from discrete Markov transition graphs over single-cell snapshot data, using first and second local moments to build a Finsler structure motivated by the Freidlin-Wentzell theory. It goes beyond prior generative approaches that rely only on population marginals, symmetric geometries, or single velocity vectors.

entry.title: ReCast: Attribution-Oriented Step Representation Learning for LLM-Based Agent Systems

author.name: Weilin Jin, Mingyu Wang, Taiyu Zhu, Ziqi Zhou, Wenbo Li, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Yifan Wu, Ying Li, Zhonghai Wu

entry.summary: This paper addresses failure attribution in LLM-based agent systems, aiming to identify the earliest step responsible for a downstream failure. The authors show empirically that hidden-state representations from LLMs poorly separate root-cause steps from others, and propose ReCast, which transforms frozen LLM hidden states into attribution-oriented step representations for more reliable failure tracing.

entry.title: AtomWorld-Mirror: Macro-Step World Modeling of Critical Evolution Backbones for Materials Dynamics

author.name: Ziming Pan, Ruge Zhang, Haozhi Han, Junkai Zhou, Xingyuan Chen, Yifeng Chen, Yunquan Zhang, Ting Cao, Yunxin Liu, Kun Li

entry.summary: AtomWorld-Mirror is a time-aware world model that distills short micro-event segments of atomistic simulation into macro-step transitions between key structural states, jointly predicting sparse structural edits and accumulated physical quantities. It targets the evolutionary-resolution bottleneck in long-horizon materials simulation.

entry.title: MemTrial: Learning When to Trust Memory in LLM Portfolio Agents

author.name: Guanghao Wu, Zhuo Cai, Shoujin Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a credit-assignment flaw in LLM agents for portfolio management: crediting experiences by realized market outcomes tracks the market itself rather than the experience. MemTrial instead puts memory on trial by drafting the same decision with and without an experience against identical market conditions, so shared market moves cancel out in the comparison.

entry.title: LEVER: Adaptive Cost-Aware Proof Search Over AND/OR Graphs

author.name: Nihal Jain, Shuangjie Yao, Begum Cicekdag, Zhuo Zhang, Suman Jana

entry.summary: Proposes LEVER, a proof search algorithm for LLM-powered theorem provers that makes the objective over correct proofs programmable and optimizes it during search rather than only after a proof is found. It scores partial proofs over an AND/OR graph combining realized values with predictions for open subgoals, optimizing cost, proof length, or weighted combinations while a Lean kernel enforces correctness.

entry.title: Is Memorization Context-Sensitive? Prefix-Based Extraction Beyond Isolated Prefixes

author.name: Ali Satvaty, Narjes Sharafi, Jirui Qi, Suzan Verberne, Fatih Turkmen

entry.summary: Investigates whether contextual conditioning — instructions, retrieved documents, or other task context as in RAG — mitigates prefix-based memorization extraction or merely changes which memorized samples become extractable. Using paired item-level measurements of probabilistic suffix extraction, the study shows context can expose different memorized content rather than suppress extraction.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Learn Their Way to the Top? Evaluating Heuristic Learning in a Long-Running Game Agent Competition

author.name: Kaisen Yang, Qingle Liu, Kejin Wang, Yicheng Zhao, Jieming Li, Shenghan Zheng, Ruize Yang, Bojun Yang, Heng Gong, Xiang Gao, Lanyue Zhang, Kaiyu Zhong, Zhuo Liu, Shaoxuan Li, Chengxi Li, Yong Yan, Weixuan Zhang, Tianwei Luo, Situ Wang, Youjie Zheng, Sihan Zhao, Shengyuan Wang, Huan-ang Gao, Jiazheng Xu, Xiaohui Xie, Wentao Han, Hongning Wang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Adversarial Heuristic Learning, where AI agents refine executable game policies and supporting software while keeping model weights fixed, and introduces AAArena, a benchmark of 12 adversarial games with 1,920 archived human programs evaluated under real competition protocols. Agents must interpret rules, choose opponents, analyze replays, and iteratively revise their game agents.

entry.title: From Pixels, Without Pre-training: Joint Generative and Self-Supervised Representation Learning in One Model

author.name: Vicente Balmaseda, Ching-Long Lin, Tianbao Yang

entry.summary: Presents a single model that jointly performs self-conditioned image generation (via flow matching) and self-supervised contrastive representation learning, requiring no labels, pretrained encoders, or autoencoders. The work resolves the objective mismatch between contrastive invariance and the fine-detail preservation that generation demands.

entry.title: Real Long-Term Memory for AI: A 50-Million-Token Window That Is Faster and Cheaper Than Recompute

author.name: Sietse Schelpe

entry.summary: This paper tests a KV-state persistence layer (galahad-kv) that saves each ~16k-token block's KV cache to encrypted local NVMe and reloads it byte-exact later, evaluated on 50 million tokens of real text with Gemma 4 12B and 31B served through vLLM on one H100. Loading was 2.8x-4.3x faster than recomputation and used 8.8x-12.3x less GPU energy.

entry.title: Rethinking the Tradeoff Between Temporal Encoding and Nonlinear Computation in Spiking Language Models

author.name: Hanfei Liu, Shuchang Feng, Yanxia Chen, Changzeng Fu, Shiqi Zhao

entry.summary: Spora jointly designs spike encodings and attention operators for spiking language models, introducing binary temporal weights that give T spikes up to T bits of representational capacity versus O(log T) for spike-count readout, with unipolar and bipolar binary spiking schemes. These enable efficient accumulation-and-shift dot products and integer-exponent mappings in attention.

entry.title: When Citations Mislead? A Claim-Level Benchmark for Legal Hallucination Detection

author.name: M. Mikail Demir, M. Abdullah Canbaz

entry.summary: PARCEL is a benchmark of 3,396 parenthetical-style claims from recent New York Court of Appeals decisions, labeled Supported, Refuted, or Not Found, cast as a three-way NLI task for detecting legal claims unsupported by their cited authority. Zero-shot evaluation of frontier LLMs shows high accuracy (up to 0.97) but persistent failures marking unsupported claims as supported.

entry.title: RAG-Stress: Probing the Limits of Evidence Reliance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Shunyuan Zhou, Hao Chen, Tianyu Wang, Goose Lin, Zaiyuan Wang, Haiying Zhao

entry.summary: RAG-Stress is a controlled diagnostic protocol measuring how misleading retrieved evidence causes models to abandon previously correct answers, holding questions fixed and editing one assertion to support a designated wrong answer while varying source priority and answer position. It reports misleading rates on the subset of questions a model answers correctly without retrieval, separating evidence-driven error from preexisting mistakes. This offers a cleaner measurement of RAG over-reliance than accuracy metrics.

entry.title: Rethinking Contrastive Loss in CLIP Post-training: A Complementary Framework with Frozen Text Encoder

author.name: Zidan Wang, Yaqian Li, Xiaokai Zhang, Kaiwen Long, Kun He, Hanpeng Liu

entry.summary: This paper revisits the claim that contrastive loss is unsuitable for CLIP post-training due to catastrophic forgetting, showing the forgetting stems primarily from an inappropriate contrastive temperature rather than insufficient negatives. Setting tau sufficiently small lets contrastive post-training improve the pretrained CLIP, and the authors propose a complementary framework using a frozen text encoder. This is a useful corrective to a recent narrative in the CLIP adaptation literature.

entry.title: Conditional Residual Prediction: Improving Autoregressive Video Diffusion without a Bidirectional Teacher

author.name: Bowen Zheng, Zhiguang Liu, Jiarong Ou, Rui Chen, Tianyang Hu

entry.summary: This paper trains causal video diffusion models from image-model initialization without any bidirectional video teacher or distillation pipeline, making the training path simpler and more scalable. The authors identify that training on ground-truth history creates strong dependence that breaks under inference-time error accumulation, and propose conditional residual prediction to fix it. This targets streaming, interactive, and long-video generation.

entry.title: DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Anhao Zhao, Haoran Xin, Junlong Tong, Yingqi Fan, Xuan Lu, Ping Nie, Wenjie Li, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: The paper shows that training on fewer selected tokens can outperform full-token on-policy distillation, because low-low tokens (negligible probability under both teacher and student) can receive large log-ratio rewards that hinder learning. DIAL-OPD selects tokens by learning value, weighting reward magnitude with the logarithmic mean of teacher and student probabilities to bridge log-probability and probability spaces.

entry.title: HI3D 3.0 (Twinkle3D): Object-specific 3D Asset Generation with High Resolution

author.name: Ziying Li, Shengchu Zhao, Huiang He, Yiyang Chen, Jianwen Huang, Bailin Li, Changhao Li, Jianhui Li, Jie Li, Ruiyang Liu, Yibo Luo, Tengjiao Sun, Pei Tang, Shiwen Wang, Jiaqi Wu, Kang Wu, Kaiqiao Yang, Zherui Yang, Hu Zhang, Xuezhi Zhao, Xinhe Zheng, Yukun Li, Heliang Zheng, Rongfei Jia

entry.summary: Hi3D 3.0 is an image-to-3D generation system focused on object-specific fidelity, addressing the common failure of image-to-3D methods to reproduce identity-defining details such as inscriptions, brand marks, and repeated structures. Its Twinkle3D geometry model generates watertight triangle meshes at 2048-cubed resolution and claims improvements along four dimensions, including better surface quality than prior high-precision voxel approaches. This matters for production-grade 3D asset creation in gaming, e-commerce, and digital content pipelines.

entry.title: Evaluating Exact Output and Checkpoint-State Prediction in Real Programs

author.name: Xiaohong Chen, David Bucur, Chenglong Ma, Yi Zhang, Lingming Zhang, Sriram Vishwanath, Grigore Rosu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark extending CRUXEval-style tasks to test whether models can predict a program's final output and intermediate checkpoint states from source code and input alone, without execution tools. It spans 400 cases from 371 Python and C++ programs across seven evaluation settings and four model families, finding reasoning-enabled modes outperform non-reasoning modes by 33-55 percentage points, with the best setting reaching 93.0% on shorter-trace output prediction.

entry.title: A Closer Look at Agentic BBO: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Black-Box Optimization

author.name: Ming Chen, Rong-Xi Tan, Ke Xue, Yu-Jie Zhou, Taiye Lu, Zhi-Xuan Gao, Peng Xie, Zijun Shen, Chen Lu, Haopu Shang, Chao Qian

entry.summary: This paper introduces AgenticBBO-Bench, a cross-domain benchmark for evaluating LLM agents performing black-box optimization across tasks such as synthetic functions, hyperparameter optimization, database tuning, and chip design. It addresses the lack of comparability in existing agentic BBO studies by standardizing task domains and system configurations so individual design choices can be isolated.

entry.title: RoboRSI: Stable, efficient, and reusable robot self-evolution in complex real-world environments

author.name: Zimo Wen, Yijin Chen, Yuxuan Cao, Wendi Chen, Yanwen Zou, Wenye Yu, Fuhang Kuang, Han Xue, Jun Lv, Chuan Wen, Cewu Lu

entry.summary: RoboRSI is a robot self-improvement system built on Top-Down Skill Refinement, decomposing tasks into compound, atomic, and base skills with explicit input-output contracts so each code repair is attributed to the responsible capability, supported by execution evidence, and validated before reuse. It targets stable and reusable self-evolution in complex real-world settings.

entry.title: SPERA: Spherical Prior EEG Foundation Model with Geometry- and Frequency-Aware Latent Prediction

author.name: Minsu Kim, Ye-Sung Kim, Hyeseong Jeon, Wooseok Hyung, Joshua Lee, Chang-Hwan Im

entry.summary: Presents SPERA, an EEG foundation model using a JEPA-style latent-prediction objective with a Legendre-polynomial spherical spatial prior to handle heterogeneous electrode montages and devices. By predicting in latent space rather than reconstructing raw signals, it separates neural from non-neural components and targets general-purpose EEG representation learning.

entry.title: How Hackable Is Your Speech Quality Metric? A Corrected Protocol, a Benchmark, and What Patching Buys

author.name: Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson

entry.summary: This work examines how easily speech quality predictors can be hacked when used as reward signals, showing that standard measurement protocols are flawed: failing to reference the unperturbed round trip through a neural codec inflates measured hackability by up to 4x, and single-attacker evaluations are unreliable since seed variation alone spans success rates from 0.00 to 0.38. The paper proposes a corrected protocol and benchmark comparing published predictors and defenses.

entry.title: Predictive Multiplicity in Cell-Fate Assignment: Label-Free Rashomon Sets and the Limits of Per-Cell Certification

author.name: Arjun Bhupatiraju, Abhiram Bhupatiraju

entry.summary: This paper studies predictive multiplicity in single-cell trajectory inference, where equally well-fitting models assign conflicting cell fates. FateMultiplicity constructs a label-free Rashomon set via non-inferiority testing on cross-fitted held-out genes, calibrated against random-seed variation. The analysis finds multiplicity depends more on model-space diversity than size, and questions whether per-cell certified fate margins yield more reliable assignments than fitted models.

entry.title: Policy Alignment: New Signals for Membership Auditing in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yilong Yang, Wenzhuo Shang, Yule Liu, Jiale Teng, Zhuo Ma

entry.summary: Introduces PAMA, a membership auditing framework for on-policy distillation that uses the teacher-induced direction of student policy updates as a signal, beyond likelihood-based confidence and checkpoint drift. This addresses privacy concerns around private distillation prompts. It matters as knowledge distillation becomes a common training paradigm with underexplored privacy leakage.

entry.title: Compile the Table: Query-Calibrated Operator Compression for Tabular In-Context Learning

author.name: Xu Zhao, Jiaming Zhao, Bin Zhao, Yong Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces QCOC, a method that compiles the full KV cache of in-context examples for tabular prediction into compact joint-KV prototypes shared across queries, preserving per-cluster multiplicities and the original example count. It aims to resolve the accuracy-throughput tradeoff in tabular in-context learning by enabling cache reuse and batching without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: Credal Machine Learning for Risk-Averse Decision Making

author.name: Timo L\"ohr, Paul Hofman, Maximilian Muschalik, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: The paper proposes representing epistemic uncertainty about the loss distribution via credal sets to make risk-averse prediction via CVaR reliable, addressing the failure mode where a learner's uncertainty about the true CVaR undermines worst-case guarantees. It develops a credal-set-based method for risk-averse decision making.

entry.title: SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Qitong Wang, Xinwei Niu, Mingluo Su, Shanwei Zhao, Shiai Zhu, Huan Wang

entry.summary: SparseDecoding addresses a distribution-shift flaw in Hessian-guided training-free LLM pruning: Hessians are computed on natural text, but decoding consumes self-generated tokens. The method aligns pruning calibration with the decoding-time token distribution, reducing latency in the memory-bound decoding stage. This is directly relevant to making LLM inference cheaper.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Recovering from Observation-Space Shift at Long-Horizon Skill Seams

author.name: Pranav Wagh, Yu Fang, Yue Yang, Mingyu Ding

entry.summary: The paper studies why long-horizon robotic manipulation degrades when independently trained skills are chained, identifying Observation-Space Shift at skill seams as the key failure mode. Using privileged simulator resets, the authors show displaced scene state, not robot configuration, dominates the shift, and build a learned detect-restore mechanism to recover performance.

entry.title: A General $\widetilde{\Omega}(\sqrt{T \gamma_T})$ Lower Bound for Kernel Bandits

author.name: Chenkai Ma, Jonathan Scarlett

entry.summary: This paper establishes a general minimax regret lower bound of order sqrt(T*gamma_T/log T) for kernel bandits over RKHS functions, where gamma_T is the maximum information gain. Previously, near-matching lower bounds existed only for specific kernels like squared exponential and Matern, leaving the generality of upper-bound optimality unclear.

entry.title: PageWeaver: KV-Guided Query Unions for Sparse Attention

author.name: Zhiyuan Li, Zihan Li, Zefang Yuan, Lei Wang, Hao Wang

entry.summary: PageWeaver addresses the gap between sparse attention theory and GPU efficiency by grouping queries based on their selected KV-page affinity so page loads are shared and Tensor Core tiles are populated. It includes a bounded GPU search for query grouping and an ID-aware kernel that avoids materializing reordered tensors, with FP8 KV experiments on H200 hardware demonstrating throughput gains.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Future Conditioning for Temporally Robust Robot Manipulation

author.name: Mohammad Khoshnazar, Mohammad Dehghani Tezerjani, Zhiyuan Gao, Deyuan Qu, Max Gandyra, Yanxiang Zhan, Mehreen Naeem, Andrew Melnik, Jeroen Schafer, Qing Yang, Michael Beetz

entry.summary: The authors show that temporal misalignment in generated video guidance can actively harm robot manipulation policies: on CALVIN, a five-frame early shift reduces success from 81.3 percent to near the no-future baseline. They propose Reliability-Aware Future Conditioning, which reframes trust in generated futures as a control problem, estimating per-step reliability and selecting among nearby temporal hypotheses with fallback to future-free behavior. This is a practical fix for video-conditioned VLA policies.

entry.title: Beyond Spatio-Temporal Priors: A Generalizable Approach for Dense Correspondence Matching

author.name: Luping Liu, Bingyi Kang, Yifan Wang, Dong Xu

entry.summary: FreeMatching addresses dense correspondence matching for image editing and reference-guided generation, where transformations preserve visual identity but break classical smooth-motion and rigid-geometry assumptions. It combines generative and semantic foundation representations with heterogeneous supervision from classical datasets, tracked videos, and synthetic scenes, plus teacher-guided iterative refinement that removes the need for dense correspondence annotations. This matters for controllable generation and editing pipelines that rely on identity-preserving spatial alignment.

entry.title: One Block, Multiple Depths: Recurrent Vision Transformers with Depth-Programmed Experts

author.name: Adrian Bulat, Yassine Ouali, Georgios Tzimiropoulos

entry.summary: The authors show that a single transformer block applied recurrently can match a full-depth vision encoder at comparable inference FLOPs by restoring depth-specific transformations through a convex mixture of a small shared expert FFN bank, programmed by a continuous normalized-depth coordinate. Evaluated on supervised ImageNet-1k training and DINOv2 distillation, weight-space merging emerges as the strongest MoE family tested. This matters for parameter-efficient vision architectures that decouple depth from parameter count.

entry.title: Not Every Change Is Necessary: Recoverable Drift in Large Language Model Unlearning

author.name: Xunlei Chen, Qinghui Gong, Jingkun Xue, Qihe Liu, Shijie Zhou, Fei Ye

entry.summary: The paper observes that collateral parameter changes from LLM unlearning can impair non-target capabilities, and that some of these changes are reversible while preserving forgetting performance. It proposes PTP-U, a propose-then-project framework that applies local analytic edits to weaken target knowledge and then projects non-target output distributions back toward the original model.

entry.title: ViSkill: Reinforcing VLM Agents with Evolving Visual-Native Skills

author.name: Hongxing Li, Dingming Li, Yixin Li, Yong Du, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: ViSkill is a visual-native skill learning framework for VLM agents that stores successful interactions as composite visual skill cards, which are retrieved to guide both inference and reward shaping, with new trajectories continuously distilled back into the library. Unlike text-centric skill approaches, it preserves geometric and spatial structure, and skill improvement is coupled with policy optimization rather than kept separate. This aims to improve sample efficiency of embodied and GUI-style agents.

entry.title: No Distillation Needed: Single-Pass Real-Time Talking Heads via Acausal Noise Shaping

author.name: Yu Han, Dejan Markovic, Alexander Richard, Wojciech Zielonka, Akshay Venkatesh, Cheng-hsin Wuu, Michael Zollhoefer

entry.summary: For audio-driven facial animation, the paper argues that diffusion-based generators are unnecessarily costly for streaming and that facial motion lies on a low-dimensional manifold where a single-pass causal GAN suffices. The key technical insight is that causal generators driven by i.i.d. noise cannot suppress output spectra without collapsing per-step innovation, so the authors introduce an acausal noise-shaping solution. This enables real-time, distillation-free talking-head generation.

entry.title: PathLang: A Language-Centered Benchmark for Vision-Language Models in Computational Pathology

author.name: Fanqi Cheng, Kuo Gong, Shangke Liu, Beidi Zhao, Junchao Zhu, Zheyu Zhu, Leiyue Zhao, Fengbei Liu, John Cannon, Gang Wang, Zu-hua Gao, Kenji Ikemura, Yihe Yang, Yaohong Wang, Yuankai Huo, Xiaoxiao Li, Mert R. Sabuncu, Ruining Deng

entry.summary: Introduces PathLang, a zero-shot benchmark for pathology VLMs that holds slides, labels, and evaluation direction fixed while systematically varying only the diagnostic language, testing linguistic robustness across reports, institutions, and phrasings. From a large, credible team including pathology and ML researchers.

entry.title: Dino Forcing Flow Models: Do not denoise what you can predict

author.name: Arijit Ghosh, Lucas Degeorge, Paul Couairon, Alexei A Efros, Vicky Kalogeiton, David Picard

entry.summary: Proposes simplifying representation-guided flow matching by directly predicting pretrained DINO representations and conditioning on the prediction, instead of co-denoising them via a second ODE trajectory. This removes schedule complexity while converging faster and improving FID, outperforming latent-space state of the art on ImageNet at 2x fewer epochs.

entry.title: Healthy Counterfactual Generation via Diffusion Inpainting for Mammography Classification

author.name: In\^es Cruchinho Garcia, Mariana Mour\~ao, Francisco Maria Calisto, Carlos Santiago, Jacinto Nascimento

entry.summary: This paper proposes counterfactual data augmentation for breast cancer screening CAD systems by training a DDPM on healthy BI-RADS 1 mammograms and using RePaint-style inpainting to erase lesions and fill in realistic healthy tissue within annotated bounding boxes. The generated healthy counterfactuals preserve patient anatomy while enriching the training distribution, aiming to reduce costly false negatives.

entry.title: WorldGuide: Goal-Directed Video World Model for Procedural Task Execution

author.name: Ankan Deria, Komal Kumar, Hisham Cholakkal, Fahad Shahbaz Khan, Salman Khan

entry.summary: WorldGuide formulates procedural video generation as closed-loop task execution in visual world space: given an initial image and a task goal, it predicts an action from its generated state, executes it, and recognizes task completion, adapting to what has actually been produced rather than open-loop planning. This bridges the gap between deciding an action and successfully realizing it.

entry.title: How Firm Should a Grasp Be?

author.name: Matthew Beveridge, Shree K. Nayar

entry.summary: This paper proposes a visuotactile method for estimating an object's material properties (mass, elasticity, friction) in real time during grasping, then using those estimates to compute the minimum safe grasp force. The authors also contribute a dataset of real fruits and vegetables with measured physical properties used to train the force estimation model.

entry.title: OmniHOI: Dexterous Hand-Object Interaction from Monocular Human Video

author.name: Ting Mao, Yanming Shao, Ziheng Wang, Haoyu Liu, Yiqun Wang, Xuanye Wu, Yao Mu

entry.summary: OmniHOI is a pipeline converting a single RGB video of human hand-object interaction into an interaction-faithful trajectory on dexterous robot hands. It enforces physical consistency stage by stage: image evidence during reconstruction, contact geometry during retargeting, and dynamics during physics-in-the-loop optimization, avoiding task-specific RL training or motion-capture assumptions.

entry.title: Learning Language-Conditioned Traversability Representations for Adaptive Visual Navigation

author.name: Senda Chen, Changxu Cheng, Fangdi Li, Tao Wang, Wuyue Zhao

entry.summary: LaTraNav learns language-conditioned traversability representations so navigation can adapt to robot capabilities and user preferences without hand-crafted costmap rules. It uses an asynchronous architecture pairing a slow VLM producing latent traversability/goal representations with a fast flow-matching planner, plus a simulation data pipeline for training.

entry.title: RESETTLE: Robotic Recovery through Disagreement-Triggered Retrieval and Efficient Corrective Control

author.name: Yuxin Chen, Senqiao Yang, Zixuan Wang, Jinhui Ye, Changsheng Lu, Pengguang Chen, Shu Liu, Zhuotao Tian, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: RESETTLE is a model-agnostic framework for correcting emerging execution errors in frozen robot policies. It triggers recovery when two independently sampled action proposals under identical conditions persistently disagree, then retrieves a same-task demonstration and applies efficient corrective control, avoiding the latency of repeated vision-language reasoning or online optimization.

entry.title: Equal Path Cost, Unequal Output Effects: Understanding Perturbation Propagation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Wei Guo, Yaowen Zhang, Xingtong Ge, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework for how perturbations along diffusion sampling trajectories propagate to outputs, combining dynamical analysis of the sampling process with information-theoretic output characterization. It quantifies perturbation strength via KL divergence between perturbed and reference trajectory distributions, termed path cost, which bounds output effects.

entry.title: Overcoming Prior Barriers: Supervised Fine-Tuning under Long-Tail Distribution

author.name: Haohui Wang, Jiahao Xu, Wangzhi Zhan, Tong Zeng, Dongqi Fu, Hong Li, Swastik Roy, Naren Ramakrishnan, Chris North, Jian Kang, Yujun Yan, Dawei Zhou

entry.summary: The paper introduces prior barrier, a measure of how strongly a pretrained LLM supports competing concepts over a target concept, and shows these barriers follow a long-tail distribution so head and tail concepts start SFT from very different positions. It derives theoretical analysis and proposes approaches to help tail concepts overcome higher barriers.

entry.title: Nullify: Null-Space Activation Steering for Training-Free LLM Unlearning

author.name: Wei Zhai, Xiang Liu, Qiang Huang, Rui Qian, Lemao Liu, Ziwei Li, Ziqi Wang, Zhitao Huang, Dejing Dou

entry.summary: Proposes Nullify, a training-free LLM unlearning method that uses inference-time steering vectors to redirect privacy-related activations away from memorized answers while a null-space constraint keeps retained-query activations essentially unchanged. The approach avoids costly fine-tuning and aims to balance forget quality against utility preservation.

entry.title: SafeInferCom: Safe Inference-Time Compute via Verifier-Guided Mid-Generation Intervention for Robotic Task Planning

author.name: Weizhe Xu, Jialiang Fan, Mengyu Liu, Fanxin Kong

entry.summary: SafeInferCom addresses a failure of large reasoning models in robotic task planning where continued reasoning overwrites valid intermediate plans or leaves constraint violations unresolved. It introduces an inference-time monitor that exposes and verifies intermediate plans without disrupting decoding, then uses formal-verifier guidance to preserve valid plans and direct error correction mid-generation. Experiments reveal reasoning-response inconsistency and limited self-correction under one-shot inference across multiple LRLMs and domains.

entry.title: Elucidating the Space of Enzymatic Reaction: A Unified Benchmark and Pretrained Model

author.name: Yutong Hu, Tianming Huang, Yanbo Zhao, Qiongyu Zhang, Shixiang Tang, Lei Bai, Ziyi Zhou, Liang Hong, Pan Tan

entry.summary: The authors introduce VenusRX-Bench, a unified benchmark covering forward reaction prediction, single-step retrosynthesis, and EC-number prediction with standardized curation and leakage-controlled splits, plus a pretrained model of the enzymatic reaction space linking reactants, products, and enzyme annotations. Benchmarking reveals a clear chemical-to-enzymatic domain gap driven by limited domain data.

entry.title: REACT: Rolling Denoising and Dual Decoupling for Reactive Robot Control with VLA Models

author.name: Houlong Xiong, Zhenqi Qiu, Zechen Wang, Suohang Zhang, Yiyu Ren, Wanting Xu, Hongfei Niu, Chengyang He, Ge Sun, Ran Cheng, Qian Zhu

entry.summary: REACT improves the reactivity of flow-based vision-language-action models by maintaining a persistent action buffer with staggered flow timesteps, denoising the full horizon with each new observation rather than regenerating entire action chunks. This resolves the closed-loop trade-off between smooth long chunks and frequent replanning in robot control.

entry.title: Deflating the Hessian: Rank-4 W4A4 Quantization for Multimodal Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Shiwen Wang, Pengxiang Zhao, Xiaoming Yuan

entry.summary: The paper presents a unified framework for low-rank-assisted W4A4 post-training quantization of diffusion transformers, modeling low-rank compensation and residual quantization as a coupled calibration problem with optimization-based solvers. Unlike prior work that treats these separately or ignores activation quantization error in second-order updates, the method achieves competitive 4-bit results with very low rank (rank-4) compensation. This targets the heavy compute cost of multimodal diffusion transformer inference.

entry.title: Just Weather Scoring: Efficient End-to-end Nowcasting with Distributional Diffusion

author.name: Jannik Wiese, Johannes Schusterbauer, Tommaso Martorella, Bj\"orn Ommer

entry.summary: JWS is a single-stage, end-to-end diffusion model for probabilistic precipitation nowcasting that forecasts directly in radar space, eliminating separately trained compression components and enabling few-step generation via Masked Asynchronous Diffusion. This simplifies training and inference while removing uncertainty from lossy compression.

entry.title: Learning Kilometer-Scale Weather Prediction with Global-Regional Alignment

author.name: Guowen Li, Yang Liu, Yujie Wang, Qiuyan Sun, Haoyuan Liang, Juepeng Zheng, Hong Cheng, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: ScaleCast is a regional weather forecasting framework that aligns pretrained global weather model representations with high-resolution regional prediction, avoiding costly additional training of global components. Its Global-Regional Alignment mechanism handles grid mismatches and integrates large-scale guidance with local interactions. Kilometer-scale forecasting matters for local severe-weather warnings, an area where ML weather models (e.g., Google's WeatherNext line) are advancing rapidly.

entry.title: When Listening Becomes Easier: Scrubbing Visual Cues for Shortcut-Free VLAs

author.name: Jasper Gerigk, Kenzo Aspuru-Takata, Chin-Hsuan Wu, Mohammad Mohammadi, Shuhong Zheng, Igor Gilitschenski

entry.summary: The authors find that vision-language-action model backbones differ substantially in susceptibility to visual shortcut learning and propose an action-margin metric that predicts this without policy rollouts. They develop a method to scrub spurious visual cues from action representations, mitigating shortcut exploitation in robot policies trained on limited demonstrations.

entry.title: WAM-Cache: Staleness-Bounded KV Reuse for Efficient World Action Models

author.name: Kai Ding, Yang He, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: WAM-Cache accelerates world action models for robot manipulation by caching layerwise KV representations from the video DiT across control chunks and recomputing only a sparse refresh set, with staleness bounds. The paper shows intuitive visually-drifted-token heuristics plateau below dense baselines and derives a better refresh criterion.

entry.title: Embedding-Bias in Conditional Independence Testing

author.name: Nikolaj Thams, Anton Rask Lundborg

entry.summary: This paper analyzes when conditional independence tests that condition on text or image embeddings instead of raw data remain valid, showing rejection probability under the null can tend to one when the embedding discards relevant dependence. It derives a relaxed validity condition for a residual-correlation test based on the Generalised Covariance Measure.

entry.title: FAITH: Feasibility-Aware Safety-Filtered RL for High-Dimensional Systems

author.name: Songyuan Zhang, Baljeet Singh, Sarthak Ranjeet Kaingade, Chuchu Fan, Bryan Trinh

entry.summary: FAITH is a model-free safe RL framework that approximates an optimal state-action safety value and amortizes minimal-intervention safety filtering with a feedforward network, separating safety from the task objective while remaining aware of long-horizon feasibility. Unlike classical filters, it handles cases where no instantaneously safe action exists and accounts for task return through filtered dynamics. This matters for deploying RL on high-dimensional robotic systems where safety cannot be an afterthought.

entry.title: Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Xiaobing Chen, Zhiqi Pang

entry.summary: Residual Advantage bridges RLVR and on-policy distillation by treating the teacher-student probability residual as a bounded one-step reward signal, addressing the credit-assignment weakness of outcome-only RLVR and the teacher-mismatch problem of unbounded log-ratio OPD supervision when student paths diverge from teacher paths.

entry.title: Latent Core Tokenizer: Compress, but Meaningfully

author.name: Felermino D. M. A. Ali, Millicent Ochieng, Ogbemi Ekwejunor-Etchie, Ade Famoti, Jacki O'Neill, Debjit Paul

entry.summary: The Latent Core Tokenizer separates structural discovery from vocabulary construction, using Minimum Description Length, entropy-based boundary signals, and morphotactic constraints to identify reusable linguistic units. Across 104 languages with a 200K vocabulary, LCT achieves lower fertility and higher MorphScore than BPE, Unigram, and parity-aware BPE while improving multilingual downstream performance.

entry.title: SteerablePlex: Can We Steer Full-Duplex Models?

author.name: Haolong Zheng, Maike Z\"ufle, Dominik Mach\'a\v{c}ek, Peter Pol\'ak, Xulin Fan, Xavier Sumba, Siyin Wang, Ond\v{r}ej Klejch, Mark Hasegawa-Johnson

entry.summary: This paper introduces SimIF-Bench, a benchmark measuring whether full-duplex conversational speech models stay within prescribed scenarios and complete ordered goals, finding that current open-source models struggle significantly. It then proposes GDPO (Group Reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization), a training recipe that improves instruction-following for full-duplex models used as user simulators. Reliable user simulators matter for trustworthy evaluation of conversational AI systems.

entry.title: GATOR: Generative and Agentic 3D Object Reconstruction From Casual Images

author.name: Qirui Wu, Stan Birchfield, Hesam Rabeti, Angel X. Chang, Bowen Wen

entry.summary: GATOR reconstructs complete, scene-aligned, textured 3D object assets and their poses from one or a few casual images. A local modality mixer couples patch-aligned RGB, mask, and pointmap features before cross-view reasoning, with text-guided semantic conditioning through stage-specific adapters for structure, geometry, and appearance. A generated asset then initializes a multimodal agent that iteratively refines the reconstruction, combining generative priors with agentic verification.

entry.title: GenIA: Generative Reconstruction with Test-Time Input Alignment

author.name: Stefano Esposito, Naama Pearl, Polina Karpikova, Samuel Rota Bul\`o, Lorenzo Porzi, Peter Kontschieder, Andreas Geiger, Jonathon Luiten

entry.summary: GenIA grounds SAM3D's generative 3D prior in observed geometric and photometric evidence at test time without retraining, improving pose via geometry-derived translation and scale while retaining the learned rotation prior, and aligning appearance through visibility-biased attention, cross-observation fusion, and differentiable-rendering guidance during denoising. It targets faithful reconstruction from monocular or sparse views.

entry.title: Autoregressive Retriever: Improving Query Understanding from Item Feedback for Universal Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Jianfei Zhao, Yifan Wang, Feng Zhang, Xin Sun, Chong Feng, Zhixing Tan, Yang Luo, Boyuan Pan, Xu Kai, Yao Hu

entry.summary: ARR is a multimodal retrieval model that iteratively refines the query embedding using the content of retrieved items, rather than encoding the query once and ranking statically. It trains item selection and feedback usage via stepwise contrastive supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning that treats feedback items as actions.

entry.title: ManiUnit: A Manipulation Skill Dataset and Benchmark for Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Guoting Wei, Dawei Yan, Xia Yuan, Gengming Zhang, Yelin He, Guodong Du, Jiaquan Ye, Heng Zhang, Xinming Wei, Xianbiao Qi, Chunxia Zhao, Haokui Zhang, Rong Xiao

entry.summary: ManiUnit is a manipulation skill dataset and benchmark derived from 50 BEHAVIOR-1K activities, containing 137,899 segments across 21 skills, designed to diagnose skill-level failures in long-horizon mobile manipulation. It addresses skill selection ambiguity, state-inheritance issues between skills, and the lack of skill-specific metrics.

entry.title: Generative Neural Retargeting for Human-to-Robot Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Dechen Gao, Yue Yang, Ben Abbatematteo, Nathan Godwin, Pengcheng Wang, Roger Boldu, Steven Man, Zhiyang Dou, Chuan Qin, Sho Nakagome, Eric Whitmire

entry.summary: The paper tackles the embodiment gap in transferring human demonstrations to dexterous robot hands, proposing a generative retargeting approach that avoids the pitfalls of IK (dynamics-infeasible motions), RL (unstable training, reward engineering), and per-trajectory MPC (poor scaling). The generative model amortizes retargeting so that solving one trajectory helps with the next.

entry.title: Agent-Controlled Forgetting for Tool-Using Agents: Reversible Context Curation in Practice

author.name: Jan-Peter Franke

entry.summary: This paper proposes agent-controlled forgetting, where the acting model replaces previously observed tool results with short notes while archiving recoverable originals, without task-specific training. In an OpenTelemetry debugging case, the method cut prompt tokens from about 912k to 232k and halved cumulative input tokens.

entry.title: Learning How to Search for Plans with Exponentially Less Space

author.name: Dominik Drexler, Simon St{\aa}hlberg, Markus Fritzsche, Blai Bonet

entry.summary: The authors learn domain-specific search control as indexical policies with registers and a choose rule marking backtracking points, proving that structural termination bounds every execution polynomially in the number of objects. A depth-first procedure then finds plans in polynomial space regardless of state-space size.

entry.title: RL-ARC: Calibrating Large Reasoning Models via Reasoning-guided Uncertainty

author.name: Gukhyeon Lee, SangKeun Lee

entry.summary: The paper observes that RL with verifiable rewards degrades calibration in reasoning models, producing overconfidence, and that prior calibration-aware training trades off reasoning performance. RL-ARC is a training framework that uses reasoning confidence as an auxiliary signal alongside answer confidence to jointly improve calibration and reasoning.

entry.title: ReTeach: Building a Self-Teacher through Multi-Round Reflection and Retry

author.name: Yafeng Tang, Hao Li, Hongsheng Yu, Qiang Fu

entry.summary: ReTeach is a reflective self-distillation framework that constructs a self-teacher through multi-round reflection and retry using only self-generated attempts and outcome-level verification, without reference answers or rich task feedback. It gives the teacher an advantage over the student purely via explicit error diagnosis and revision guidance.

entry.title: Scalable AI Uncertainty Quantification via Generalized Laplace Active Subspaces

author.name: Wouter N. Edeling, Peter V. Coveney

entry.summary: Proposes a low-rank generalized Laplace approximation for neural-network uncertainty quantification that restricts a local Gaussian posterior to a small number of data-informed curvature directions. Posterior variances in the retained subspace are closed-form and the prior is calibrated by empirical Bayes, making full-Bayes-like UQ computationally feasible for pretrained networks.

entry.title: Looking Inside LLMs: Small-World Connectivity as a Signature of Reasoning Performance

author.name: Zheng Huang, Sansheng Cao, Enpei Zhang, Weikang Qiu, Elynn Chen, Xiang Zhang, Yaoqing Yang, Rex Ying, Dawei Zhou, Yujun Yan

entry.summary: Inspired by neuroscience links between intelligence and small-world brain organization, this paper builds functional graphs from attention-head activation similarities and shows the small-world index correlates with fluid reasoning performance across models and checkpoints. It further analyzes how local head clustering contributes to this organization.

entry.title: SLVR: Structured Latent Visual Reasoning via Human-like Reasoning Flows

author.name: Albert Gao, Bing Xue, Andrea Zanette

entry.summary: Proposes SLVR, a training framework for multimodal LLMs that structures latent reasoning states so that planning, grounding, and evidence selection can be separately supervised, bridging explicit chain-of-thought and fully latent reasoning. The goal is to reduce reliance on linguistic priors in visual question answering without the inference cost of autoregressive rationales.

entry.title: Grammar Concept Annotation at Scale: Deployed Fine-Tuned Small Language Models Outperform Prompted Frontier Models

author.name: Marjan Celikik, Ana Peleteiro Ramallo, Javier Morales

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune Qwen3.5-based small language models on filtered teacher-generated supervision and deploy an efficient 0.8B model as an end-to-end grammar mastery tracker for all English learners on their platform. The 0.8B model outperforms prompted frontier models on two human-curated benchmarks while being far cheaper at scale.

entry.title: Higher-Order Action Supervision Makes A Strong Policy Class

author.name: Peng Cheng, Yunxian Hou, Zhi Zhou, Qian Zhang, Chang Huang, Xianyuan Zhan

entry.summary: The paper argues that imitation learning and reinforcement learning instability in real-world robotics and driving stems from supervising only zeroth-order action labels, and shows that simultaneously supervising zeroth- and first-order actions (action dynamics and temporal consistency) dramatically enhances robustness. This reframes policy design around a broader supervision target. It has direct relevance to deploying learned controllers safely in physical systems.

entry.title: CRISP: Fixing Flying Pixels in Latent LiDAR Generation via Diffusion Decoding

author.name: Andrea Ceron, Michael Schmidt, Alvaro Marcos-Ramiro, Sebastian Schmidt, Benjamin Busam

entry.summary: CRISP addresses the flying-pixels artifact in latent LiDAR generation, where convolutional VAEs blur sharp radial depth discontinuities, by introducing a pixel-space diffusion decoder with a DiT-based denoiser and support mask predictor. Replacing only the decoder while keeping the latent generator fixed reduces FSVD/FPVD by roughly 50% on average across KITTI-360, SemanticKITTI, and nuScenes, with up to 71-74% reductions for generic video VAEs. This identifies decoding as a major, directly correctable bottleneck in LiDAR generation pipelines.

entry.title: Rewiring Semantics, Dynamics, and Control: A Simple yet Effective Action-Centric Tri-Stream Transformer

author.name: Shuang Luo, Yilun Kong, Yunpeng Qing, Yihang Jiao, Zhi Hou, Shunyu Liu, Xiaogang Wang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: ACT3 is an action-centric tri-stream transformer that combines semantic understanding from pretrained VLMs with predictive dynamics from video-generation world models as complementary guidance for robot manipulation policies. It addresses the challenge that VLM backbones lack physical dynamics priors and that fusing semantics with dynamics prediction is nontrivial. The design claims simplicity and effectiveness in complex robotic manipulation settings.

entry.title: Beyond Report Imitation: Clinically Aware Multi-Image Ultrasound Report Generation from Visible Evidence

author.name: Yuchen Yang, Xin Wang, Lufan Wang, Yinghong Pan, Yujuan Feng, Yuqing Yang

entry.summary: CAMEO is a framework for generating ultrasound reports from multiple images that grounds text in only what is visible across archived views, addressing the misalignment between raw-report supervision and available visual evidence. It uses a two-stage pipeline learning visual-language primitives and clinically aware orchestration to avoid unsupported claims and conservative template collapse.

entry.title: GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts

author.name: Hexuan Deng, Zihao Yan, Xuebo Liu, Shuo Nie, Yue Wang, Chen Wang, Zhaohua Zhang, Tianwen Jiang, Qiuyong Xiao, Jihong Zhang, Min Zhang

entry.summary: GRPODropout addresses policy entropy collapse in GRPO-based RL for LLM reasoning by selectively excluding some generated rollouts from policy updates before the update step, under the same sampling budget. This rollout-level intervention complements existing algorithm-level and token-level approaches and can improve learning since not all rollouts contribute positively.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Enhancement: Adaptive Multi-Context Steering to Mitigate LVLM Hallucinations

author.name: Shuran Ma, JiaLe Li, Yuxin Dong, Shan Zheng, Qingyun Jiang, Xiang Chen, Qi Zhu, Deyi Ji, Yifan Yang, Jianfeng Pan, Yu Tian, Xue Yang

entry.summary: The paper studies how large vision-language models coordinate visual, textual, and other context sources during decoding and proposes adaptive steering that dynamically regulates context contributions to suppress hallucinations. Unlike prior contrastive decoding or visual enhancement approaches, it exploits an intrinsic vision-attending tendency in LVLMs and balances it with textual context.

entry.title: VibeEdit: Image Editing with Canvas Instructions

author.name: Jinjing Zhao, Fangyun Wei, Yitong Wang, Xiuyu Wu, Yunuo Chen, Yang Yue, Sirui Zhang, Wenbo Wang, Hongyang Zhang, Dong Chen, Yan Lu, Chang Xu

entry.summary: VibeEdit proposes a spatial marking interface for image editing where users place marks and short notes directly on an image, forming canvas instructions that specify where and what to edit without a separate text prompt. The authors build a dataset of 1.55 million edit pairs with object masks and structured descriptions to train an editor supporting addition, removal, replacement, attribute modification, and movement.

entry.title: Prediction-Powered Data Fusion for Treatment Effect Estimation

author.name: Yonghan Jung, Shu Yang

entry.summary: The authors propose a framework for estimating average and conditional treatment effects that fuses small randomized controlled trials with large observational studies without special assumptions on the observational data, using prediction-powered inference principles. Existing methods either impose assumptions on the observational data, model confounding, or trade bias for variance.

entry.title: PXtal: Learning to Align Powder X-Ray Diffraction and Crystal Structures under Information Asymmetry across Modalities

author.name: Zhuoran Yang, Christopher M. Collins, Bei Peng, Luke M. Daniels, Matthew J. Rosseinsky, Vladimir V. Gusev

entry.summary: Introduces PXtal, a framework aligning powder X-ray diffraction patterns with crystal structure representations under physically imposed information asymmetry, using Unbalanced Optimal Transport and coupling-level generalized KL divergence. Achieves consistent improvements across six test sets including four zero-shot transfer sets.

entry.title: World-Model Policy Arbiter for Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Junwei Quan, Evgenii Opryshko, Nicholas Rhinehart, Igor Gilitschenski

entry.summary: Rather than deploying a single best policy for offline goal-conditioned RL, this work treats a set of frozen goal-conditioned policies as a portfolio and learns an arbiter that selects which policy acts at each state. Key challenges include comparing policies with incomparable or missing value functions and judging policies by the states they would reach, which the authors address using a world model. This can outperform any single constituent policy across environments and task phases.

entry.title: Residual spectral instabilities in representation learning

author.name: Zhen Li

entry.summary: This theoretically ambitious paper formulates dimension-wise posterior collapse in VAEs as a fluctuation theory around partially collapsed states, interpreting the negative ELBO as an effective free energy whose quadratic expansion defines a Gaussian theory. Collapsed directions form an invariant fluctuation sector with an exact mass spectrum derived from a conditional residual operator, and a local reactivation direction lowers free energy when decoder variance falls below a residual threshold. It imports statistical-physics tools into representation learning.

entry.title: RAGenome: Scaling Retrieval-Based Genomic Language Models to Long Contexts

author.name: Frederikke Isa Marin, Panagiotis Antoniadis, Dionysia Danai Brilli, Andreas Bjerregaard, Rachael DeVries, Yan Li, Ole Winther, Wouter Boomsma

entry.summary: Extends retrieval-augmented approaches to genomic language models, enabling MSA-style pretraining benefits over long genomic contexts where existing models are restricted to short inputs. This expands gLM applicability beyond short-range tasks like variant effect prediction toward broader genomic function understanding. Addresses both the compute burden and context limits of standard genomic LMs.

entry.title: SCORE: Spectral Correlation Estimation for Multivariate Gaussians

author.name: Christopher B\"ulte, Emil Partow, Astha Gupta, Pascal Esser, Gitta Kutyniok

entry.summary: SCORE is a scalable framework for predictive modeling with high-dimensional Gaussian targets that decomposes learning into marginal distributions plus a structured correlation matrix learned in spectral space, achieving dense dependencies with linear storage and O(d log d) cost. It uses the closed-form Gaussian kernel score for training, which remains defined for degenerate covariances with bounded gradients.

entry.title: Toward Optimal Regret in Adversarial MDPs with Stochastic Hard Constraints

author.name: Qian Zuo, Francesco Emanuele Stradi

entry.summary: The paper studies episodic constrained MDPs with adversarial losses and stochastic hard constraints, improving on prior regret bounds of O(sqrt(T)/min{d,d^2}) to achieve optimal dependence on the constraint margins matching the lower bound of Omega(sqrt(T)/rho). This closes a gap in constrained adversarial online learning theory.

entry.title: Closing the Horizon Gap in Policy Optimization for Adversarial MDPs

author.name: Mingyi Li, Taira Tsuchiya

entry.summary: The authors close a known gap between policy-optimization and occupancy-measure regret bounds for episodic tabular MDPs with adversarial losses and bandit feedback. Using regularized Q-functions to stabilize local updates jointly across state-action pairs, they achieve near-optimal high-probability regret of order sqrt(HS(H+A)T) with known transitions. This resolves a fundamental discrepancy in online reinforcement learning theory.

entry.title: Enabling Preference-driven Unlearning in Few-step Distilled Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Gaurav Patel, Jun Fang, Greg Ver Steeg, Qiang Qiu, Sravan Sripada

entry.summary: This work identifies that data-driven unlearning objectives rely on multi-step denoising dynamics and therefore fail on few-step distilled text-to-image diffusion models. It proposes a preference-driven unlearning method tailored to FSD models that avoids the costly re-distillation pipeline, addressing safety risks in fast-inference image generators.

entry.title: VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression

author.name: Neha Verma, Sungwon Kim, Kenton Murray, Kevin Duh

entry.summary: VFold reduces LLM KV cache memory by merging value caches across layers using a symmetry-aware strategy that requires no architectural changes and avoids significant performance degradation during decoding. The method composes with existing techniques like high-ratio quantization and key cache pruning to achieve compression ratios neither approach reaches alone. This is relevant because KV cache memory dominates long-context inference costs.

entry.title: CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering for Motion Generators

author.name: Lizhi Yang, Yiling Hou, Yao Tang, Junheng Li, Daniel Weng, Blake Werner, Aaron D. Ames

entry.summary: CSF is a training-free filter that grounds natural-language safety rules in safe and unsafe reference trajectories generated by text-conditioned motion generators, enforcing them with a safe reference tracking CBF-QP. Unlike prompt inspection or geometric constraints, it accounts for how scene context changes a motion's meaning, e.g., the same action targeting an object versus a person. It works across four pretrained generators with different architectures, making it relevant for deploying motion generation safely in human environments.

entry.title: Lossy Compressive Text Autoencoders

author.name: Vinko Sabol\v{c}ec, Angelos Katharopoulos, David Grangier

entry.summary: The paper explores learned compressed latent representations of text via an autoencoder that performs residual down/upscaling along the time axis with a low-dimensional discrete bottleneck. The authors analyze quantization methods, training objectives, and datasets, evaluating reconstruction quality at surface (BLEU) and semantic (LLM-judge) levels plus downstream QA and semantic similarity tasks. This sits at the intersection of data compression and representation learning, relevant to efficient text storage and latent-space reasoning.

entry.title: From Retrieval to Reconstruction: Constructing Evolvable Cognitive Memory for Long-Term Dialogue

author.name: Zirui Liao, Zhengxian Wu, Zhuohong Chen, Yunyao Yu, Xiaoyu Liu, Yifan Xu, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: CogMem is a cognitive memory architecture for long-term dialogue agents built on a Person-Event-Concept-Claim-Fact graph schema, with dedicated Claim nodes preserving provenance of subjective statements and incremental conversion of dialogue turns into provenance-aware graph representations. It moves beyond passive RAG-style storage toward reconstructed, evolvable memory supporting belief-source reasoning.

entry.title: HarnessSQL: Harness-Native Training for SQL Agents in Realistic Database Environments

author.name: Haolin Yang, Jipeng Zhang, Jian Xie, Shuaishuai Gong, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: HarnessSQL addresses the train-deploy mismatch in text-to-SQL by training agents inside the full interactive execution harness throughout both SFT and RL, using isolated executable database environments with hidden execution oracles. This preserves the stateful, multi-turn interaction structure (schema inspection, probe queries, error diagnosis) that real database agents need.

entry.title: Beyond Speech Captions: Speech-Rewarded Style Planning for Conversational Text-to-Speech

author.name: Shiao Zhu, Lianbo Liu, Sizhen Lyu, Yuzhe Wang, Sheng Li, Takahiro Shinozaki

entry.summary: The paper shows that natural-language style descriptions used as pseudo-labels only weakly predict acoustic quality in controllable text-to-speech, and proposes Speech-Rewarded Style Planning (SRSP), which trains an LLM-based style planner end-to-end against a frozen downstream TTS model using group-relative policy optimization. This directly optimizes style instructions for their actual acoustic effect rather than descriptive fidelity. It matters because it reframes LLM-to-TTS interfaces as optimizable pipelines rather than captioning problems.

entry.title: SPLIT-RL: Staged Perception-Language Reasoning Training with Claim-Level Advantages

author.name: Raja Kumar, Rajat Koner, Ritwick Chaudhry, Zhuowei Li, Nishant Sankaran, Yifan Xing

entry.summary: SPLIT-RL is a staged post-training approach for vision-language reasoning that trains visual reasoning and language reasoning in disjoint phases so that group-relative advantages isolate capability-specific errors, instead of a single chain-of-thought with a final-answer reward. It further introduces Claim-Level Advantage CLA-GRPO for finer-grained credit assignment within rollouts. This targets the coarse credit assignment problem in RL with verifiable rewards for multimodal models.

entry.title: Fluid-Gen-Zero: Grounding Pretrained Video Generators in Physics without Training

author.name: Hong Huang, Yuqiu Liu, Chenyu You, Daniel Martin, Chuhang Zou, Wuyang Chen

entry.summary: Fluid-Gen-Zero is a training-free framework that grounds pretrained video generators in fluid physics by delegating motion dynamics to a physics simulator while preserving the generator's appearance modeling, connected via a two-level agentic workflow: a VLM agent plans generation from simulation rollouts, and region-aware latent wrapping injects simulation signals during denoising. It is plug-and-play with current video foundation models. This addresses the well-known physical implausibility of generated video without costly fine-tuning.

entry.title: Diffusion Meta-Prompting and Steering for Generalizable Foundation Model Adaptation

author.name: Deepak Sridhar, Yi Li, Kartikeya Bhardwaj, Shuangjun Liu, Taotao Jing, Yuan Li, Shuai Zhang, Jiancheng Lyu, Dashan Gao, Nuno Vasconcelos

entry.summary: The authors introduce Diffusion Meta-Prompt (DMP), which models the distribution of previously learned prompts using a diffusion model so new prompts can be synthesized for unseen classes, domains, and task compositions from natural-language descriptions alone. A test-time steering strategy anchors sampling to the best training-selected prompt for stability. Notably, training requires no access to original task data or losses, only the prompt repository.

entry.title: When Scene Text Hijacks the Scene: Uncovering, Exploiting, and Mitigating Rendered-Text Semantic Leakage in Image Generation Models

author.name: Feifei Li, Runjie Wang, Xiaohan Zhang, Zhenxing Qian, Mi Wen, Mi Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies rendered-text semantic leakage in image generation models: text that should be reproduced verbatim as a local visual element also carries linguistic semantics that the model interprets as scene instructions, effectively a control channel beyond the prompt. The authors study modern instruction-following image generators, demonstrate exploitation of this leakage, and propose mitigations. This has implications for the reliability and safety of generative image systems.

entry.title: Memory Forcing: Attendable Mid-Horizon History for Streaming Video Generation

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Xinyu Wang, Huafeng Shi, Gangshan Wu, Limin Wang

entry.summary: Identifies mid-horizon forgetting in autoregressive streaming video diffusion, where events leaving the fixed KV cache window cannot be attended to later. Memory Forcing partitions the cache into sink, archive, and working banks to retain diverse intermediate history under fixed memory, with bank-aware RoPE reindexing to handle temporal index drift.

entry.title: Slot3R: Set-Associative Spatial Memory for Streaming 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Xiyuan Zhang, Yanming Yang, Kaiyuan Xu, Ruibo Li, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Slot3R critiques Point3R for conflating spatial proximity with memory-entry identity in streaming 3D reconstruction, which can destroy complementary evidence when nearby pointers are averaged. It proposes a training-free, set-associative retrieval design where location determines the memory address but not whether observations must merge, preserving evidence until later frames disambiguate it.

entry.title: Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Kairui Hu, Siyuan Hu, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: This paper reframes robot control as an Embodied Turing Machine, where environment and robot state form the tape and policy logic is written entirely in code that measures state from camera images and proprioception. The proposed Code-Only-as-Policy approach removes VLMs and VLAs from the control loop, sharing one code library across tasks and episodes, with implications for recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: Demonstrating Arena 5.0: A Photorealistic ROS2 Simulation Framework for Developing and Benchmarking Social Navigation

author.name: Volodymyr Shcherbyna, Linh K\"astner, Duc Anh Do, Hoang Tung, Huu Giang Nguyen, Maximilian Ho-Kyoung Schreff, Tim Seeger, Eva Wiese, Ahmed Martban, Huajian Zeng, An Tran, Nguyen Quoc Hung, Jonas Kreutz, Vu Thanh Lam, Ton Manh Kien, Harold Soh

entry.summary: Arena 5.0 is the fifth iteration of an open social navigation benchmarking framework that integrates NVIDIA Isaac Gym for photorealistic, efficient simulation while retaining ROS2 support, environment randomization, and planner APIs. The paper benchmarks state-of-the-art social navigation strategies across diverse generated worlds and human scenarios.

entry.title: WAND: Learning Robust Navigation under Complex Wind Disturbances and Dense Obstacles for Quadrotors

author.name: Zhonghan Tang, Chenhui Li, Shuai Liang, Zhongrui You, Jianan Li, Bin Zhao, Zhigang Wang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: WAND is a reinforcement learning framework for quadrotor navigation in dense obstacle fields under time-varying wind disturbances, explicitly estimating wind-induced disturbance acceleration rather than forcing the policy to infer it from partial observations. The explicit disturbance estimation improves robustness and collision avoidance.

entry.title: SkillWeave: Weaving Heterogeneous Demonstrations into Long-Horizon Manipulation Skills

author.name: Ryosei Tamura, Xiaoxiang Dong, Uksang Yoo, Yuemin Mao, Romina Mir, Jonathan Francis, Jeffrey Ichnowski

entry.summary: SkillWeave combines teleoperation for coarse reaching/transport with kinesthetic teaching for precise contact-rich skills in a heterogeneous demonstration framework for long-horizon dexterous manipulation. It handles the demonstrator-visual-mismatch problem with an object-mask-conditioned diffusion policy using offline segmentation and a lightweight learned mask predictor at deployment.

entry.title: LiteNWM: Efficient Latent World Models for Onboard Visual Navigation in the Wild

author.name: Linkai Liu, Yuntian Zhang, Zhenshan Bing, Chen Chen, Lingjuan Lyu, Shangguang Wang, Mengwei Xu, Dongqi Cai

entry.summary: LiteNWM is a latent navigation world model that shares visual encoding across candidate trajectories and jointly predicts action-conditioned future representations at multiple horizons, with a learned scorer selecting among candidates. On RECON, SCAND, and SACSoN it reduces trajectory error by 17.56% versus NoMaD+NWM-XL while achieving a 128x end-to-end speedup on an RTX 5090.

entry.title: NLAs miss some internalized behaviors

author.name: Andrii Shportko

entry.summary: Andrii Shportko shows that Natural Language Autoencoders, recently hailed in the mech interp community as a scalable unsupervised white-box monitoring breakthrough, reliably detect side tasks given via in-context instructions but mostly miss the same behavior when it is fine-tuned into the model. Using a steganography test case encoding bits via British versus American spellings, the author demonstrates a sharp gap in NLA confession rates between instructed and internalized behavior. This challenges optimistic readings of NLA-based eval-awareness detection results.

entry.title: TaReD: Tool-Aware Recursive Decomposition for Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Wei-Xiang Mao, Zhi-Kai Chen, De-Chuan Zhan, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: TaReD tackles unreliable single-chain agent execution on long-horizon tasks by recursively decomposing them into subtasks matched to available tool capabilities, explicitly handling the case where the tool library is too large to expose in context. The approach aims to prevent error propagation from growing histories and improve tool retrieval under realistic tool-count constraints.

entry.title: Environmental Feedback Modeling Matters: Rethinking Feedback Treatment in Agentic Hindsight Self-Distillation

author.name: Hangxi Guo, Fengyuan Liu, Yue Wang, Yuhua Qi, Haoyi Xiong, Fei Sun, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: The paper rethinks how environmental feedback is used in agentic hindsight self-distillation for RL without rewards, arguing that merely conditioning the teacher on feedback is insufficient. It introduces SELF, a framework that jointly optimizes environmental feedback modeling and hindsight self-distillation, exploiting feedback as rich supervision of environment dynamics.

entry.title: Universal Textual Teaching for LLMs

author.name: Zhanyi Lu, Huan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces UTT, a parameter-update-free knowledge distillation framework that distills teacher-student knowledge gaps into a textual, interpretable, and reusable natural-language artifact called a Primer, identified through paired evaluation of representative gap cases. This enables teaching API-only or costly-to-train models without touching their weights.

entry.title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators

author.name: Julian Chan, Javier Mora Jimenez

entry.summary: This study examines whether LLM scientific agents actually use experimental feedback when selecting fine-tuning configurations for neural operators under limited trial budgets, using controlled interventions to attribute performance. The LLM's first configuration already ranks near the top of the random-search pool, suggesting strong reliance on priors rather than feedback.

entry.title: Beyond Type-checking: Towards Holistic Evaluation of Formal Specification Generation

author.name: Srijith Nair, Aditya Vempaty, Jia Liu, Ashish Jagmohan

entry.summary: Addresses a key weakness in LLM-based verified code generation: type-checked or proof-checked specifications may still misrepresent user intent, so correctness proofs against them are hollow. The authors assemble a unified dataset of 350 Lean tasks to enable holistic evaluation of specification generation beyond mere compilability.

entry.title: RISR: Residual-Informed Scientific Equation Discovery with Large Language Models

author.name: Haobo Li, Wenshuo Zhang, Wenxiao Zhao, Eunseo Jung, Rui Sheng, Yushi Sun, Peiqin Zhuang, Hao Chen, Fenghua Ling

entry.summary: RISR uses residual error patterns to guide LLM-based symbolic regression: a residual encoder compresses inputs, targets, predictions, and residuals into tokens that condition an LLM to propose formulas, while a dual-view relational encoder predicts which candidate corrections are worth fitting. It achieves 63.57% and 38.50% in-distribution accuracy on scientific tasks from LLM-SRBench. The work moves beyond aggregate fit scores by making error structure an explicit signal in equation discovery.

entry.title: La-Ribo: RNA Co-Design via Geometry-Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Runze Ma, Will Hua, Shuangjia Zheng

entry.summary: La-Ribo is a generative framework for joint RNA sequence-structure co-design using geometry-latent flow matching, encoding nucleotide identity and local conformation in residue-wise latents with a shared flow network.
