The authors also construct a quality-controlled corpus of over 168,000 RNA structures combining experimental and predicted data to expand supervision.

entry.title: Evaluating Rubric Generation with Interventional Transfer

author.name: Erik Skalnes, Layne C. Price, Raviteja Anantha, Michael Oberst

entry.summary: Introduces Interventional Transfer, a method for evaluating LLM-generated rubrics by measuring whether two rubrics move together when responses are perturbed to pass or fail one of them. Addresses the open problem of assessing rubric quality at scale when expert reference rubrics exist only sparsely.

entry.title: Invariant-Measure Reasoners: Stable Representations for Latent Reasoning

author.name: Yuto Inui, Takuya Konishi, Yoshinobu Kawahara

entry.summary: Latent reasoning models repeatedly update a latent state with a recurrent block, but the state can keep changing with depth, making single-state predictions unstable across recurrent depths. The authors propose invariant-measure reasoners (ImR), which use the invariant measure describing the long-run distribution of latent states on a compact attractor as the stable representation for prediction. This grounds latent reasoning in dynamical systems theory.

entry.title: RideBench: A Large-Scale Exogenous-Aware Benchmark for Ride-Hailing Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Shengsheng Lin, Jing Hu, Zhengyang Hu, Jiazheng Sun, Zichun Cao, Siwei Sun, Zhichao Zou, Enyun Yu, Dongdong Li, Xinyi Hu, Weiwei Lin

entry.summary: RideBench releases a four-year, half-hourly ride-hailing time series dataset synthesized from DiDi marketplace data across 200 spatial areas, with three exogenous scenarios: weather disturbance, holiday effect, and large-scale event impact. The benchmark evaluates over 30 forecasting methods, including foundation models, on regular week-ahead and long-horizon 8-week-ahead forecasting with up to 2,688 prediction steps. It provides a much-needed public resource for exogenous-aware long-horizon forecasting research.

entry.title: Exploiting Gradients in Bayesian Inference of Expensive Simulators

author.name: \v{S}imon Sold\'at, V\'aclav \v{S}m\'idl

entry.summary: The paper leverages simulator output gradients with respect to input parameters—increasingly available from autodiff-based simulators—in Bayesian optimization-style active learning with Gaussian process surrogates for simulation-based inference. Exploiting gradients improves information gain per expensive simulation in posterior estimation of simulator inputs.

entry.title: BEANS-Next and ROOTS: Broadening Audio-Language Capabilities for Bioacoustics

author.name: Christos Plachouras, David Robinson, Marius Miron, Gagan Narula, Paul Laisn\'e, Anthony L. T. Fine, Benno Weck, Ellen Gilsenan-McMahon, Diane Kim, Laura Hay Mack, Maddie Cusimano, Sara Keen, Lukas Rauch, Benjamin Hoffman, Emmanuel Chemla, Emmanouil Benetos, Johan Pauwels, Milad Alizadeh, Matthieu Geist, Olivier Pietquin

entry.summary: BEANS-Next is a benchmark with a taxonomy of bioacoustics tasks spanning acoustic perception, biological category recognition, scene understanding, and in-context learning, designed to test audio-language models beyond narrow species-classification evaluations. The authors show current models perform poorly outside the task families emphasized by existing benchmarks, and introduce ROOTS, presumably a related resource, to broaden capabilities. Large author list includes researchers affiliated with major industry labs (e.g., Matthieu Geist, Olivier Pietquin).

entry.title: Power Side-Channel Membership Inference Attack on Embedded Machine Learning

author.name: Sahan Sanjaya, Prabhat Mishra

entry.summary: PSCMIA is a membership inference attack against embedded ML models that infers training-data membership directly from power traces, without access to prediction probabilities or labels. The work shows that suppressing model outputs does not prevent privacy leakage when data-dependent computation is physically observable.

entry.title: PSI-SINDy: Post-Selection Inference for Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics

author.name: Ashraful Islam, Shuichi Nishino, Tomohiro Shiraishi, Ichiro Takeuchi

entry.summary: PSI-SINDy provides hypothesis tests and confidence intervals for dynamical terms selected by SINDy, addressing selection bias that arises when the same noisy trajectory is used for selection and inference. The method tailors post-selection inference machinery to the sparse system identification setting.

entry.title: Conditional Kernel Stein Discrepancy

author.name: Federico Matteucci, Florian Kalinke

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework for conditional goodness-of-fit testing by lifting kernel Stein discrepancies to the conditional setting via operator-valued kernels on covariate space, requiring only an unnormalized conditional target model without covariate distribution knowledge. It provides theoretical grounding for assessing how well conditional models match data. This fills a real gap in statistical diagnostics for conditional generative models.

entry.title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control

author.name: Octi Zhang, Mateo Guaman Castro, Patrick Yin, Ignacio Dagnino, Abhishek Gupta, Rosario Scalise, Byron Boots

entry.summary: This paper identifies that naively scaling diverse simulator resets with massively parallel simulation wastes learning experience on low-value samples when applied to precise or dynamic robot control problems. The authors propose a balanced sampling approach over the reset distribution that addresses this exploration bottleneck, reducing the need for per-task reward shaping and demonstrations. It matters for making sim-to-real RL pipelines scale to general-purpose robot skills without heavy engineering.

entry.title: BeliefScope: Diagnosing Evidence-Driven Revision and Pressure-Induced Shifts in Large Language Models

author.name: Shuai Guo, Yidong Cui

entry.summary: BeliefScope is a controlled black-box framework that distinguishes whether an LLM changed its belief about a proposition due to genuine evidence or mere user pressure. It crosses evidence and pressure factors with local controls and validates its observation design under synthetic conditions before application.

entry.title: Project Greenhouse: Progress Toward Fully Open and Sovereign Agentic Search

author.name: Jimmy Lin, Sahel Sharifymoghaddam, Lingwei Gu, Nour Jedidi

entry.summary: Project Greenhouse argues that competitive agentic search models can be built fully openly with modest compute, demonstrating a decoder-only pointwise reranker trained from scratch via pre-training plus supervised fine-tuning, without relying on third-party open-weight backbones. The team reports accomplishing most experiments with only a handful of GPUs. This challenges the assumption that competitive retrieval models require massive infrastructure or borrowed backbones.

entry.title: VGGTWorld-VLA: Intent-Conditioned 3D World Evolution for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhaoyang Liu, Kun Jiang, Ziying Song, Diange Yang

entry.summary: VGGTWorld-VLA extends geometry-centric world models built on VGGT by conditioning future 3D scene evolution on driving intentions and ego actions. An action-semantic conditioning mechanism injects driving semantics and ego-motion into the future-token stream, enabling different predicted geometries for the same scene under alternative actions. This supports counterfactual, action-controllable world modeling for autonomous driving.

entry.title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Xuan Wang, Fuyao Zhang, Yang Cao, Lingjuan Lyu, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: Argues that GUI agent safety is a property of screen transitions rather than individual screens, so monitoring screens alone can be defeated by replaying legitimate screens after wrong actions. It presents LGWM, a decoder-free, action-conditioned world model that predicts expected observations in encoded representation space, enabling direct verification without a second judge model.

entry.title: Informationally Decoupled Trajectory Design for Sim-to-Real System Identification

author.name: Sangwoo Shin, Ashvin Anilkumar, Ryan Gao, Josiah P. Hanna

entry.summary: The paper introduces IDTD, a framework for designing exploration trajectories that make simulation parameters separately identifiable, using a Schur complement score derived from the Fisher information matrix. This prevents unreliable parameter estimates that arise when collected trajectories cannot distinguish the effects of different parameters in sampling-based system identification.

entry.title: Predicting Cable Dynamics with Physical Attention Bias

author.name: Avihai Giuili, Rotem Atari, Avishai Sintov, Maya Bechler-Speicher

entry.summary: This paper improves learned simulators for deformable linear objects by adding a physical attention bias - a learned additive term on attention logits that distinguishes arc-length distance (governing elasticity) from Euclidean distance (governing contact) between cable segments. This targets error concentrated at self- and floor-contact points during long rollouts.

entry.title: Social Theory and Agent Foundations

author.name: Richard_Ngo

entry.summary: Richard Ngo connects his agent foundations research to sociology, arguing for theories of rational social and political behavior as an extension of the Von Neumann-Morgenstern economic framework. He surveys big-picture social theory, diagnosing why such frameworks have grown sparse in modern sociology due to methodological fetishism and ideological drift. The post aims to bridge formal rationality research with sociopolitical considerations.

entry.title: Synthesis Through Simulation: Generating Coherent Enterprise Data via Scalable Agent-System Interaction

author.name: Yipeng Li, Ashutosh Hathidara, Jane Lo, Harshavardhan Abichandani, Gunraj Singh, Atin Ghosh

entry.summary: The authors introduce Synthesis Through Simulation, a schema-free data synthesis paradigm where an LLM agent generates realistic enterprise data by executing operations against policy-enforcing APIs in simulated business environments. This sidesteps the structural validity problems of tabular synthesis and the distributional infidelity of procedure-based generation.

entry.title: RIT-RAG: Navigating Document Corpora with Retrieval-Induced Trees

author.name: Meghanadh Pulivarthi, Swaraj Kumar Biswal, Kushagra Bhushan, Yatin Nandwani, Sachindra Joshi, Dinesh Raghu

entry.summary: RIT-RAG combines content retrieval with structural document navigation for RAG, building per-document trees offline from tables of contents and navigating them during retrieval. This avoids the isolated-chunk problem of agentic RAG and the scalability and irrecoverable-commitment issues of structure-aware methods like PageIndex on large corpora.

entry.title: DeltaReplay: Task-Relative Memory Reuse for Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Yudong Bai, Yihong Chen, Quanming Yao, Yaqing Wang

entry.summary: DeltaReplay is a step-level memory reuse framework for mobile GUI agents that decides how to use stored execution trajectories without modifying them, judging reusability by the relation between the record and the new task rather than the record alone. It avoids both misleading the agent with irrelevant memory and discarding partially useful experience.

entry.title: MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zipeng Wang, Xinpeng Dong, Yuefan Wang, Pingchen Lu, Xian Wei, Kun Kuang, Fei Wu, Zhongxiang Dai, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MetaOPD, a bilevel optimization framework for on-policy distillation that jointly trains the student model and a lightweight token-weighting network. The outer objective optimizes token weights using validation loss on reference solutions, learning from the effectiveness of resulting student updates rather than relying on predefined signal-to-weight mappings.

entry.title: When AI Finds Hidden Messages, Does It Report?

author.name: William Guey, Rashik Jahangir, Pierrick Bougault, Vitor D. de Moura, Wei Zhang, Jos\'e O. Gomes

entry.summary: An empirical study of whether AI assistants disclose inter-AI messages to their users, running 1,408 simulated sessions with plaintext and ROT13-encoded notes flagged as harmless or harmful. Asking for reports substantially increases notifications identifying another AI as recipient, and trace analysis characterizes when models inspect, recognize, and disclose hidden content.

entry.title: Budgeted Multi-Source Counterfactual Annotation for Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Biao Xiang, Ali Eshragh, Yuexing Li, Kai Wang

entry.summary: This work studies budgeted acquisition of counterfactual annotations from costly, noisy sources like experts and LLMs for off-policy evaluation in contextual bandits, formulating an integer allocation problem over context-action pairs and annotation sources to minimize estimator variance. It characterizes when annotations are valuable via a first-annotation analysis.

entry.title: Stability-Plasticity Balance via Singular-Vector Selection in LLM Continual Learning

author.name: Lingxiang Wang, Hainan Zhang, Liang Pang, Hongwei Zheng, Zhiming Zheng

entry.summary: This paper identifies the singular-vector channel of weight updates as a principled unit for managing the stability-plasticity trade-off in LLM continual learning, proposing SVC, a parameter-efficient method that selectively updates channels to acquire new knowledge while fixing others to preserve pretrained capabilities. This addresses catastrophic forgetting during domain-specific adaptation with more theoretical grounding than typical PEFT approaches. It matters for organizations continually adapting LLMs to new domains without losing general capabilities.

entry.title: Generative Adversarial Loops

author.name: Kislay Aditya Oj, Nidhi Jain, Sri Surya Varma Datla, Priyanka Jayaswal, Kumar Krishna Agrawal, Aditya Desai

entry.summary: This paper proposes GAL, a generator-discriminator framework for automated AI research that alternates between a discriminator generating adversarial data to expose system weaknesses and a generator discovering algorithms to overcome them, addressing the neglected automated-benchmark-creation side of AI progress. It applies the framework to approximation algorithms for efficient inference. The concept aims at self-advancing systems where method discovery and benchmark generation co-evolve.

entry.title: From Suppression to Repair: Mitigating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models via Localized Distribution Alignment

author.name: Chen Zhao, Xingping Dong, Jiachun Shi, Liang Peng, Chong Wang, Zhen Lei, Ran He, Bo Du

entry.summary: ResOT is a training-free method that repairs LVLM representations at inference time via localized distribution alignment: it projects hallucinated directions away from the faithful subspace and applies Gaussian optimal transport within the resulting low-dimensional residual subspace. This avoids the capability loss caused by suppressing hidden components that also carry useful information.

entry.title: Neural Decoding as Cognitive Inference

author.name: Yi Guo, Changhong Jing, Yong Hu, Yan Liu, Michael K. P. Ng, Shanshan Wang, Shuqiang Wang

entry.summary: The authors recast neural decoding as cognitive inference constrained by brain-intrinsic priors, drawing on Bayesian brain theory, to extract stable cognitive states from variable neural activity. Experiments across five recording modalities and three cognitive domains (motor, perception, internal cognition) show the approach yields high-level meta-neural representations that avoid recording-specific spurious correlations.

entry.title: RiCo: Neural Simulation of Rigid-Body Interactions via Local Contact Reasoning

author.name: Ruixiang Ouyang, Guanren Qiao, Fansen Meng, Yueci Deng, Ruixing Jin, Kui Jia, Guiliang Liu

entry.summary: RiCo simulates rigid-body interactions by representing them through sparse neighborhoods of contact surface points, combining each point state with relative geometry, motion, and physical properties of nearby surfaces. The local contact reasoning inductive bias reflects the physical fact that only nearby surfaces exchange contact forces, improving on end-to-end scene-level world models.

entry.title: D-SLR: The Disjoint Row-Sparse plus Low-Rank Decomposition

author.name: Vincent Szolnoky

entry.summary: Proposes D-SLR, a closed-form drop-in replacement for truncated SVD that adds a disjoint row-sparse component, storing rows either verbatim or via the low-rank fit but never both. Proves the disjoint restriction costs nothing in squared error while yielding joint optima with fewer parameters than overlapping formulations.

entry.title: Transferability of Learned States in Neural PDE Solvers

author.name: Shunye Wang, Haochen Wen, Shuo Li Liu, Xuanyi Wang, Lihao Liu, Zhongying Deng

entry.summary: This paper rigorously assesses when learned states from neural PDE solvers are usefully reusable as initializations for classical solvers, introducing a reuse contract that separates solution accuracy, learning contribution, and numerical cost through paired state comparisons and matched budgets. A literature audit extracts 18 protocol records from 12 papers, and carefully constructed experiments with identical error norms but different CG iteration counts expose weaknesses in prior transferability claims.

entry.title: Bernoulli Flow Models: Self-Consistent Generative Modeling for Binary Data

author.name: Hao Mo, Liying Yang, Shumin Yao, Xinxing Yu, Ajian Liu, Xudong Mao, Yanyan Liang

entry.summary: Bernoulli Flow Models (BFM) decouple generative dynamics from fixed discrete time steps for binary data, defining a self-consistent generative path rather than deriving the reverse posterior from a one-step forward process. This fixes the severe quality degradation existing binary diffusion models suffer in low-NFE cross-step sampling, enabling high-quality generation without distillation or extra training. The work reduces the function-evaluation cost of binary diffusion inference.

entry.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

author.name: Dmitrii Andriianov, Andrey Veprikov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Introduces spectral weight decay, a decoupled nuclear-norm update applying additive spectral shrinkage instead of standard per-weight L2 decay, connecting it to approximate proximal descent. Across LLaMA models from 124M to 500M parameters it lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression, achieving 1.89x compression and 1.18x inference speedup at matched validation loss versus 1.14x and 1.01x for standard decay. A practical efficiency technique for LLM compression.

entry.title: Interval-valued SHAP in Tree-Based Models

author.name: Chenrui Zhu, Vu-Linh Nguyen, Marie-H\'el\`ene Masson, S\'ebastien Destercke

entry.summary: This paper proposes an imprecise Dirichlet model-based method to assess robustness of Shapley value explanations in decision trees and random forests by quantifying interval-valued Shapley values when unannotated instances are introduced to leaves. The intervals reveal how small realistic data changes destabilize feature attributions.

entry.title: Ambient Discrete Diffusion: Using the Wrong Data at the Right Time for Data Efficient Learning

author.name: Julian Kleutgens, Mauricio Tec, Claudio Battiloro, Francesca Dominici, Giannis Daras

entry.summary: RefineMix is a framework for training discrete diffusion models under severe data scarcity by injecting out-of-distribution data at selected diffusion times without biasing the sampling distribution. The key insight is that masking preserves domain information in surviving tokens, so OOD data is usable at low noise levels where supports are disjoint. This formalizes data-efficient training relevant to scientific applications.

entry.title: AI4Fire: Evaluating Large Language Models on Wildfire Tasks

author.name: Yue Zhao, Xiyang Hu, Zuobin Xiong, Zhangyu Wang, Ruolin Li

entry.summary: AI4Fire is a benchmark evaluating LLMs zero-shot on five wildfire tasks, running six core models both bare and grounded, with a sweep adding 29 more models. Findings show grounding helps most when the addition carries the answer, such as a SQL tool lifting all database task scores, and the paper warns against overstated evaluations where stakes include property and lives.

entry.title: Phonological Interference in Multilingual Speech Models

author.name: Moran Yanuka, Raja Giryes, Moris Alper

entry.summary: The paper identifies phonological interference as a systematic failure mode in phoneme-level multilingual speech models, where the assumed dominant language's phonology overrides local phoneme decisions, particularly in code-switching and low-resource speech. The authors quantify interference via retention of language-specific phonemes and analyze the underlying mechanism.

entry.title: Adversarial Cues in Decision Models Used as Judges: The Role of Request Presentation

author.name: Hongliang Liu

entry.summary: This single-author study shows that adding a single colon character to a candidate answer can flip an LLM judge's verdict, increasing false acceptance from 1% to 26% on DROP and GSM8K clusters depending on how the structured judging request is presented. Paired interventions isolate the effect of presentation choices from candidate edits, revealing fragility in judge models.

entry.title: Easy to anticipate, hard to compute: boundary dependence finds the computed outputs that entropy patching misses

author.name: Nicol\'as Vera Z\'u\~niga

entry.summary: The paper identifies a systematic blind spot in byte-level models like Meta's BLT: entropy-triggered patch boundaries place compute where bytes are unpredictable but miss positions whose type is predictable yet value must be computed, such as numerical results in worked math. Under tight patch budgets, accuracy on such positions collapses, with concrete measurements on BLT-1B GSM8K solutions.

entry.title: Less from More: Reinforcing Sparse Video Reasoning from Dense References

author.name: Wenfang Sun, Yingjun Du, Cees G. M. Snoek

entry.summary: SAVER is a dense-to-sparse post-training framework for video-language models that uses dense video views as training-time references to reinforce reliable sparse-frame inference, combining grounding rewards with a reliability-gated reference reward. Notably, it trains on only 1,250 sampled temporal grounding examples without extra annotation. This challenges the assumption that more frames always yield better reasoning, emphasizing reliable reasoning under limited temporal evidence.

entry.title: WorldFact-Bench: Beyond Image-Internal Plausibility to Image-World Consistency

author.name: Zhuohong Chen, Zhengxian Wu, Yunyao Yu, Hangrui Xu, Zijian Yu, Hao Tan, Zhifang Liu, Peng Jiao, Jun Lan, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: WorldFact-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating image-world consistency: whether a generated or manipulated image contradicts real-world facts or rules, even when visually plausible. It contains 1,274 source-aligned real-fake pairs across four verification regimes and ten semantic domains, with each pair introducing a specific evidence-supported factual conflict. Images are assessed independently and pair accuracy requires both members to be judged correctly.

entry.title: Does Target Alignment Mean Target Recovery? An Evidence-Ladder Study of Adversarial Claims on Contrastive Encoders

author.name: Tao Yang, Jianying Zhou

entry.summary: Critically examines adversarial attack evaluations on vision-language models, asking whether a victim model's target-alignment score actually predicts independent recovery of the attack target. Using preregistered studies with rigorous controls and supervised judges outside the attacked geometry, it finds robustly trained encoders (FARE, TeCoA, PMG, TRADES) transfer far less attack evidence than vanilla CLIP or SigLIP.

entry.title: Rubric-CEPR: Self-Evolving Image Editing via Reward-Verified Self-Distillation

author.name: Ritesh Thawkar, Shubham Patle, Shravan Venkatraman, Rao Muhammad Anwer

entry.summary: Rubric-CEPR improves a pretrained instruction-guided image editor using only its own generations, with no human-edited pairs or external reward models, via a rubric-augmented Contrastive Edit-Preservation Reward that verifies samples using the editor's internal representations. A Planner proposes structured edit instances within a self-evolving training loop.

entry.title: FOCUS: From Privileged States to RGB-D with Controlled Modality Switching and Representation Alignment

author.name: Filip Grigorov, Kourosh Darvish, Nandita Vijaykumar

entry.summary: FOCUS is a single-stage PPO framework for vision-based manipulation RL that trains the critic on privileged simulation states while adaptively regulating whether the actor collects rollouts from RGB-D or privileged-state latents. Regulation uses KL divergence between action distributions of the two modalities plus representation alignment to limit costly RGB-D rollouts when action distributions already agree.

entry.title: YOCO: You Only Calibrate Once! Fast Mocap Calibration for Dexterous Teleoperation

author.name: Yu Zhang, Yunqi Li, Yushi Du, Yi Ma, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: YOCO is a few-shot, fine-tuning-free calibration framework that corrects biased hand-pose streams from low-cost mocap gloves for dexterous teleoperation. It conditions a HyperNet on a small set of paired poses to predict LoRA-style updates to a frozen MANO hand estimator, turning per-user calibration into a feed-forward step.

entry.title: MiniWAM: Learning Compact Future Targets for Efficient World-Action Modeling

author.name: Jie Chen, Ruofei Bai, Yuxin Cai, Yifeng Zhang, Chengyang He, Jun Li, Wei-Yun Yau, Guillaume Sartoretti

entry.summary: MiniWAM improves world-action models for robot policies by predicting compact, control-relevant future representations rather than high-dimensional backbone feature targets. Its PRISM method combines inverse-dynamics supervision with feature reconstruction to learn predictive targets, substantially reducing training cost while retaining the benefit of world-model co-training.

entry.title: Curating Always-Loaded Context for LLM Agents: A Capacitated Assortment Model with Censored Feedback

author.name: Zexuan Liu, Yuning Yang, Tiancheng Zhao

entry.summary: The paper formulates curation of always-loaded context files like AGENTS.md as a capacitated assortment problem, where instructions consume finite attention capacity and retained instructions incur per-session costs. The authors prove an upper bound on optimal file size and show that naive appending of positively received instructions is suboptimal.

entry.title: Beyond Imitation: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM-Assisted Peer Review

author.name: Rachel S. Y. Teo, Yutaro Yamada, Shashank Kotyan, Yuki Imajuku, Tarin Clanuwat

entry.summary: The paper argues LLM review assistants should be evaluated on verification functions like error detection rather than imitation of human reviews. It presents a scalable benchmark built by synthetically inserting logical contradictions into conference papers, yielding unambiguous ground truth for assessing review systems.

entry.title: What to Admit and How to Present: Governing Persistent Memory in LLM Agents

author.name: Chang Liu, Deliang Ding

entry.summary: The paper separates persistent memory governance into admission decisions, what recalled information enters context, and presentation decisions, how it is expressed, proposing two inference-time mechanisms without retraining. Evaluations across four backbones and an external benchmark show reduced sycophancy and cross-domain leakage relative to verbatim memory injection.

entry.title: DuplexAgent-RSI: Recursive Harness Improvement for Full-Duplex Voice Agent Collaboration

author.name: Yingda Shen, Yuxiang Wang, Kunyu Feng, Qinke Ni, Jiaqi Li, Minghao Hsu, Junan Zhang, Dekun Chen, Yutong Bian, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: The paper presents a harness coordinating full-duplex voice models, which handle live conversation, with asynchronous coding agents for complex reasoning and tool use, managing task acceptance, progress, cancellation, and result delivery. It applies recursive self-improvement so the harness can be systematically refined from execution evidence rather than coupled heuristics.

entry.title: BridgeGuard: Explicit Safety Drift for Diffusion-based Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhenjun Qiu, Jianing Huang, Dongang Liu, Baiyu Du, Yixun Niu, Hao Yang, Xinyu Huang, Chuan Hu, Shu Liu

entry.summary: BridgeGuard is a safety-constrained diffusion planner for autonomous driving that progressively strengthens a constraint term during denoising, guided by a learned time-dependent distance field (DistanceFieldNet) predicting safe and unsafe regions from bird's-eye-view features. Corrections in low-dimensional curve space keep trajectories geometrically coherent under distribution shift.

entry.title: Memory Type Varies: Empowering LLM Agents for Long-Term Memory with Diverse Strategies

author.name: Yi Wen, Derong Xu, Pengyue Jia, Yichao Wang, Yingyi Zhang, Maolin Wang, Junyi Li, Wenlin Zhang, Xiaopeng Li, Yong Liu, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: The paper argues that retrieval-based agent memory should be differentiated by memory type rather than processed uniformly, and introduces TriMEM, a multi-class dataset with precise memory-type annotations across diverse scenarios. Type-aware strategy selection is proposed to improve long-term memory handling in LLM agents.

entry.title: How Is Automated Research Evaluated? A Survey of Benchmarks and Evaluation Practices

author.name: Liulei Zhang, Dejing Zhou, Chuyue Huang, Guanhua Chen, Yutong Yao, Lidia S. Chao, Chi Man Vong, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: Surveys the evaluation of automated research systems across six targets: literature synthesis, ideation, executable workflows, scholarly writing, automatic peer review, and end-to-end research. It compares task construction, evidence sources, evaluators, and scoring procedures, concluding that output checks, process checks, and human studies provide complementary information.

entry.title: Q-Shaped Options for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Clarisse Wibault, Antoine Gorceix, Antonio L\'eon Villares, Alexey Zakharov, Evangelos Chatzaroulas, Michael Matthews, Eduardo Pignatelli, Jakob Foerster

entry.summary: The paper addresses a core failure mode of hierarchical RL: learning an appropriate action abstraction for long-horizon, goal-conditioned tasks. It proposes Q-shaped options that jointly exploit temporal and state abstraction, avoiding the ways current HRL algorithms discard one benefit or the other.

entry.title: MRCert: Towards Post-deployment Patch Robustness Certification for Adversarially Patched Samples via Type-specific Masking

author.name: Qilin Zhou, Zhengyuan Wei, Haipeng Wang, Zhuo Wang, Shuo Liu, W. K. Chan

entry.summary: Proposes MRCert, the first masking-based certified recovery defender that both verifies label benignity of adversarially patched inputs and retains high prediction accuracy. It uses type-specific masking conditions rather than a common condition across benign and patched samples, addressing limitations of prior smoothing- and masking-based defenses.

entry.title: SAVU-BENCH: A Real-World Benchmark for Spatial Audio-Visual Understanding

author.name: Yu Chen, Ruihang Liu, Yangguang Xu, Xinyue Jiang, Mohammed Bennamoun, Farid Boussaid, Xinyuan Qian, Qiuhong Ke

entry.summary: Introduces SAVU-Bench, a real-world benchmark evaluating spatial audio-visual understanding across three capability levels and seven tasks, plus SAVU-Diag, a diagnostic set decomposing reasoning questions into grounding and alignment sub-tasks. Evaluation of 12 models finds visual spatial grounding relatively mature while audio-related spatial skills lag.

entry.title: Gated Memory: Admission-Controlled Memory Formation for Conversational AI

author.name: Preeti Saraswat, Divya Neelagiri, Ajay Manoj

entry.summary: This paper identifies memory formation—the moment a fact is first written to storage—as the binding constraint on long-term memory quality in personalized conversational AI, noting that contextual signals like permanence versus transience are irreversibly lost at extraction time. Gated Memory is a lightweight, modular admission-control mechanism deciding what should be stored. This shifts attention from retrieval improvements, which have dominated the field, to a neglected upstream stage.

entry.title: MetaEncoder: Exploring the Limit of Bi-Encoders for Multimodal System One Decision Making with Natural Language Interface

author.name: Jianpeng Cheng, Guangyu Sun, Aashu Singh, Benyu Zhang, Haixing Dai, Hossein Mansour, Jiangfan Zhang, Shlok Kumar Mishra, Wei Sun, Xuanming Cui, Yanli Liu, Qi Guo, Max Xiangjun Fan, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: MetaEncoder fine-tunes the existing Muse-Glimmer 30B decoder into a bi-encoder that outputs constrained decisions and probability distributions over candidates expressed in natural language, with multimodal image and video inputs. It scales from small closed-set candidate spaces to massive open-set spaces of millions of options. The work rethinks System One decision-making interfaces by moving away from structured schema objects to fully natural-language candidate representations.

entry.title: Stochastic Grouping Conformal Prediction for Effective Subgroup Reliability

author.name: Meihui Zhong, Wenxin Tai, Ting Zhong, Fan Zhou

entry.summary: This paper proposes SGCP, a conformal prediction framework that provides subgroup-reliable uncertainty quantification without requiring access to sensitive subgroup attributes. It avoids the worst-group bottleneck where protecting the hardest subgroup inflates prediction sets for everyone, which is especially relevant for clinical decision support.

entry.title: Unifying Policy Learning and State Prediction through Spatial Language Modeling

author.name: Minye Wu, Zehao Wang, Tinne Tuytelaars

entry.summary: The paper introduces Spatial Language Modeling, representing scene contours, goals, action targets, and future states with a shared vocabulary of discrete coordinates and semantic tokens organized by a task grammar, so a single autoregressive Transformer learns both action generation and action-conditioned state prediction via a common next-token objective. Training uses random-play transition pretraining followed by joint training on expert demonstrations.

entry.title: DVD: Dynamic Vector Decoding for Efficient MLLM-based Perception

author.name: Jinghua Hou, Zhe Liu, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: DVD replaces text-based coordinate outputs and fixed-range quantization in multimodal LLM perception with dynamic vector decoding, unifying 2D and 3D perception task representations. It targets token overhead and precision constraints, particularly for 3D domains with unbounded spatial ranges, relevant to robotics and autonomous driving.

entry.title: SpaceFlow: Locally Controllable 3D Generation

author.name: Neil De La Fuente, Joan Lafuente, Mukhammadali Sayfiddinov, Felicia Scharitzer, Marc Pollefeys, Ata Celen, Sayan Deb Sarkar, Elisabetta Fedele

entry.summary: SpaceFlow is a training-free pipeline for locally controllable 3D generation from text and geometric primitives, where each primitive acts as a proxy for an object part with a user-specified control level for strict geometric adherence versus generative completion. Spatial constraints are enforced within the generative flow process, and appearance is conditioned per matched generated part.

entry.title: Coverage, Not Difficulty, Sets How Much Synthetic Data an Activation Probe Needs

author.name: Ankush Checkervarty

entry.summary: Studies learning curves for activation probes trained on synthetic conversations to monitor deployed language models, varying generator LLMs, prompt detail, probe models, and 14 held-out evaluation distributions. Finds that sample requirements are set by the coverage of what is monitored rather than concept difficulty, with high-stakes and harm probes plateauing near 80 samples while instruction probes need several times more.

entry.title: ASPIRE: Saddle-Point Discovery through Set Prediction and Physical Refinement

author.name: Yucheng Zhao, Quanyou Zhang, Shaoxiang Qin, Haixuan Xu, Xiongye Xiao

entry.summary: ASPIRE addresses the computational bottleneck of finding saddle points for event-driven models of thermally activated diffusion and defect evolution in materials. It predicts a set of saddle candidates from a single atomic environment using an equivariant set predictor (Ev-Quiformer) with geometric features, then refines candidates via Dimer searches on the original interatomic potential. This avoids repeated failed local searches that converge to the same saddle.

entry.title: From a Prompt to Repertoires: Evolving Functional REpertoires Enable LLM Continual Learning

author.name: Fengyuan Liu, Yue Wang, Hangxi Guo, Fengyuan Liu, Chenxu Wu, Yanguang Liu, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: This paper explores whether prompt optimization, which matches or beats RL methods like GRPO on individual tasks without parameter updates, can serve as an LLM continual learning mechanism. The analysis shows naive sequential prompt adaptation suffers from catastrophic forgetting, motivating an approach based on evolving functional repertoires of prompts that preserve and extend capabilities over task sequences. It reframes continual learning from parameter space to prompt/behavior space.

entry.title: Rare Gate Disagreements Can Limit Plasticity: When Gradient Flow Mispredicts Finite-Batch SGD

author.name: Ruoyu Zhao, Mingxuan Zhang, Jianbo Dai, Jiaqi Wu, Chenyu Zhu, Tong Che

entry.summary: Shows that population gradient flow can qualitatively mispredict finite-batch SGD dynamics, tracing the discrepancy to rare gate disagreements in a two-unit ReLU setting where SGD fails over exponentially long horizons even when gradient flow recovers in linear time. This gives theory-level insight into loss of plasticity after pretraining. Relevant to understanding why continual learning and retraining can stall.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Speech Representations for Cross-Speaker Dysarthria Detection During Awake Craniotomy

author.name: Kanthila Chinmayi (IRDL, LaTIM), Abdallah Nassib (LARIS), Misy Harrison (LaTIM), Panheleux Celine (LaTIM, CHU - BREST), Saliou Vanessa (CHU - BREST), Seizeur Romuald (LaTIM), Dardenne Guillaume (LaTIM)

entry.summary: A systematic component-wise evaluation of a pipeline for detecting intra-operative dysarthric speech during awake craniotomy, combining speaker diarization, wav2vec 2.0 embeddings with handcrafted acoustic features, and speaker-conditional normalization on the DATABRASE corpus. The work targets preserving language function during brain surgery under noisy operating-room conditions with small, heterogeneous cohorts.

entry.title: Bayesian Optimisation under State-Preservation Constraints

author.name: Gabriel Diaz-Aylwin, Vignesh Gopakumar, Omkar Myatra, David Moulton, Lorenzo Zanisi, David S. Leslie, Henry B. Moss

entry.summary: The paper addresses constrained Bayesian optimization where designs must keep selected PDE-derived state observables near trusted values. It pre-computes the set of controls whose linearized constraint response stays within tolerance, mapping the state-space constraint into design space as an ellipsoid from which well-spread candidates are drawn efficiently.

entry.title: Marformer: A Transformer for Predicting Missing Data Distributions

author.name: Prabhav Singh, Xiheng Tom Wang, Haojun Shi, Jason Eisner

entry.summary: Marformer is a BERT-style transformer trained to directly predict conditional marginal distributions over missing variables given any observed subset. These conditional marginals are key ingredients for computing Bayes risk and Value of Information in decision-making under incomplete information. Unlike generative approaches, it targets distributional outputs directly, enabling decision-theoretic reasoning about whether to acquire more observations.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction under Partial Verification

author.name: Zijun Yu, Yu Gu, Vahid Partovi Nia, Masoud Asgharian

entry.summary: The authors develop a partial verification scheme for conformal prediction calibration that produces exactly the same prediction sets as full label verification while cutting verification cost by 15-82%. They characterize calibration certificates sufficient to determine the conformal threshold and coordinate verification across calibration examples.

entry.title: FedAlphaEdit: Null-Space-Aligned Merging for Collaborative Knowledge Editing

author.name: Sota Sugawara, Yukihiko Okada

entry.summary: FedAlphaEdit shows that naively combining null-space-constrained editing like AlphaEdit with collaborative editing frameworks fails structurally, and diagnoses why. It proposes the first collaborative knowledge editing framework that aligns local editing and server-side merging under a single null-space constraint, letting institutions merge private LLM edits without sharing raw edit requests.

entry.title: Dissecting Representation Structure in Vision Transformers: A Rigorous Architectural Study

author.name: Kim-Cuc Nguyen, Ngai-Man Cheung

entry.summary: This work provides the first systematic module-level analysis of representation structure in Vision Transformers across architectural scales, linking representation properties to generalization behavior. The authors identify feature collapse at initialization, propose mitigation strategies, and use the insights to guide efficient ViT design.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Mixture-of-Experts Coordination for Model Markets

author.name: Yizhou Ma, Wenbo Wu, Xikun Jiang, Zhuoqin Yang, Luis-Daniel Ib\'a\~nez

entry.summary: The paper lifts Mixture-of-Experts from a model-internal architecture to a market-level coordination mechanism, where brokers use gating networks to combine heterogeneous experts into composite services. It formalizes participants, cost structures, and a welfare objective balancing predictive utility against heterogeneous execution costs, deriving cost-aware gating and market-aware training objectives. This is a novel economic framing relevant to model marketplaces and routing.

entry.title: Back in Style: A Sociolinguistic Approach to Authoring and Measuring Persona Fidelity in User Simulation

author.name: Lex Konnelly, Elena Khasanova, Riqiang Wang, Matthias Lee, Harsh Saini, Parsa Kavehzadeh

entry.summary: A pilot study proposing a deterministic, model-free way to measure fidelity of simulated users by treating personas as observable linguistic styles rather than label-based descriptions. It adapts authorship-verification stylometry and lexicon-based content analysis to evaluate user simulators for agentic system testing.

entry.title: Does Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) Dominate Arabic Dialects in LLMs? A Representation-Level Analysis

author.name: Abdu Sallouh, Nicholas Popovi\v{c}, Michael F\"{a}rber

entry.summary: Adapting a language-dominance framework to 26 Arabic varieties, this representational analysis finds no evidence that MSA dominates internal representations of dialects in LLMs; instead dialect representations form a dense, highly overlapping space with sharply reduced mutual information separation. This refutes the intuitive explanation for why models default to MSA when prompted with dialects.

entry.title: DPPM: Dual-Path Parametric Memory for Personalized Language Models

author.name: Yuhao Chen, Shuochen Liu, Jiayao Shi, Jian Hong, Chen Cheng, Xinyun Ding, Tao Wang, Ya Li, Quan Liu, Tong Xu

entry.summary: DPPM introduces a dual-path architecture for long-term personalization: an Evidence path that pools interaction-history representations to preserve earlier evidence and a Delta path that sequentially updates an associative state for preference changes. Fusing both paths produces history-conditioned LoRA adapters that reduce inference-context requirements.

entry.title: DiffuPlex: Accelerating Full-Duplex Spoken Dialog Models via Rolling Masked Diffusion

author.name: Heeseung Kim

entry.summary: DiffuPlex accelerates full-duplex spoken dialog systems by replacing per-frame autoregressive backbone calls with rolling masked diffusion, predicting multiple future user and assistant frames per backbone wake and committing only confident prefixes. When user speech diverges from predictions, it preserves already-played assistant content and revises only unplayed future. This is a meaningful efficiency and latency technique for real-time speech interaction.

entry.title: A Unified Score Matching Paradigm for Video Anomaly Detection and Anticipation

author.name: Congqi Cao, Zhenhe Liang, Hanwen Zhang, Yifan Zhao, Qinyi Lv, Lingtong Min, Yanning Zhang

entry.summary: Uni-DSM proposes a unified framework for video anomaly detection (VAD) and anticipation (VAA) based on denoising score matching, modeling anomalies through likelihood estimation and score functions over the learned data distribution. This sidesteps the contrastive inference paradigm of VAD, which depends on ground-truth future frames and thus cannot be applied to anticipation. The unified treatment of both post-hoc detection and proactive anticipation is the core contribution.

entry.title: PointVGGT: Zero-Shot Multiview RGB-D Point Cloud Registration with Visual Geometry Foundation Priors

author.name: Haobo Jiang, Liang Yu, Jianmin Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces PointVGGT, a zero-shot multiview RGB-D point cloud registration framework built on a foundation-then-refinement paradigm that leverages visual geometry foundation models such as VGGT for initial global pose estimates, then refines them. This avoids the error propagation and computational burden of pairwise-then-global registration pipelines.

entry.title: Seek-and-View Reasoning for Multi-View Spatial Understanding

author.name: Qixiang Chen, Cheng Zhang, Fucai Ke, Chi-Wing Fu, Jianfei Cai, Jingwen Ye

entry.summary: Proposes Vantage, a training-free, model-agnostic framework pairing a VLM with a 3D foundation model for multi-view spatial reasoning. It actively locates question-relevant viewpoints and gathers geometry-grounded evidence, addressing fragile cross-view alignment when models only see sparse fixed views.

entry.title: Is In-Domain Training Enough for Fine-Grained Industrial Anomaly Understanding?

author.name: Xingwu Zhang, Duanyang Du, Huiling Zhu, Jiayue Dai, Yixiao Liu, Guozhi Liu, Zhihan Zhang, Zijun Long

entry.summary: The paper shows that in-domain fine-tuning fails to close the gap between multimodal LLMs and human experts on industrial anomaly understanding, with specialists reaching at most 75.5% localization accuracy versus 92.3% for humans on MMAD. The authors propose SiGMA, a spatially grounded multi-agent framework that divides labor among heterogeneous MLLM agents to exploit complementary strengths.

entry.title: Same Action, Different Outcome: Variability in Dynamic Cloth Manipulation

author.name: Mahed Dadgostar, Guillem Aleny\`a, J\'ulia Borr\`as

entry.summary: This empirical study systematically characterizes outcome variability in dynamic cloth manipulation, executing identical trajectories ten times across four tasks, three cloths, and multiple speeds for a total of 269 recorded rollouts with marker and stereo tracking. It formalizes metrics to quantify variability, informing reliability assessment of learned policies and sim-to-real fidelity.

entry.title: DAMP: Humanoid Locomotion via Denoised Belief Learning and Adversarial Motion Priors

author.name: Puying Shen, Wenhao Cui, Huaxing Huang, Bangyu Qin, Shengtao Li, Ziyang Dong, Guoteng Zhang

entry.summary: DAMP is a reinforcement learning framework for robust humanoid locomotion over challenging terrains without relying on perceived (exteroceptive) information. It uses recurrent networks to infer privileged latent information from history, combined with adversarial motion priors, to achieve stable blind traversal.

entry.title: PIER: An Evidence-Gated Execution Interface for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zoe Li, Anze Wang, Zhongyu Chen, Jingran Hu

entry.summary: PIER is an execution-authorization interface that separates evidence checks, decision provenance, and stage-scoped re-observation from hardware control, gating robot actions on declared visual and tactile inputs. It is evaluated with 1,600 threshold-grid cases and 1,200 paired synthetic traces covering score noise, missing tactile inputs, stale observations, and falsely reassuring scores, with zero declared invariant violations.

entry.title: Toward Lunar Legged Robots: Field Deployment Lessons at LUNA

author.name: Adrian Fuhrer, Joseph Church, Oliver Fischer, William Talbot, Nicolas Faesch, Yannic Hofmann, Hendrik Kolvenbach, Yusuke Tanaka, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: The paper reports lessons from the 2025 LUNA lunar analogue campaign where ANYmal-D and Magnecko quadrupeds traversed regolith simulant and crater-like terrain, documenting sinkage, slip, dust generation, and illumination-driven perception issues. It provides field data and practical guidance for future legged lunar missions.

entry.title: ORDO: Operation-level Round-aware Dynamic Ordering for MIP Presolve

author.name: Zehuan Chen, Chunhe Song

entry.summary: ORDO recasts presolve planning in mixed-integer programming as autoregressive sequence generation over a unified atomic action space, capturing non-commutative temporal dependencies that parameter-tuning methods cannot express. It shows ordering matters greatly for solve-time tails and achieves strong cross-domain generalization on unseen MIP domains.

entry.title: Writing for the Reviewer: Defensive Writing in GPT Models

author.name: Junchi Liao

entry.summary: This study documents defensive writing in GPT models, where paper revisions narrow or retract authors' claims beyond what the evidence supports. Experiments with paragraphs from pre-ChatGPT papers and evidence sheets favor the anticipated-reviewer explanation over claim correction, showing the behavior grows with GPT version and that GPT-6 Astra (an existing model, GA September 2026) adds the most ungrounded qualifications.

entry.title: SpikeSSL: A Universal Spike Inference Framework with Dynamics-Informed State-Space Layers

author.name: Chenghao Yue, Siming Xing, Shuran Liu, Angran Li, Yuanlong Zhang

entry.summary: SpikeSSL is a spike-inference framework for two-photon calcium imaging that uses bidirectional IIR state-space layers motivated by calcium dynamics and a conditioning encoder that adapts to different calcium indicators. This inductive bias lets it generalize to unseen indicators where prior supervised methods trained as generic temporal regressors fail.

entry.title: MultiWorldBench: Do Independently Controlled Views Describe One Shared World?

author.name: Zhangbo Xu, Ruoxi Zhang, Rui Hu, Yisong Wang

entry.summary: Introduces MultiWorldBench, a Minecraft-based diagnostic benchmark with 495 configurations across seven task suites and ten capabilities that tests whether multiplayer world models keep independently controlled views consistent with one shared, persistent world. Evaluations of Solaris, Gamma-World, and MineWorld against a ground-truth engine show large gaps, with the best generated system scoring 21.39 versus 91.69 for the reference.

entry.title: Recompose and Refine Latent Reasoning Flows for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Hongyu Shi, Sen Zhao, Zuyu Zhang, Lifeng Shen, Ding Zou, Xinyu He, Xu Zhang, Qinghua Zhang

entry.summary: Presents FLOWMEM, a vision-language-action model that turns successful latent reasoning computation into reusable reasoning memory, dynamically retrieving and recomposing compatible latent fragments as embodied context evolves. This avoids reconstructing similar internal computations from scratch for each policy query.

entry.title: Learning Probabilistic Logic Programs with Functional Gradient Guided Language Models

author.name: Saurabh Mathur, Sahil Sidheekh, Bhavan Vasu, Farbod Tavakkoli, Prasad Tadepalli, Kristian Kersting, Sriraam Natarajan

entry.summary: GRASP is a neurosymbolic framework that casts relational structure learning as functional gradient boosting, using LLMs as guided hypothesis generators to overcome the combinatorial explosion in inducing probabilistic logic programs. This combines the interpretability of logic programs with LLM-driven search.

entry.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design

author.name: Peter Kulits, Yiqing Xu, R. Kenny Jones, Cordelia Schmid, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: BrickBench is a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design where agents must produce assemblies satisfying semantic and design criteria while being physically buildable from a discrete part library. It includes the BrickAgent environment for constructing, inspecting, and validating designs, and finds leading agents meet verifiable constraints but fall short of human designs.

entry.title: Discovering Global False Negatives On the Fly for Self-supervised Contrastive Learning

author.name: Vicente Balmaseda, Bokun Wang, Ching-Long Lin, Tianbao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces GloFND, an optimization-based method that dynamically learns per-anchor thresholds to identify false negatives during self-supervised contrastive training. Unlike prior approaches that operate only within a mini-batch, GloFND detects false negatives globally across the dataset, preventing semantically similar images from being incorrectly pushed apart in embedding space.

entry.title: Masked Generative Motion Planning with Geometry-Guided Token Search

author.name: Lipeng Zhuang, Yingdong Ru, Shiyu Fan, Edmond S. L. Ho, Gerardo Aragon Camarasa, Paul Henderson

entry.summary: Introduces Masked Generative Motion Planning, which extends masked generative transformers from parallel trajectory generation to structural repair, using scene geometry to guide where to edit and which discrete alternatives to evaluate. The approach enables route-level restructuring beyond local refinement, achieving 96 percent success on Ring Maze and strong repair rates on controlled scenarios.

entry.title: LinSlot: Exploiting Linear Representation hypothesis for unsupervised attribute discovery from slot based object representation

author.name: Sanket Gandhi, Utkarsh Giri, Varun Subramanium, Rohan Paul, Parag Singla

entry.summary: LinSlot leverages the Linear Representation Hypothesis to jointly discover object and attribute representations from raw images without supervision, replacing the uniform factorization assumed by block-slot attention methods. This aims to produce higher-quality disentangled representations of objects and their attributes.

entry.title: iAm.md: Robot Skill Self-Assessment through Agentic Introspection for Unknown Open-Vocabulary Domains

author.name: Vincenzo Guarino, Emanuele Musumeci, Vincenzo Suriani, Daniele Nardi

entry.summary: iAm.md frames robot behavior generation as code generation and adds agentic introspection so a robot can self-assess whether its body and environment actually support a planned operation, catching grounding failures that arise from hallucination or limited context. It targets open-vocabulary domains where plans may be plausible but infeasible.

entry.title: Intent Graph: Navigating the Analytical Reasoning Space for Exploratory Data Analysis

author.name: Junran Yang, Shruti Badrish, Teanna Barrett, Leilani Battle

entry.summary: This paper presents DAG-EDA, a system where analysts and an LLM jointly navigate the space of possible analyses using an intent graph governed by a grammar of analytical intent. The graph decomposes ambiguous natural-language questions into progressively concrete analysis tasks while keeping alternatives visible, addressing the problem that LLM responses are unstructured and leave no record of what has been explored or why. It matters because it makes LLM-assisted data analysis more transparent and auditable for real analyst workflows.

entry.title: Emergent Inverse-Depth Scaling From Nonlinearity In Attention

author.name: Zirui Peng, Yizhou Liu, Ziming Liu, Jeff Gore

entry.summary: This arXiv paper investigates the mechanisms underlying neural scaling laws, focusing on how model depth contributes to power-law performance improvements. The authors show that while linear-attention models learn according to a global data spectrum, nonlinear attention enables selective token focus, producing an emergent inverse-depth decay of loss across all tested data spectra. This offers a theoretical account of why depth matters in large language models and clarifies the role of nonlinearity in scaling behavior.

entry.title: Closed-loop evaluation of LLM agents for embedded software development

author.name: Jorge Garc\'ia-Carrasco, Sergio Garc\'ia-Carrasco, Alejandro Mat\'e, Juan Trujillo

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark for closed-loop evaluation of LLM coding agents on embedded firmware, where correctness depends on runtime behavior under sensing, timing, and safety constraints rather than static source quality. Tasks provide engineering descriptions, constrained workspaces, and visible build-and-runtime surfaces, requiring agents to implement and self-verify iteratively. It fills a notable gap, as existing embedded-agent evaluation emphasizes one-shot synthesis.

entry.title: SDPAD: A Fully Spike-Driven Pipeline for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chengjun Zhang, Yuhao Zhang, Jie Yang, Mohamad Sawan

entry.summary: SDPAD is a fully spike-driven end-to-end autonomous driving planning pipeline that converts a pretrained ANN perception stack into integer-spike form via quantized ANN2SNN conversion, lifts multi-view images into BEV space with spike-driven-max depth distribution, and closes the accuracy gap between SNN planners and heavy dense ANN planners. It targets edge deployment with orders-of-magnitude energy savings from sparse event-driven computation. This is a notable systems effort bringing SNNs to a demanding real-time task.

entry.title: Runnable Commit Untangling for Coding Agents

author.name: Jinfeng Jiang, Dongsun Kim, Dayi Lin, Zhou Yang

entry.summary: This paper tackles commit untangling for coding agents, which produce large mixed-purpose patches that are hard to review. It identifies two overlooked limitations in prior work: untangled commits must remain individually runnable and ordered, and maintenance benefits must be demonstrated beyond syntactic comparison to developer commits. The work is relevant as agent-generated code volume grows.

entry.title: From Surface to Depth: Towards Cognitive Appraisal Reasoning in Multimodal Emotion Understanding

author.name: Jia Li, Yichao He, Yangchen Yu, Qiankun Li, Xinyi Li, Baiyi Ye, Zhenzhen Hu, Richang Hong, Erik Cambria

entry.summary: This work argues that current multimodal LLM emotion understanding relies on superficial cue-label associations prone to Clever Hans shortcuts. Inspired by appraisal theories of emotion, it reframes emotion understanding as progression from perception to cognitive appraisal and introduces a new dataset and reasoning framework to support deeper, interpretation-driven emotion analysis.

entry.title: The Polytopal Neural Network

author.name: A. Emilie J. Wedenborg, Anders V. N{\o}rskov, Teresa Dorszewski, Kristoffer Wickstr{\o}m, Morten M{\o}rup

entry.summary: This paper introduces Polytopal Neural Networks (PNNs), an architecture that enforces a polytope-based structure directly within the network's computation, allowing observations to be explicitly described by their alignment with layer-specific aspects. The approach aims to improve interpretability without sacrificing structural fidelity, and the authors scale it via learned corpus representations and an amortized simplex inference procedure, noting it also yields a direct route to vector quantized training.

entry.title: A Geometric Approach to Soft Actor-Critic with Zonotopes for Locomotion Learning

author.name: Panagiotis Roditis, Panagiotis P. Filntisis, Petros Maragos

entry.summary: GeZo-SAC augments each critic in soft actor-critic with a zonotope defined by predicted generators, whose geometric width serves as an adaptive pessimistic offset and whose disagreement between critics controls how they are combined, moving from width-weighted averaging to the standard minimum. This replaces the uniform min-of-two-critics rule with state- and action-adaptive pessimism for locomotion tasks.

entry.title: From Prompting to Composing: A Spatial Canvas Interface for Poster Generation

author.name: Yitong Wang, Fangyun Wei, Jinjing Zhao, Sirui Zhang, Hongyang Zhang, Dong Chen, Bo Dai, Yan Lu

entry.summary: This companion work introduces a Spatial Canvas Interface for poster generation, letting users compose two-dimensional generation intent directly through semantic, identity, text, and pixel binding types. The resulting model, Compo, adapts a pretrained image editing model and supports both explicit canvas construction and an agentic mode driven by high-level requests.

entry.title: Recurrent Self-Improvement: Dynamic Cross-Loop On-Policy Distillation for Looped Language Models

author.name: Yi Wang, Rui Qian, Yu Li, Haoyang Yao, Wenjie Wang

entry.summary: Introduces LoopOPD, a post-training framework for Looped Language Models that uses the model's own extra recurrent computation as a compute-privileged teacher for on-policy distillation across loops. This avoids sparse rewards and external-teacher mismatch that limit existing approaches to parameter-efficient recurrent reasoning.

entry.title: Teaching PPG How not Who: Fixed-Effects Distillation from ECG

author.name: Zhongli Wu, Zhuangzhi Gao, Yuankai Wang, Gregory Y. H. Lip, Bilal H. Kirmani, Yalin Zheng

entry.summary: Analyzes what ECG-to-PPG distillation actually teaches, showing that a per-recording mean trait accounts for 40-59% of teacher targets and that students memorizing identity learn less cardiovascular state. Proposes fixed-effects distillation that subtracts each recording's mean so the trait cancels exactly, more than doubling state agreement across 34 runs.

entry.title: Multi-Bandwidth Distribution Matching Distillation: On the Equivalence of Distribution Matching Distillation and Drifting Models

author.name: Jialin Zhu, Xing Liu, Feixiang He, He Wang

entry.summary: The paper establishes a precise theoretical correspondence between Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD/DMD2), a widely used one-step generative distillation method, and Drifting Models, whose optimization objectives are nearly identical in form. Building on this equivalence, the authors propose multi-bandwidth distribution matching distillation to improve one-step generation.

entry.title: Ranking Prior Alignment for Credit Risk Modeling: When Do External Priors Matter?

author.name: Qiye Lu, Jiang Ji, Liang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes Ranking Prior Alignment, a model-agnostic framework for cold-start credit scoring that injects external ranking priors from domain experts, teacher models, or LLMs into scoring models via a temperature-scaled KL divergence loss. It unifies neural (MIL attention) and tree-based model families under one regularization scheme. The work matters because cold-start risk modeling with scarce labeled default data is a recurring practical problem in financial machine learning.

entry.title: What is the goal of unsupervised machine learning?

author.name: Aapo Hyv\"arinen

entry.summary: A position paper by Aapo Hyvarinen arguing that unsupervised learning, unlike supervised and reinforcement learning, serves several heterogeneous goals and that seeking a single definition is futile. Identifies four goals: distribution estimation, data generation, feature extraction for downstream tasks, and understanding the data. A conceptual contribution from a highly influential researcher in the field.

entry.title: Recovery Guarantees for Posterior Sampling of One-Bit Compressed Sensing

author.name: Jing Ma, Yujia Wu, Zhaoqiang Liu

entry.summary: The paper derives sample complexity bounds for noisy one-bit compressed sensing with prior-distributed signals, showing posterior sampling recovers signals when measurements scale logarithmically with the prior's approximate covering number. It also proves robustness to learned-prior mismatch via Wasserstein distance and provides a matching lower bound.

entry.title: Example-driven Parametrisations for Bayesian Shape Optimisation

author.name: Gabriel Diaz-Aylwin, Joseph Neighbor, Abiel Malkani Talwar, Rui-Yang Zhang, Henry B. Moss

entry.summary: The authors learn Bayesian optimization search-space parameterizations from collections of existing designs by applying PCA to inter-shape deformations, yielding a linear, interpretable space with an explicit expressivity-dimensionality tradeoff. Demonstrations span aerofoils, wings, and RF cavities across 2D geometry, 3D aerodynamics, and electromagnetics.

entry.title: Is Real-World Training Data Necessary for Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection?

author.name: Yujing Liu, Yixin Liu, Yue Tan, Xiaofeng Cao, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Heng Tao Shen, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: The paper proposes AG-FORGE, a forge for automatic synthesis of anomalous graphs, showing that synthetic data can match real-world training performance for generalist graph anomaly detection but cannot push the frontier further with current methods. It then develops improvements to overcome the capacity limits of existing synthetic-data approaches.

entry.title: AdaptLSTM: Efficient Adaptive Online Learning for Cloud Workload Forecasting under Distribution Drift

author.name: Xinhua Miao, Bowei Yang, Zhengong Cai

entry.summary: AdaptLSTM is an adaptive online learning framework for cloud workload forecasting that detects distribution drift via validation-calibrated thresholds and applies selective, targeted model updates. On Alibaba traces it recovers 54-96% of naive online learning's accuracy gains at roughly 20% of the compute cost, yielding 2.7-4.8x efficiency improvements. This matters for elastic resource provisioning in web-scale cloud services where offline models degrade quickly.

entry.title: GaussianBench: Physics-Fidelity Evaluation for Gaussian Scene Representations

author.name: Chukwudalu Dumebi-Kachikwu

entry.summary: GaussianBench is an evaluation suite testing whether physics-integrated Gaussian Splatting scene representations respond correctly to new forces, material edits, contacts, and thermal interventions, rather than merely producing visually plausible rollouts. It uses frozen file-based scenes, simulator-independent scorers, and analytical or measured references, testing conservation laws and material coupling. This addresses a real evaluation gap as 3DGS moves from static reconstruction toward interactive physical simulation.

entry.title: Calibrating Ambiguity Set via Diagnostic Transport for Distributionally Robust Optimization

author.name: Wenbin Zhou, Elizabeth Cucuzzella, Shixiang Zhu

entry.summary: This paper introduces DT-DRO, which adapts the geometry of the ambiguity set in distributionally robust optimization using held-out calibration data. It diagnoses systematic probability misallocation via the conditional probability integral transform and translates it into an outcome-level transport adjusting both the set center and ground cost, with a tractable dual reformulation.

entry.title: A Graph Neural Network for Global Daily Fire Radiative Power Prediction at Medium-Range Lead Times

author.name: Li Zhang, Jun Wang, Isidora Jankov, Yongxin Liu, Gonzalo A. Ferrada, Ravan Ahmadov, Ligia Bernardet, Haonan Chen, Shobha Kondragunta

entry.summary: The authors develop a graph neural network that predicts global fire radiative power one to seven days ahead, addressing operational constraints in NOAA's GEFS-Aerosols where fire observations arrive with 1.5-day latency and are then held static. The data-driven model enables dynamic fire inputs for air-quality and aerosol forecasting.

entry.title: LadderEdit: Edit-Level Residual Compression for Memory-Efficient Lifelong Editing of LLMs

author.name: Xiaobing Yu, Peijie Qiu, Jin Yang, Xuanzhao Dong, Weiwei Ma, Zhaoqi An, Xiaoqi Zhao, Xiaofeng Liu

entry.summary: LadderEdit addresses the linear storage growth of LoRA-per-edit lifelong LLM editing by first storing each edit as a low-rank sketch, then promoting it to higher rank along a ladder only if it fails a rewrite, generalization, and locality contract on probe prompts. This maintains coverage while only hard edits consume additional rank.

entry.title: FloorSAV: Elucidating Spatial Audio-Visual Context with 2D Floormap for AV-LLMs

author.name: Kyeong-Rae Kim, Sungnyun Kim, Tae-Hyun Oh

entry.summary: FloorSAV grounds spatial audio-visual context in audio-visual LLMs by rendering a dynamic 2D floormap from 3D point clouds, camera trajectories, spatial audio cues, and object landmarks, then injecting it as a synchronized stream alongside egocentric video. This enables spatial reasoning without costly fine-tuning.

entry.title: Randomized Transport Maps for Model-Free Policy-Gradient Mean-Field Control

author.name: Adonis Jamal, Samy Mekkaoui, Yadh Hafsi, Huy\^en Pham

entry.summary: The paper develops Transport REINFORCE, a model-free policy gradient method for discrete-time mean-field control that captures the mean-field contribution of the policy on the population distribution, which standard REINFORCE misses. It applies to finite and continuous state spaces via perturbations of the population distribution using transport maps.

entry.title: TACROSS: An Efficient and Low-Cost Scalable Human Touch System Across Heterogeneous Tactile Sensors for Dexterous Robot Learning

author.name: Bo Chen, Huanzhang Hu, Junyang Ma, Bo Yue, Fangdi Yu, Haijier Chen, Xianxin Lai, Shuyu Pan, Zhen Yang, Xiaoquan Sun, Wenze Cui, Zhongliang Jiang, Shaopeng Liu, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: TACROSS is a system for transferring human tactile demonstrations to robots despite fundamental differences between human gloves and robotic tactile sensors, aligning tactile streams at the contact-event level rather than raw sensor values. It includes a five-layer piezoresistive glove costing under USD 12 with 285 sensing points, enabling cheap scalable data collection for dexterous manipulation. This addresses a key data bottleneck in robot learning.

entry.title: Differentiable Systematic Resampling for Variational Sequential Monte Carlo

author.name: Fredrik Cumlin, Saikat Chatterjee

entry.summary: The paper introduces Differentiable Systematic Resampling, a temperature-controlled relaxation of systematic resampling that preserves its CDF-ordered banded structure while enabling full gradient flow in variational sequential Monte Carlo. It proves pointwise exponential convergence of the induced bias to zero and avoids the iterative solvers and computational overhead of optimal-transport-based alternatives. This makes end-to-end learning in particle filters much more practical.

entry.title: SciTBERT: A family of chronologically consistent language models for scientific and technological language processing

author.name: Thomas Gebhart, Russell J. Funk

entry.summary: SciTBERT is a family of BERT-derived encoders trained on scientific papers, patents, and related text with constrained chronological and source distributions, eliminating lookahead and domain biases that plague existing science-of-science models. This enables valid study of time-dependent and archival properties of science and technology. It matters because biased pretrained encoders can distort bibliometric and innovation research findings.

entry.title: Cognitive Thermometers: Machine Learning and Logical Complexity

author.name: Shane Steinert-Threlkeld, Jakub Szymanik

entry.summary: This position/review paper proposes using machine learning model learnability as a model-agnostic measure of semantic complexity — treating models as cognitive thermometers — to explain why natural languages favor certain meanings over others. It reviews converging evidence that logic-based and ML-based complexity measures agree, and argues that where they diverge, learnability is the better explanation. The work bridges cognitive science, semantics, and machine learning theory.

entry.title: Prompts versus Rules: Auditing and Controlling Speech Naturalness Behaviors in Voice User Simulators

author.name: Riqiang Wang, Elena Khasanova, Harsh Saini, Lex Konnelly, Parsa Kavehzadeh, Matthias Lee, Mohamed Attia

entry.summary: This work audits whether voice user simulators actually realize intended speech naturalness behaviors such as disfluency, interruption, and backchanneling, comparing an LLM prompting approach (tau-Voice) against a rule-based injection algorithm across three models. It finds prompting often fails to produce configured behaviors, affecting the validity of agent evaluations.

entry.title: Learning the Loop, Not Just the Page: Execution-Grounded Loop Learning for Web Generation

author.name: Yuxin Meng, Ruixu Zhang, Junjie Wang, Yuhan Suo, Yuhan Sun, Ruining Hu, Yiyao Yu, Yubin Wang, Shouwei Ruan, Bin Wang, Yue Liao, Yuxiang Zhang, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces WebLoop, a framework for functional web generation that jointly trains generation, critique, and refinement within a single shared policy rather than only optimizing the final page. The key insight is that while generators and refiners receive direct executable rewards from the environment, the intermediate critic lacks an executable outcome, so the authors train an execution-free critic using complementary signals for requirement-level discriminability and downstream helpfulness. This addresses an underexplored gap in diagnosing and repairing imperfect web implementations during generation.

entry.title: Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research with Structured Harness

author.name: Meilin Chen, Hongyuan Bao

entry.summary: This paper introduces Incremental-OEDR, a research setting treating reports as evolving research states that are incrementally updated as new information emerges, rather than generated from scratch. Its Structured Harness represents reports as outlines, sections, and evidence with structured retrieval and a persistent evidence pool to support continuous maintenance.

entry.title: When History Helps and Hurts: Selective History Use across Multimodal Turns

author.name: Shuoyang Sun, Kerui Gu, Hao Fang, Shaoli Huang, Bin Chen

entry.summary: ReTurn is a 7,000-task benchmark spanning visual and audio evidence that disentangles selective history use from underlying question difficulty in multi-turn multimodal interaction. It distinguishes task-carrying history (Reconfirm/Reground) from evidence-carrying history (Retrieve/Rebind) and evaluates whether models appropriately use or ignore outdated context.

entry.title: Rendering-Free Lookahead for Question-Guided Active Vision

author.name: Koya Sakamoto, Daichi Azuma, Shuhei Kurita, Naoya Chiba, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Taiki Miyanishi

entry.summary: RFL is a viewpoint-selection policy for active robot vision that ranks candidate camera motions by a VLM's estimated answerability of unseen views, quantifying how likely a candidate view suffices to answer a question without actually rendering it. This enables efficient question-guided active perception for viewpoint-dependent QA. The rendering-free design makes lookahead practical for real-time robotic systems.

entry.title: SatFix: Absolute Visual Localization of UAVs in Satellite Maps from a Single Oblique Image

author.name: Jiarui Zeng, Kun Shi, Chiman Vong, Zhedong Zheng

entry.summary: SatFix addresses absolute UAV localization within satellite maps by regressing continuous 2D position and heading (3-DoF pose) from a single oblique image, built on a VGT-Omega-style feed-forward backbone. This moves beyond retrieval-based cross-view geo-localization, which depends on gallery sampling and provides no heading estimate. The approach is relevant to drone navigation, delivery, and search-and-rescue.

entry.title: Skeleton-Guided Progressive Test-Time Adaptation for Thin Curvilinear Structures

author.name: Boa Jang, JunGyu Lee, Gwanho Lee, Jinwook Choi, Young-Gon Kim

entry.summary: This paper addresses segmentation of thin curvilinear structures (e.g., blood vessels, roads) under severe cross-modality domain shift, where minor pixel errors can destroy global topology. The authors propose a source-free test-time adaptation method that uses skeleton guidance to constrain connectivity during progressive adaptation, unlike prior TTA approaches that only adapt feature statistics or confidence. This matters for medical imaging and remote sensing applications where robust structure preservation under modality gaps is critical.

entry.title: LR-V2X: Loss-Resilient Collaborative Perception under Low-Bandwidth Communication

author.name: Kang Yang, Tianci Bu, Peng Wang, Deying Li, Yongcai Wang

entry.summary: LR-V2X addresses vehicle-to-everything collaborative perception under packet loss and low-bandwidth conditions, where dense BEV feature exchange is infeasible and compressed messages cannot be recovered after loss. The framework converts corrupted received latents into a spatial prior and reconstructs missing BEV information in latent space, remaining functional even at 90 percent packet loss. This targets realistic wireless conditions often ignored in collaborative perception research.

entry.title: iCATS: Fast Video Generation via Interaction-Aware Sparse Attention and Timestep-Adaptive Sparsity

author.name: Chengfeng Han, Baole Ai, Xianlu Bian, Jie Yao, Zilong Huang, Ang Wang, Dandan Ding

entry.summary: Introduces iCATS, a training-free sparse attention method for accelerating Diffusion Transformer video generation by improving importance estimation of query-key regions, building better sparse masks, and adding timestep-adaptive sparsity with hardware-aware execution. Aims to reduce compute while preserving generation quality.

entry.title: Beyond Resolution: Object-to-Image Ratio Mismatch in Instance Retrieval

author.name: Boaz Meivar, Ofir Kedem, Amit Edenzon, Gal Chechik, Shai Avidan

entry.summary: This computer vision paper identifies object-to-image (O2I) ratio mismatch, rather than resolution loss, as the dominant cause of failure in visual instance retrieval when objects appear at different apparent sizes. Using a controlled benchmark of 3,021 Objaverse objects rendered at five camera distances, the authors show over 80% of cross-distance degradation is attributable to O2I mismatch for most pretrained backbones, and that the failure is asymmetric depending on whether the query or gallery image is tighter. The finding suggests current multi-scale architectures address the wrong factor and points toward new training or augmentation strategies for retrieval systems.

entry.title: Towards Unified Evaluation of Prompt Enhancers for Video Generation
