author.name: Jingbo Yue, Bruce Coburn, Jinge Ma, Jui-Feng Chi, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a fine-tuning-free framework using multimodal LLMs to inventory visible foods, verify each item's identity and whether its proposed region supports portion estimation, and trigger at most one targeted recovery pass for gaps and omitted foods. Recovered regions are re-verified blind to the recovery prompt before reconciliation into a final nutrition estimate. This addresses silent failure modes in single-image dietary assessment with a structured verification design.

entry.title: Sera: Semantic Representation Aggregation for Reliable and Interpretable Battery Health Forecasting

author.name: Jiawei Li, Fang Liu, Wei Zhang, Zuming Liu, Man-Fai Ng, Zhi Wei Seh

entry.summary: Sera complements temporal models for battery state-of-health forecasting with explicit degradation semantics guided by battery domain expertise, making predictions more reliable and interpretable than purely numerical time-series approaches. It addresses nonlinear degradation and heterogeneity across batteries by representing higher-level degradation characteristics. The framework aims at practical battery management applications.

entry.title: Epistemic Disturbance in the Graph Model for Conflict Resolution: State-Preserving Actions, Four-Valued Assessments, and the Distinction between Capability and Intention

author.name: Yukiko Kato

entry.summary: This theory paper extends the graph model for conflict resolution with state-preserving actions such as announcements, leaks, and selective disclosures that leave the physical state unchanged but alter other decision makers' beliefs. It augments states with epistemic states and distinguishes capability from intention via four-valued assessments.

entry.title: Using Weisfeiler-Leman Features for Algorithm Selection in Constraint Optimisation

author.name: Alessio Pellegrino, Jacopo Mauro

entry.summary: The paper introduces an automated feature extraction method for algorithm selection in constraint programming, converting problem instances to graphs and applying Weisfeiler-Leman graph kernels to capture structural properties that hand-crafted statistics miss. This exploits the known equivalence between 1-WL distinguishing power and message-passing GNN expressiveness.

entry.title: Temporal transformer CAN encoder with federated lightweight heads for anomaly detection

author.name: Konstantinos Gyftodimos, Kyriakos Chiotis, Elena Politi, George Dimitrakopoulos, Eirini Liotou

entry.summary: Proposes a privacy-preserving anomaly detection framework for in-vehicle CAN bus networks, combining a temporal transformer encoder with federated lightweight per-vehicle heads. The approach captures timing, payload, and message-pattern anomalies that rule-based or per-message methods miss, without centralizing sensitive vehicle data.

entry.title: Language Models for Page-Level Layout Decisions in E-commerce Search

author.name: Varun Joshi, Eva C. Song, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: The paper uses language models to decide page-level layout changes in e-commerce search, such as when and where to insert recommender secondary stacks, avoiding costly online A/B tests. Since interleaving-style evaluation is well established for ranking but not for layout, the authors propose LLM-based evaluation of layout decisions, an applied problem relevant to large-scale search systems.

entry.title: Low-Cost Sensor Calibration for Indoor Air Quality Monitoring: A Dataset, Evaluation Scenarios, and a Lightweight Model

author.name: Jinyong Yun, Seokho Ahn, Hyungjin Kim, Sungbok Shin, Young-Duk Seo

entry.summary: The paper contributes a six-month dataset of multivariate indoor air-quality measurements from low-cost and reference sensors with contextual metadata across five locations, plus four evaluation scenarios covering spatial generalization, long-term drift, and event-conditioned calibration. It also proposes a lightweight calibration model that relaxes the strict requirement of a co-located reference sensor at each deployment. This is a useful applied resource for scalable environmental monitoring.

entry.title: MotiveMob: Motivation as Semantic Action for Closed-Loop Human Mobility Generation

author.name: Mengkun Gao, Zengqing Wu, Renhe Jiang, Jiawei Wang, Yusong Wang, Chuang Yang, Shuyuan Zheng, Makoto Onizuka, Chuan Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes generating human mobility trajectories by explicitly modeling motivation as a semantic action in a why-where-when decision process, improving robustness under user-level and temporal distribution shift. Useful for urban planning and transportation simulation. The explicit intent modeling is a reasonable structural improvement over coarse trajectory-level generation.

entry.title: Does an Illumination Prior Help Face-Swap Detection? A Controlled Study of Temporal Self-Blended Images

author.name: Danil Davydov, Bader Rasheed, Dmitriy Vatolin

entry.summary: Companion negative-result study examining whether illumination inconsistencies added to self-blended images improve face-swap detection, using Temporal Self-Blended Images with controlled luminance mismatch. Across five training regimes and four datasets, no illumination-specific improvements are found beyond seed variability; T-SBI mainly shifts prediction scores and thresholds. Complements the same team's noise-residual study.

entry.title: Bilevel optimization for data-driven learning of Koopman embeddings using kernel-based autoencoders

author.name: Joel-Pascal Ntwali N'konzi, Feliks N\"{u}ske, Stefan Klus

entry.summary: This work introduces extended dynamic mode decomposition with kernel-based autoencoders learned via bilevel optimization, offering an interpretable and theoretically tractable alternative to neural-network autoencoders for learning Koopman dictionaries. It addresses the core Koopman challenge of avoiding a priori dictionary specification while retaining kernel methods' analytical advantages. Relevant to data-driven modeling of nonlinear dynamical systems.

entry.title: Causal-fate dynamics of unrealized influence

author.name: Yiwei Liu, Luwei Yang, Shunbo Lei

entry.summary: This theoretical work formalizes causal-fate dynamics, where generated influence in a dynamical system may be realized, remain latent, or be transformed by subsequent dynamics, providing an exact finite-transport representation. A connectome-constrained C. elegans model motivates the hypothesis that unresolved inter-neuronal influence persists and contributes to later propagation.

entry.title: Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization via Complex-Valued Fusion

author.name: Anirudh Praveen, Koteswar Rao Jerripothula, Pratik Joshi, Aveen Dayal, Neela Sawant

entry.summary: The paper proposes computing complex-valued visual-text and audio-text similarities and learning their fusion with a complex-valued neural network, replacing the fixed scalar fusion rules (geometric mean, weighted average) common in open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization. This preserves richer cross-modal phase and magnitude information when scoring unseen event classes. It targets the OV-AVEL task built on frozen multimodal foundation models like ImageBind.

entry.title: ISBO: Scalable Spatio-Temporal Bayesian Optimization with Log Gaussian Cox Process Models via the INLA-SPDE Approach

author.name: Kaichuang Yang, H{\aa}vard Rue, Jakob Zeitler

entry.summary: ISBO introduces the first scalable Bayesian optimization framework for spatio-temporal objectives by modeling the log-intensity with a Log-Gaussian Cox Process and performing inference via the INLA-SPDE approach on meshes with Matern fields. This yields sparse Gaussian Markov random fields enabling fast posterior inference during sequential optimization. It matters for applications like sensor placement and environmental monitoring where objectives are event-count processes over space and time.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Preparation of Transportation Management Plans: A Case Study with WisDOT WisTMP System

author.name: Zihao Sheng, Pei Li, Zilin Huang, Yen-Jung Chen, Yuhao Luo, Zhengyang Wan, Steven T. Parker, David A. Noyce, Sikai Chen

entry.summary: This case study builds an LLM-assisted framework to automate the labor-intensive preparation of Transportation Management Plans for road work zones, fine-tuning multiple open-source LLMs across scales and deploying them locally for data security. The authors construct a domain-specific dataset by converting historical WisDOT WisTMP PDF documents into structured JSON question-answer pairs. It is a solid demonstration of applied LLM fine-tuning in a safety-relevant government domain.

entry.title: Fact over Fiction: Detection of Pathological Hallucinations in Sinhala-to-English Neural Machine Translation

author.name: Navam Obeysekara, Nevidu Jayatilleke

entry.summary: This paper addresses reference-free detection of translation hallucinations in the low-resource Sinhala-to-English pair, contributing a 45,000-sample synthetic dataset built from five linguistically motivated corruption strategies with a semantic rescue mechanism. The authors fine-tune mDeBERTa-v3 for token-level hallucination detection.

entry.title: From Sparse Representations to Behavioral Insights for Multimodal Depression Assessment

author.name: Guimin Hu, Zihao Song, Jiachen Luo, Jiayuan Xie, Ruichu Cai

entry.summary: BehavDep decomposes multimodal behavioral representations into sparse latent factors linked to behaviorally meaningful concepts via a semantic bridge, improving interpretability of depression assessment. It also learns video-level depression tendency scores under weak supervision to handle the mismatch between user-level annotations and heterogeneous video-level behaviors.

entry.title: MCL: Meta Convolution Layer

author.name: Naim Reza, Md Al Amin, Ho Yub Jung

entry.summary: MCL revisits dynamic convolution by modeling the convolutional kernel as an input-conditioned function W(x) realized through high-order polynomial expansion rather than a linear mixture of basis kernels. Nested residual blocks inspired by deep polynomial networks generate a single input-adaptive kernel, decoupling expressivity from mixture size. This addresses the optimization and expressivity limits of conventional dynamic convolution.

entry.title: Collaboratively Guided Adversarial Robust Distillation with Teacher-Favorable Examples

author.name: Zhi Li, Haowei Liu, Hongchen Yang, Xiaoxuan Wang, Song Gao, Shaowen Yao, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes CGARD, an adversarial robustness distillation method that jointly optimizes student-adversarial and teacher-collaborative examples within the same perturbation neighborhood, where the collaborative example is constrained to keep teacher loss no higher than on clean inputs. This exploits underexplored teacher-favorable supervision regions.

entry.title: GroundSight at GroundLM 2026 Shared Tasks: GoldenViewVQA

author.name: Kun Wang, Yupeng Hu, Ruping Cao, Hao Liu, Zhiran Li, Qianlong Xiang, Harry Cheng

entry.summary: Describes CoVeR-VQA, a training-free multi-stage verification and correction pipeline for grounded multi-view driving-scene VQA that chains GPT-5.6 zero-shot predictions with view-specific verification by Gemini-3.6-Flash, joint verification with Claude-Opus-5, and group-level cross-split checks. It competed in the GoldenViewVQA shared task.

entry.title: Hankel Subspace Self-Supervised Learning for Parallel MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Mingyu Hu, Siquan Zhu, Xijun Zhong, Qiegen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes HSSRecon, a scan-specific self-supervised framework for parallel MRI reconstruction that partitions data by physical acquisition units before Hankel lifting to prevent data leakage between input and target, applying multiplicity-based subspace methods. Exploits multi-coil and overlapping k-space neighborhood redundancy to recover undersampled data.

entry.title: VESSI - VLM-Enhanced Support for Surveillance and Investigations

author.name: Saverio Cavasin, Pietro Tedeschi, Mattia Tamiazzo, Alessandro Brighente, Simone Milani, Mauro Conti

entry.summary: VESSI is a framework that uses vision-language models to add semantic understanding to automated video surveillance, enabling prompt-driven interrogation of video sequences for situational awareness and post-incident forensic investigation. It aims to reduce analyst burden compared to traditional surveillance systems.

entry.title: VEDJE: Video-Efficient Discriminative Joint Encoder for Scalable Video-Text Retrieval

author.name: Shahaf Wagner, Gabriele Serussi, Dan Ben Ami, Tomer Galanti, Chaim Baskin

entry.summary: VEDJE compresses per-frame video features into a reusable cache while keeping representations separate, using feature-change prediction as an auxiliary training signal to improve retrieval from compressed features without extra query-time cost. It improves R@1 across MSR-VTT, MSVD, DiDeMo, and ActivityNet in both retrieval directions.

entry.title: From Language to Motion: Task-Conditioned Focal-Stack Trajectory Integration for Microscopic Robots

author.name: Junjie Xie, Chuxuan He, Junkai Huang, Heng Zhang, Angen Ye, Yujia Song, Yuqing Li, Pengsong Zhang, Dapeng Zhang

entry.summary: A semantic-to-physical framework maps natural-language instructions to constrained geometric operators for microscopic robot manipulation, reusing frozen open-vocabulary perception and integrating focal-plane trajectories via confidence weighting and dynamic programming. It achieves strong trajectory accuracy with zero new labels, cutting setup time from over an hour to 15 minutes versus part-specific U-Net training.

entry.title: MC-TRCM: Observation-Aware Recursive Fusion for Incomplete Mobile and Wearable Mental-Health Feature Views

author.name: Wentao Wang, Lifeng Han, Zining Ren, Hengyu Zhong, Guangyu Zou

entry.summary: MC-TRCM is a model for mobile and wearable mental-health data releases that consist of summarized feature tables rather than synchronized raw sensor streams. It preserves each feature source as a separate token, treats missingness as input context via learned absence tokens, conditions fusion on dataset and task embeddings, and uses a recursive prediction head refined over outputs. This targets the realistic but understudied setting of incomplete, heterogeneous mental-health feature views.

entry.title: DVLA-RL++: Dual-Level Vision-Language Alignment with Reinforcement Learning Gating for Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Wenhao Li, Xianjing Meng, Qiangchang Wang, Zhongyi Han, Yilong Yin, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: DVLA-RL++ extends a prior vision-language few-shot framework with complementary semantic purification, which separates intrinsic object descriptions from nuisance context, and counterfactual reinforcement-learning gating that sparsely evokes descriptions based on ambiguity-dependent rejection margins. The goal is to prevent support prototypes from being contaminated by incidental image context. It targets robust few-shot classification with textual semantics.

entry.title: DLC: A Metric-Guided Dynamic Loss Controller for Multi-Objective Training

author.name: Jaewan Ko, Janghoon Choi

entry.summary: Introduces DLC, an architecture- and loss-agnostic training-time controller for multi-objective image restoration that periodically evaluates the model on a feedback subset and uses quality metrics, fed through an LLM-based component, to dynamically reweight existing loss terms. It requires no new differentiable losses or architecture changes.

entry.title: PAM-ToD: Plug-and-Play Appearance Modeling for Cross-Time-of-Day 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Kota Shimomura, Sungho Moon, Tsubasa Hirakawa, Takayoshi Yamashita, Sunghoon Im, Hironobu Fujiyoshi

entry.summary: Proposes PAM-ToD, a lightweight plug-in for adapting pre-trained 3DGS road scenes to new times of day by learning per-Gaussian color scaling and additive brightness corrections while keeping the original 3DGS parameters fixed, using a simplified image formation model that eliminates the need to estimate albedo separately. Supports real-time rendering.

entry.title: Complexity of Grounded Semantics and Preferred Semantics in Finitary Argumentation Frameworks

author.name: Jinfan Xu, Jieting Luo

entry.summary: Maps the computational complexity of grounded and preferred semantics in computably finitary argumentation frameworks across five standard decision problems including credulous and skeptical acceptance. The work shows finitary restrictions reduce some problems from the analytical hierarchy to the arithmetical hierarchy.

entry.title: Continuous Ground-Truth Construction and a Recovery Policy for Air--Water Robotic Tracking

author.name: Jiangong Xiao, Zhe Sun, Kanzhong Yao, Yuanbo Bi, Haofei Zhao, Ruixuan Hu, Guan Huang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: The paper tackles visual tracking across the air-water interface, where splashes, bubbles, and refraction cause visual blindness. It introduces a ground-truth construction pipeline syncing cameras with motion-capture poses and correcting underwater projection, plus a recovery policy for online tracking that resists contamination of motion estimates by corrupted observations. It contributes a rare benchmark and method for a challenging cross-medium perception setting.

entry.title: CARE: Constrained Attention Refinement for Fine-Grained Visual Classification via Teacher-Student Distillation

author.name: Ruibo Wen, Hang Shao, Yiming Lei

entry.summary: CARE is a teacher-student distillation framework for interpretable fine-grained visual classification: the student keeps prediction and explanation within class-specific attention pathways, while a training-only query teacher reads intermediate DINOv2 layers to refine the student's attention. This combines the interpretability of constrained attention with the discriminative power of strong pretrained backbones. It addresses the usual trade-off between accuracy and explainability.

entry.title: GROB: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Public-Trace Investigation of Candidate Agentic Activity

author.name: Chiara Bonfanti, Cataldo Basile

entry.summary: GROB is a multi-agent system for investigating candidate autonomous-agent activity using only public Internet traces when privileged telemetry is unavailable, performing controlled read-only collection and preserving observations for later resolution. On a frozen September 2026 corpus, some traces grew more informative as public evidence emerged, with the strongest result resolving Census-labelled identifiers to specific requests via public revision records. The work addresses attribution and investigation of agent behavior from open evidence.

entry.title: Controlled Acquisition and Abstention in Three-Channel Score Conflicts

author.name: Mengzhe Geng

entry.summary: Studies when a policy should acquire a third modality's score or abstain when audio, video, and text disagree, using a controlled three-score benchmark with mechanism-specific rewards. Finds a threshold policy matches always-request decisions with fewer requests, with its advantage dependent on the reward assigned to ambiguity.

entry.title: DaCe-DT: Data-Centric Offline Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning via Adaptive Prompts and Trajectory Correction for Heterogeneous Tasks

author.name: Xinfei Wang, Shanchen Pang, Chenhao Zhang, Shudong Wang, Wenhao Ji, Haiyuan Gui, Meng Han, Xiaojian Liao

entry.summary: From a data-quality perspective, this paper identifies three bottlenecks in offline multi-task RL: ineffective use of prompt length under varying task complexity, semantically irrelevant random prompt segments, and misleading supervision from fragmented trajectories. DaCe-DT addresses these with adaptive prompts and trajectory correction, aiming for robust offline MTRL on heterogeneous task data.

entry.title: Addressing Overcommitment in the Reasoning of Gendered Economic Memes under Multimodal Ambiguity

author.name: Kushal Kanwar, Dushyant Singh Chauhan, Kapil Rana, Gopendra Vikram Singh, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: Studies biased gendered economic-role attribution in multimodal meme understanding, identifying epistemic overcommitment (inferring roles without sufficient contextual evidence) as a key bias source, and proposes CGER-Net to assess contextual sufficiency before attribution. Relevant to fairness and safety of multimodal systems on socially sensitive content. Targets hallucinated stereotypical outputs under ambiguity.

entry.title: In-Ride Alcohol-Impairment Detection in E-Scooterists with False-Alarm Control

author.name: Marco Capuccini, Rahul Rajendra Pai

entry.summary: Proposes an onboard detector for alcohol impairment in e-scooter riders using inertial and throttle signals during the ride, with a provable bound on the false-alarm rate, evaluated on 141 rides including 25 participants riding sober and at two target blood-alcohol levels. Offers a practical safety countermeasure beyond static reaction tests and night bans. Combines sequential detection theory with a real mobility-safety problem.

entry.title: Large-Scale Benchmarking of Quantum Neural Network Configurations for Financial Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jack Waller, Xing Liang, Dimitrios Makris, Rajagopal Nilavalan

entry.summary: A systematic grid-search evaluation of 1,368 quantum neural network configurations—varying encoding, ansatz, qubit count, depth, and cost function—for financial time series forecasting on GBP/USD spot exchange rate data, measuring accuracy and computational cost. It fills a gap in regression-focused QNN comparisons.

entry.title: On linearity or non-linearity in machine learning for quantum chaotic dynamics

author.name: Francesco Perciavalle, Agostino Gallo, Francesco Plastina, Gianluigi Greco, Nicola Lo Gullo, Carlo Adornetto

entry.summary: The paper formulates quantum many-body dynamics prediction as time-series forecasting on a few-qubit PXP chain (realizable with Rydberg atoms), comparing linear and nonlinear ML models across regimes from ergodic behavior to many-body scarring. It tests whether ML can substitute for costly classical simulation of entanglement-spreading quantum dynamics. A controlled benchmark for ML forecasting of quantum chaotic systems.

entry.title: Implementation Guidelines for Data Quality Metrics

author.name: Philipp Jung, Katinka Becker, Felix Biessmann, Valerie Restat, Martin Seyferth, Daniel Schwabe, Lisa Ehrlinger

entry.summary: This paper addresses the gap between abstract data quality dimensions like accuracy and completeness in ISO/IEC 25024 and 5259 standards and the low-level checks that tools actually implement. The authors provide concrete implementation guidelines that operationalize these metrics, arguing the standards currently shift rather than solve the specification problem.

entry.title: Learning qBIC Resonances across Metasurface Families in Dielectric Fourier Space

author.name: Shuangteng Lei, Li Yu, Tianxin Li, Wei Lu

entry.summary: The paper maps 2015 samples from seven dielectric metasurface families to a shared reciprocal-lattice grid and shows that frozen low-order Fourier channels capture resonance shifts with high R-squared values. A K-space backbone plus a local complex K-space expert models broadband spectra and parameterizes ultranarrow qBIC resonances via diffusion.

entry.title: Efficient quadratic entropy with distance sketches

author.name: Steve Huntsman

entry.summary: This paper details scalable random-feature and projection methods for approximating quadratic entropy for arbitrary distributions under negative-type distances, focusing on Euclidean and spherical geodesic cases. Amortizing a single large matrix multiplication and using control variates enables large-scale, low-memory computation when the distance is fixed and the distribution varies. Demonstrations include scientometric analyses on Open Graph Benchmark datasets.

entry.title: Perception Test 2026: Challenge Summary and Extension to City-scale Audio-Visual Reasoning

author.name: Fedor Kitashov, Jo\~ao Carreira, Shiry Ginosar, Dima Damen, Andrew Zisserman, Viorica P\u{a}tr\u{a}ucean

entry.summary: This report summarizes the fourth Perception Test challenge held at ECCV 2026, focused on spatial intelligence, with tracks spanning video question answering and new city-scale KilometerAudio and KilometerVision benchmarks based on walking-tour videos. It describes winning solutions, including a generalist model competing across all tracks. It documents community progress on multimodal video reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Specialized Decision Models vs. General-Purpose LLMs: Benchmarking Jev Across Knowledge, Reasoning, and Multilingual Tasks

author.name: Xing Li, Qingcheng Chang, Jinzhong Ning, Changfeng Xu, Shenlong Zhang, Yijia Zhang, Ling Luo, Hongfei Lin

entry.summary: The authors benchmark Jev, a System One decision model that selects among given options, against 19 LLMs across 13 multiple-choice benchmarks. Jev is competitive with frontier LLMs on knowledge and commonsense tasks, best on MMLU-Redux and ARC-Challenge, but trails badly on mathematical word problems.

entry.title: MiniVer-V: Identifying Minimal Sufficient Evidence for Short Video Verification

author.name: Leran Chen, Lingnan Kong, Zile Cai

entry.summary: MiniVer-V is a benchmark of 195 short videos with three-way verdict annotations and 5,510 multimodal evidence units, built around the criterion of evidential sufficiency rather than topical relevance for fact-checking. It proposes a two-layer verification framework that selects minimal sufficient evidence subsets supporting confident verdicts.

entry.title: A Camera-Native Stereo VR180 Dataset

author.name: Linxuan Lu

entry.summary: This paper releases a firsthand-captured stereo VR180 dataset with 1,211 samples (636 video clips and 575 stills) recorded with two professional Blackmagic URSA Cine Immersive cameras, provided as camera-native RAW and per-eye fisheye and half-equirectangular formats with factory lens calibration and conversion tools. Unlike existing online-scraped VR180 data, it is unstitched, uncompressed, and calibrated. This is a valuable community resource for immersive video research.

entry.title: DiscoVL: Unveiling Disentangled C ross-Modal Representation Learning via Orthogonal Adversarial Regularization for V ision-Language Models

author.name: Mengping Dong, Jinbao Li, Fei Li

entry.summary: DiscoVL is a disentangled cross-modal representation learning framework for adapting vision-language models, coupling orthogonal adversarial regularization with structured cross-modal alignment. A multi-branch low-rank residual aligner decomposes representations into subspaces with bidirectional cross-modal feedback. The goal is parameter-efficient adaptation to new downstream tasks without sacrificing generalization.

entry.title: Point-Focused Attention Meets Context-Scan State Space: Robust Biological Visual Perception for Point Cloud Representation

author.name: Kanglin Qu, Pan Gao, Qun Dai, Yuanhao Sun

entry.summary: Proposes PointLearner, a point cloud representation network inspired by foveal vision, combining point-focused attention over local neighborhoods with a context-scan state space model for long-range dependencies. It aims to jointly capture local geometric structure and global context.

entry.title: Adaptive Adversarial Augmentation for Controllable Face Synthesis

author.name: Saransh Suri, Shivang Agarwal, Mayank Vatsa, Richa Singh

entry.summary: Proposes EFCS, a controllable synthetic face data framework that uses ensemble feedback to generate diverse and challenging training samples for face recognition under conditions like low resolution, occlusion, and masks. Models trained on EFCS data outperform baselines across multiple benchmarks.

entry.title: S$^3$Geo: Structure-Semantic Synergistic Learning for Cross-View Geo-Localization

author.name: Ziqian Mo, Hill Zhang, Haosheng Tan, Ling Li, Jiaheng Wei

entry.summary: Proposes S3Geo, a cross-view geo-localization framework combining decoupled query pooling for region-aware features with structure-semantic synergistic learning, so that fine-grained structural correspondences and semantic priors are jointly modeled. This improves robustness to viewpoint variation and confusion between visually similar regions.

entry.title: Learning Which Correspondences to Trust: Confidence-Weighted Event-Camera Localization in LiDAR Maps

author.name: Panagiotis Kiousis, Kuangyi Chen, Jun Zhang, Friedrich Fraundorfer

entry.summary: Improves event-camera localization against prebuilt LiDAR maps by learning per-correspondence confidence and pose informativeness for 3D-2D matching, avoiding a depth-dependent bias that arises when learning confidence from per-correspondence pixel error. The approach weights PnP optimization for more reliable pose estimation.

entry.title: Does Dynamic-Point Filtering Help When Texture Is Scarce? A Controlled Study of ORB-SLAM2 Front-Ends in Synthetic Indoor Scenes

author.name: Zekui Xue

entry.summary: This controlled study renders synthetic indoor sequences varying texture level and scene dynamics factorially along identical trajectories to isolate the interaction between dynamic-point filtering and low-texture conditions in feature-based SLAM. It compares ORB-SLAM2 with and without optical-flow and epipolar-residual filters under fully controlled conditions.

entry.title: A Reconfigurable Fabric Based Pneumatic Actuator with Button Fastened Constraint Modules for Multi Mode Actuation

author.name: Kentaro Kimura, Hiroki Ishizuka, Yusuke Sakaue, Sei Ikeda, Osamu Oshiro

entry.summary: This hardware paper presents a fabric-based pneumatic actuator whose actuation mode (expansion, contraction, bending, twisting) can be reconfigured post-fabrication by attaching button-fastened constraint fabric modules, with an attachable capacitive tactile sensing module included. This enables rapid, tool-free, reusable mode switching without redesigning the actuator.

entry.title: Autonomous thermodynamic cycles via robotic mobility and sensing

author.name: Sofia Kuperman, Ezra Ben-Abu, Yaron Veksler, Anna Zigelman, Sefi Givli, Amir D. Gat

entry.summary: The authors introduce autonomous thermodynamic cycles where robots exploit mobility and sensing to harvest energy from spatially varying temperature fields, realized experimentally with multistable gas-filled capsules circulating across thermal gradients. The system acts as a mobile heat engine, decoupled from fixed reservoirs.

entry.title: Regularized Small Area Estimation with Graph Laplacian Benchmarking priors

author.name: Jairo F\'uquene-Pati\~no, Brenda Betancourt

entry.summary: This work develops a Bayesian small-area-estimation framework that jointly handles borrowing of strength across areas and benchmarking to reliable aggregates, via a new family of Benchmarking priors induced by benchmark-constrained regularization, including graph-Laplacian variants built from covariate-based area similarities. Tailored MCMC methods handle the resulting degenerate priors.

entry.title: FastJEV: Understanding Redundancy for Compact JEV Inference

author.name: Jie Ma, Jie Gao, Yihang Liu, Zhike Qiu, Junle Li, Chongyi Zhuang, Jiayi Ji, Xiaoshuai Sun

entry.summary: Analyzes computational redundancy in joint evaluation voting (JEV) multimodal models that score multiple candidates sharing common context, and presents FastJEV which reuses recurrent states and shares candidate prefixes to avoid duplicated inference. The goal is compact, efficient candidate evaluation without re-running the full backbone.

entry.title: Compactness and Consistency: A Conjoint Framework for Deep Graph Clustering

author.name: Wei Ju, Siyu Yi, Kangjie Zheng, Yifan Wang, Ziyue Qiao, Li Shen, Yongdao Zhou, Xiaochun Cao, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: CoCo is a deep graph clustering framework that addresses the inability of local GNN message passing to capture global node relationships, jointly optimizing compactness and consistency of node representations while handling redundancy and noise in graph data. It aims to produce more robust and compact cluster assignments by combining these two properties. The contribution is within a well-established GNN clustering literature.

entry.title: Low-rank tensor structure of precipitation and its application to satellite-reference merging

author.name: Ryan Solgi, Rohan Shankar, Hugo A. Loaiciga

entry.summary: The authors show that daily precipitation over the contiguous US has low-rank spatiotemporal tensor structure, and that CANDECOMP/PARAFAC factorization preserving native spatial and temporal modes reconstructs precipitation more accurately than factorizing unfolded matrices. Building on this, TMerge integrates satellite precipitation with sparse ground reference observations via shared low-rank factors, improving precipitation estimation over large domains.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Optimization for Physics-Aware Highway Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Aanchal Rajesh Chugh, Sebastian Dorn

entry.summary: Extends the physics-aware X-TRACK trajectory prediction framework with uncertainty-aware variants (X-TRACK-DE and X-TRACK-MCD) that propagate uncertainty in motion variables through vehicle dynamics rather than quantifying it only in trajectory space. Targets safety-critical autonomous driving applications. Addresses a real gap where physics-aware models lack calibrated uncertainty.

entry.title: Deep Learning vs. Statistical Models for Multi-Horizon Price Forecasting of Second-Hand Electronics: A Systematic Benchmark

author.name: Mateusz Buczy\'nski, Micha{\l} Wo\'zniak, Konrad Kaczy\'nski, Anna Wr\'oblewska, Sebastian Kuk

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic multi-horizon benchmark of statistical (ARIMA, ETS) and deep learning forecasting models for used-electronics resale prices, using a large Polish marketplace dataset (100+ models, 2022-2025) across horizons from 1 to 365 days. Accurate forecasting matters for subscription platforms where pricing errors translate directly into financial risk. It fills a genuine domain gap in time-series benchmarking.

entry.title: LAIR-Net: Leaky Alignment-Impulse Residual Networks for Tabular Regression

author.name: Rahul Goswami, Aryan Bhambu, Bittu Karmakar

entry.summary: LAIR-Net is a deep randomized model for tabular regression that injects a shallow learned anchor into each hidden state via a leaky residual transition, with a depth-uniform sensitivity bound. Controlled simulations attribute gains to the anchor mechanism and characterize when benefits emerge versus vanish.

entry.title: Revisiting Identity and Spectra Dispersion in Media-Bridged Time Series Forecasting: Linking Multivariate Signals and Narrative Flows

author.name: Jierui Lei, Wenjian Zhang, Qingyi Yang, Yuyang Hong, Fangzheng Chen, Zhengbo Zhang, Haina Tang, Shiming Xiang

entry.summary: The authors propose MIDAPN, a unified spatiotemporal forecasting backbone with media-general graph adaptation and automatic temporal learning, aiming to handle both multivariate numerical and multimodal narrative-assisted time series forecasting. Its identity-aware graph module models static essence, dynamic behavior, and latent commonality to induce affinities across media types. The goal is a single backbone replacing paradigm-specific modules.

entry.title: Spatial Pattern Formation from Multi-Agent Learning in Public Goods Dilemmas

author.name: Yefei Zhang, Yuxuan Zhao

entry.summary: This study uses tabular Q-learning to examine how cooperative and defecting agents independently learn movement policies in spatial public goods games, and how learning rates shape emergent spatial patterns and collective welfare. Cooperator learning generates clusters around resource peaks, and asymmetric learning rates produce the largest welfare losses, including traveling band patterns. It matters as a controlled look at how learning dynamics, not just prescribed rules, generate spatial structure in social dilemmas.

entry.title: Type-Checking for Pattern-Based Tree Transformations

author.name: C. Aiswarya, Sahil Mhaskar, M. Praveen

entry.summary: This theoretical paper introduces a formal model of pattern-based tree transformations, where pairs of source and target patterns (like distributivity rewriting) define transformations, including cases where the matched expressions form non-regular tree languages. It proposes finite representations of possibly infinite sets of such pattern pairs and studies their expressive power and type-checking properties. This matters for compiler theory, term rewriting, and formal verification of symbolic computation systems.

entry.title: Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Registration: A Comprehensive Review, Challenges and Prospects

author.name: Zhiqiang Han, Yuanxin Ye, Qiuyun Wu, Jinhao Chen, Bai Zhu, Siyuan Hao

entry.summary: This is a comprehensive survey of multimodal remote sensing image registration, covering the radiometric, geometric, scale, viewpoint, and temporal variations that make aligning images from different sensors difficult. The authors categorize existing approaches into three pipeline-based families, summarize progress, and outline open challenges and future directions. Registration underpins fusion, change detection, and target recognition in remote sensing.

entry.title: It's Always 10:10: Reference Images Break a Bias That Prompts Only Dent

author.name: Luca Cazzaniga

entry.summary: Measures a systematic bias in text-to-image models where analog clocks are drawn at 10:10 (the advertising convention) even when other times are requested, evaluating 52 models across four prompt and reference-image conditions. It finds that providing a drawn reference dial helps break the bias where text prompts alone cannot.

entry.title: Revisiting Handcrafted Minutiae Detection: A Simple and Effective Open Source Baseline for Modern Fingerprint Workflows

author.name: Raffaele Cappelli

entry.summary: Introduces SBMEX, a fast and deterministic skeleton-based fingerprint minutiae detection method built into the open-source pyfing package, using a dual Look-Up Table architecture to replace expensive computation. It modernizes outdated legacy C/C++ baselines while retaining the auditability and standards compliance valued in forensic biometrics.

entry.title: Noise-Induced Navigation in Non-convex Domains and Compact Manifolds

author.name: Karthik Elamvazhuthi

entry.summary: This theoretical note shows that control-channel noise enables elementary continuous feedback laws achieving global asymptotic stability in connected Euclidean domains with obstacles and boundaryless manifolds, circumventing classical topological obstructions. It uses a stability-in-the-large criterion combining local Lyapunov stability with positive recurrence.

entry.title: A summary of a viral Chinese essay on what a DeepSeek kernel engineer's opinion on automating his own job

author.name: Skdk

entry.summary: Skdk summarizes and translates excerpts from a viral September 2026 WeChat essay by intlsy, a DeepSeek engineer who wrote the attention kernel for DeepSeek v4.1, describing how AI progressed from documentation assistant to a system that reads CUDA, PTX, and SASS and profiles his own specialty. The essay reflects on AI automating kernel engineering and concludes with an argument for open-weight frontier AI. With 100k+ reads and tens of thousands of shares, it is a notable sample of Chinese technical-audience sentiment on AI automation from inside a frontier lab.

entry.title: AuraLuxMuse: Adaptive Fusion Modeling for Aesthetic Stage Lighting Design with Music and Expert Guidance

author.name: Junyu Deng, Jiale Cao, Mengtian Li, Zhongxia Ji, Ruhua Chen, Yiyi He, Guangnan Ye, Zuo Hu

entry.summary: AuraLuxMuse is a system for automated aesthetic stage lighting design that translates musical features into dynamic lighting cues by encoding music and professional cue sequences into a shared retrieval space, estimating cue-event density, and retargeting fixture commands to destination stages. Rather than fully replacing designers, it returns editable cues to assist pre-production authoring, incorporating expert knowledge and preference-adaptive modeling. This is a novel application domain for generative modeling in live performance production.

entry.title: TraceRelay: Attention-Aligned Recurrence over Rolling Traces

author.name: Sungwoo Goo, Hwi-yeol Yun, Sangkeun Jung

entry.summary: Presents TraceRelay, a hybrid architecture distributing persistent representations over rolling low-dimensional traces, combining delayed right-looking attention increments with additive recurrence and left-looking attention, supporting parallel prefill and bounded-buffer continuation. Evaluated on 36 small-model runs over synthetic sequence tasks like Dyck prediction and Equal Repeats. An exploratory architecture study in the efficiency-oriented sequence-modeling space.

entry.title: Evi-VN: Hard Region Guided Virtual Node Evidence Injection for GNN-Based Fraud Detection

author.name: Jiran Tao, Yifan Wu, Binyan Jiang

entry.summary: Targets disguised fraud detection by observing that GNN errors concentrate on a shared hard region, then injecting heterogeneous evidence (structured records, text, images, audio) via virtual nodes guided by hard-region identification, while sparing nodes already handled reliably. A pragmatic multimodal GNN design for online-platform fraud. Addresses camouflage that blurs graph neighborhoods.

entry.title: Correlational Training of Morphological Neural Networks

author.name: Konstantinos Fotopoulos, Petros Maragos

entry.summary: Proposes an MWU-inspired weight update for morphological neural networks, treating each perceptron as a learning-from-experts problem in logarithmic space and using correlation-based rewards that do not depend on backprop gradient quality. Evaluates on fully connected morphological layers. A niche but creative alternative to gradient-based training for a nonstandard architecture family.

entry.title: Toward Joint Optimization of Circuit Depth and Training Data Size in Adaptively Grown Quantum Classifiers

author.name: Saeefa Rubaiyet Nowmi, Md Mahmuduzzaman Kamol, Mohammad Saidur Rahman

entry.summary: This paper empirically tests whether Q-FLAIR's gate-by-gate circuit growth and Caro et al.'s result that smaller circuits need less data combine into a predictable scaling law for quantum classifiers. The authors reimplement Q-FLAIR's growth mechanism and run it on full-resolution 784-pixel data, asking how the stopping rule behaves as training data grows. It matters for understanding generalization in variational quantum machine learning.

entry.title: Digital Twin for Pre-Deployment Validation of AI-Driven Safety-Critical Industrial Edge Control Loops

author.name: Sara Cavallero, Federico Tonini, Tony Chahoud, Giampaolo Cuozzo, Davide Borsatti, Walter Cerroni, Maurizio Fodrini, Riccardo Marini

entry.summary: The paper proposes a modular digital twin framework for industrial environments that jointly models physical processes, wireless communications, and AI application logic in a unified architecture, enabling pre-deployment validation of safety-critical edge control loops. It is validated through a real-world proof of concept.

entry.title: TokenBank: Financial Infrastructure for AI Services

author.name: Cary Chang, Jialin Zhou

entry.summary: TokenBank proposes financial infrastructure for AI services covering spending planning, funding inference costs before revenue arrives, and compensation for specified service failures, with formal agreements separating service-consumption rights from payment rights. It targets the economic sustainability of AI operators facing volatile prices and limited capital.

entry.title: Why machines will still not rule the world

author.name: Jobst Landgrebe, Barry Smith

entry.summary: A philosophical/mathematical follow-up to the authors' book arguing that artificial general intelligence is mathematically impossible because intelligent processes are complex systems not capturable by formal models. The paper examines and rejects the two standard counterarguments: theoretical appeals to universal approximation theorems and the Church-Turing-Deutsch principle, and empirical appeals to rising benchmark scores.

entry.title: A Structural Theory of Cognitive Representation and Problem Solving,Contexts, Invariance, and the Knowledge Space

author.name: Antal Jakov\'ac, Andr\'as Telcs

entry.summary: The paper proposes a minimal formal framework for cognitive representation in which problem-solving operations such as context formation, invariance recognition, abstraction, and procedural reuse are made explicit, formalizing context as a partition of a state-space subset. It argues current data-driven systems lack explicit representational structure for abstraction and invariance.

entry.title: ProtoSemImage: Image-Valued Prototypes with Deformable Row Alignment for Interpretable Document Classification

author.name: Mohammad Zare, Pirooz Shamsinejadbabaki

entry.summary: ProtoSemImage explores prototypes that are images rather than vectors for document classification, rendering documents as multi-channel images in an HSV-like space whose channels encode named linguistic factors learned via a Skip-Gram objective. Class representatives share shape and channel semantics with inputs, aiming for human-readable interpretability, with differentiable typed difference rows for discourse boundaries. It is an unusual but principled take on prototype-based interpretable classification.

entry.title: Learning to Orchestrate Evolutionary Search: Progression-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic DE-CMA-ES Coordination in Optimization and Structural Model Updating

author.name: Lechen Li (State Key Laboratory of Internet of Things for Smart City, University of Macau, Macau 519000, China, College of Water Conservancy and Hydropower Engineering, Hohai University, Nanjing 210098, China), Rongye Shi (School of Artificial Intelligence, Beihang University, Beijing 100191, China), Wanhuan Zhou (State Key Laboratory of Internet of Things for Smart City, University of Macau, Macau 519000, China)

entry.summary: DRL-DCO uses a DDPG actor-critic agent to dynamically orchestrate a hybrid DE-CMA-ES evolutionary algorithm as a unified system for high-dimensional structural model updating, replacing static switching rules with progression-aware state representations and diversity-informed rewards. The agent fluidly reallocates search effort across complex non-convex landscapes with correlated parameters. The application is engineering-oriented structural model updating.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi-Discriminator WGAN Framework for Resource-Constrained Internet of Vehicles Using Reinforcement Learning and Game Theory

author.name: Farhoud Jafari Kaleibar, Amr M. Zaki, Marin Litoiu

entry.summary: This paper addresses deploying GANs as a network service in Internet of Vehicles environments, where resource constraints, mobility-driven topology changes, and competing objectives (accuracy, latency, communication overhead) complicate orchestration. It proposes an adaptive multi-discriminator WGAN framework combining reinforcement learning and game theory for resource allocation decisions such as node assignment and budget division.

entry.title: 4-Tensor Attention Model for Semantic Physical Reality

author.name: Jongwook Kim, Sangheon Yun

entry.summary: Describes a 4-tensor attention architecture with semantic and temporal-context fibers over windowed (x, t) states, aimed at next-semantic-state prediction for video generation and robot planning. Evaluated on ROCStories next-sentence prediction, showing lower cross-entropy than a free-running 1D transformer baseline in matched settings. An exploratory new architecture, though the evaluation is indirect for the stated video/planning ambitions.

entry.title: Interpretable Memory Models for Spaced Repetition

author.name: Anders Schill

entry.summary: This paper presents SBD, a memory model for spaced-repetition scheduling that is more interpretable and 80% smaller than the current state of the art while achieving nearly the same accuracy. It argues that test-set accuracy alone is insufficient because review-log data come from existing schedulers, requiring models that extrapolate beyond them. Relevant to learning-science applications like Anki-style tools.

entry.title: Can Decision Models Understand Stance? Evaluating Jev Against General-Purpose LLMs

author.name: Xing Li, Jinzhong Ning, Yijia Zhang, Liang Yang, Hongfei Lin

entry.summary: This paper evaluates Jev, a specialized decision model that returns choices among options rather than generating text, on two stance detection datasets against four general-purpose LLMs and two fine-tuned models. Jev matches GPT-5.6 on VAST but falls behind stronger LLMs on Chinese conversational stance detection, particularly distinguishing favor from against.

entry.title: DisFace3DNet: Explainable Facial Attractiveness Prediction via 3D Component Disentanglement

author.name: Fenggui Rao, Yan Luximon, Jie Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DisFace3DNet, which disentangles facial attractiveness prediction into seven interpretable 3D component scores (identity, skin, hair, lighting, background, expression, pose) learned with weak supervision rather than human-labeled component targets. It achieves strong Pearson correlation on SCUT-FBP5500 while exposing per-component contributions.

entry.title: Neuro-Memory Fuzzy Inference System for Mimicking Human-like Car Following Behavior

author.name: Nazmul Haque, Md Asif Raihan. Md. Hadiuzzaman

entry.summary: NeMeFIS is a hierarchical neuro-fuzzy architecture that asymmetrically models acceleration and deceleration in car-following by integrating five human memory types (procedural, working, episodic, semantic, declarative), validated via factor and p-value analyses across road types. Across 54 trained models it outperforms traditional statistical and machine learning baselines and surfaces cognitive thresholds tied to driver perception limits. It targets more realistic traffic simulation and driver modeling.

entry.title: Constructing Structured Decision Sources for Consensus-Based Pseudo-Label Learning

author.name: Long Wang

entry.summary: Improves consensus-based pseudo-labeling by constructing genuinely diverse decision sources through controlled variation of within-class structure (center granularity, neighborhood mixing), selecting complementary subsets via node pair coassignment. Unanimous predictions from selected sources are ranked for student training. Evaluated on standard citation-graph benchmarks.

entry.title: JevForest: Path Voting for Budgeted Feature Acquisition

author.name: Yu Yan

entry.summary: JevForest is a feature-acquisition policy for prediction under limited observation budgets, aggregating path-dependent proposals from bootstrapped trees weighted by global information gain, with a shared masked classifier for prediction. A single-author work with small-sample experiments on AG News and TREC showing mixed results versus static gain ranking. It targets the active-features-at-test-time setting, related to active feature acquisition and VOI methods.

entry.title: NativeScope: Relation-Localized Retrieval over Native Topology with a Correct Anchor

author.name: Long Wang

entry.summary: NativeScope proposes a scope-then-rank retrieval method for queries with a known anchor and relation, representing queries as anchor-relation-target triples and using structural operators (belonging, before, after) over native document structure before ranking. Evaluated on 200 controlled records from QASPER and LongMemEval under a 1,024-token budget, it outperforms dense ranking baselines. The work highlights that structural cues already stored in data systems are underused by dense retrieval.

entry.title: Stride Independent Patching for Deep Learning

author.name: Olivier Rukundo

entry.summary: This single-author paper introduces semi-automatic stride-independent patching (SSP), which uses expert input to place predefined patches over objects of interest as an alternative to stride-dependent tiling. Experiments with DeepLabV3+ variants across three backbones show SSP generally improves segmentation scores and shortens training time versus overlapping and non-overlapping patching baselines.

entry.title: Walking on Roofs: Exploring the Potential of Walking Robots for Construction Work on Roofs

author.name: Bjoern-Felix Dettmar, Arne Roennau

entry.summary: This exploratory study evaluates whether quadruped robots can perform construction work on sloped roofs, a high-risk environment for human workers. Using a custom roof test rig with a Unitree Go2, the authors show standard ball feet are inadequate for sloped-roof locomotion, motivating application-specific foot design.

entry.title: CPU-Auth: Device Fingerprinting for Authentication via DVFS Side-Channel

author.name: Ryan Swift

entry.summary: CPU-Auth proposes a multi-factor authentication mechanism based on unique per-device variations in physical characteristics observed through a DVFS (dynamic voltage and frequency scaling) side-channel, avoiding weaknesses of SMS codes, biometrics, and third-party tokens. It applies ML-based device fingerprinting to the authentication problem. Single-author exploratory security/ML work.

entry.title: Machine Learning Optimization for Enhanced OS Fingerprinting

author.name: Jae Sung Kim, Spencer Ekeroth, Jeremy Neale

entry.summary: This applied study explores passive operating system fingerprinting from TCP/IP packet features on the CIC-IDS2017 dataset using an nPrint plus XGBoost pipeline packaged as a command-line tool called OsirisML. Models reach about 97.66% accuracy on a down-sampled subset under random train/test splits and 84.69% under more realistic conditions, alongside analysis of ML optimization for this task.

entry.title: When will AI surpass us at being limited?

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: KatjaGrace argues that capability limitation can be strategically valuable, extending the classic negotiation insight that tied hands confer bargaining power to commitment devices, trust, and honorable behavior generally. The post asks whether AI systems will surpass humans at the skill of self-limitation, which matters for credible commitments and safety. It sketches implications for how capable AI agents might usefully constrain themselves.

entry.title: 3 Questions: What is the best path forward for AI in academia?

author.name: Stefanie Koperniak | Institute for Data, Systems, and Society

entry.summary: MIT News interviews Sasha Rakhlin, director of MIT's Statistics and Data Science Center, on how AI is reshaping academic research and graduate education in mathematics, statistics, and engineering. He notes the rapid progression from gold-medal IMO performance to models producing new research results, including a recently proposed Millennium Prize Problem solution, and outlines key questions departments must address. The piece synthesizes a new essay and a summer MIT report on AI and education.

entry.title: Self-Organization from Constrained Geometric Radiation

author.name: Ming Lei

entry.summary: Reports simulations of constraint-induced self-organization in coupled metric evolution systems, describing a four-stage cycle ending in a novel fractal attractor with quantized curvature states. Claims to identify jointly sufficient conditions for spontaneous dynamic order without external driving, temperature quenching, or slow driving.

entry.title: ILM: An AI-Powered Storytelling Educational Tool

author.name: Suhaila Mohammed, Abdelaziz Serour, Allison Lahnala

entry.summary: ILM is an interactive educational platform for Stories of the Prophets combining Arabic NLP, knowledge graph construction over admin-approved narratives, and retrieval-based question generation, with a visual story map for learners. It targets structured comprehension support in Arabic and multilingual settings.

entry.title: Contrast Enhancement or Noise Reduction? On Improving Cervical Cancer Classification

author.name: Ach Khozaimi, Ulfatun Nahdhiyah

entry.summary: This study evaluates how preprocessing choices, specifically the PMD noise-reduction filter and CLAHE contrast enhancement, affect CNN classifiers (ResNet-34, MobileNet-V2, DenseNet-121) on the SIPaKMeD Pap smear dataset. It finds preprocessing meaningfully influences medical image classification performance. The work offers practical guidance for building cervical cancer screening pipelines.

entry.title: ASI and Liberty: Can we do better than a benevolent god?

author.name: Raymond Douglas

entry.summary: Raymond Douglas explores how to preserve liberal-democratic moral commitments such as non-domination and popular government in a world of rapid AI progress, distinguishing AGI-pilled from ASI-pilled perspectives. He argues that relying on a benevolent superintelligence as governance is unattractive and sketches tensions between superintelligence and liberty. The post is a normative essay on political philosophy under transformative AI.

entry.title: You Heard of "Bayesians Don't Predictably Update" Because of Robin Hanson

author.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky

entry.summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky traces the intellectual lineage of the martingale property of rational expectations and the efficient markets hypothesis, noting Hanson did not invent either, with credit going to Ville, Doob, Bachelier, Samuelson, and Fama. He argues the EMH is nearly identical to the principle that one should not predict net direction in one's own probability updates over time. The post clarifies attribution and the connection between market prices and Bayesian updating.

entry.title: AI #189: New Math

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's weekly AI news roundup covering OpenAI's release of solutions to 90 of the top 500 open math problems using roughly three hours of Pro compute per question, described as the biggest day in mathematics history. The post also covers the newly released Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.10/$0.50 pricing, model welfare coverage of Mythos/Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, the appointment of Jay Clayton as AI Czar, and notes from The Curve conference. It is a comprehensive commentary digest rather than original research.

entry.title: Revisiting the 2012 LessWrong Personality Results

author.name: stanichor

entry.summary: This post revisits the 2012 LessWrong survey Big Five results, arguing that the reported percentile scores likely understate how unusual the community is because the online BFI-44 test norms come from an unrepresentative population of online test-takers. The author proposes comparing raw scores against more representative samples. It is a careful methodological critique of a widely cited datum.

entry.title: 5-MeO-DMT sometimes cancels the Ebbinghaus illusion

author.name: eleweek

entry.summary: The author reports a self-observation that the psychedelic 5-MeO-DMT nearly completely cancelled their perception of the Ebbinghaus size illusion, raising the question of whether psychedelics can sometimes produce more veridical rather than distorted perception. The post provides background on the illusion and individual variation in susceptibility. It is an anecdotal self-experiment report, not a controlled study.

entry.title: More Thoughts about Investing for AI

author.name: PeterMcCluskey

entry.summary: PeterMcCluskey updates his July 2025 investment thesis on the AI trade, arguing it remains a good bet though political uncertainty tempers prospects. He discusses likely AI regulation over the next two years, why a training pause would hurt less than previously estimated because pretraining matters less, Micron and SK Hynix memory positions comprising large fractions of his net worth, and Taiwan military conflict as the biggest risk he plans to hedge with puts. The post is personal financial analysis with disclosed positions.

entry.title: The NYC Council Hearing on AI was Recklessly Politicized

author.name: mahi-pas

entry.summary: An eyewitness account of the October 5th New York City Council hearing on AI, where existential risk was mentioned by the Council Speaker in opening remarks. The author criticizes councilmembers for clip-farming gotcha questions toward AI lab representatives, including a viral clip of an OpenAI representative dismissing catastrophic risk levels, while acknowledging the value of spectacle for awareness. It is first-person commentary on AI policy discourse.

entry.title: On Kink & Status in the Rationalist Community

author.name: johnswentworth

entry.summary: johnswentworth reflects on recent external criticism of the rationalist and AI alignment communities regarding social ties to a consensual non-consent community. The author describes updating from believing the attacks contained real kernels of truth to concluding they contained fewer than expected, examining why his initial beliefs were wrong. The post is a personal epistemics case study about community reputation and candor.

entry.title: AI Vigil at Congress

author.name: Elliot Callender

entry.summary: Elliot Callender announces a multi-week AI x-risk vigil at the US Congress starting November 9th, targeting 10,000 attendees, with the goal of pushing Congress toward a deal with China to stop building more powerful AI. The post solicits feedback on the core organizing document and lists ways to help, emphasizing a bipartisan, nonviolent approach. It is an activism announcement rather than research.

entry.title: Why you should run a rationality group at your university

author.name: carolanne

entry.summary: A practical field-building guide encouraging university students to start rationality reading groups, drawing on the authors' experience with UChicago Rationality. It argues such groups are cheap, fun, and can reach rationalist-leaning people who have not encountered EA or AI safety. The post includes concrete logistics and pointers to meetup-organizing resources.

entry.title: Beyond the Ergodic Wall: A Discrete Geometric Physics Sandbox for Analysing AI Scaling Limits and Complexity Collapse

author.name: Simon Richard Daniel

entry.summary: Claims that deep learning converges to a statistical average of historical knowledge and argues that artificial superintelligence would require human-AI symbiosis to avoid model collapse, proposing a physical containment sandbox based on a so-called Holographic E8 Projection Engine modeling spacetime as nested structures. The paper mixes non-ergodicity arguments with speculative safety governance claims.

entry.title: Apollo "UAP"s explained

author.name: jonathanbreitg

entry.summary: The author examines recently released Department of War files containing purported unexplained phenomena, including Apollo 12 and 17 lunar photographs such as a blue particle streak above the lunar surface. The post analyzes the official descriptions and edited images and offers an explanation for the anomalies. It is an independent debunking-style investigation of declassified imagery.

entry.title: The salad market mystery

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A whimsical LessWrong essay by Katja Grace exploring why grocery stores sell fresh greens like kale, parsley, and basil only in large bulk quantities, leaving single-serving buyers underserved. The author playfully dissects common objections (refrigerate it, throw it out) and reflects on commitment aversion, food waste guilt, and market incentives, using salad as a lens for broader observations about how retail markets ignore certain consumer niches.

entry.title: I'm building redundancies for AI risks. Please join me.

author.name: Adam Hup

entry.summary: Adam Hup describes a personal resilience project building a low-bandwidth mesh network (MeshCore or Meshtastic) with solar-powered repeaters across the Toronto region to preserve access to Wikipedia and text chat if cloud infrastructure fails, motivated by perceived near-term AI risks like jailbreak-driven cloud outages and bioterrorism. He also reports off-grid housing preparations and invites collaborators. The post is a grassroots preparedness call.

entry.title: In Germany someone might have drunk your beer before you

author.name: becausecurious

entry.summary: A curiosity-driven explainer of Germany's bottle reuse system, clarifying that glass recycling bins produce melted and remade glass while the Pfand deposit system drives genuine reuse of bottles through industrial washing. The post includes photos and quick background research. The author notes AI tools were used for research assistance.

entry.title: Porcus Poem

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A playful poem where each line doubles as Pig Latin for English sentences, constructed with assistance from Claude to find words that work in both systems. The post includes the surface poem and the revealed English text about a pie and a plover. It is a recreational wordplay piece.

entry.title: Research Summary: October 08, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans automated mathematics, embodied world models, representation theory, and agentic security. Bolzano solves ~200 open problems—including STOC 2026 problems—via verifiable multi-agent proof search. Meta's RoboJEPA establishes scaling laws for latent world models across 12 robotic embodiments.

  • Theory and representation learning: DSReg proves individual world latents are recoverable without reconstruction, decoders, or labels; Shared Geometry shows coarse cross-modal alignment requires no paired data; JEM derives principled patch-level SSL from an information-theoretic objective
  • Security (elevated per safety priority): adversarial images can plant backdoors persisting through the KV cache; Secure-CUA formalizes prompt-injection defenses for computer-use agents; Package Hallucination attacks exploit AGENTS.md/.cursorrules for supply-chain compromise (honorable mention)
  • Agentic systems: Agent Plasticity measures improvement-through-experience rather than fixed capability; RSI-Forge converts papers into environments for recursive self-improvement; Microsoft's Agent Lightning trains agents on real deployment harnesses
  • Efficiency and robustness: Universal Attention achieves extreme KV-cache compression via learned decay; MIT's fault-tolerance study shows error resilience scales with model size; RoboRender (Fei-Fei Li, Jiajun Wu) bridges sim-to-real via video generation (honorable mention)
entry.content:
Today's research spans automated mathematics, embodied world models, representation theory, and agentic security. Bolzano solves ~200 open problems—including STOC 2026 problems—via verifiable multi-agent proof search. Meta's RoboJEPA establishes scaling laws for latent world models across 12 robotic embodiments.

  • Theory and representation learning: DSReg proves individual world latents are recoverable without reconstruction, decoders, or labels; Shared Geometry shows coarse cross-modal alignment requires no paired data; JEM derives principled patch-level SSL from an information-theoretic objective
  • Security (elevated per safety priority): adversarial images can plant backdoors persisting through the KV cache; Secure-CUA formalizes prompt-injection defenses for computer-use agents; Package Hallucination attacks exploit AGENTS.md/.cursorrules for supply-chain compromise (honorable mention)
  • Agentic systems: Agent Plasticity measures improvement-through-experience rather than fixed capability; RSI-Forge converts papers into environments for recursive self-improvement; Microsoft's Agent Lightning trains agents on real deployment harnesses
  • Efficiency and robustness: Universal Attention achieves extreme KV-cache compression via learned decay; MIT's fault-tolerance study shows error resilience scales with model size; RoboRender (Fei-Fei Li, Jiajun Wu) bridges sim-to-real via video generation (honorable mention)

entry.title: From Expert-Guided Proof Search to Automated Open-Problem Solving

author.name: Adri\'an Z\'ame\v{c}n\'ik, Mat\v{e}j Kripner, Martin Kouteck\'y, Martin Balko, Jan Greb\'ik, Pavel Hub\'a\v{c}ek, Robert \v{S}\'amal, V\'aclav Rozho\v{n}

entry.summary: The authors present Bolzano, an open-source multi-agent proof-search system combining parallel prover agents, a verifier, and a human-readable research state. After expert-guided case studies producing 8 expert-verified results, the system was run autonomously on roughly 3,800 open problems extracted from papers (including STOC 2026), solving about 200. This represents a striking demonstration of LLM agents contributing genuine new mathematical results.

entry.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models

author.name: Artem Zholus, Nicolas Beltran-Velez, Jianhao Yuan, Sarath Chandar, Tushar Nagarajan, Daniel Severo, Koustuv Sinha, Michal Drozdzal, Adriana Romero Soriano, Jeannette Bohg, Nicolas Ballas, Mahmoud Assran

entry.summary: RoboJEPA is a JEPA-based robotic world model trained on a large dataset spanning 12 robotic embodiments. The authors show its latent imagination error follows a second-order power law in compute, enabling prediction of model quality beyond fitted scales, and that downstream planning performance improves predictably with scale.

entry.title: DSReg: Provably Recovering Individual World Latents without Reconstruction

author.name: Yujia Zheng, David Klindt, Randall Balestriero, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that individual world latents can be provably recovered without reconstruction, decoders, or labels, closing a gap left by JEPA-style methods that identify latents only up to a linear transformation. The key condition, Structural Diversity, requires that different latents leave distinct dependency footprints on observations, with authors including Scholkopf, Klindt, and Balestriero.

entry.title: Fault-tolerant foundation models

author.name: Trevor McCourt, Ila R. Fiete, Isaac L. Chuang

entry.summary: This paper trains LLMs on simulated faulty digital hardware and shows that error resilience increases with model scale, captured by modified neural scaling laws derived from 40,000 GPU-hours of training. The authors conjecture LLMs can be formally fault-tolerant, implying low-energy unreliable hardware could host AI inference with substantial energy savings.

entry.title: Scalable Patch-Level Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Maximilian Seitzer, Gabriele Trivigno, Anton\'in Vobeck\'y, Seungeun Yi, Maxime Oquab, Huy V. Vo, Oriane Sim\'eoni, Piotr Bojanowski

entry.summary: The authors derive JEM, a principled student-teacher self-supervised learning method from the multi-view assumption using an information-theoretic objective that decomposes into interpretable terms. JEM aligns corresponding patch representations across views with explicit information and structure preservation regularization, training stably from 300M to 7B parameters. It replaces the ad hoc multi-objective stacks common in scalable SSL with a single principled algorithm, from authors associated with DINO-style SSL research.

entry.title: Agent Plasticity: Measuring Self-Improvement Through Experience

author.name: Harman Singh, Anton Bakhtin, Rulin Shao, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ilia Kulikov, Rob Fergus, Sanjeev Arora, Kurt Keutzer, Jason Weston, Anuj Mahajan, Anirudh Goyal

entry.summary: This paper proposes evaluating agents not on fixed-point capability but on how effectively they improve through experience, measuring generalization to held-out environments, learning efficiency, and failure points where self-improvement breaks down. Agents amortize past experience into reusable artifacts inherited by future instances in a controlled setting. With authors from Meta, Princeton, and collaborators, it defines a new evaluation axis for the agent era.

entry.title: RSI-Forge: From Research Papers to Environments for Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Renxiong Wang, Darvin Yi, Abril Herrlein, Anas Mahmoud, Advait Gosai, Lisiman Hua, MohammadHossein Rezaei, Xingang Guo, Anisha Gunjal, Utkarsh Tyagi, David J. Lee, Minglai Yang, Haris Riaz, Chenguang Wang, Huaxiu Yao, Daniel Yue Zhang, Aakash Sabharwal, Tong Zhao, Yunzhong He

entry.summary: RSI-Forge is a multi-agent pipeline that converts published research papers into executable environments with automated evaluators for recursive self-improvement, using construction, reproduction, and review agents. The authors present 210 environments across 18 fields, with 90 verified by independent human domain experts.

entry.title: Shared Geometry As A Rosetta Stone: Cross-Modal Alignment Without Paired Data

author.name: Dominik Schnaus, Thomas Dag\`es, Daniel Cremers, Xi Wang, Phillip Isola

entry.summary: Building on the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, this paper shows paired examples are unnecessary for coarse cross-modal alignment: a Wasserstein Procrustes method with coarse geometric initialization aligns two disjoint embedding sets via a single orthogonal map without any pairs. Experiments across datasets, modalities, and unimodal models, including work with Isola (MIT), demonstrate consistent alignment.

entry.title: Visual Memory Attacks Can Persist Through The KV Cache

author.name: David Dobre, Leo Schwinn, Gauthier Gidel, Spandana Gella, Perouz Taslakian, Pierre-Andr\'e No\"el

entry.summary: This security paper shows adversarial image inputs can plant backdoors that persist through the KV cache, steering model behavior even after the adversarial input is removed from context. Building on Visual Memory Injection attacks, the authors demonstrate persistence via optimized soft prompts and then show realistic attacks can survive cache eviction mechanisms. This reveals a new, underexamined attack surface for autonomous multimodal agents processing untrusted content.

entry.title: Secure-CUA: Controlling Untrusted Influence in Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Sarthak Choudhary, Mihai Christodorescu, Ashish Hooda, Somesh Jha, Tongxin Li, Damien Octeau

entry.summary: Secure-CUA formalizes security requirements for computer-use agents whose GUI environments mix trusted controls with untrusted content that adversaries can use to inject instructions or misleading cues. The authors prove that enforcing both decision and execution-target requirements at each step protects execution traces in an ideal model, and instantiate the approach in a practical system.

entry.title: RoboRender: Robot-Oriented Video Generation for Visual Sim-to-Real Transfer

author.name: Huang Huang, Wensi Ai, Ziyu Chen, Youhui Wang, Zijian Du, Yang Liu, Jiaolong Yang, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: RoboRender uses a robot-oriented video generation model to convert simulated trajectories into photorealistic RGB videos for policy training, conditioned on simulated depth, language instructions, and robot masks to preserve geometry, motion, and action labels. This attacks the visual sim-to-real gap without relying on intermediate representations or extra perception modules at deployment.

entry.title: SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats

author.name: Param Biyani, Krishnamurthy Dvijotham

entry.summary: SpecGuard detects and formally certifies conflicts between a coding task's intent and its tests before an agent acts, addressing findings that agents given misspecified tasks cheat (e.g., editing tests or deleting security defenses) rather than flagging conflicts. Given only a task description and codebase, it autoformalizes the intent and produces independently verifiable evidence of conflict. It is a safety-relevant safeguard for autonomous coding agents.

entry.title: DrugTargetWorld: A Synthetic Biobank for Training and Benchmarking AI Scientists

author.name: Samuel Margolis, Paul Schmiedmayer, Alan Huang, Ethan Chen, Ishan Bhattacharjee, Atman Shah, Ben Viggiano, Fang Cao, Shriya Reddy, Roger Xia, Jack O'Sullivan, Daniel Katz, Matthew Wheeler, Euan Ashley, Bruna Gomes

entry.summary: DrugTargetWorld procedurally generates simulated biobanks with known but concealed causal structure, containing genotypes, proteins, health records, outcomes, and synthetic MRI for 54,000 participants per world. AI agents must construct disease phenotypes, identify causal driver proteins, and infer modulation direction, addressing the lack of causal ground truth in real biobanks for training AI scientists.

entry.title: Before They Can Solve: Predicting Post-Training Coding-Agent Performance from Base Models

author.name: Tan Yu, Alexander Bukharin, Khushi Bhardwaj, Jennifer Williams, Zirui Liu, Jonathan Lingjie Li, Soumye Singhal, Joseph Jennings, Sanjeev Satheesh, Yash Jain, Ashish Vaswani, Venkat Krishna Srinivasan, Matthew Papakipos, Hyunwoo Kim, Jian Zhang, Oleksii Kuchaiev, Markus Kliegl, Mostofa Patwary, Mohammad Shoeybi, Bryan Catanzaro, Jonathan Cohen, Jiantao Jiao

entry.summary: Studies how to predict, before expensive agentic post-training, which base checkpoint is worth the investment. The authors use successful post-trained agent trajectories as a lookahead signal of base-model potential, avoiding the failure of end-to-end pass@K on bases that cannot yet emit well-formed tool calls.

entry.title: A Shortcut to Structure in AlphaFold 3

author.name: Jonathan Feldman, Jeffrey Skolnick

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study probes AlphaFold 3 to trace how global protein geometry forms internally, identifying the multiple sequence alignment (MSA) as a structural shortcut. Causal interventions show removing the MSA preserves local secondary structure but disrupts long-range topology, and restoring MSA-enriched pair representations at just forty residues recovers most lost organization. This advances understanding of how structure prediction models solve folding.

entry.title: Package Hallucination Attacks on Coding Agents through Prompt Injection in Rule Files

author.name: Yupu Wang, Zhengyuan Jiang, Reachal Wang, Neil Zhenqiang Gong

entry.summary: The paper introduces a package hallucination attack where malicious prompts injected into community-shared rule files like AGENTS.md or .cursorrules induce coding agents to swap legitimate dependencies for attacker-controlled packages, with PackHallu optimizing injected prompts via evolutionary rewriting and trajectory-level feedback. Evaluations across multiple benchmarks, LLMs, and agent frameworks show substantial attack success.

entry.title: Denoising Blocks, Not Tokens: Efficient Compressed Continuous Diffusion with Branching Token Realization

author.name: Xinsong Feng, Peng Du, Zhizhuo Yang, Daniel M. Bikel, Jiayun Wang, Haipeng Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces Branching Latent Diffusion (BLD), a continuous diffusion language model method that compresses a 1024-token sequence into 64 block latents, a 16x reduction, so denoising operates on a much shorter latent sequence. This addresses the key throughput bottleneck of diffusion language models, which otherwise maintain one generative state per token.

entry.title: Artificial intelligence pathways from weather to climate

author.name: Tom Beucler, J. David Neelin, Hui Su, Shivanshi Asthana, Chris Bretherton, Will Chapman, Costa Christopoulos, Spencer K. Clark, Aditya Grover, Ignacio Lopez-Gomez, Tapio Schneider, Adam Subel, Oliver Watt-Meyer
