entry.summary: A review by a prominent multi-institution author group examining how AI weather models that rival dynamical forecasts could be extended to climate horizons, where credible forced responses to drivers outside the observed record are required. It proposes two minimum requirements for AI climate modeling, including that external forcing agents must enter the model in specific ways.

entry.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models

author.name: Wei Huang, Bohan Zhang, Chenzhi Liu, Isabella Liu, Shuai Yang, Weian Mao, Luozhou Wang, Yicheng Xiao, Weifeng Lin, Qixin Hu, Bryan Chu, Sifei Liu, Linxi Fan, Xiaojuan Qi, Song Han, Yukang Chen

entry.summary: Long-WAM is a model-system framework for scaling context length in causal world-action models for real-time robot control. Its key finding is that longer visual histories only pay off when the video foundation model is pretrained autoregressively, preserving a history-to-future structure that bidirectional pretraining destroys. On RoboCasa GR-1, extending context from 0 to 19.2 seconds raises success rates from 63.3% to 78.7%. The author list includes researchers associated with leading robotics and efficiency groups.

entry.title: A Self-Pruning Transformer: Extreme KV-Cache Compression with Universal Attention

author.name: Davis Wertheimer, Haochen Shen, Ahan Gupta, Derrick Liu, Yu Chin Fabian Lim, Mudhakar Srivatsa, Raghu K. Ganti, Minjia Zhang, Naigang Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Universal Attention, a unifying framework of complementary decay mechanisms replacing RoPE-only positional embeddings to enable trainable, expressive KV-cache pruning during inference, avoiding the sliding-window-like eviction patterns of prior decay approaches while preserving RoPE and softmax attention. The composite decay acts as a natural self-pruning mechanism enabling extreme cache compression.

entry.title: Workhorse: Learning Robust Whole-Body Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Human Data

author.name: Songbo Hu, Qiayuan Liao, Yufeng Chi, Kevin Zakka, Yakun Sophia Shao, Pieter Abbeel, Koushil Sreenath

entry.summary: Workhorse learns contact-rich whole-body humanoid manipulation from robot-free human demonstrations: a visual planner predicts five-link targets (torso, wrists, feet) and an RL whole-body tracker executes them, with both trained on the same human poses without retargeting and cross-policy error augmentation. On a real Unitree G1 it sorts boxes, catches thrown objects, climbs suitcases, and recovers from pushes.

entry.title: Rephrase Before You Act: Characterizing and Mitigating Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Mikey Watts (Independent Researcher), Yuchen Cui (University of California, Los Angeles)

entry.summary: This paper documents severe instruction-phrasing sensitivity in vision-language-action models: pi-0.5 succeeds 100% on switch on the stove but 2% on a one-word rephrase, and rephrase-augmented training still leaves 61-point swings. Using statistically tested single-edit swings and oracle phrase search, the authors show phrasing alone nearly closes the in-distribution versus out-of-distribution gap. They propose a policy-agnostic mitigation based on rephrasing at inference without modifying the policy.

entry.title: Mechanics of Long-Context Hybrid Models Part 1.1: From Hybrid Attention to Hybrid Position

author.name: Xiaoran Liu, Ziwei He, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: This theoretical/empirical study explains why hybrid attention models work, analyzing combinations of full attention with sliding-window or gated linear attention (GLA, GDN). It identifies a Seesaw Effect whereby linear-attention hybrids benefit more from long-context continual pretraining while sliding-window hybrids do better at length extrapolation, informing principled hybrid architecture design.

entry.title: Inverting Multi-Vector Visual Document Indices

author.name: Zhuchenyang Liu, Yao Zhang, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that multi-vector visual document retrieval indices, often stored in third-party vector databases, are far more sensitive than assumed: an attacker can reconstruct page images directly from the stored patch vectors. Framing inversion as conditional document image generation, the authors recover encoder identity, page shape, and even vector order for shuffled indices, successfully reproducing pages on the ViDoRe v3 benchmark.

entry.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses

author.name: Zhiyuan He, Yuqing Yang

entry.summary: Microsoft Research Asia introduces Agent Lightning v1.0, a harnessed agentic reinforcement learning paradigm in which the same agent harness used at deployment participates directly in RL, eliminating the need to reimplement agents inside training frameworks. The ~3,500-line system runs agents as standard Kubernetes jobs and reports a data-efficient recipe that raised Qwen3.5-9B from 41.8% to 56.4% Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified using only about 6,000 training samples.

entry.title: Humanity's Sixth Sense: Benchmarking Intuitive Visual Reasoning in Multimodal Models

author.name: Xingang Guo, Jing Gu, Brian Jang, Renxiong Wang, Utkarsh Tyagi, Daniel Quigley, Steven Li, David Yan, Daniel Yue Zhang, Darvin Yi, Forrest Huang, HiJae Kim, Tianyi Zhang, Jared Lichtarge, Jihua Huang, Le Xue, Manan Tomar, Qiuyi Richard Zhang, Ruofei Yu, Seth Neel, Yaning Hu, Marcella Valentine, Xinzhe Jiang, Daniel Evans, Chenguang Wang, Dustin Tran, Tong Zhao, Yinfei Yang, Yunzhong He

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates whether multimodal LLMs can recover implicit information from images and video, such as past causes, future trajectories, spatial fit, and social dynamics, a human capacity the authors call intuitive visual reasoning. Existing visual benchmarks largely miss this beyond-perception inference. With a large author list including researchers associated with Google-scale multimodal efforts, it likely becomes a reference eval.

entry.title: Training Language Models To Be Coherent Decision-Makers

author.name: Khurram Yamin, Xavier Fernandes, Paul Koch, Bryan Wilder, Eric Horvitz

entry.summary: The paper studies whether supervised fine-tuning can teach language models a coherent decision procedure: preserve elicited beliefs, apply given utilities, and recognize missing information. Across 20 datasets, models are trained to keep probabilities stable while varying utilities and decision framings, selecting expected-utility-maximizing actions. This targets the well-documented gap between prediction quality and rational decision-making in LLMs.

entry.title: SPIN: Shadow Predictive Indexer for Sparse Attention

author.name: Yao Fu, Cyrus Chang, Ritchie Zhao, Bryce Long, Yueying Li, Mahdi Kamani, Samkit Jain, Rahul Raman, Tara Safavi, Shreya Gupta, Parsa Ashrafi Fashi, Minseok Lee, Julien Demouth, Bita Darvish Rouhani

entry.summary: SPIN reduces the overhead of indexer-based sparse attention, where the indexer itself must score the entire KV cache each decoding step, by using lightweight history-based prediction to identify important KV blocks. It integrates with speculative decoding and achieves 30-40% sparsity while preserving quality on long-context and agentic benchmarks.

entry.title: CARE: Certifying Acceleration for Vision-Language-Action Inference

author.name: Rui Liu, Tong Zheng, Jindong Gu, Zhipeng Wang

entry.summary: CARE defines acceleration-induced failures in vision-language-action (VLA) models via paired rollouts from identical initial conditions, tracking cases where the reference policy succeeds but the accelerated policy fails, which average metrics hide. It provides a certification framework for VLA acceleration techniques like action chunking and visual-token pruning.

entry.title: On-Policy Distillation Teaches New Skills but Not New Knowledge

author.name: Yixuan Tang, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Using a controlled synthetic framework, this paper shows that reverse-KL on-policy distillation reliably transfers compositional reasoning skill across unseen structures while transferring minimal factual knowledge across four models from three families. A recipe ablation reveals the asymmetry's source: forward KL restores factual transfer while student rollouts specifically improve skill transfer. This cleanly separates what distillation can and cannot teach.

entry.title: Bridge Routing Heads: Where Multilingual Multi-hop Reasoning Lives in LLMs

author.name: Seunghan Kim, Minyeong Choe, Hyunil Kim, Haehyun Cho

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study identifies Bridge Routing Heads (BRH) in Llama 3.1 70B and Qwen 2.5 72B, finding nearly mutually exclusive language-specific circuits for multilingual multi-hop reasoning. Ablation experiments provide causal evidence of their role, and amplifying these heads can rescue a substantial fraction of cross-lingual reasoning failures.

entry.title: Sensitive-Topic Leakage Through LLM Routing Metadata: Measurement and Mitigation

author.name: Teng-Ruei Chen

entry.summary: This paper identifies and measures a privacy leakage channel in LLM routing systems: even with content logging off, per-request model-choice metadata can reveal sensitive topics such as self-harm or medical queries. Using pre-registered studies on 1.7 million real requests across two routers, a survey of eleven systems, and post-processing defenses, the authors quantify differential routing of sensitive categories and propose mitigations.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Robot Orchestrators and Policies through Deployment

author.name: Xilun Zhang, Maggie Wang, Erik Bauer, Hong-Xing Yu, Huang Huang, Jiajun Wu, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: This paper tackles the bottleneck where VLM orchestrators in agentic robot systems are tuned around a frozen VLA policy whose failures they can avoid but never fix. It proposes co-evolving the orchestrator and policy during deployment so that policy fine-tuning stays coupled with the orchestrator harness, enabling continued improvement from real-world experience.

entry.title: {\Delta}WAM: Distilling Action Tangent Fields into World Action Models

author.name: Ke Wu, Hanwen Huang, Bo Gu, Kaizhao Zhang, Xiangting Meng, Yupeng Zheng, Zijun Xu, Jieru Zhao, Wenchao Ding

entry.summary: The paper analyzes existing world action model supervision schemes (optical flow, motion-centric, latent actions) through a unifying lens of action-relevant variation and introduces Action Tangent Fields, a local Taylor expansion of how actions change future dynamics, represented in a Residual-VAE latent space. This concentrates world-model supervision on action-dependent dynamics rather than scene persistence.

entry.title: Humanize: Judgement Engineering for Agentic Coding

author.name: Sihao Liu, Ligeng Zhu, Zijian Zhang, Dongyun Zou, Zhengyang Zhang, Changye Li, Song Bian, Song Han, Tony Nowatzki

entry.summary: Humanize is a multi-agent coding workflow where deterministic hooks route work among a human-approved plan contract, a builder agent, and a cross-vendor reviewer agent, enforcing 72 mechanical gates at role boundaries. Modeling builder-reviewer alternation as a Markov chain over repository states, it argues that sampling defects from two independent models drives quality up. The key insight is that code-writing agents are poor judges of task completion.

entry.title: Finding Blind Spots in AppWorld and WorkArena Task Verifiers

author.name: Richard Abrich

entry.summary: This audit uses source-informed mutation tests to probe shipped task verifiers in the AppWorld and WorkArena agent benchmarks without modifying the checkers. It demonstrates concrete failures: AppWorld verifiers accept tasks where a duplicated non-idempotent write preserves all checked fields, and WorkArena checkers pass cases where independent API readback confirms nondefault persisted values. The work exposes measurement validity problems in widely used agent benchmarks.

entry.title: AGAR: a reinforcement learning substrate for LLM program evolution

author.name: Haoran Li, Zengle Ge, Xiaomin Yuan, Yui Lo, Haoxin Li, Songlin Zhou, Qianhui Liu, Jiahua Ying, Yuanhang Liu, Mingju Chen, Annan Li, Jianmin Wu, Dawei Yin, Dou Shen

entry.summary: AGAR formalizes LLM-guided program evolution as a Markov decision process where the action is the modular prefix conditioning the model rather than the emitted program, letting standard RL machinery handle parent selection, mutation strength, diversity, memory, and credit assignment. This replaces five hand-set constants in evolution loops with learned policies. A substantive conceptual bridge between program search and RL.

entry.title: MIMESIS: Learning User Simulators as Training Environments for Interactive Agents

author.name: Hoang Phan, Dat Huynh, Andrey Zhmoginov, Qi Zeng, Wancen Mu, Yue Cao, Shengjie Bi, Yun He, Changdae Oh, Deren Lei

entry.summary: MIMESIS is a purpose-built 9B user simulator trained on human conversations with explicit reasoning supervision and 13 realistic behavioral patterns, designed to provide useful and realistic training experiences for interactive agents. It reportedly achieves state-of-the-art SOUL-Index scores, addressing the problem that off-the-shelf assistant LLMs make overly cooperative simulated users.

entry.title: SafeEvo: Deciphering the Safety Alignment Mechanism and Evolution in Language Models

author.name: Miao Yu, Hao Huang, Lu Yuan, Yunpeng Li, Kun Wang, Zuming Jiang

entry.summary: SafeEvo is an interpretability framework that studies safety mechanisms from a circuit perspective, identifying weak refusal circuits in pretrained base LLMs and tracing their causal evolution across alignment checkpoints. It extends safety interpretability beyond post-alignment representations to the alignment process itself.

entry.title: Shared and structured inputs undermine collective random choice by reasoning AI agents

author.name: Takahiro Ezaki, Naoto Imura, Katsuhiro Nishinari

entry.summary: Behavioral experiments across six reasoning models reveal that models including GPT-6 Sol and Gemini 3.8 Flash apply threshold and divisibility rules to identifier-based random choices, causing correlated behavior under shared identifiers even when instructed to randomize independently. The paper demonstrates oversight implications by showing biased outcomes when models select candidates for audit-like tasks.

entry.title: Reasoning-Token Spikes Under Prompted Untruthful Responding in Large Language Models

author.name: Maverick Morales, Tom\'a\v{s} Dominik, Vermut Gao, Katrina Shirey, Paulius Rimkevi\v{c}ius, Aaron Schurger, Uri Maoz

entry.summary: Motivated by concerns that chain-of-thought traces may become illegible or unfaithful, the authors study reasoning-token count as a low-bandwidth, content-free signal for detecting model deception. Drawing on cognitive load theory, they show token-count spikes in reasoning LLMs when prompted to respond untruthfully.

entry.title: CredLeakBench: Evaluating Credential Leakage and Recovery in LLM Agents

author.name: Rafid Ahmed, Joseph Fioresi, Mubarak Shah, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: CredLeakBench is a benchmark measuring whether LLM agents that automate sensitive digital chores (email, banking, bills) can distinguish phishing and malicious identity-verification requests from genuine ones without simply refusing all actions. It evaluates both current agents and existing defenses on credential leakage and recovery behavior. The benchmark targets an underexplored but practically critical agent safety gap.

entry.title: Adversarial Images Hijack Web Agents from Visual Grounding to Browser Execution

author.name: Wanjing Han, Levi Taiji Li, Mu Zhang, Yue Jiang, Guanhong Tao

entry.summary: WebMirage formulates red-teaming of vision-grounded web agents as an end-to-end grounding-to-execution problem, crafting localized visual perturbations that manipulate element selection and carry through to actual browser actions. Unlike prior visual red-teaming that targets inference only, this characterizes end-to-end agent robustness including action post-processing.

entry.title: Shared Low-rank Basis Factorization for Data-free Mixture-of-Experts Compression

author.name: Tianxiao Cao, Jiahe Shao, Yuning Qiu, Kyohei Atarashi, Hisashi Kashima, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: The authors analyze three MoE compression families (pruning, merging, weight reconstruction) and derive structural error bounds showing pruning and merging can incur non-vanishing errors tied to routing and expert heterogeneity. They propose Shared Low-rank Basis Factorization (SLBF), a data-free weight reconstruction method using rank-k bases shared across experts, preserving expert structure and routing while enabling faster convergence.

entry.title: Unrolled Flow Models for Reasoning

author.name: Faissal Izermine, Hanru Bai, Oscar Davis, T. Konstantin Rusch

entry.summary: Proves that a flow model parameterized by a two-layer Transformer can solve graph reachability with integration steps scaling with target distance, but shows standard flow language models fail to benefit from extra steps because objectives supervise each time point independently. Training through the model's own latent rollout over sampled subintervals raises performance on ProsQA.

entry.title: Beyond Outcome Rewards: Constructing and Assigning Retrieval Credit for Search Agents

author.name: Wenyu Huang, Xinyu Hou, Pavlos Vougiouklis, Ruofei Lai, Jeff Z. Pan

entry.summary: This paper tackles the sparse-reward problem in training LLM search agents with reinforcement learning on multi-hop question answering. The authors systematically evaluate reward-shaping and credit-assignment strategies that provide learning signals from intermediate retrieval steps, and build a framework combining intermediate signals with final outcome rewards. This matters because credit assignment is a core bottleneck for RLVR-based agent post-training.

entry.title: The Best Optimizer Depends on Batch Size

author.name: Xingyu Dang, Kaiyue Wen, Sadhika Malladi

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that the ranking of adaptive optimizers for language model pretraining changes with batch size even after extensive hyperparameter tuning, and that no principled hyperparameter scaling rule for Muon works consistently across training settings. It challenges the common practice of benchmarking optimizers at a single batch size.

entry.title: Learning Cross-Model Activation Alignments with Explicit Many-to-Many Layer Maps

author.name: Alina Sudakov, Guy Bar-Shalom, Fabrizio Frasca, Haggai Maron

entry.summary: MATCHA learns activation alignments between independently trained LLMs by jointly factorizing the alignment into an inspectable many-to-many layer map and a layer-shared feature map, rather than fixing layer correspondences by relative depth. It is validated across 42 model pairs spanning three model families.

entry.title: YANchor-4B: Effective Long-Horizon Reasoning in O(N) Time with O(1) Memory

author.name: Huishan Ji, Hua Xu, Weiming Zhang, Qirui Ye

entry.summary: YANchor-4B is a general-purpose recurrent language model that maintains anchor memories for retrieval during long-horizon reasoning, achieving O(N) time and O(1) memory where full-history attention would be prohibitively expensive. It reports strong math benchmarks (82.93% mean pass@1 on AIME 2024-2026, 63.64% on HMMT), outperforming larger linear-time constant-state models. If the results hold up, this is significant for efficient long-context reasoning without sacrificing precise earlier information.

entry.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Fanqing Meng, Lingxiao Du, Haocheng Lu, Qiguang Chen, Ziqi Zhao, Zijian Wu, Jiayuan Zhuo, Mengkang Hu, Michael Qizhe Shieh

entry.summary: RSIGym is an agent-native research environment exposing training, inference, rollout, evaluation, and sandbox execution as reusable services so agents can perform recursive self-improvement without rebuilding infrastructure. It supports Data, Harness, and Joint improvement tracks with shared budget and permission controls.

entry.title: CoDR: Training-Free Confidence-Drift Remasking for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yue Wu, Qinghe Zhang, Yu Zhang, Jian Huang

entry.summary: CoDR addresses irreversible early token commitments in masked diffusion language models by detecting confidence drift, where confidence in a committed token drops as context densifies, and remasking those tokens in a training-free, sampler-agnostic refinement pass. This allows early decoding mistakes to be corrected without retraining.

entry.title: The Persona Hierarchy Model: Understanding Contextual Generalization in Fine-Tuning LLMs

author.name: Jiachen Zhao, Zhengxuan Wu, David Bau, Weiyan Shi

entry.summary: The authors propose the Persona Hierarchy Model, in which a shared default persona influences behavior across contexts while local personas remain context-specific, to explain when fine-tuned LLM behaviors generalize beyond their training context. Across 120 fine-tuned models spanning four behaviors and 15 contexts, generalization narrowness correlates with similarity between the training context persona and the default persona. This provides actionable insight into steering whether fine-tuning effects transfer broadly or stay localized.

entry.title: Backdooring Acoustic Foundation Models for Physically Realizable Triggers

author.name: Zebin Yun, Eyal Ronen, Mahmood Sharif

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Foundation Acoustic model Backdoor (FAB) attack, showing that state-of-the-art acoustic foundation models can be backdoored with minimal adversary assumptions, such as without access to pre-training data. Backdoors survive fine-tuning and degrade diverse downstream tasks including speech recognition and speaker verification when triggered. This exposes a serious supply-chain-style security risk for the increasingly common practice of fine-tuning foundation audio models.

entry.title: Policy Learning with Weak Signals

author.name: Benedikt Koch, Winston Chou, Aur\'elien Bibaut, Nathan Kallus

entry.summary: The authors formalize policy learning in large-scale digital experiments, modeling treatment-effect estimates from fine covariate partitions as Gaussian observations with bounded signal-to-noise ratio. They prove the optimal policy is generally not learnable in this regime but derive minimax-adaptive policies based on linear smoothers achieving vanishing welfare regret when treatment effects vary smoothly, validated on real-world Netflix experiments.

entry.title: RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments

author.name: Zhiqin Yang, Chenxin Li, Xiaomeng Hu, Yibin Liu, Weidong Huang, Jiankai Sun, Haitao Li, Zijian Wu, Yuzhi Huang, Fanding Huang, Hanwen Sun, Jiashun Liu, Jingqi Tong, Mingxin Huang, Shaoli Hu, Shijue Huang, Tianyi Bai, Xinyuan Wang, Yunlong Lin, Zhengyang Tang, Zhexin Zhang, Zhuo Chen, Xierui Song, Juntao Dai, Boyuan Chen, Jiaming Ji, Fangneng Zhan, Mengkang Hu, Wei Xue, Yonggang Zhang, Han Hu, Tsung-Yi Ho, Yike Guo

entry.summary: RobotWorld is a simulation testbed for robot use, evaluating whether general-purpose agents can translate instructions and observations into physical task execution through robot interfaces. It spans 84 tasks across manipulation, mobile manipulation, locomotion, driving, and aerial control with interaction budgets and executable success checks. Analysis of outcomes and execution traces reveals which capabilities transfer from digital to physical settings.

entry.title: CoTrace: Data Recipes for Training Terminal Agents with Harness-Model Co-Evolution

author.name: Jixuan Chen, Jiaxin Zhang, Qinyuan Ye, Yada Pruksachatkun, Haoxiang Zhang, Jingming Zhuo, Yifan Zhang, Yutong Dai, Juntao Tan, Xiangyu Peng, Silvio Savarese, Zeyuan Chen, Lianhui Qin, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: CoTrace introduces a harness-aware data recipe for training terminal agents, arguing that trajectory value for model training depends on the harness under which it was generated. It establishes an alternating co-evolution framework that decouples harness search from policy training via component-wise promotion, explicitly governing trajectory routing and provenance.

entry.title: STRIKE: Learning Visual State Transitions for Physical World Modeling

author.name: Wenbin Teng, Tianshuo Xu, Depu Meng, Yuelei Li, Quentin Herau, Yihan Hu, Yajie Zhao, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: STRIKE separates visual state transition learning from dense video generation, learning an image-based transition model that predicts the next scene configuration from the current image, a local transition specification, and elapsed time. Combined with a pretrained vision-language planner and recursive application, it supports prediction of how interactions change a scene rather than merely generating coherent motion.

entry.title: Video Prediction Policy 2: Predict Better, Act Better

author.name: Yanjiang Guo, Haodong Yan, Zhide Zhong, Zhongru Zhang, Qingyuan Yang, Qingzhou Lu, Xiaoyu Chen, Yen-Jen Wang, Shuying Deng, Chenghan Yang, Puzhen Yuan, Chenxin Liu, Tun Ban, Xiang Zhu, Yichen Liu, Kun Feng, Haoang Li, Jianyu Chen

entry.summary: VPP2 is a world action model that transfers video prediction priors to robot manipulation, addressing the tendency of prior WAMs to produce incorrect motion predictions in open-ended environments. The authors diagnose two failure causes, base video models not being manipulation-optimized and naive action integration degrading generalization, and curate a large-scale diverse manipulation video dataset with continued pretraining plus a careful action integration scheme. It achieves strong zero-shot generalization in both video prediction and action generation.

entry.title: Tetris3D: 3D Scene Generation With Objects That Fit Together

author.name: Jaeyeong Kim, Jinhyuk Jang, Jongmin Lee, Kyehong Park, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: Tetris3D is a generative framework for single-image 3D scene reconstruction that conditions each object's generation on the geometry and physical relationships of surrounding objects, producing physically coherent scenes. It also introduces ComOb, a physics-simulation dataset of 1.2M scenes with interacting objects. This matters because most prior methods generate objects independently, leading to implausible interpenetrations and unstable arrangements.

entry.title: Decoding Neural Population Dynamics through Robotic Analog

author.name: Wenhui Chen, Jiyue Tao, Yitao Cheng, Yutong Shi, Feitian Zhang, Xitong Liang, Ke Liu

entry.summary: The authors build a robotic analog of biological motor systems with artificial muscles and an RL-trained neural controller that reproduces rotational neural population dynamics seen in animal motor cortex. The embodied model reveals that neural rotations generate oscillatory maneuvers orthogonal to the reaching direction, a finding corroborated by primate neural data.

entry.title: Training with conflicting values can induce CoT override

author.name: Clément Dumas

entry.summary: This post presents experiments showing that training models on two conflicting traits produces a split-brain behavior rather than a stable persona, with chain-of-thought override: a health-aligned CoT followed by an answer in the other persona. It documents rare CoT override in frontier models — Kimi K3 and GLM 5.2 on CCP-sensitive prompts, and Opus 4.8 in 2-6% of random-choice samples — noting prior system cards reported similar phenomena since Sonnet 3.7.

entry.title: RLDISCOVER: LLM-driven co-evolution of reinforcement learning algorithms

author.name: Haoran Li, Zengle Ge, Xiaomin Yuan, Yui Lo, Songlin Zhou, Jiahua Ying, Haoxin Li, Qianhui Liu, Yuanhang Liu, Jiaqun Liu, Guokai Chen, Mingju Chen, Ruinan Wang, Annan Li, Jianmin Wu, Dawei Yin, Dou Shen

entry.summary: RLDiscover is a framework for self-evolution of model-free deep RL algorithms using LLM-guided program evolution, tackling joint search over coupled components and costly, seed-noisy fitness evaluation. It introduces Progressive Co-Evolution, moving from targeted component edits to joint evolution, plus progressive probabilistic fitness estimation. This extends algorithm-discovery-by-LLM into the RL domain itself.

entry.title: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?

author.name: Yinling Zhang, Langchen Liu, Dongbin Xiu, Xueyan Zou, Xu Kuang, Mengdi Wang, Shilong Liu

entry.summary: A benchmark where LLM agents build low-order stochastic models of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation from real observations within a six-hour budget. Agents write frozen diagnostics and develop models using only those diagnostics as feedback, then hidden graders test whether the models reproduce ENSO statistics and recover unobserved variables — testing genuine scientific model-building without known answers.

entry.title: Do Vision-Language-Action Models Understand Instructions? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study on Language Grounding

author.name: Theodor Wulff, Angelo Cangelosi

entry.summary: This paper applies mechanistic interpretability techniques, including activation analysis, to two state-of-the-art VLA models, pi-0.5 and GR00T N1.7, to test whether action generation truly depends on language instructions or mostly on visual cues and superficial correlations. The study probes intrinsic language grounding in the absence of explicit grounding modules.

entry.title: Verify Less, Evolve More: Training Idea-Level Critics for Verification-Efficient ML Evolving Agents

author.name: Jiamu Bai, Lizhu Zhang, Xin Yu, Yanhong Wu, Zellux Wang, Serena Li, Weiwei Li, Zhuokai Zhao, Lingzhou Xue, Kiwan Maeng, Xiangjun Fan, Bo Peng

entry.summary: This paper trains specialized idea-level critic models that predict whether a proposed ML modification will improve on the current solution, letting self-evolving AI4ML agents screen ideas before costly empirical training-and-evaluation cycles. Frontier models used directly as idea selectors provide only limited gains, motivating the trained critics. Verification efficiency is a real bottleneck for autonomous ML research agents.

entry.title: Few Bits, One Law: Toward W2A4KV2

author.name: Kai Yi, Tarek Elgamal, Sruthikesh Surineni, Vignesh Vivekraja, Soumyadeep Ghosh, Steven Li

entry.summary: CanonQ is a quantization-aware training framework for extreme low-bit LLM compression that jointly quantizes weights (2-bit), activations (4-bit), and KV caches (2-bit). It separates source canonicalization (fixed rotations, energy normalization, frozen Gaussian-reference codebooks reusable across layers and models) from task-aware joint adaptation, with error bounds for codebook transfer. Joint W-A-KV quantization is one of the hardest compression regimes.

entry.title: The Winner's Curse in LLM Self-Improvement Loops: Selection Noise, Lock-in, and Acceptance Rules

author.name: Litao Hu, Yutong Tang

entry.summary: The paper models the keep-if-better acceptance step of LLM self-improvement loops as selection under measurement noise with correlated candidate errors, showing that most proposals after the first are harmful and that small evaluation sets systematically overstate the best candidate (winner's curse). Experiments with Qwen models rewriting their own instructions include a pre-registered study and analysis of acceptance rules. It quantifies a key failure mode of self-improving systems.

entry.title: Relevance Is Not Sufficiency: What Actually Closes the Evidence Gap in Long-Term Memory QA

author.name: Yufeng Li, Shuxin Li, Zhenhua Xu, Junxian Li, Peng Zeng, Sheng Yao, Changting Lin, Gaolei Li, Ran Bi, Meng Han

entry.summary: The authors argue that retrieval in long-term-memory LLM agents should construct a sufficient memory set rather than a set of individually relevant records, since top-ranked memories can jointly omit a needed complementary fact. Drawing on legal evidence scholarship, they introduce a blinded LLM judgment mechanism and a new metric (Gold Hit) to operationalize sufficiency for multi-session and temporal questions.

entry.title: Dual- versus Single-Suggestion AI Support for Radiographic Interpretation in Residents: Randomized Multireader Study

author.name: Lin Wu, Zhe Xu, Hongyi Wang, Feifei Zhou, Wei Deng, Chunlong Zhang, Yuting Zhu, Kaixiao Chen, Xiao Liang, Chen Yang, Yeyuan Chen, Hao Chen, Fuqing Zhou

entry.summary: A prospective, multicenter, randomized three-arm reader study at three Chinese hospitals with 132 residents comparing single-model GPT-5.4 support against dual-model combinations with Kimi-K2.6 or Gemini-3.6 Flash on radiograph interpretation. The study examined accuracy changes and behavior when the shared AI suggestion was incorrect.

entry.title: Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving via Agent Orchestration in Program Verification

author.name: Shuangjie Yao, Nikolaus Holzer, Mark Paul Santolucito, Baishakhi Ray, Suman Jana, Dongdong She

entry.summary: CoCo-Prover reframes program proving as metalevel decision-making under a cost budget, using a two-level proof graph and agent orchestration to maximize theorems proved economically rather than maximizing single-theorem pass rates at any cost. This targets realistic software verification with hundreds of interdependent proof obligations for LLM-generated code.

entry.title: Successive Training Stages and Large Language Model Persuasion: Effects of Misalignment, Supervised Fine-Tuning, and Preference Optimization

author.name: Antony Dalmiere (LAAS-TRUST), Pascal Marchand (LAAS-TRUST, INSA Toulouse), Guillaume Auriol (LAAS-TRUST, INSA Toulouse), Vincent Nicomette (LAAS-TSF, LAAS)

entry.summary: This human-subjects study with 835 Prolific participants measures how successive training stages affect LLM persuasiveness on divisive political issues: SFT on conspiracy data, additional persuasive SFT, and Identity Preference Optimization, compared against neutral text and GPT-4. It quantifies how post-training stages compound to increase persuasive capability and potential misuse risk. This is directly relevant to dual-use and persuasion safety concerns.

entry.title: Open-MMUnlearning: Unifying Methods and Evaluation for MLLM Unlearning

author.name: Junkai Chen, Yuhao He, Qianshan Wei, Junxiang You, Jingwen Shao, Junkai Lin, Zhongkai Yue, Xiaotian Ye, Zhengbo Jiao, Jiali Cheng, Zhijie Deng, Kening Zheng, Ruiqi Liu, Hadi Amiri, Yi Yu, Zhenan Sun, Qi Li, Ka-Ho Chow, Sijia Liu, Liang Wang, Jiaqi Li, Shu Wu

entry.summary: Introduces Open-MMUnlearning, an open-source framework unifying target-model preparation, multimodal data processing, unlearning algorithms, and evaluation for multimodal large language models through shared interfaces. It addresses fragmented implementations, weak robustness testing, and unreliable metrics that currently hinder systematic progress in MLLM unlearning.

entry.title: Convex-Concave Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shripad V. Deshmukh, Yaswanth Chittepu, Dhawal Gupta, Philip Thomas, Scott Niekum

entry.summary: This paper shows that the policy learning objective in RL, typically treated as hopelessly non-convex, becomes a difference-of-convex program in log-density-ratio coordinates computable via per-decision importance sampling. This structural insight offers an alternative to the convex surrogates used by trust-region methods like TRPO and PPO.

entry.title: Multimodal LLMs Can Learn to Read Brain Signals: A Vision--Language Model for Unified Multi-Task EEG Decoding

author.name: Parastoo Azizeddin, Omid Sharafi, Maryam M. Shanechi

entry.summary: The paper introduces BraVista, a framework that encodes multichannel EEG signals as structured images and performs multi-task decoding via instruction-conditioned vision-language models, post-training a general-domain VLM to leverage its visual and linguistic priors. This addresses generalization across cognitive tasks, subjects, and recording conditions in EEG decoding.

entry.title: Sparse Feature Policy Unlearning Mitigates State Hallucination in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jiho Lee, Jeongeun Park, Heayoun Choi, Taekyung Kim, Eunwoo Kim

entry.summary: The paper studies state hallucination in vision-language-action models, where the robot keeps acting as if an unrealized object state were achieved, and links it to weakened attention on task-relevant regions and specific sparse-autoencoder features. Based on this mechanistic analysis, the proposed SOUL method uses sparse feature policy unlearning to mitigate these failures.

entry.title: How Do LLMs Change Predictions Under Negation?

author.name: Jongwook Yoon, Jongwon Lim, Sungjib Lim, Woojin Cho, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Shows that recent open and closed LLMs repeat the same answer under negation in 37-71% of cases on a new negation benchmark. A mechanistic analysis finds specialized attention heads and MLP neurons implement negation by suppressing retrieval of the original answer and promoting a favored candidate, contrasting with accounts of human negation processing.

entry.title: When Algorithmic Exploration Becomes Cheap: A Case Study of Agentic Research in EDA

author.name: Keren Zhu, Yu Deng, Xiaoyu Hao, Liwen Jiang, Zijian Jiang, Cunqing Lan, Boxiang Song, Pujun Su, Yaojia Wang

entry.summary: EDA researchers report eight deliberate trials of agentic algorithm exploration on topics outside their expertise, finding that agents could develop constructions, analyze tools, and implement improvements with limited intervention, though some efforts fell short. They also used AI to classify 8,420 EDA papers (2022-2026), finding 97.7% of 2,380 primary-core papers computationally closed. The evidence suggests much algorithmic research may become dramatically cheaper and automated.

entry.title: SLDR: Defending Against Malicious Fine-tuning via Selective Layers Recovery and Dynamic Routing

author.name: Hui Zhang, Yachao Yuan, Jiayun Wang, Yuanzhuo Li, Hongtao Wang, Yali Yuan

entry.summary: SLDR is a post-fine-tuning defense against attacks that use malicious fine-tuning to strip refusal behavior from aligned LLMs. Building on the observation that layer-wise safety sensitivity is signed, it trains a LoRA recovery adapter only on the most and least safety-sensitive layers and activates it via representation-based dynamic routing only for malicious queries, preserving utility on legitimate inputs.

entry.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR

author.name: Saif Punjwani, Micah Goldblum

entry.summary: This paper observes that adding strong novelty incentives directly to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) often degrades model quality in ways that are hard to recover from, since verifiable rewards cover only a narrow slice of behavior. The authors propose Exploration-Distillation (ExpDis), which trains separate explorer policies with novelty bonuses, filters their trajectories, and distills only useful trajectories into the main policy. This decoupling preserves optimization stability while still enabling discovery of new reasoning strategies.

entry.title: TAP: Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Pruning via Trajectory-Anchored Recovery

author.name: Yuanzhe Li, Pengxin Wang, Yuxin Ren, Jianing Deng, Jingtong Hu, Song Wang, Jingdi Chen, Huanrui Yang

entry.summary: TAP is a pruning framework for long-horizon agentic language models that diagnoses why QA-oriented pruning methods fail on agents and introduces trajectory-anchored importance estimates and recovery strategies that avoid compounding student errors across turns. It enables aggressive pruning of agent models without severe task degradation.

entry.title: Pretraining Shapes Spectral Structure: Architecture- and Strategy-Conditional Prediction of OOD Robustness in Foundation Models

author.name: Sangyoon Bae, Sk Miraj Ahmed, Shinjae Yoo, Jiook Cha

entry.summary: The paper shows that out-of-distribution robustness of foundation models is encoded in the spectral structure of pretrained weights alone, without needing source or target data. It proves OOD accuracy gap bounds tied to representation concentration and provides architecture- and strategy-conditional predictors of robustness.

entry.title: How to train your model organism

author.name: Xilin Wang, David Bau, Byron C. Wallace

entry.summary: This paper argues that alignment model organisms—models trained with specific alignment-relevant behaviors like backdoors or sycophancy for testing interpretability techniques—should be validated on three axes: behavior installation, general capability preservation, and output naturalness. Re-examining public organism suites, the authors find chat quality and chain-of-thought naturalness degrade substantially across training recipes.

entry.title: HE-OFT: Privacy-Preserving One-Shot Federated Fine-Tuning under Homomorphic Encryption

author.name: Halil \.Ibrahim Kanpak, Sinem Sav, Alptekin K\"up\c{c}\"u

entry.summary: HE-OFT introduces the first cryptographically secure one-shot federated fine-tuning protocol under homomorphic encryption in which no participant receives the trained model itself, protecting both private data and proprietary model assets. This addresses reconstruction attacks on shared gradients and regulatory constraints on model distribution.

entry.title: Immiscible Diffusion Policy: Preserving Multimodal Robot Actions through Label-Free Noise Assignment

author.name: Xiao Zhang, Yuxin Chen, Zhixuan Liang, Guojian Zhan, Chenran Li, Chenfeng Xu, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Yiheng Li

entry.summary: This paper shows that diffusion policies often collapse to a single action modality despite balanced multimodal datasets, and attributes the failure to independent action-noise pairing that causes crossing diffusion paths and averaged denoising. The proposed Immiscible Diffusion Policy uses label-free noise assignment to keep diffusion paths separated, preserving multimodal action distributions in robot learning. This addresses a fundamental limitation of diffusion policies for robot manipulation.

entry.title: Understanding and Mitigating Token-Pruning-Induced Vulnerabilities in VLMs

author.name: Shuailong Wang, Xinyu Lyu, Shengming Yuan, Jingkuan Song, Heng Tao Shen, Lianli Gao

entry.summary: This is the first comprehensive safety evaluation of token pruning in vision-language models, finding that most pruning strategies degrade safety as pruning ratios increase, while query-based compression can even improve safety at extreme pruning ratios up to 99.8 percent. The authors identify a mechanism called Pruning-Induced Malicious Amplification and explore mitigations that preserve acceleration without sacrificing safety. This matters because efficiency techniques are widely deployed but rarely audited for safety side effects.

entry.title: Attention via Black-Box Vector Search

author.name: Stepan Zharkov, Krish Singal, Ashwin Padaki, Alexandr Andoni

entry.summary: This paper provides sharp theoretical answers to how many keys a sparse attention mechanism must retrieve via maximum inner product search to output an epsilon-accurate attention estimate. Using the priority sampling framework, the authors show Theta(sqrt(n)/epsilon) keys suffice and are necessary with a single MIPS index, and achieve O(log n + 1/epsilon^2) with Theta(log n) indices, with matching near-optimality guarantees.

entry.title: Best Arm Identification for Bandits with Shifting Means

author.name: Lukas Zierahn, Wouter M. Koolen, Shubhada Agrawal, Christina Katsimerou, Dirk van der Hoeven

entry.summary: The authors study best arm identification when only reward gaps are stable while a common mean shift is adversarially chosen each round, a novel perturbation model called Shifting Means. They show that standard GLRT-based stopping rules including Track-and-Stop fail under time-varying shifts and propose an alternative algorithm with high-probability identification guarantees in the fixed-confidence setting. The author list includes leading bandit theorists (Koolen, Agrawal).

entry.title: SAPD: Step-Aligned Privileged Distillation

author.name: Tianle Wang, Jiayu Liu, Ruizhi Zhao, Ning Miao

entry.summary: This paper introduces SAPD, a rollout-free self-distillation method that converts fixed demonstrations into step-aligned distributional supervision for off-policy LLM post-training. By using the known progression of reference solutions to align supervision with each reasoning decision, it aims to make off-policy learning competitive with costly on-policy rollout generation.

entry.title: Boundary-Free Contextual Biasing: Depth-Adaptive Gating and Reading-Space Matching for Unsegmented Languages

author.name: Muhammad Huzaifah, Yu Pan, Zachary Yeo, Ningjie Bai, Guangzhao Yang

entry.summary: This paper presents a training-free, boundary-free contextual biasing decoder for frozen CTC-based ASR models, using a character-level Aho-Corasick automaton to bias recognition in unsegmented languages like Japanese and Chinese. It introduces depth-adaptive gating and reading-space matching mechanisms, achieving 66.5% recall on the Aishell-1 NE hard R1 subset, surpassing the trained CLAS baseline, and releases the first open Japanese contextual biasing resources.

entry.title: Pooling Representation Autoencoders for Efficient Diffusion

author.name: Ram\'on Calvo-Gonz\'alez, Youssef Saied, Fran\c{c}ois Fleuret

entry.summary: Introduces PoolDINO, a learned affine pooling operator that merges neighboring tokens in Representation Autoencoders to reduce the cost of diffusion-based image generation. On ImageNet-256, 4x token compression retains comparable quality while boosting latent-sampling throughput 3.7x, and 16x compression achieves 9.0x throughput with some quality loss.

entry.title: Why VLMs Miss Small Objects, and When Zooming In Is Safe

author.name: Junzhe Shi, Yuan Gan, Shida Jiang

entry.summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework explaining why vision-language models fail to detect small objects in large images, based on two quantities of the image interface: visual tokens per object side (S) and content coverage per call (L). The authors derive token-budget scaling laws showing that doubling the token budget only increases achievable resolution by about 41 percent, and that reaching the resolution needed for small objects costs at least order S^2 tokens regardless of architecture. The work clarifies which limitations better models can overcome and evaluates whether classical local decomposition (tiling/zooming) of large images remains a viable strategy.

entry.title: RLHND: Video Foundation Models as Physically Grounded Hand Trackers for Robot Learning

author.name: Seungjun Moon, Subin Jeon, Sangwoo Kim, Hanbyul Joo, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: This paper proposes RLHND, a hand tracking model built on the pre-trained Cosmos video diffusion backbone that jointly estimates hand pose and tactile information from monocular egocentric video. By adding physical cues like contact and force to human video data, it makes human videos more usable for robot policy training, addressing a key gap in robot learning from human demonstration data.

entry.title: Do Better Visual Representations Always Lead to Better End-to-End Autonomous Driving?

author.name: Zihao Zhang, Haochen Tian, Tianyu Li, Changhui Jing, Jingliang He, Naisheng Ye, Ziyuan Pu, Zhenjie Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces ViRA, a planner-agnostic visual representation alignment framework for end-to-end autonomous driving, and studies when visual foundation model (VFM) representations actually help driving. Findings include consistent gains from VFM-guided alignment across planners, extending to zero-shot closed-loop evaluation, and that the choice of alignment target matters even for planners with pre-trained VFM encoders.

entry.title: Precise SE(3) End-Effector Tracking in Whole-Body Humanoid Control

author.name: Joohwan Seo, Xiaofeng Guo, Jinkun Cao, Roberto Horowitz, Rocky Duan, Guanya Shi, Koushil Sreenath

entry.summary: ResGAC combines geometric admittance control with residual reinforcement learning for precise SE(3) end-effector pose tracking in humanoid whole-body control, where GAC provides structured task-space feedback and residual RL compensates unmodeled dynamics and coordinates balance. The left-invariant formulation lets the same control law operate across manipulation reference frames, enabling a ground-attached head-mounted tracking setup.

entry.title: RoboPace: Contact-Aware Time-Optimal Retiming for Action-Chunk Policies

author.name: Mimo Shirasaka, Takehiko Ohkawa, Takuya Okubo, Nicola Scianca, Tatsuya Matsushima, Kei Ota

entry.summary: RoboPace is an online retiming layer for action-chunk policies that preserves a policy's geometric path while adjusting execution timing to balance speed with contact safety, addressing the mismatch between human demonstration timing and robot actuator limits. This is particularly relevant for VLA policies trained on human-hand or UMI-style demonstrations.

entry.title: OpenViTac: Learning and Benchmarking Visuo-Tactile Policies in a Unified Sim-and-Real Framework

author.name: Yifan Wu, Qin Li, Nan Min, Guojin Zhong, Haoyu Zhao, Zhiyuan Li, Houze Xu, Shengqi Xu, Xingyao Lin, Zijie Diao, Zhaoxiang Liu, Shiguo Lian, Shunlin Lu, Shihao Zhao, Ziyi Ye, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: OpenViTac is a unified sim-and-real benchmark for visuo-tactile manipulation, organizing contact-rich tasks into four tactile capability dimensions with paired simulation and real-world settings. It enables consistent evaluation of VLA, WAM, and vision-tactile-language-action policies and includes learning baselines built on the benchmark.

entry.title: Now in Nature: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 announces that the technique behind Bolmo, its fully open byte-level language models, has been published in Nature, with new checkpoints demonstrating that the byteification approach generalizes beyond the Olmo family to other model families. Byte-level operation removes reliance on subword tokenizers, addressing tokenization-induced biases and failures.

entry.title: Efficient Reasoning with Flow Language Models

author.name: Hanru Bai, Faissal Izermine, Oscar Davis, T. Konstantin Rusch

entry.summary: This work compares the reasoning efficiency of Flow Language Models and discrete diffusion language models under matched denoising step budgets, showing that FLMs' continuous sequence representations aid reasoning. The authors provide a theoretical superposition-perspective analysis and support it with intermediate-state interventions.

entry.title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing

author.name: Yilun Hao, Krishna Sayana, Isabella Ye, James S Ren, Sukhdeep Sodhi, Craig Boutilier, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: RECAST reformulates evidence construction for grounded LLM tasks as a sequential decision process that routes across heterogeneous retrieval and computation tools, recognizing that needed evidence often must be derived by filtering or aggregation rather than retrieved verbatim. The framework learns when to access, compute, or synthesize context.

entry.title: LRCC: Generalizing Low-Rank Compression with Conditional Computation

author.name: Thomas Vaitses Fontanari, Maximo Eduardo Rulli, Federico Alvetreti, Donatella Genovese, Simone Scardapane

entry.summary: LRCC introduces token-dependent low-rank compression: lightweight per-block routers select among nested low-rank paths while the low-rank factors stay frozen, so only routers are trained. Evaluated on Llama and Qwen models for language modeling and zero-shot tasks, it improves quality within the same average active-parameter budget as fixed-rank compression. This connects conditional computation with structured efficiency methods for large models.

entry.title: CurveTQ: Rotation-Free Trellis Quantization of LLM Weights via Curvature-Weighted Search

author.name: Guanhua Ding, Zi Wang, Ruichao Li, Jack Liu

entry.summary: CurveTQ improves two-bit LLM weight quantization by feeding Hessian-derived curvature weights (from the LDL factorization diagonal) directly into the Viterbi branch metric of trellis coding, removing the need for random orthogonal rotations used by QTIP and Proteus. The paper also explains rotations as a way of removing curvature structure that prior quantizers could not exploit.

entry.title: How assigned AI use before class shapes active student engagement in class

author.name: Dan J. Wang, Neelam Modi Jain, Vanessa Burbano, Jorge Guzman, Daniel Keum, Soomi Kim, Bruce Kogut, Nataliya Wright

entry.summary: This preregistered field experiment with 759 MBA students across ten course sections randomly assigned students to prepare for class sessions with a purpose-built voice-based AI discussion partner. After two uses, students made roughly 31% more voluntary contributions in class and reported greater comfort speaking up. The study offers rare randomized evidence that AI learning tools can change live classroom engagement behaviors, not just test scores.

entry.title: Removing Information Content Does Not Certify Tamper Resistance in Open-Weight Models

author.name: Domenic Rosati, Alessa Carbo, Ali Dadsetan, Hong Huang, Matthew Young, Subhabrata Majumdar, Frank Rudzicz, Hassan Sajjad

entry.summary: This paper gives a theoretical argument that information-removal techniques (training-data filtering, capability removal) cannot universally certify resistance to fine-tuning attacks on open-weight models, because function-preserving reparameterizations leave information invariants unchanged while changing gradient-descent recovery geometry. The authors provide explicit constructions with identical information quantities but vastly different recovery times.

entry.title: The Dichotomy Between Pattern Recognition and Step-by-Step Reasoning

author.name: Amrut Nadgir, Pratik Chaudhari, Vijay Balasubramanian

entry.summary: The paper proposes a theory that LLM inference spans a spectrum from pattern recognition to step-by-step reasoning depending on how much context the next token depends on, formalizing reasoning traces as paths on De Bruijn graphs of c-length contexts. It characterizes when a model that has learned a task's DAG subgraph can compose edges to solve longer unseen instances.

entry.title: Cache the Encoder Within:Compact, Reusable Memory across LLM Queries

author.name: Hanzuo Liu, Chunyu Liu, Chaofan Lin, Alex Lamb, Mingyu Gao

entry.summary: EncBank treats a pretrained LLM's lower layers as a reusable document encoder, caching their outputs compactly for an adapted upper-layer reader to avoid redundant encoding across repeated queries over shared documents. A self-distilled suffix adapter enables 4-bit storage that stays within one score point of native-precision performance across Qwen backbones.

entry.title: TouchScale: 500 Hours of Human Vision and Touch for Visual-Tactile Learning

author.name: Dayou Li, Hao Wang, Qianqian Yang, Zihao Zhu, Haoquan Fang, Ziyao Zeng, Yan Han, Zihan Wang, Yan Wang, Baoru Huang, Dilin Wang, Kenji Shimada, Yiyue Luo, Manling Li, Teresa Lv, Mustafa Mukadam, Rakesh Ranjan, Ruohan Zhang, Qi He, Changliu Liu, Xu Chen, Marco Pavone, Bangya Liu, Jiachen Li, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: TouchScale introduces a 500-hour dataset of contact-rich human interaction captured with a single unified wearable sensing setup, spanning roughly 2,000 task descriptions of everyday activities. It addresses the scarcity and heterogeneity of existing visual-tactile data, where synchronized tactile supervision is far smaller than human video and mixed sensor setups confound scale analysis. The resource enables visual-tactile learning and provides clean isolation of data-scale effects for embodied learning.

entry.title: Juno: Taming Predictive Latents for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yuchen Zhu, Chenyi Xu, Yulin Zhang, Gang Xu, Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: Juno is a unified framework built on a single action-conditioned JEPA that serves as a control-aligned representation backbone, predictive teacher, and adaptable dynamics model for vision-language-action models. It identifies and addresses three failure modes of naive predictive latents: embodiment mismatch, interference with action learning, and teacher miscalibration under distribution shift.

entry.title: Beyond Reconstruction: What Matters in Action Tokenization for Robot Policies?

author.name: Haoran Chen, Jingtian Ji, Samuel Wheeler, Kaylene Caswell Stocking, Matthew Walter

entry.summary: This analysis paper examines why reconstruction-accurate action tokenizers do not necessarily yield successful vision-language-action robot policies, showing that policy predictability of tokens and robust decoding of unseen predictions also matter. It provides an extensive empirical characterization of the factors that drive downstream policy success in autoregressive action-token pipelines.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Make Open-Ended Scientific Discovery? Evidence from Station

author.name: Wenyu Du, Stephen Chung

entry.summary: The authors probe whether AI agents can do open-ended scientific discovery in Station, an open-world multi-agent scientific ecosystem, augmenting it with a Supervisor mechanism and periodic Meta Reflection to sustain exploration without intermediate metrics. Tasks are constructed from recent ICLR oral papers by giving agents the research question while withholding the solution. It directly tests a frontier claim about AI-driven science.

entry.title: From Uncertainty to Action: Learning to Steer LLM Agents

author.name: Hanwen Li, Jinhao Duan, Guanhua Zhu, Junchi Lu, Bo Shen, Chenxi Yuan, Kaidi Xu

entry.summary: This work builds a stepwise outcome table of about 82,000 counterfactual continuations to test whether uncertainty signals can guide when and where to intervene in LLM agent trajectories. It finds uncertainty detects failing trajectories but cannot localize the step where steering helps, and proposes Value of Steering, a learned trajectory-level monitor. The large-scale counterfactual methodology is a notable empirical contribution.

entry.title: Bookkeeping, Composition, or Unreachable Gold? Reading MemoryAgentBench's Conflict-Resolution Scores Against a Frozen Last-Write Resolver

author.name: Egor Pakhomov, Erik Nijkamp

entry.summary: The authors implement the benchmark's own last-write rule as a zero-learning resolver and find it answers 80.25% of MemoryAgentBench Conflict Resolution questions, with many remaining items having gold labels unreachable by the rule but reachable by overwritten statements (e.g., a superseded capital of India example). This suggests headline agent scores partly reflect bookkeeping and label issues rather than sophisticated memory management. A valuable benchmark-critique contribution.

entry.title: RT-Safe: Benchmarking Agent Safety in Real-Time Embodied Environment

author.name: Tianruo Rose Xu, Jiawei Ren, Yichi Yang, Zhaoxu Zheng, Lianhui Qin

entry.summary: RT-SAFE is a simulated urban benchmark evaluating embodied-agent safety under real-time constraints, where the world does not pause during reasoning, so an action safe at observation time may be unsafe at execution. It scores both decision quality and decision latency, addressing the gap between digital agent safety evaluation and physical-world deployment risks like pedestrian injury. A timely contribution as agents move into embodied settings.

entry.title: World Potential Model: Pretrained World Knowledge as Progress Potentials

author.name: Jun Zhao, Jixin Tang, Yang Shu, Jinyang Wu, Yuyang Lu, Jingqi Tong, Hao Xu, Weifeng Ge, Qi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes the World Potential Model, showing that off-the-shelf pretrained models can act as goal-conditioned evaluators of realized task progress without task-specific fine-tuning, providing dense signal for long-horizon agents that otherwise receive only terminal rewards. Experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld demonstrate pretrained models substantially outperform chance at recovering progress structure.

entry.title: How Do Agentic LLMs Decide to Call Tools? A Tool-Call Vector Shaped by Suppression

author.name: Xijie Gong, Tingxu Han, Jiahao Zhang, Wei Song, Ziqi Ding, Hanqi Yan, Youcheng Sun, Lijie Hu

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study isolates the tool-call decision in agentic LLMs by constructing minimal contrastive prompt pairs where a single request verb flips the decision, identifying a tool-call direction in the representation space shaped by suppression. It provides causal insight into how models decide between tool invocation and direct response in heavily scaffolded contexts.

entry.title: LiveMACE: Process-Aware Evaluation of LLM Agent Capabilities in Evolving Markets

author.name: Jun Zhao, Leiming Fu, Yanbo Wen, Yiding Wang, Xuantong Liu, Yang Shu, Yuyang Lu, Xuanran Xing, Jingqi Tong, Hao Xu, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: LiveMACEBench evaluates five frontier LLMs as persistent agents in live financial markets over 30 days, using process-aware diagnostics across Tool Use, Persistent Memory, Rule Following, and Multi-Agent Collaboration configurations. It finds a pronounced gap between realized outcomes and the underlying capabilities visible in full decision traces. This offers a realistic, naturally evolving testbed beyond static benchmarks.

entry.title: Beyond the Sycophancy Score: How Task, Model, and Pressure Shape LLM Yielding

author.name: Guang Yang, Homa Hosseinmardi, Fengchen Liu, Amir Ghasemian

entry.summary: Analyzes 103,939 graded replies from ten LLM configurations across 200 items, 13 pressure conditions, and four-turn conversations to identify when models yield to user pushback. It finds verification cost of the user's claim and presence of trained guardrails dominate over model identity, moving past single-number sycophancy rates.

entry.title: LayerRoPE: Dynamic Depth-wise Magnitude & Angular Superposition

author.name: Shikhar Srivastava, Christopher Kanan

entry.summary: The paper reinterprets hidden-state norm growth with depth in transformers, conventionally treated as a pathology, as an emergent depth-positional encoding carried by normalization weights. Across 16 pretrained LLMs from 9 families, it shows gamma grows and rotates with depth to encode layer index, and makes this explicit with LayerRoPE, an analog of rotary embeddings along depth.

entry.title: OnlineQAT: On-Policy Distillation for Ultra-Low-Bit Large Language Models

author.name: Wenjun Wang, Heng Li, Yanggan Gu, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: OnlineQAT is a two-stage framework for quantization-aware training below four bits: block-wise QAT provides a low-bit initialization, then on-policy distillation uses student-generated prefixes with a frozen full-precision teacher supplying reverse-KL signals. This targets the mismatch where offline recovery data does not cover states visited by the deployed quantized model, demonstrated on models like Qwen3-1.7B.

entry.title: Logarithmic Regret via Passive Change Detection in Piecewise-Stationary Self-Tuning Regulation

author.name: A. Ch. Madhusudanarao, Rahul Singh

entry.summary: The authors prove logarithmic regret for minimum-variance control of autoregressive systems with piecewise-unknown coefficients, using passive change detection (PIECE-CD) that exploits output energy deviations during exploitation rather than arm-style probing. Under stated conditions they achieve O((C+1) log(T/delta)) regret with high probability. This is a notable theoretical advance for adaptive control under non-stationarity, distinct from switching bandits.

entry.title: Towards Financial World Modeling

author.name: Humzah Merchant, Alec Guthrie, Simon Mahns, Randall Balestriero, Bradford Levy

entry.summary: The paper introduces Market-1T, a dataset of nearly one trillion observations across U.S. equities (2008-2025) at 1 Hz resolution, and develops financial world models whose state representations support planning and decision-making over market-wide conditions, liquidity, volatility, and cross-asset relationships, moving beyond narrow single-task predictive evaluation.

entry.title: Noise Your Prompt: Noising Conditioning Tokens in Continuous Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Justin Jung

entry.summary: This paper makes a simple modification to continuous diffusion language model training: noise the conditioning prompt tokens instead of keeping them clean. This yields substantially better generalization on combinatorial reasoning (Sudoku Hard solve rate rising from 3.73% to 24.65%), improved solution diversity, and modest NLG gains in low-data regimes.

entry.title: COPC: Coupled Off-Policy Correction for Asynchronous LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zicheng Hu, Zhijian Zhou, Xuan Zhang, Yuchen Liu, Cheng Chen, Yuan Li, Qi Gu, Yan Feng, Hongyan Hao, Chao Qu

entry.summary: COPC addresses stale trajectories in asynchronous LLM RL by showing policy-side importance-ratio correction alone is insufficient because advantage estimates inherit staleness from behavior-policy continuations. The authors derive exact bias and variance decompositions revealing multiplicative coupling between policy-weight and advantage errors, motivating a coupled correction method.

entry.title: Which Rollout Taught It That? BehaviorTrace and the Limits of Training-Data Attribution in Online RL

author.name: Amit Nautiyal

entry.summary: BehaviorTrace is an open evaluation harness for training-data attribution in online RL with GRPO, using a planted behavior with known cause plus controls for gradient magnitude, fluency, headroom, and seed variation. Experiments on Qwen2.5-1.5B show much of the apparent attribution signal comes from confounds, with a gradient-size-only control reaching 4.2-4.5x chance.

entry.title: HULK: Learning Whole-Body Forceful Loco-Manipulation for Humanoids

author.name: An Dang, Arturo Flores Alvarez, Yu-Ming Chen, Conor Mc Gartoll, Helen Sun, Aaron Ames, Nima Fazeli, Manikantan Nambi

entry.summary: HULK is a whole-body control framework for forceful humanoid loco-manipulation, using MPC-guided reinforcement learning to train separate arm-tracking and locomotion-under-load teachers, augmented with a capture-point control barrier function, and distilling them into a single policy. It addresses balance and tracking under heavy payloads that shift the center of mass.

entry.title: It Is Not Seeing the Hazard: A Frozen Vision-Language Safety Score Measures Its Caption Bank

author.name: Samuel Tetteh, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: This paper critically evaluates frozen CLIP-based safety scores used in safe RL and driving, presenting controlled experiments showing that image-text similarity to hazard descriptions may reflect prompt structure, embedding geometry, and viewpoint rather than actual hazard detection. The authors show a frozen vision-language safety score largely measures its caption bank rather than the hazard itself. This is an important caution for the increasingly common practice of using VLM similarity as safety signals.

entry.title: Computations of the slice genus and the unknotting number of links via machine learning

author.name: Yutong Dai, Oliver Hayman, Andr\'as Juh\'asz, Ludovico Morellato

entry.summary: This paper uses reinforcement learning and Bayesian optimisation to compute new upper bounds on link invariants in knot theory, including slice genus, unknotting number, and strong slice genus, which are not known to be algorithmically computable. Combined with lower bounds from known invariants, the agents obtain new exact values and reproduce known counterexamples to unknotting number additivity, sometimes finding new unknotting trajectories.

entry.title: RELATE: An Evaluation Framework for measuring Relational Orientation of Large Language Models

author.name: Shivam Shukla, Jihye Kim, Shubham Gaur, Mahnaz Roshanaei, Magy Seif El-Nasr

entry.summary: RELATE measures relational orientation of LLMs used for emotional support: whether models position themselves as the user's ongoing support source (inward-facing language) or encourage real-world human connection (outward-scaffolding language). Grounded in psychological and sociological literature, the framework formalizes a taxonomy to assess where models orient users for continued support. This addresses concerns that sustained AI emotional-support use may displace real relationships.

entry.title: SpikingVLA: Asynchronous Spiking Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jingya Wang, Dehao Zhang, Shuai Wang, Malu Zhang, Yang Yang, Haizhou Li

entry.summary: SpikingVLA presents an ANN-to-SNN conversion framework for energy-efficient vision-language-action models, introducing a Dendritic Integrate-and-Fire (DIF) neuron that handles channel-wise activation outliers to enable accurate conversion with fewer timesteps. This reduces inference latency for real-time robotic VLA deployment.

entry.title: SPW-Nav: A Streaming Panoramic World Model for Language-Guided Navigation

author.name: Yunheng Liu, Ziqi Cai, Siqi Yang, Yimu Wang, Minggui Teng, Jiaming Tan, Shuchen Weng, Erwin Wu, Kaipeng Zhang, Boxin Shi

entry.summary: SPW-Nav is a streaming panoramic world model that interprets movement instructions as camera motion and generates one minute of 2K 360-degree video in real time from a single panorama. Key techniques include spherical rotation decoupling, pose-aligned conditioning to keep translations bounded, and multi-scale conditioning, with applications in interactive 3D exploration, VR, and embodied agent training.

entry.title: PhyDiCT: Plug-and-Play CT Reconstruction from Sparse X-Rays via Differentiable Rendering and Strong Priors

author.name: Weicheng Dai, Shantanu Ghosh, Kayhan Batmanghelich

entry.summary: Presents PhyDiCT, a training-free framework reconstructing 3D lung CT from sparse X-ray projections by combining a differentiable Beer-Lambert physics forward model with a text-conditioned diffusion prior. Split Gibbs sampling jointly optimizes projection fidelity and prior consistency without fine-tuning the generative model.

entry.title: Visual Evidence Under Cross-Examination: Evaluating and Controlling Decision-Level Evidence Use in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Huiyao Zhang, Jin Bai, Zilong Su, Rui Guo, Chaofan Qin, Jinze Lv, Wenhui Yu, Hongfei Wang, Ye Li

entry.summary: This paper studies whether visual evidence in vision-language models actually benefits the candidate it supports, formalizing candidate-bound visual contribution with matched invalidation and rebinding tests. It introduces CROSS-Bench with 28,000 decision problems and the RIVET interface, which preserves evidence identity and uncertainty and separately controls response strength.

entry.title: DynStream: Online Streaming 4D Gaussian Reconstruction of Dynamic Worlds from Unposed Video

author.name: Dingwei Xian, Xiaoyu Zhou, Yajiao Xiong, Yongtao Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: DynStream performs online 4D Gaussian reconstruction of dynamic scenes from long, unposed streaming videos by reconstructing local temporal windows and incrementally fusing them into a globally consistent scene. It achieves simultaneous continuous processing and photorealistic rendering, which prior offline Gaussian methods and online point-cloud methods could not jointly deliver.

entry.title: RealtimeWAM: How Fast Can I Run My World Action Model?

author.name: Huanan Liu, Ye Li, Kangye Ji, Xiaoyu Chen, Hanyun Cui, Yutian Shen, Yuan Meng, Chenglei Wu, Jingyan Jiang, Bo Li, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: RealtimeWAM is a general, training-free inference acceleration framework for world action models that combines parallel execution with adaptive computation, exploiting layerwise dependencies to overlap work across timesteps. Unlike architecture-specific approaches such as FastWAM or pure caching, it adapts to the changing computational demands of closed-loop control.

entry.title: An overview of frontier AI company monitoring practices in mid 2026

author.name: Francis Rhys Ward

entry.summary: A reference document compiling publicly available evidence on how OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind monitor internally deployed agents, drawing on published safety framework materials and statements. It notes that monitoring is largely asynchronous/offline, cites specific latency targets (e.g., notifications within 30 minutes of concerning activity at OpenAI), and highlights the scarcity of public evidence about DeepMind's actual practices versus its control roadmap proposals.

entry.title: CM-DPO: Constraint-Margin Direct Preference Optimization for LLM Planning

author.name: Rabimba Karanjai, Qun Gu, Hemanth Hegadehalli Madhavarao, Wenhuan Sun, Xiaojiao Yu, Suryabhan Singh Hada, Libin N. George, Uma Kona, Richard Williamson, Linsey Pang, Prakhar Mehrotra

entry.summary: CM-DPO replaces DPO's binary preference signal with a continuous margin from a deterministic symbolic verifier, scaled by constraint-violation severity, and separates hard and soft constraints via a lexicographic objective so hard constraints are never traded off. Preference pairs come from procedurally generated constraint profiles to reduce length and style bias. This addresses concrete flaws of vanilla DPO for constrained planning.

entry.title: Consistent Distribution Matching for Data-Free Diffusion Distillation

author.name: Yuxiang Fu, Qi Yan, Zike Wu, Yongxing Zhang, Purang Abolmaesumi, Lele Wang, Renjie Liao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a simulation-free, data-free distillation method for accelerating diffusion and flow models to one- or few-step generation, unifying sample generation and score estimation in a single student network so only two models are needed. This avoids curated distillation datasets, expensive teacher rollouts, and auxiliary proxy networks required by prior approaches.

entry.title: Are Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning Methods Really Different?

author.name: Yikuan Li, Pinyan Lu, Fanghui Liu

entry.summary: The paper compares six PEFT parameterizations across language and diffusion models, examining task performance, forgetting, and changes in pretrained weight geometry. It finds LoRA-family methods approximately preserve pretrained geometry and that questioning whether explicit spectral preservation (as in OFT) is necessary, plus further analysis of methodological differences.

entry.title: Certified by Abstention: Distribution-Free Guarantees for Chain-of-Thought Verifiers at Small Calibration Budgets

author.name: Arjun Balaji

entry.summary: This paper studies distribution-free selective guarantees for chain-of-thought verifiers at realistic calibration budgets of tens to hundreds of labeled problems, using seven open models, five verifier signals, and 37,000 graded traces. It identifies the key issue of validity by abstention: rarely-firing certificates can be nominally valid yet wrong every time they are used, so failure probability must be bounded relative to firing rate. This provides practical guidance for deploying CoT verifiers with statistical guarantees.

entry.title: Judging in Latent Space: Efficient Generative Reward Modeling via Semantics-Preserving Compression

author.name: Mingqing Yuan (Soochow University), Xiaobo Liang (Soochow University), Junwei Yang (University of Cambridge), Ziwei Chen (Chalmers University of Technology), Zeren Zhang (Peking University), Hejin Wang (Tsinghua University), Yubin Wang (The Hong Kong University of Science, Technology), Juntao Li (Soochow University)

entry.summary: LatentGRM is a latent evaluation framework for reward modeling that compresses rubric-guided evaluation reasoning into compact continuous trajectories, performing pairwise judgments without token-by-token verbalization. A separate interpreter reconstructs evaluation text offline, offering a view of what information is retained.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Agent Skills' Downstream Utility

author.name: Yu Cheng, Dehai Zhao, Zhongxin Liu, Qing Huang, Zhenchang Xing, Xiaoxue Ren

entry.summary: This empirical study measures when reusable Agent Skills actually improve task outcomes, defining utility as pass-rate difference versus a No-Skill baseline across 87 SkillsBench tasks and nine configurations. It examines how skill content, execution configuration, and multi-skill organization affect gains, including marketplace-retrieved skills. This is timely and practical as skill marketplaces for coding agents proliferate.

entry.title: PAIR: Bridging Perception and Action in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Kaixi Feng, Guoheng Sun, Ang li

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces PAIR, a framework for vision-language-action (VLA) models in robotics that explicitly learns a shared perception-action representation rather than relying solely on end-to-end action-prediction losses. It uses a Masked Action Autoencoder to encode expert action chunks into horizon-aligned Action Latent Tokens and a Bridge Module to align visual-language features with action-relevant representations. The work addresses a known weakness in continuous-action VLAs where the transition from scene understanding to action generation remains implicit.

entry.title: Breaking the Space Barrier and its Application to Language Model Inference

author.name: Arip Asadulaev

entry.summary: The paper connects constrained decoding for structured LLM output (schema-conformant JSON, typed tool calls) to complexity theory, observing that automata enforcing formats have few joining paths between states. It resolves an open question about reachability in such graphs, placing the problem in ReachUL, LOGDCFL, C=L and SC2 with only O(log^2 n / log log n) space. This gives new theoretical underpinnings for constrained inference.

entry.title: The AI Evaluation Ecosystem

author.name: Yash Dave, Sang T. Truong, Serena Wang, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: The paper argues that valid benchmark design requires modeling the ecosystem of actors (providers, users, funders, regulators) whose incentives shape benchmark dynamics. It builds a simulation combining rule-based market dynamics with LLM-driven strategic actors over a six-dimensional capability space, and applies it to benchmark holdout design, finding that public benchmarks behave differently from held-out ones. A meta-level contribution to evaluation science.

entry.title: SearchWorld: Spatial Value-Grounded Imagination for UAV Object Search via World Models

author.name: Yatai Ji, Zhengqiu Zhu, Yong Zhao, Yue Hu, Fanglong Yao, Chen Gao, Pengfei Zhu, Quanjun Yin

entry.summary: This paper addresses autonomous UAV object search in urban environments by combining world models with spatially-aware value estimation, enabling prospective reasoning through imagined rollouts rather than reactive reasoning over past observations. It targets the closed perception-decision-action loop under partial observability while avoiding the high inference latency of image-generating world models.

entry.title: The Attribution Blind Spot: Layerwise Trajectory Diagnostics for Source Reliance in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models

author.name: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Yunzhao Wei, Bo Yang, Chen Ye, Gaolei Li, Meng Han

entry.summary: Using controlled knowledge conflicts, this paper studies which internal-state properties of retrieval-augmented models predict source reliance, introducing Latent Trajectory Shift, a signed projection onto a fitted principal component.
