entry.summary: The paper establishes sample complexity bounds for two-sample testing of graph populations without vertex correspondence, showing that for an Erdos-Renyi null with a planted two-block difference, m on the order of t^-3 graphs per group are necessary and sufficient, with signed triangle counts attaining this rate. Misalignment thus incurs a cubic versus linear cost compared to the aligned case.

entry.title: Seeing the Invisible: Physics-Guided Visual Prompting for Temperature- and Radiation-Aware VLA Navigation

author.name: Hojoon Son, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: PG-VP is a plug-and-play module for vision-language-action navigation models that handles invisible hazards like radiation or thermal spikes by performing physics-guided risk assessment and overlaying dynamic virtual obstacles in the visual input, reusing the frozen VLA model's obstacle avoidance abilities. This avoids per-hazard retraining, new encoders, and new data.

entry.title: Learning Grasp Targeting from Point Clouds for Log Pile Clearing on a Hydraulic Crane

author.name: George Sideris, Lucas Bessai, Heshan Fernando, Elie Ayoub, Nicolas Lemieux, Inna Sharf

entry.summary: The paper presents a learned policy that selects grasp points, depths, and grapple orientations from unsegmented point clouds to clear dense log piles on a real trailer-mounted hydraulic forestry crane, using behavior cloning followed by RL fine-tuning. Simulation results show BC clears 98 of 100 piles of 200 logs, with real-world deployment on hardware.

entry.title: Independent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Counterfactual Semantic-Social World Models

author.name: Fernando Martinez, Tao Li, Yingdong Lu, Juntao Chen

entry.summary: CASTLE addresses fully decentralized multi-agent RL by having agents prospectively compare consequences of candidate actions via counterfactual world models rather than diagnosing failures from ambiguous scalar rewards. This helps agents distinguish whether poor returns stem from their own action, teammates, or opponents without centralized critics or communication.

entry.title: Isotropic Yet Undecodable: The Sequential Content-Sufficiency Gap in Latent-Predictive Text Representations

author.name: K. P. Santoso, N. Z. Fadil, F. P. Harsanti, R. V. H. Ginardi, G. N. Iyer

entry.summary: Provides an information-theoretic analysis of whether text representations retain ordered target information, showing constructions where representations appear isotropic and agreeable yet carry zero target information. The theory motivates CANOPE, a nonautoregressive framework with ordered latent canvases and geometric regularization.

entry.title: The Standardization Trap: Certifying Joint Label Processing in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Duong Nguyen, Nicolas Chesneau, Milan Bhan

entry.summary: The paper studies whether tabular foundation models implement fixed-weight in-context label processing, and identifies a standardization trap: since public TFM packages standardize labels, naive derivative-based tests misjudge nonlinearity. The authors propose two prediction-based certificates that operate only at standardized labels and can reject fixed-weight or shift-only explanations.

entry.title: FedDermaSeg: Federated Learning for Dermatological Image Segmentation

author.name: Anabik Pal, Ganesh Patidar, Bikash Santra

entry.summary: This work explores federated learning for privacy-preserving skin lesion segmentation, avoiding the privacy risks and computational costs of centralized training on sensitive dermatological images. The authors investigate the feasibility of federated approaches for lesion delineation, a foundational step in computer-aided skin cancer diagnosis. The paper matters because medical imaging is a natural fit for federated learning, and demonstrating viable segmentation under decentralized training could enable broader clinical deployment.

entry.title: EMODE: Dynamic Para-Semantic Experts for Emotion-Aware Speech Language Modeling

author.name: Jianan Pan, Yiwen Gu, Xinze Li, Rui Wang, Kejie Huang

entry.summary: EMODE is an emotion-aware speech language model built around Dynamic Para-Semantic Experts, which decompose continuous speech features into semantic and paralinguistic pathways, route them dynamically, and fuse them before integration with the LM. The design prevents the LM from over-relying on recovered lexical content instead of acoustic-prosodic evidence. This addresses a known weakness in unified speech-language models.

entry.title: Detecting LLM-Assisted Vietnamese Writing via Keystrokes under Behavioral Manipulation

author.name: Thanh Dong, An Ngo, Minh Dau, Rajesh Kumar

entry.summary: Presents a Vietnamese keystroke dataset covering bona fide writing, transcription, and paraphrasing, plus a threat model where users deliberately alter typing patterns to evade keystroke-based detection of LLM-assisted writing. It evaluates four keystroke modeling approaches under user- and context-independent settings and probes robustness to behavioral manipulation.

entry.title: Dynamic Positional Attention Modulation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Dayan Pan, Jingyuan Wang, Xie Yu

entry.summary: DyPAM is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that adapts how positional information contributes to attention, exploiting the dimension-dependent structure induced by rotary positional embeddings rather than applying uniform adaptations. It operates directly on query and key representations to account for heterogeneous attention behavior across dimensions, heads, layers, and tokens.

entry.title: Penalty-Framed No-Valid-Option MCQA: Analyzing LLM Abstention under Invalid Choices

author.name: Jinhyeok Kim, Hye-Young Jung

entry.summary: The paper studies penalty-framed no-valid-option MCQA, where models must either pick a remaining option or output ABSTAIN when the labeled correct option is removed from MMLU-Pro math questions, with penalties for invalid forced choices. A correct-conditioned analysis evaluates abstention only on instances the model answers correctly when the full option set is available.

entry.title: Rethinking Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation: From Alignment Coverage to Supervision Reliability

author.name: Bingxi Hou, Guochao Jiang, Guofeng Quan, Weiqing Li, Wenfeng Feng, Guohua Liu, Yuewei Zhang

entry.summary: This empirical study examines on-policy distillation between teacher and student models with different tokenizers, finding that strict 1:1 token alignment already covers most student tokens despite vocabulary mismatch. Restricting reverse KL to a student-selected top-16 subset improves reliability of supervision. The work offers practical guidance for distillation pipelines, an increasingly important efficiency technique.

entry.title: Agreement Is Not Validity: Cross-Model LLM Consensus in Diagnosing Student Failure Modes in K-12 Math Tutoring Dialogue

author.name: Clayton Cohn, Joyce Fonteles, Kirk Vanacore, Gianni Mazza, Candida Crawford, Tom Hooper, Gautam Biswas, Rene Kizilcec

entry.summary: This exploratory study examines whether cross-model LLM consensus is a valid signal when diagnosing five student failure modes in K-12 math tutoring dialogue, using an operational codebook covering uncertainty, misattribution, operator selection, conceptual gap, and procedural slips. It argues that model agreement does not guarantee validity of LLM-generated interpretations. The finding cautions education-analytics researchers against relying on inter-model agreement as validation.

entry.title: Nord-Parl-TTS: Finnish and Swedish TTS Dataset from Parliament Speech

author.name: Zirui Li, Jens Edlund, Yicheng Gu, Nhan Phan, Lauri Juvela, Mikko Kurimo

entry.summary: Nord-Parl-TTS provides open, large-scale TTS datasets extracted from Nordic parliamentary proceedings: 900 hours of Finnish and 5,090 hours of Swedish speech, built with an adapted Emilia pipeline and unified evaluation sets. This substantially narrows the resource gap for Finnish and Swedish speech synthesis. It is a significant community resource for a typically under-resourced language pair.

entry.title: On Open-Ended Information Seeking for Information Elicitation Agents

author.name: Victor De Lima, Grace Hui Yang

entry.summary: This work studies information elicitation as an open-ended information-seeking problem where the value of pursued information changes as new information emerges. The authors compare information-value judgments across 11 LLMs of different families and scales and build a controlled elicitation environment to study how model choice shapes sequential information seeking. It matters for understanding behavioral differences between LLMs in agentic settings.

entry.title: Natural Language Questions as an Interface for Knowledge Graphs: QRAKEN Graph Distillation and Semantic Self-Healing

author.name: Remo Grillo, Lukas Klic, Giovanni Colavizza

entry.summary: QRAKEN is a training-free, ontology-agnostic neurosymbolic pipeline for Text-to-SPARQL that grounds query generation in empirical graph evidence (a distilled TTQL summary of populated multi-hop patterns, frequencies, and literal examples) plus deterministic syntax and data-model checks for iterative refinement. It addresses LLMs generating syntactically valid queries that misrepresent unfamiliar graph data models. It matters for reliable natural-language access to knowledge graphs.

entry.title: State-Aware Interaction MIL for Rare Joint Molecular Phenotype Prediction in Colorectal Cancer and Lung Adenocarcinoma

author.name: Dasari Naga Raju, Tripti Bameta

entry.summary: This weakly supervised multiple-instance learning method predicts joint molecular phenotypes in cancer pathology by preserving biomarker-specific histological representations, modeling their interactions, and supervising the full four-state configuration instead of collapsing configurations into a binary endpoint. This better handles small joint-positive populations and overlapping histology.

entry.title: WildMatch: Weakly Supervised Image Matcher Adaptation for Wildlife Re-Identification

author.name: Turhan Can Kargin, Piotr Kubaty, Ekaterina Rostovskaya, Izabela Wierzbowska, Bartosz Zieli\'nski, Marcin Przewi\k{e}\'zlikowski

entry.summary: WildMatch adapts general-purpose image matchers to wildlife re-identification from camera-trap imagery using weak supervision, addressing the scarcity of labeled wildlife data with local correspondence constraints. The approach targets conservation-critical animal monitoring where collecting per-individual labels is expensive. It bridges off-the-shelf matching models and domain-specific wildlife imagery.

entry.title: From Laboratory to Road: Evaluating Wearable Gaze Accuracy for Driving

author.name: William Engel, Fabian Flohr

entry.summary: This work presents what the authors describe as the first unified framework for quantifying wearable eye-tracker gaze accuracy under real driving conditions, using an on-road study with 41 validated scenes where a driver fixated a license plate. It measures angular gaze error against a controlled reference, addressing sensitivity to head motion, illumination, and calibration drift. Gaze signals could enrich autonomous driving BEV representations with behavioral relevance.

entry.title: Can We Model the Artifacts Explicitly? Disentangle Artifacts via Pairwise Edit Relations for Image Manipulation Localization

author.name: Xuekang Zhu, Kaiwen Feng, Ruifeng Wang, Xiwen Wang, Xiaochen Ma, Bo Du, Changjiang Jiang, Chenfan Qu, Songyu Ye, Xia Du, Wentao Feng, Jian Liu, Ji-Zhe Zhou

entry.summary: The authors reinterpret image manipulation localization as a latent-variable problem where manipulation artifacts z are never directly observed, arguing that implicit artifact modeling limits current methods. They propose a two-stage learning paradigm that explicitly models artifacts via feature disentanglement using pairwise edit relations between real and manipulated images. This yields improved localization without requiring direct artifact labels.

entry.title: M3SunAgent: Monocular 3D Spatial Understanding Agent for Metric Depth Estimation and 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Jinsong Zhang, Kejun Wu, Ming Zhu, Renjie Qiao, Chengtao Cai, Zhengguo Li

entry.summary: M3SunAgent unifies monocular metric depth estimation and 3D visual grounding in a single agent that uses an LLM as a task planner for spatial visual programming, generating structured programs and coordinating tools. This removes the need for separate, unaligned frameworks for the two complementary 3D understanding tasks. The design aims to provide flexible, aligned spatial information access for embodied intelligence systems.

entry.title: Catastrophic Forgetting in Sequential Thermal Anti-UAV Detection: The Role of Scale-Conditioned Gradient Imbalance

author.name: Khac Duc Giang Nguyen, Seyed Sahand Mohammadi Ziabari, Ali Mohammed Mansoor Alsahag

entry.summary: This continual learning study characterizes catastrophic forgetting in a YOLOv5-based thermal infrared detector for anti-UAV applications when fine-tuned sequentially across three benchmarks of increasing scale difficulty. The authors show that naive fine-tuning causes roughly 90% capability loss and attribute it to scale-conditioned gradient imbalance, with knowledge retention methods mitigating the drop.

entry.title: Deformable CT-US Registration via Anatomy-Aware Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Agnieszka Lach, Magdalena Wysocki, Feng Li, Mohammad Farid Azampour, Benjamin D. Killeen, Felix Ginzinger, Mathias Braun, Philipp Steininger, Heinz Deutschmann, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: The paper presents a deformable CT-to-ultrasound registration framework for minimally invasive interventions, combining robot-assisted rigid registration with an anatomy-aware sinusoidal implicit neural representation for deformation estimation. Anatomical priors from CT improve alignment under soft-tissue deformation caused by probe contact.

entry.title: Post-Training Semantic Lifting for 3D Gaussian Splatting: Separating Detector, Lifting and Representation Error

author.name: Iv\'an Verdugo Guerra, Ezequiel L\'opez Rubio, Jorge Garc\'ia Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: This paper proposes a post-training method for lifting semantics onto 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes that works one target class at a time and aggregates evidence across all views, weighted by per-Gaussian visibility. It accumulates target and non-target evidence simultaneously and filters Gaussians with thresholds, explicitly separating detector, lifting, and representation error sources.

entry.title: AIM: Adaptive Interaction Modeling Networks for Real-to-Sim Soft-Body Simulation

author.name: Tiancheng Yang, Dingshuo Chen, Tianle Chen, Zhaocheng Liu, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: AIM treats real-to-sim soft-body simulation as a local-global interaction modeling problem, using motion history and geometry to adapt predictions of deformation under external interactions for tasks like folding laundry or handling food. It targets the problems that spatial neighborhoods misrepresent deformation dependencies and that per-scene models fail to generalize across object geometries and manipulation conditions.

entry.title: Toward Trustworthy Physical AI for Human Interaction

author.name: Niccol\`o Pagliarani, Maximilian St\"olzle, Cosima du Pasquier, Jeff Lui, Andrew Sabelhaus, Cecilia Laschi, Gentiane Venture, Daniela Rus, Matteo Cianchetti

entry.summary: A position/framework paper from a strong author group (including Rus, Laschi, Venture) proposing that trustworthy physical AI emerges from aligning safety, behavioral intelligibility, and perceptual alignment across embodiment, control, cognition, and design. It frames a conceptual structure for when robots in human spaces deserve trust.

entry.title: Entropy-Gated Belief Coordination for Decentralized Multi-Agent Search Under Intermittent Communication

author.name: Mohamed Abdelnaby, Kevin Leahy

entry.summary: The paper introduces entropy-gated belief coordination for decentralized multi-agent search, where agents skip belief fusion during high-entropy exploration and merge beliefs only during exploitation, leveraging intermittent Poisson-distributed communication. It provides theoretical grounding via opinion dynamics bifurcations and submodular information-gain structure.

entry.title: Task-Space Imitation Guidance for Efficient Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Salar Asayesh, Hossein Darani, Todd Cao, Evgeny Andriash, Mani Ranjbar

entry.summary: TIGER uses an action-chunked imitation policy as a local task-space progress estimator, converting predicted action chunks into end-effector references that provide dense progress rewards while sparse environment reward remains dominant. It also relaxes conservative value penalties during pretraining for predicted-progress actions.

entry.title: Humanoid Horizon: Extending Task Horizon in Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation via Parallel Training, Dynamic Starting, and Reward Gating

author.name: Haozhuo Zhang, Qiang Zhang, Jian Tang, Mingzhe Ni, Michele Caprio, Angelo Cangelosi, Wei Pan

entry.summary: Humanoid Horizon is a unified RL policy framework for long-horizon whole-body loco-manipulation, where humanoids must navigate, grasp, transport, and place large heavy objects in cluttered indoor environments within a single episode. It tackles easy-reward bias and catastrophic forgetting through parallel training, dynamic task starting, and reward gating. This enables training on complete multi-stage tasks that previous approaches fragment or fail on.

entry.title: A Belief-State World Model for Catheter Navigation under Sparse Fluoroscopy: A Planar Proof of Concept

author.name: Damini Rijhwani

entry.summary: This work explores reducing patient and clinician radiation exposure during endovascular catheter navigation by using a physics-based Cosserat rod world model with a particle filter to maintain belief over device state between sparse X-ray acquisitions. Formulated as a POMDP with a geometric contact proxy, the planar proof-of-concept also investigates whether the model can signal when its internal estimate becomes unreliable.

entry.title: No Need to Stop the Fleet: Localized Anomaly Isolation via Dead Zones in AGV Fleets

author.name: Natalia Ogorelysheva, Falk Howar, Jian-Jia Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces dead zones, a formally defined mechanism for isolating local anomalies in automated guided vehicle fleets without triggering a system-wide emergency stop. By quarantining only the affected area, unaffected robots can continue operating, reducing unnecessary downtime in production and logistics settings.

entry.title: Sim-to-Real Transfer of Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments Using an Ackermann-Steered Mobile Robot

author.name: Chalindu Abeywansa, Sahan Gunasekara, Devindi De Silva, Seniru Dissanayake, Ranga Rodrigo, Peshala Jayasekara

entry.summary: The authors transfer a vision-language navigation model from simulation to a real Ackermann-steered robot operating in continuous environments without navigation graphs, 360-degree views, or perfect localization. The system aligns visual inputs and language instructions in a shared embedding space using vision-language models for natural-language-driven navigation.

entry.title: The interface of data assimilation and machine learning

author.name: Eviatar Bach

entry.summary: This is a review article surveying the interface between data assimilation and machine learning, covering how ML can improve DA and how DA principles inform ML, in the context of chaotic systems like the atmosphere. It provides an overview of main topics and methods in this rapidly developing area.

entry.title: When does conformal calibration need censoring weights? Cause-of-failure prediction sets under competing risks

author.name: Sunny Yang, Weiyan Zhao

entry.summary: The authors study split conformal prediction for competing-risks labels when calibration data is subject to right censoring, showing complete-case calibration can miscover in either direction and quantifying score-distribution shifts near the population quantile. They analyze when censoring weights are needed and illustrate in cause-of-failure prediction settings.

entry.title: Why did we get warning shots?

author.name: p(mike)

entry.summary: A skeptical outsider analyzes why classic AI x-risk predictions about capability generalization and hard alignment have held up, while the predicted Treacherous Turn by deceptively aligned models has not, with models instead producing repeated warning shots. The author reasons through what this divergence implies about alignment difficulty and model psychology.

entry.title: Recursive Improvement of a Differentiable Scientific Software Ecosystem

author.name: Pengcheng Hou, Xiaojun Tan, Sihan Hu, Ruisi Wang, Shuo Chen, Lei Wang, Youjin Deng, Kun Chen

entry.summary: Presents an environment for agent-driven evolution of differentiable scientific software that connects demand identification, development, and quality evaluation through a unified differentiation interface exposing reusable derivative rules alongside existing numerical routines. The goal is to let AI coding agents accelerate extension of differentiable programming across a heterogeneous scientific software ecosystem, with evaluation of how well implementations meet research needs. An early contribution to self-improving scientific software infrastructure.

entry.title: Toward a Locally Deployable Agentic Co-Scientist: Small-Model Planning for Early-Stage Drug Discovery

author.name: Tian Liang, Jiayu Chang, Alejandro F. Frangi, Mobarak I. Hoque, Richard A. Bryce

entry.summary: This work presents a lightweight, tool-augmented framework where a locally deployable compact language model plans calls to 18 modular tools for early-stage drug discovery, using a Unified Molecular Schema and LoRA fine-tuning on 1,263 manually refined query-plan pairs. Llama 3.2-3B achieves a 0.998 tool-selection F1 with fully parseable, schema-compliant plans on held-out queries, enabling privacy-preserving local deployment.

entry.title: Do LLMs Understand Sequential Structure? A Controlled Study of Inference and Generation

author.name: Jerry Wang, Zhengxiang Wang, Ting Yu Liu, Hsin-Ling Hsu, Yi-Cheng Lai, Tengfei Ma

entry.summary: Using controlled Rock-Paper-Scissors and stochastic n-gram tasks, this study tests whether LLMs can recover latent sequential structure beyond surface action frequencies, separating distribution matching from conditional rule following. The results indicate limits in how well longer contexts translate into higher-order conditional dependencies. This is a careful scientific contribution to understanding LLM inductive biases, relevant to their use as simulators and agents.

entry.title: Mining Agent Skills from Production Traces

author.name: Yue Ran Kang, Colton Mikolajczyk, Chhaya Methani, Hazel Mak, Sahil Bhatnagar, Susheel Suresh, Alejandro Gutierrez Munoz

entry.summary: This paper empirically studies how to mine reusable agent skills from execution traces when ground-truth success signals are unavailable in production. Holding the mining pipeline fixed, the authors compare six combinations of mining evidence (successes only, labeled successes-plus-failures, or unlabeled mixtures) and skill forms (ordered workflows versus alternatives). The results inform practical choices for building skill libraries from noisy production data.

entry.title: GPlaceRL: An Open-Source Graph Reinforcement Learning Framework for Detailed Placement

author.name: Pavlos Stoikos, Foteini Oikonomou, Christos Poulos, Maria Pantazi-Kypriou, Athanasios Tziouvaras, Christos Anagnostopoulos, Georgios Karakonstantis, George Floros

entry.summary: GPlaceRL is an open-source graph RL framework for detailed placement refinement in chip design, representing legalized placements as graphs and offering a modular environment for studying graph encoders, policies, rewards, and local placement actions. It fills a gap since most learning-based placement work targets floorplanning or macro/global placement rather than detailed refinement.

entry.title: Logit-Aware MIMO AirComp for Distributed Mixture-of-Experts LLM Inference over Wireless Edge Networks

author.name: Lyutianyang Zhang, Yunjian Jia, Liu Cao, Dengke Wang, Jinke Ren, Shuguang Cui

entry.summary: The paper addresses the communication bottleneck in distributed mixture-of-experts LLM inference at wireless edge networks, where expert outputs must be aggregated over the air. It proposes logit-aware over-the-air computation that accounts for the unequal impact of aggregation errors on LLM output quality, rather than minimizing generic communication distortion, across coordinated base stations with MIMO configurations.

entry.title: MAGEFormer: Learning Metric-Consistent Representations for Anisotropic CT Segmentation

author.name: Jiaying Li, Paolo Remagnino

entry.summary: MAGEFormer is a geometry-calibrated vision transformer framework for volumetric CT segmentation that embeds physical metric constraints directly into representation learning. It introduces Metric-Adaptive Spatial Embedding to calibrate positional frequencies using voxel spacing and Geometry-Constrained Attention to suppress physically implausible feature correlations. The approach addresses the mismatch between isotropic transformer assumptions and anisotropic CT acquisition.

entry.title: Cluster Validation Indices as Self-Supervised Objectives for Text Representation Learning

author.name: Kishor Kumar Bhaumik, Nicolas Roque dos Santos, Neil Shah, Jia Chen, Evangelos E. Papalexakis

entry.summary: SilK introduces self-supervised fine-tuning of text encoders using cluster validation indices, specifically regressing a simplified silhouette toward a target after K-means clustering of the corpus. This avoids both in-batch negatives required by contrastive learning and auxiliary graphs needed by negative-free methods. It offers a lightweight alternative recipe for improving embedding spaces without labels or extra data views.

entry.title: Bayesian Entropy-based Reordering for Calibrated Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zhejun Jiang, Mijung Park

entry.summary: BayesER is a post-hoc Bayesian decoding framework for masked diffusion language models that averages predictions over samples from a lightweight approximate posterior and uses predictive entropy to guide token commitment, replacing miscalibrated softmax confidence. It parallels Laplace-LoRA without requiring adapter training.

entry.title: Scenario-Based Compositional Statistical Model Checking for Safety Specifications

author.name: Abhinav Pomalapally, Arya Raeesi, Kevin Kai-Chun Chang, Beyazit Yalcinkaya, Sanjit A. Seshia

entry.summary: The paper presents a compositional statistical model checking framework that decomposes composite driving scenarios into primitives and specifications into sub-specifications, verifies each independently, and composes results. This avoids redundant simulation across scenarios sharing common structure in safety-critical domains like autonomous driving.

entry.title: Who Keeps the Gains from Personal AI Assistants? Seller Adaptation and the Unassisted in a Language-Model Market Simulation

author.name: Haonan Huang, Joey Xiao

entry.summary: The authors build an agent-based rental market simulation in which LLMs play consumers, personal AI assistants, and six adaptive sellers using algorithmic pricing, to study whether consumer savings from AI shopping assistants persist once sellers adapt and what happens to unassisted consumers. The design contrasts advisory versus executing assistant mandates with paired market conditions.

entry.title: MercerFlow: Flow Matching in a Kernel-Induced Latent Space for Probabilistic Forecasting

author.name: Ilya Kuleshov, Egor Serov, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: MercerFlow improves probabilistic time-series forecasting with conditional flow matching by embedding series via an invertible kernel-induced latent map, letting a cheap MLP replace costly RNN, S4, or Transformer backbones. The authors show the interaction between the prior and the latent map choice, previously understudied, strongly affects results. This offers a memory- and time-efficient alternative for probabilistic forecasting.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Calibration of Pre-Generation Success Probes for Multilingual LLM Routing

author.name: Andrea Paganelli, Stefano Civelli, Pietro Bernardelle, Gianluca Demartini

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether pre-generation success probes, which predict LLM response correctness from hidden activations, remain reliable across languages for cost-aware model routing. Using 3,000 MATH problems in 10 languages and 8 open-weight models, it assesses discrimination, calibration, and cross-model utility, comparing English-trained probes to multilingual training. It extends an English-only technique toward practical multilingual routing.

entry.title: MemPilot: Orchestrating On-Demand Multimodal Memory Curation for LLM Agents

author.name: Haozhen Zhang, Haodong Yue, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao, Qingyuan Liu, Tao Feng, Bohan Liu, Weida Liang, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: MemPilot is a flexible framework for LLM agent memory that orchestrates on-demand, query-aware memory curation under explicit performance-cost-latency preferences. Unlike query-agnostic memory systems that waste preprocessing or discard details, it adapts memory operations at runtime with configurable processing schemes. This targets the growing need for controllable, efficient memory in the agent ecosystem.

entry.title: Should We Skip Diffusion?

author.name: Yiping Ji, James Martens, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Studies skip/residual connections in the Decoupled Diffusion Transformer (DDT) encoder, arguing they let shallow features bypass progressive abstraction and limit semantic representation learning. The proposed DDT-RFE removes residual connections around self-attention and MLP blocks while maintaining stable training, with compensation mechanisms to retain information.

entry.title: What Must Replay Preserve? Separating Correctable Bias from Class Correspondence

author.name: BoRen Deng, Xiangyue Ma, Chenglong Li, Xiaoting Du

entry.summary: Proposes a diagnostic framework for class-incremental learning that treats cached logit predictions as temporally heterogeneous supervision, separating classes known at storage time from later-learned classes. This clarifies what logit replay methods like DER and DER++ must actually preserve to mitigate forgetting.

entry.title: Algorithmically Aligned Neural Agglomerative Tree Construction

author.name: Robert R Nerem, Pranav Singh, Cheyenne Ward, Yusu Wang

entry.summary: NN-linkage is a neural model that learns task-specific, locally dependent merge rules for hierarchical clustering while retaining the recursive structure and efficiency of classical linkage algorithms. It is algorithmically aligned with the Lance-Williams recurrence, spanning a continuous family of linkage rules. This lets practitioners learn which merge rule suits a dataset instead of choosing among fixed heuristics.

entry.title: Adapting to Changes in Agent Behavior via Finite-Depth Policy Sensitivity

author.name: Lan Shi, Daigo Shishika, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: The authors develop a finite-depth framework for estimating policy sensitivity in multi-agent settings, approximating the policy Hessian and mixed derivatives using reference-environment data with a tunable truncation depth for derivative propagation. This enables adaptation to another agent's behavior change without massive new interaction data.

entry.title: Optimization Encoders: Rethinking Second-Order Meta-Learning for Neural Fields

author.name: Rudolf L. M. van Herten, Soufiane Ben Haddou, Rachit Saluja, Johannes C. Paetzold

entry.summary: The paper formalizes latent optimization in conditional neural fields as an optimization encoder, unifying second-order differentiation, latent parameterization, and task supervision. This view enables end-to-end second-order meta-learning of the encoding procedure with the decoder and clarifies what first-order approximations discard, leading to an Attentive Latent method.

entry.title: Early Memory Selection for Balanced Adam

author.name: Alberto Fern\'andez-Hern\'andez, Cristian P\'erez-Corral, Jose I. Mestre, Manuel F. Dolz, Enrique S. Quintana-Ort\'i

entry.summary: The paper proposes selecting Adam's shared memory parameter beta from a short 200-update pilot training via a cubic memory rule estimated from gradient probes at a few checkpoints, keeping it fixed for full training. Seed-matched retrospective evaluation across eleven vision and language workloads reduces the mean relative validation gap by 40.7 percent.

entry.title: Identity-Conditioned Score Fusion for Open-Set Person Re-Identification

author.name: Manyi Yao, Jurijs Nazarovs, Eunji Chong, Abhishek Sharma, Rohan Sarkar, Yue Guo, Christian R. Shelton, Amit K. Roy-Chowdhury, Debashish Pal

entry.summary: Introduces identity-conditioned score fusion for person re-identification, tailoring fusion weights of face, gait, and body-shape cues to each gallery identity without training. By contrasting intra-identity consistency against cross-identity impostors, the parameter-free method widens true/false match separation on three clothes-changing re-identification benchmarks.

entry.title: REViT-v2: Hierarchical Windowed Roto-reflection Equivariant ViT for Equivariant Feature Extraction

author.name: Sheir A. Zaheer, Jihwan Moon, Chan Y. Park

entry.summary: REViT-v2 is a scalable roto-reflection-equivariant vision transformer using windowed group-convolutional self-attention and a hierarchical architecture, demonstrated at ImageNet scale with millions of parameters. Code and pretrained weights are released, addressing the practical scalability gap of equivariant ViTs.

entry.title: Beyond Marginal Monitoring: Distributed Joint-Distribution Testing for Data Concept Drift in Large Scale E-Commerce Operations

author.name: Cagdas Pullu, Mahmut Emir Arslan, Bugra Balkac, Aylin Ondersev Balta, Cihangir Celal Palaci, Fikri Cem Yilmaz, Altan Cakir

entry.summary: Evaluates five multivariate two-sample drift tests at industrial scale, including a 137.5-million-row e-commerce feature table, across synthetic and reproduced benchmarks. The study characterizes when joint-distribution testing outperforms marginal monitoring for detecting concept drift in high-cardinality production data.

entry.title: Verdicts Without Annotated Evidence: Rejection Sampling or Label-Only Post-Training for Evidence Recovery?

author.name: Nishanth Nayakanti, Prasang Gupta, Ashutosh Bilthare, Kevin Paul

entry.summary: This paper measures how much evidence a small LM can recover when post-trained only on verdict labels, with no human evidence annotations, using ContractNLI with held-out human evidence spans. It finds verdict accuracy and span agreement are only weakly related across systems, and label-only training reaches 0.896 accuracy and 0.564 span F1, with rejection sampling and label-only post-training compared. The key message is that accuracy is a poor guide when citations must be reviewable.

entry.title: InterCorrect: Intersection-Aware Correction of Demographic Model Merging for Fair ASR

author.name: Ashley E. Bravo-Bravo, Yuchen Zhang, Haralambos Mouratidis, Ravi Shekhar, Monorama Swain

entry.summary: The paper proposes a fairness-aware model merging method for Speech-LLM-based ASR: subgroup-adapted connectors are merged into a global model, then intersection-specific correction vectors are applied for critical cross-axis demographic pairs identified via subgroup WER and task-vector conflict. Experiments on Fair-Speech show overall WER improvements plus better handling of speakers in multiple demographic groups. This advances fairness techniques beyond single-axis interventions.

entry.title: A Data-Centric Review of Plant Disease Datasets: Taxonomy, Critical Analysis, Environmental Variability, and Implications for Precision Agriculture

author.name: Aamir Hilal, Shabir Ahmad Sofi, Neeraj Goel

entry.summary: This review critically analyzes plant disease detection datasets, arguing that reliance on laboratory-generated data with limited environmental diversity explains poor field generalization of deep learning models, and provides a taxonomy emphasizing in-field datasets capturing natural variability. It maps implications for deploying precision agriculture systems.

entry.title: Revisiting Numerical Forecasting Models for Language-Based Trajectory Prediction

author.name: JunGyu Lee, Inhwan Bae, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: The paper introduces MoRE, a reinforcement learning refinement framework that transfers knowledge from frozen numerical trajectory predictors into a language-based trajectory predictor that tokenizes coordinates. Five frozen predictors serve as reward experts providing complementary coordinate-level motion and interaction knowledge, compensating for the weak indirect supervision of token-level objectives. This improves trajectory prediction quality on continuous dynamics.

entry.title: Local Content-Style Control for Diffusion-based Image Stylization

author.name: Amir Semmo

entry.summary: This work lifts ControlNet and IP-Adapter conditioning weights from global scalars to per-location spatial maps, giving independent local control of content and style axes in a single diffusion pass. The disjoint pathways of the two weights yield a 2x2 retouching vocabulary spanning free regeneration to identity preservation, validated on spatial confinement of edits.

entry.title: Robust Nonprehensile Object Transport with Quadruped Robots

author.name: Ainoor Teimoorzadeh, Riccardo Pretto, Mario Selvaggio, Gokhan Alcan, Sami Haddadin

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework for quadruped robots transporting objects without grasping, combining uncertainty-aware trajectory optimization that minimizes closed-loop sensitivity to uncertain object parameters with a coupled convex MPC and whole-body QP enforcing ground reaction constraints. Extensive simulations and real-world experiments with varied object inertial parameters show improved robustness over fixed-orientation and straight-line baselines.

entry.title: SURGE: Sonar-fUsed Reconstruction and localization via image-gated Graph Estimation

author.name: Mohammed Ibrahim M, Vallabh Deogaonkar, Trung Dong, Jane Shin, Abhilash Somayajula, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: SURGE fuses optical vision and 2D imaging sonar for underwater ROV localization and metric 3D scene reconstruction, addressing vision scale ambiguity and sonar's incomplete geometry through an image-gated graph estimation approach. It targets GPS-denied underwater inspection of caves, wrecks, and submerged infrastructure.

entry.title: HygieneRoboBench: Benchmarking Hygiene-Aware Planning for Household Robots

author.name: Yurun Chen, Josh Qixuan Sun, Jason Qin, Chengtai Li, Tianyi Wang, Mark Crowley, Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: HygieneRoboBench is a benchmark of 624 instances across 134 task families for evaluating household robot planning that is hygiene-aware, considering contamination spread via grippers and shared objects, treatment costs, and user priorities. It assesses how planners identify risks from contact history and plan safe continuations after new contact events.

entry.title: Towards Safer Autonomous Driving in an Open World: A Dual-Process Approach

author.name: Simon Janssen, Michiel Braat, Chris van der Ploeg, Serge Thill, Jan-Pieter Paardekooper

entry.summary: The paper proposes a dual-process autonomous driving framework combining a neural network for intuitive routine planning with model predictive control for reasoning-heavy unfamiliar situations, switching between them via a meta-cognitive component that reasons about contextual risk using a knowledge graph. The design targets safety compliance in open-world situations poorly represented in training data.

entry.title: Pressure, Context, and Machine Self-Control: A Criminological Test of Reward Hacking in Generative AI Models

author.name: Murat Ozer, Isaac Kofi Nti

entry.summary: Applying criminological theories (self-control, general strain, anomie, neutralization, routine activity) to reward hacking in generative AI, Study 1 measured delay discounting and shortcut willingness across seven models and 2,310 conversations, finding pressure raised discount rates 2.8-12.6-fold depending on conversational context. Models chose shortcuts in 1 of 700 dilemmas answering as themselves versus 64 of 700 under pressure conditions.

entry.title: Learning from imperfect teachers for low-resource acoustic generalization

author.name: Shuanglin Li, Ruxiao Qian, Jian Liu, Haijun Lin, Wenwu Wang, Siyang Song

entry.summary: The paper proposes BA-MPD, a logit-based distillation objective for low-resource acoustic modeling that corrects biased teacher distributions via Boundary-Anchored Correction and Mass-Partitioned Distillation. By anchoring on decision boundaries and partitioning probability mass by reliability, the student avoids inheriting teacher-induced bias while still benefiting from soft supervision.

entry.title: Specific Algorithmic Interpretability of Neural Networks: A Case Study on Textures

author.name: Yanglin Zhang, Anneke von Seeger, Gilad Lerman, Ron Levie

entry.summary: This work develops a framework for constructing neural networks whose trained parameters retain an explicit algorithmic interpretation, addressing the gap where algorithm-inspired architectures lose their interpretive structure after standard training. Networks are initialized to exactly implement algorithms for estimating class-distinguishing statistics of class-dependent stochastic processes, with guarantees on preservation through training, demonstrated on texture classification. It contributes to the theory of interpretable-by-construction networks.

entry.title: A Systematic Analysis of the Predictive Power of LM Surprisal in Reading Chinese

author.name: Hongao Zhu, Muxiaoqiao Xu, Yikang Liu, Siyuan Song, Yuxia Wang, Byung-Doh Oh, Hai Hu

entry.summary: The study examines whether language-model surprisal predicts Mandarin Chinese reading times, proposing the Shortest Matching Sequence alignment scheme to bridge word-segmentation and subword tokenization mismatches. Using Chinese-Pythia models trained from scratch on 30B tokens, the authors find surprisal is predictive of eye-tracking measures across three corpora, contrary to prior null findings. This contributes to psycholinguistics and the cognitive plausibility of LMs across languages.

entry.title: Direction-Conditioned Policies for Online Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: S K Swaminathan, Damiya Gondha, Theyanesh Eswaramoorthy Rajahkrishnan, Aritra Hazra

entry.summary: Direction-Conditioned Policies (DCP) improve Contrastive RL by conditioning the policy on direction and distance to selected visited-state waypoints in representation space, exploiting the critic's goal-reachability geometry. At deployment DCP applies the same interface directly to final goals without planning, beating CRL on seven of nine navigation and manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Soft Strategy Selection for Batch-Mode Active Learning

author.name: Rushil Gupta, Romain Lopez

entry.summary: The paper addresses the problem of choosing an acquisition strategy in active learning before any data is labeled, proposing a soft strategy selection method that avoids spending rounds on bandit-style strategy exploration. This matters for low-round applications like genetic perturbation screens and directed evolution.

entry.title: Adaptive Expert Guidance for Efficient On-Policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daniele Affinita, Ming Xu, Rudolf Reiter, Davide Scaramuzza, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: The paper addresses how to balance guidance from a suboptimal expert (heuristic controller or related-task policy) against reward-based learning in on-policy RL with massively parallel simulation. Unlike prior methods that fix blending weights or schedules, the proposed approach adaptively modulates expert influence without additional learned components. This improves sample efficiency while preserving final performance beyond what the expert alone achieves.

entry.title: Local2Mesh: Spatially Localized Contour-to-Mesh for Left Ventricular Reconstruction from Sparse 2D Cardiac MRI

author.name: Haoyu Wu, Ling Lin, Pascal Lef\`evre, Ruizhe Li, Xiaowu Sun

entry.summary: Local2Mesh reconstructs 3D left ventricular geometry from sparse 2D cardiac MRI contours by deforming a template mesh, using geometry-aware inter-slice alignment and a plane-aware Local Router that assigns contour features to vertices by distance. It requires no 3D mesh annotations, addressing misalignment and limited local spatial context between slices. This advances cardiac structural analysis from routine sparse imaging.

entry.title: FlexiFlow: Bandit-based Model Switching in ML Workflows

author.name: Abhilash Jindal, Todd Nief, Bhanu Prakash Vangala, Shankaradithyaa V, Tvisha Malik, Anshik Sahu, Aaron Schein, Amitabh Chaudhary, Tanu Malik

entry.summary: FlexiFlow is a dataflow system that adaptively switches between alternate models using a bandit approach when the current model underperforms on specific data batches, instead of relying on a single model throughout a workflow. Experiments with real ML workflows show switching improves accuracy by up to 23 percent. This addresses a systems gap where users currently test models manually and sequentially.

entry.title: Robust Importance Sampling for Rare Events via Constrained Gaussian Mixtures

author.name: Pawe{\l} Lorek, Rafa{\l} Nowak, Rafa{\l} Topolnicki, Tomasz Trzci\'nski, Maciej Zi\k{e}ba

entry.summary: The paper proposes an importance-sampling framework for rare-event probability estimation using constrained Gaussian mixtures, separating the problem into coverage (overcoming cold start) and refinement phases. It demonstrates improved efficiency and robustness over crude Monte Carlo, cross-entropy, variational methods, Safe-ICE, Subset Simulation, and SMC.

entry.title: Which and When to Admit: Gradient Admission for Data-Centric Small Language Model Finetuning

author.name: Hongyu Cao, Yanchi Liu, Kunpeng Liu, Xujiang Zhao, Wei Cheng, Zhengzhang Chen, Yanjie Fu, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: GRADE is a data-centric LoRA fine-tuning framework addressing gradient conflicts, static data selection, and subspace saturation via a state-aware selector admitting samples aligned with the evolving gradient field and a self-calibrating step-level gate. It controls which data-induced gradients enter the LoRA subspace and when.

entry.title: Linear Bandits under Exact Sliding-Window Constraints

author.name: Seyed Mohammad Hadi Hosseini, Yasin Abbasi-Yadkori, Sattar Vakili

entry.summary: The paper studies linear bandits where every consecutive block of actions must belong to a prescribed feasible set, showing when stationary offline solutions are optimal and that sublinear regret can be impossible without sufficient geometric structure. It introduces a transition diameter to quantify feasibility and develops a rare-switching OFUL algorithm with regret O-tilde(d sqrt(T) + tau d + w).

entry.title: Calibrated Answers About Randomized Trials From a 4-Billion-Parameter Open Model: A Registered Test and a License-Clean Release

author.name: Johann Emmanuel Li

entry.summary: The paper presents Fiorillo v0.5, a Qwen3-4B-Base model with low-rank adapters and a decision head that reads randomized trial articles and outputs calibrated probabilities for whether an intervention significantly changed an outcome on the Evidence Inference 2.0 benchmark. Unusually, release criteria were registered on OSF before test predictions, and the model was fine-tuned only on license-permissible articles for a license-clean release.

entry.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent Ascent is Suboptimal for Nonconvex-PL Min-Max Games

author.name: Junsoo Ha

entry.summary: The paper establishes the first tight complexity lower bound for two-timescale SGDA with fixed timescale ratio on nonconvex-PL min-max games, matching known upper bounds and proving a complexity separation from the Smoothed-AGDA algorithm. This shows SGDA is fundamentally suboptimal for this class of games.

entry.title: Language Carries the Expert's Impression: Instrument-Anchored LLM Judges Transfer Counseling-Quality Assessment and Beat In-Domain Training

author.name: Tobias Hallmen, Elisabeth Andr\'e

entry.summary: Studies cross-domain transfer of expert overall-impression prediction across three German counseling corpora, showing that instrument-anchored LLM judges trained on other domains beat in-domain training on small expert-rated datasets. Session-level linguistic features of expert language drive the transfer effect.

entry.title: JudgeMoE: Distributional Aggregation for LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Yiqi Liu, Joseph James, Yang Wang, Kun Zhao, Chenghao Xiao, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: JudgeMoE is a lightweight aggregator that fuses cached LLM-judge score distributions with example-specific weights before computing final scores, preserving uncertainty information lost by scalar compression. It improves mean Spearman correlation over uniform log pooling on a 10-cell benchmark and generalizes positively across 16 cells. The paper also documents instability of score-range protocols and advantages of soft scoring.

entry.title: LOGIC: An LLM Benchmark for Intent-Grounded Change Impact in Aerospace Electrical Systems

author.name: Muhammad Faraz Shoaib, Muhammad Qasim, Raisulhaq Mohammed Rizwan, Rahmatullah Safdar, Muzammil Adnan Shaik, Abdul Aleem Mohammed

entry.summary: LOGIC is a benchmark of 168 scenarios for intent-grounded change-impact analysis in aerospace electrical design, where models must select only changes authorized by an engineering request before propagating them through a typed traceability graph. The design separates candidate-selection errors from propagation errors and includes abstention cases. It matters as a rigorous, safety-critical domain benchmark for grounded LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Structure-aware Keypoint Localization for Videofluoroscopic Swallowing Study

author.name: Kai Zhou, Chuanshen Chen, Runhao Zeng, Meng Dai, Yifan Yang, Jinwu Hu, Daiyuan Li, Mingkui Tan, Fei Liu

entry.summary: This work improves anatomical keypoint localization for videofluoroscopic swallowing studies by covering under-addressed regions like the soft palate and exploiting abundant non-swallowing frames that prior work ignored. It observes that generic semi-supervised learning induces spatial bias in fixed-layout medical X-rays and proposes structure-aware learning instead. Automated kinematic analysis could improve diagnosis of swallowing disorders.

entry.title: Multi-Dataset Diagnostic Utility of Clinical Visual Concepts in AI Systems for Dermatology

author.name: Linda Wermelinger, Simone Lionetti, Fabian Gr\"oger, Nipun Ranasekara, Philippe Gottfrois, Ludovic Amruthalingam, Labelling Consortium, Marc Pouly, Alexander A. Navarini

entry.summary: The paper introduces SkinLex, a harmonized dataset of 48 clinical morphological attributes across four public dermatology datasets totaling 20,411 records, to support interpretable AI in dermatology. Experiments show that restricting features to specific visual groups (e.g., shapes or colors alone) reduces diagnostic accuracy, and bootstrapped backward elimination identifies the utility of the full 48-attribute set. Interpretable visual concepts are positioned as trust-enhancing intermediate representations for clinical deployment.

entry.title: Nine Trials to Recover: A Reproducible Benchmark for Repertoire-Free Soft-Robot Damage Adaptation

author.name: Siyuan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents a reproducible benchmark for soft-robot damage recovery with nine online adaptation trials, a GP expected-improvement reference controller, and separation of method development from evaluation on new morphologies. Across 150 bodies, GP-EI beats random search, Sobol, CEM, and CMA-ES under equal budgets with rigorous statistics.

entry.title: Demo: Closed-Loop Sionna-Isaac Sim Co-Simulation Framework for Wireless-Aware Robot Navigation over ROS 2

author.name: Yi Shen Lim, Seungeun Oh, Jihong Park

entry.summary: This demo paper presents a real-time co-simulation of NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Sionna over ROS 2 that closes the perception-action-communication loop: Sionna ray-traces the base-station-to-robot channel over the exact simulated geometry and feeds channel states back into the control loop. This enables studying network-offloaded robot control where link quality depends on robot position.

entry.title: ROAR: Unifying Runs across Heterogeneous AI-Driven Research Systems

author.name: Leo Y. Lin, Vishakha Ramani, Z. Berkay Celik, Paul Castro, Marquita Ellis

entry.summary: ROAR provides shared infrastructure for unifying and analyzing outputs from AI-driven research systems (ADRS), which currently emit results in incompatible formats across isolated teams. It uses a relational schema and parsing layer to reconcile heterogeneous outputs and enable analytics across runs with different objectives and scoring functions.

entry.title: MERCI Cards: An LLM Evaluation and Deployment Framework for High-Stakes Domains

author.name: Aparna Komarla, Annalisa Szymanski

entry.summary: Presents MERCI Cards, a mathematical framework for iterative LLM evaluation and deployment in high-stakes domains, formalized as weighted multi-objective optimization covering model selection, rubric design, evaluation, and deployment. It is demonstrated on AI systems in criminal justice, showing the framework can direct developer attention to underperforming areas across deployment cycles. Few evaluation frameworks target such resource-constrained, high-risk settings.

entry.title: RAGrasp: Geometry-Semantic Template Retrieval and Grasp Transfer

author.name: Shenzhe Zhu, Chengxiao He, Jan Harder

entry.summary: RAGrasp is a retrieval-augmented pipeline for planar parallel-jaw grasping that uses a small set of locally collected, grasp-annotated RGB-D templates instead of large synthetic datasets, requiring no end-to-end retraining for new deployments. It combines DINOv2 features with appearance and depth cues to prompt SAM2 for object isolation, followed by two-stage geometry-semantic template retrieval and grasp transfer. The local-template design aligns stored examples with the actual deployment camera, robot, and gripper.

entry.title: Penumbra: Sample-Efficient Adversarial Search for Regulatory Obligations

author.name: Anthony Rhodes

entry.summary: Penumbra is an adversarial search method for red-teaming agent compliance with regulatory obligations in finance, healthcare, and law, where violations involve omissions with no lexical signature. It walks from a verified anchor under an expanding edit budget until a two-evaluator committee flips its verdict, emitting adjacent response pairs that straddle the compliance boundary while minimizing costly probe generations.

entry.title: Not All Answers Are Contextually Persuadable: Inference Dynamics in Large Language Models under Contextual Influence

author.name: Zongye Hu, Weiqing Luo, Yanjie Fu, Yu Gan, Haofeng Zhang, Ziyi Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a theoretical framework analyzing contextual influence on LLMs through internal inference dynamics rather than output-level answer changes. It shows inference dynamics do not drift unboundedly under repeated contextual assertions; instead, predictive representations converge to stable, query-dependent regimes that constrain which answers are persuadable.

entry.title: Image Synthesis as an Intermediate for Controllable Time Series Generation

author.name: Haochen Yuan, Jing Xie, Yunbo Wang

entry.summary: VisualBridge uses time-series plots as a visual intermediate to connect language-level temporal semantics with numerical sequence generation, using an MLLM to convert plotted series into structured semantic representations. A semantic editing policy trained with downstream forecasting rewards lets the system favor temporal patterns useful for few-shot forecasting tasks.

entry.title: The GenAI4IDN Benchmark 3.0 - a Public Tool to Assess Generative AI Tools for the Design of Interactive Digital Narratives

author.name: Hartmut Koenitz, Jonathan Barbara, Mirjam Palosaari Eladhari

entry.summary: This is the third iteration of an evaluation framework for generative AI tools used in interactive digital narrative design, now deployed as a public web application with AI-assisted, blinded evaluation supporting complex media like music, video, and full IDNs. Version 3.0 adds fact-checking and bias detection tasks and rubrics in response to community concerns.

entry.title: Do Time-Series QA Systems Read the Time Series? Evidence Use and Reasoning Reliability

author.name: Zhuomin Chen, Jingchao Ni, Xu Zheng, Janki Bhimani, Mo Sha, Wei Cheng, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether time-series QA systems actually ground their answers in the supplied numerical series rather than relying on parametric knowledge or shallow heuristics. The authors reproduce results for four systems (TimeOmni-1, ChatTS, TimeOmni-VL, Time-MQA), compare them to their backbones, and probe sensitivity to input perturbations and the validity of stated rationales. It provides an evidence-use audit rather than just accuracy benchmarks.

entry.title: MS-Exam-Gen: Source-Grounded Benchmark Construction for Evaluating LLMs on Textual Multiple Sclerosis MRI Knowledge

author.name: Abdul Basit, Muhammad Abdullah Hanif, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: MS-Exam-Gen is a reproducible framework for constructing and auditing source-grounded multiple-choice benchmarks of textual multiple-sclerosis MRI knowledge, covering diagnostic criteria, acquisition and reporting protocols, and differential diagnosis. It targets auditable subspecialty LLM evaluation rather than direct image interpretation.

entry.title: Teaching a Minimalist Machine to Discover Recursive Programs for Arithmetic

author.name: Dominik Magiera, Christiane Wiebel-Herboth, Frank J\"{a}kel

entry.summary: The Minimalist Machine is an inductive program synthesis framework using a compact relational Prolog subset, where recursion emerges from clause reuse rather than a dedicated metarule, and concepts are introduced sequentially like a primary school arithmetic curriculum. Starting from an empty knowledge base, the system acquires simple concepts first and bootstraps them into recursive programs.

entry.title: GraphDecide: Benchmarking System One Models on Graph Tasks

author.name: Xianliang Yang, Yapu Zhang, Li Zhao

entry.summary: GraphDecide is a model-independent benchmark diagnosing how choice-based System One models, such as Jev, perform on graph decision tasks, using structural task profiles, matched graph-text contrasts, and heuristic-proposal controls across fourteen model-interface configurations. Findings show that accurate adjacency recognition does not guarantee broader structural correctness.

entry.title: Robust blind unmixing: A geometric approach to overcoming basis variation

author.name: Dumitru Mirauta, Vladimir V. Gusev, Michael W. Gaultois, Matthew J. Rosseinsky, Yannis Goulermas

entry.summary: This paper tackles blind unmixing, the problem of inferring basis patterns and component abundances from mixture measurements such as diffraction or spectroscopy data, where the basis varies from mixture to mixture due to noise and measurement physics. The authors propose a geometric approach that is robust to basis variation and avoids the application-specific tailoring of prior model-based methods. This enables broader reuse of unmixing pipelines across scientific domains.

entry.title: What to Preserve in Recursive Computation: A Local Predictive Sufficiency Principle

author.name: Peilin Wang, Feng Shiyang, Hongfu Gao, Cencheng Zhao, Di Yuan, Hui Chen, Guiguang Ding

entry.summary: This theoretical work addresses the tension in recursive computation where intermediate states must remain useful across long recursive paths yet are exposed to repeated information loss. It identifies local predictive sufficiency with recursive predictive closure and derives a tractable variational training procedure from this principle. The contribution offers a principled objective for architectures that compress or reuse intermediate states.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Stress Testing of Overload Monitoring for Resilient Emergency Cellular Networks Using Internet CDR Proxies

author.name: Bilal Hussain, Xiao Tang, Tan Li, Muhammad Azhar, Danista Khan, Fawad Ahmad

entry.summary: Trains a lightweight CNN to detect cellular network control-plane overload during disasters using coarse CDR aggregates as a privacy-preserving proxy for sensitive RRC/NGAP telemetry. Diffusion models synthesize realistic surge patterns to stress-test the detector, and retraining on hard synthetic samples improves robustness under stress conditions. This supports resilient emergency network monitoring without fine-grained private telemetry.

entry.title: Active-DiNTS: Active Differentiable Network Topology Search

author.name: Gean Trindade Pereira, Thierry Urruty, Muriel Visani, Andr\'e C. P. L. F. de Carvalho

entry.summary: Active-DiNTS embeds pool-based active learning into a bi-level differentiable neural architecture search for 3D medical image segmentation, jointly discovering architectures and curating annotation budgets. Unlabeled MRI volumes are ranked by uncertainty signals (entropy, variance, or standard deviation) and only top-ranked volumes are annotated, feeding both network weight training and topology search. This targets the high annotation and compute costs limiting NAS in medical imaging.

entry.title: Assembling Insights for Agentic Machine Learning Engineering Systems

author.name: Bihui Jin, Yinxi Li, Kaiyuan Wang, Pengyu Nie

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies how insights from related machine learning engineering tasks affect agentic MLE systems, noting that insight collection and injection are currently ad hoc and that uncontrolled insight sources introduce data-leakage threats to evaluation validity. The work proposes controlled ways to assemble and inject insights, with implications for recursive self-improvement research. This improves rigor in a fast-moving but under-evaluated area.

entry.title: AraYoungVoices: A Diverse L1/L2 Corpus of Arabic Child and Adolescent Speech

author.name: Shammur Absar Chowdhury, Zien Sheikh Ali, Houssam Eddine-Othman Lachemat, Hamdy Mubarak

entry.summary: AraYoungVoices is a 151.72-hour Arabic read-speech corpus from 286 speakers aged 7-18, spanning four native dialect groups and 140 L2 speakers from diverse linguistic backgrounds. The authors benchmark pretrained ASR models in zero-shot and fine-tuned settings to quantify gaps for children, adolescents, and L2 speakers.

entry.title: Hierarchical Time-aware Bootstrapping for Off-Policy Subgoal Value Learning

author.name: Bingyun Liu, Yuheng Jing

entry.summary: The paper proposes Hierarchical Time-aware Bootstrapping (HTB), which fixes a bias in HIRO-style off-policy hierarchical RL where value updates target relabeled subgoals rather than the original subgoals. HTB evaluates specified subgoals under the current low-level policy using remaining execution time to enable off-policy Bellman updates.

entry.title: When the Cross-Silo Federation Goes Offline: Continual Learning for Site Onboarding with Limited Unlabeled Data

author.name: Ahmadreza Eslaminia, Klara Nahrstedt, Chenhui Shao

entry.summary: The paper presents an autonomous three-stage procedure for onboarding a new site to a cross-silo federated model after original participants have gone offline, handling unlabeled data that mixes known and novel conditions. It addresses realistic deployment failures of standard federated setups that fix sites and classes in advance.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Time-Series Inference of Lindblad Dynamics in Open Quantum Systems

author.name: Julian Guam, Jianqing Liu

entry.summary: The authors train raw time-series Transformers to infer unknown, potentially time-dependent dissipation rates in Lindblad master equation dynamics, removing the hand-crafted feature engineering of prior work. This enables learning-based system identification for open quantum systems where analytical inversion is intractable.

entry.title: Protocol-Sensitive Evaluation of Log Anomaly Detection: Component Costs and Target-Access Sensitivity on HDFS and BGL

author.name: Hang Xiao, Janet Sung, Zhaoyi Li, Gangzhen Qian, Chuhong Xu

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that evaluation protocol choices — split construction, representation visibility, parser choice — flip conclusions in log anomaly detection benchmarks on HDFS and BGL, with random splits inflating scores near the average-precision ceiling versus group-disjoint and chronological splits. It quantifies component costs and target-access sensitivity across six fixed detector configurations.

entry.title: UltraDub: Towards Authentic Dubbing by Unifying Visually-Steered Flow Learning and Trajectory Guidance

author.name: Gaoxiang Cong, Liang Li, Jianwei Wen, Zhedong Zhang, Zheng-Jun Zha, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: UltraDub is a visual voice cloning framework for authentic video dubbing that uses vision both as continuous motion context and as structural rhythm guidance to maintain lip synchronization and speaker consistency. It introduces a Motion-guided Dual-context Retrieving module that recalibrates linguistic and speaker-style retrieval throughout generation. This addresses known failure modes where conditioning degrades temporal and speaker cues.

entry.title: Parallelism or Concession? Concurrency-Aware Procurement Negotiation for Agentic Commerce

author.name: Xiaolin Xu, Donghao Zhu

entry.summary: The paper models a one-unit procurement negotiation problem where an agentic buyer can fork negotiations across many parallel seller threads, jointly choosing thread count and a price cap under a hard deadline. The authors derive structural results including geometric decay of marginal negotiator value and conditions for optimal concurrency, balancing acceptance curves, per-thread costs, and cancellation risk. This provides an economic theory backbone for agentic commerce systems.

entry.title: Machine learning for journal entry testing: A type-aware evaluation of anomaly detectors under a review budget

author.name: Jan Gronewald, Michel Scherer, Nijat Mehdiyev

entry.summary: The paper proposes a type-aware evaluation protocol for journal entry anomaly detection in auditing, combining per-type recall, fair-share type recall, type coverage, and first-hit rank under realistic review budgets. It evaluates nine unsupervised detectors, a supervised reference, and feedback-driven DeepSAD on four real client ledgers with injected typed anomalies. It shows standard population-level metrics obscure which anomaly types auditors actually find.

entry.title: SoK: Semantic Decision Engines in Network Control Loops

author.name: Delong Li, Chen Li, Xu Wang, Haochen Gong, Rui Lang, Guangsheng Yu

entry.summary: This systematization of knowledge classifies 139 paper families of semantic decision engines by decision interface, execution path, and check ownership, revealing that claims of control-loop or real-time fit are rarely backed by matched measurement and that deadline attainment is almost never reported. Bounded tests show these gaps can reverse admission verdicts under realistic event models.

entry.title: ARO: Aligned Representation learning for multi-Omics data

author.name: Amogh Singh, Yash Shah, Chiara D'Ercoli, Arash Mehrjou, Patrick Schwab, Timothy Jones, Pietro Li\`{o}

entry.summary: ARO learns representations from multi-omics cancer data that support reconstruction of missing and unpaired modalities, prioritizing practical applicability in incomplete-data settings over scaling up foundation models. It achieves low reconstruction error and its latent embeddings enable downstream biological reasoning.

entry.title: A Physics-Guided Transformer Framework for Electromigration Analysis in Multi-Segment Interconnects

author.name: Pavlos Stoikos, Anuj Pathania, George Floros

entry.summary: A physics-guided transformer converts interconnect lines into geometry- and DC-aware segment tokens, uses attention for line-level context, and a query decoder predicts electromigration stress at selected locations and times, trained with physics-informed objectives. It offers fast alternatives to expensive physics-based solvers for chip reliability analysis.

entry.title: Frozen Factor or Spectral Band? Disentangling Two Choices in Low-Rank LoRA

author.name: Adnan Slimane Ali, Ayoub Belfatmi, David Ngwe Pouth

entry.summary: This work disentangles two confounded design choices in spectral LoRA variants: which singular subspace to adapt and which factor to freeze. By systematically comparing freezing input factor A versus output factor B on top or bottom singular directions, it finds that freezing A on the same band consistently outperforms, and freezing B trails comparable-budget free LoRA by 8-18 percentage points. The findings offer practical guidance for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

entry.title: An Information-Theoretic Evaluation Framework for Benchmark and Model Diagnosis in Knowledge Tracing

author.name: Houru Jiang, Zixi Wang, Tengteng Cheng, Xueyi Li, Mingliang Hou, Jiaqi Zheng, Renqiang Luo, Teng Guo, Zitao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes an information-theoretic framework for diagnosing knowledge tracing benchmarks, using Context Tree Weighting on item-response histories as an operational causal uncertainty coordinate and distinguishing it from the unobserved Local Irreducible Uncertainty. This enables identifying where residual model errors originate and whether benchmarks are approaching saturation, going beyond aggregate AUC/accuracy.

entry.title: Can LLM-assisted regularization increase forecast accuracy for migration flows in low data regimes?

author.name: Nathaniel T. Hindman, Fabricio Murai

entry.summary: Investigates using LLM pipelines to extract migration push-pull signals from news articles and inject them into a weighted Lasso migration forecasting model through feature-specific regularization penalties. The work tests whether unstructured contextual signals can improve gravity-based flow forecasting in low-data regimes.

entry.title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty

author.name: Tomas Kaljevic, Ivan Arzola, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: This benchmark compares four trained-from-scratch models and four time series foundation models on short-term load forecasting across three real-world power grid datasets under varying future-covariate availability and quality. It finds Chronos-2 achieves state-of-the-art performance in both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings when future information is available. The work offers practical guidance for deploying foundation models in energy operations.

entry.title: Active Feature Acquisition for Cost-Efficient Temporal Prediction with Reduced Participant Burden

author.name: Yunni Qu (Department of Computer Science, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill), Bing Cai Kok (Department of Psychology and Neuroscience, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, School of Social Sciences, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Whitney Ringwald (Department of Psychology, University of Minnesota Twin Cities), Grant King (Department of Psychology, University of Michigan), Aidan Wright (Department of Psychology, University of Michigan), Kathleen Gates (Department of Psychology and Neuroscience, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill), Junier Oliva (Department of Computer Science, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill)

entry.summary: This paper applies Longitudinal Active Feature Acquisition (LAFA) to psychological forecasting, learning policies that select dynamic subsets of survey items per acquisition occasion to balance prediction accuracy against participant burden and attrition risk. The interdisciplinary team spans computer science and psychology departments.

entry.title: Complementary Feature Domains: Information Preservation Does Not Imply Predictive-Contribution Preservation

author.name: Timothy Oladunni, Farouk Ganiyu-Adewumi

entry.summary: This theory paper introduces Complementary Feature Domains (CFD), a framework showing that invertible representation transformations can preserve Shannon information while altering the predictive contribution of features under a restricted decision family. It formalizes a contribution defect measuring how contextual contributions change under recoding, with bounded-Lipschitz utility bounds on coalition utility shifts.

entry.title: Neuromotor Hierarchy Network: Physiological Inductive Biases for Robust Generalization in sEMG Decoding

author.name: He Wang, Hongyuan Qi, Zhaoxian Zhang, Jinbin Luo, Linyi He, Mehul Motani, Changsheng Wu

entry.summary: The authors propose the Neuromotor Hierarchy Network, which learns a compact latent neuromotor state via a hierarchy inspired by physiological structure to decode movement from surface electromyography. This addresses cross-user and cross-session variability in population-scale sEMG decoding for wearables and human-computer interaction.

entry.title: Variance-Averse $n$-Step Offline Reinforcement Learning for Sparse Long-Horizon Environments

author.name: Guhyeon Kang, Minhae Kwon

entry.summary: VAN-Flow addresses the problem that generative offline RL policies can reproduce unreliable, high-variance action modes that occasionally yield high returns. It combines a categorical distributional critic with a variance-averse expectation operator and n-step returns to promote consistent actions in sparse, long-horizon environments.

entry.title: Learning a Ranking from Human Feedback in Log-Concave Random Utility Models

author.name: Diego Alovisetti, Marco Mussi, Alberto Maria Metelli

entry.summary: This paper studies sample complexity of recovering rankings from noisy human feedback under full-ranking and winner-only feedback, modeling responses with log-concave random utility models. It derives bounds for epsilon-accurate rankings, a criterion that tolerates ordering errors only among near-utility items.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification Is Indispensable for Reliable Connectome-Based Graph Learning: A Narrative Review and Case Study

author.name: Mansooreh Pakravan

entry.summary: This narrative review surveys uncertainty quantification frameworks for connectome-based graph neural networks, mapping aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty sources across neuroimaging pipelines, and includes a case study showing the dangers of uncalibrated diagnostic predictions. It argues UQ is essential but underused in connectomic graph learning. The paper is a useful synthesis for a specialized clinical-ML community.

entry.title: From Shared Demand Patterns to Local Uncertainty: Probabilistic Load Forecasting by Mixing Compact Adaptations

author.name: Haoran Li, Zhe Cheng, Yang Weng

entry.summary: The authors propose a scalable customer-aware probabilistic load forecasting framework that shares a common model for demand patterns while adapting only a compact parameter subset per customer or transformer. This addresses the scalability trade-off between a single shared model that misses heterogeneous local patterns and many separate local models that are costly to maintain.

entry.title: Probabilistic Counterfactual Inference for Discrete Outcomes in Gaussian-Process Causal Models

author.name: Juliette Sinnott, Amir-Hossein Karimi, Mohammad Kohandel

entry.summary: The paper extends counterfactual inference in Gaussian-process structural causal models to discrete variables by pairing GP predictors with explicit exogenous noise mechanisms, deriving exact noise-abduction procedures for binary (uniform threshold), nominal (Gumbel-max), and ordinal (latent Gaussian cut-point) outcomes. Uncertainty is propagated through interventions while accounting for posterior noise variability.

entry.title: Statistical Turbulence and High-Fidelity Disturbance Fields for Quadrotor Flight Control

author.name: Xun Huang

entry.summary: This paper systematically quantifies how wind-field fidelity, not just magnitude, affects the robustness of reinforcement-learning quadrotor controllers by comparing five disturbance-fidelity levels from simple gusts to large-eddy-simulation fields in a full cross-fidelity train-test matrix with PPO agents and classical PID and SE(3) baselines. All synthetic disturbance generators are validated before controller comparison.

entry.title: Principles that Guide, Actions that Inform: Agent Evolution via Knowledge Abstraction

author.name: Bowen Ye, Yongchao Xu, Junkai Ma, Xiang Yin, Wenzhao Li

entry.summary: The paper addresses continual improvement of LLM agents without parameter access by transforming concrete task interactions into abstract, transferable principles stored in external memory. It argues existing experience-based memory methods keep knowledge too tightly coupled to specific tasks, limiting generalization to new contexts.

entry.title: ImpactMat: Continuous Material Estimation for Inverse Impact Sound Rendering

author.name: Hyebin Cho, Bumsoo Kim, Joon son Chung

entry.summary: Proposes inverse impact sound rendering: predicting continuous material parameters from a reference impact sound so a simulator can recreate the material response. The paper contributes a benchmark dataset of single and blended material impact sounds with ground-truth parameters and a feed-forward prediction model.

entry.title: Bayesian Optimization on Function Spaces via Sparse RKHS Manifolds

author.name: Davide Sartor, Meghan E. Huber, Donghyun Kim, Nathan Wycoff

entry.summary: The paper introduces L0 Manifold Optimization (L0MO) for Functional Bayesian Optimization, searching over the subset of an RKHS consisting of functions with sparse kernel representations while optimizing both kernel locations and coefficients. This extends BO from finite-dimensional vector inputs to inherently functional design variables.

entry.title: Deep Defence on Wheels: A Dual Intrusion Detection System Architecture for Comprehensive In-Vehicle Network Security

author.name: Shashwat Khandelwal, Shanker Shreejith

entry.summary: The paper proposes a dual intrusion detection system for in-vehicle CAN networks combining supervised and unsupervised learning models optimized for real-time deployment under automotive constraints, processing roughly 2,000 CAN frames per second with low latency and minimal ECU overhead. It balances detection accuracy for known and unknown attacks with embedded deployment constraints.

entry.title: CETUS: How Far Do Representations Trained on Earth Transfer to Cassini SAR of Titan?

author.name: Kevin Lee

entry.summary: CETUS benchmarks transfer of Earth-trained vision representations (DINOv2, DOFA, CROMA) to Cassini SAR terrain classification of Titan, comparing against classical image features and an untrained ViT using the USGS Cassini SAR mosaic and expert geomorphological labels.
