entry.summary: This paper empirically tests whether an LLM acting as an integration layer above specialized diagnostic tools actually outperforms the best standalone tool across five industrial fault diagnosis datasets (bearing vibration, process monitoring, semiconductor equipment). It finds that conflicting external information can overturn initially correct LLM judgments and that implicit LLM integration never consistently beats the stronger standalone source, confirmed on a pre-registered Tennessee Eastman test. The result is a caution against assuming LLM orchestration automatically adds value over specialized components.

entry.title: From Traces to Agentic Worlds: Agentic Language World Models for Interactive Environment Simulation

author.name: Quanyu Long, Xiao Chen, Jianda Chen, Haozhen Zhang, Qisheng Hu, Jianzhu Bao, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: Trace2Env is a learning-free framework that reconstructs historical interaction traces into a reusable environment worldbook, allowing a world-model agent to simulate a stateful environment for training and evaluating LLM agents when the original system is inaccessible. This agentic language world modeling paradigm supports faithful simulation without rebuilding executable environments. It addresses a real bottleneck in agent development and evaluation.

entry.title: The Same Zero: Why Identical ASR Can Imply Different Guarantees in LLM-Agent Security

author.name: YaJie Yin

entry.summary: The paper applies a Verification Autonomy Levels (VAL) taxonomy - from LLM self-declaration to impossible completeness - to 22 agent-security defenses, providing a falsifiable framework for what a defense actually guarantees. It also runs a controlled budget-matched comparison showing a VAL-guided stack outperforms a mainstream intuition stack across 50 scenarios and 12 attack variants.

entry.title: ASD-FEAT: A Multi-Modal Infant Video-Derived Dataset for Early ASD Risk Prediction

author.name: Sidrah Liaqat (University of Kentucky), Halil Helvaci (University of Kentucky), Sen-Ching Cheung (University of Kentucky), Chongruo Wu (University of California Davis), Dongjie Chen (University of California Davis), Chen Nee Chuah (University of California Davis), Sally Ozonoff (MIND Institute, University of California Davis)

entry.summary: ASD-FEAT is a multimodal dataset from infant-adult interaction videos with longitudinal coverage through 36 months, clinically validated developmental outcomes, expert frame-level behavioral annotations, and privacy-conscious feature representations. It uniquely combines these characteristics at scale for early autism spectrum disorder risk prediction.

entry.title: Trust the View That Sees the Target: Mining Cross-View Conflicts for Reliability-Gated Disaster Damage Assessment

author.name: Yifan Yang

entry.summary: This paper studies failure cases in multi-view building damage assessment where overhead imagery and ground-level photos disagree, mining conflict samples from wildfire and hurricane datasets where they comprise 10-33% of data. It shows an oracle that trusts the correct view dramatically outperforms symmetric fusion methods, motivating reliability-gated fusion rather than equal-weighting both views.

entry.title: Super-Resolution in The Right Latent Space: A Frozen Vision-Foundation Substrate

author.name: Wanzhou Lei, Cuifeng Sheng, Yanjin He, Maohua Li, Hua Yuan, Per-Olof Persson, Hanlin Tang

entry.summary: This paper argues that real-world super-resolution should be performed in the latent space of a frozen vision-foundation model rather than in reconstruction-oriented latent spaces or pixel space, since degraded images land far from the manifold of sharp natural images in those substrates. The authors propose mapping degraded embeddings back onto the image manifold while preserving semantics and pixel detail. The reframing could make SR simpler and cheaper if the foundation-model latent space proves to be a better substrate.

entry.title: Triggering Generalist Reasoning via Predictive Uncertainty for Dual-System VLA

author.name: Hyemin Yang, Wooseong Jeong, Giwon Lee, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: TUD is an adaptive inference framework for dual-system vision-language-action models that selectively skips slow generalist calls by measuring cross-step dispersion of action re-predictions under the cached generalist context as an uncertainty signal. This replaces fixed-frequency invocation, saving computation in easy phases while reacting faster to unexpected scene changes. The approach improves the efficiency of fast-slow robot control architectures.

entry.title: SemCam: Semantic Camera Motion Control for Video Generation

author.name: Janna Bruner, Omer Talmi, Ianir Ideses, Lior Fritz, Lior Wolf, Sagie Benaim

entry.summary: This paper introduces semantic camera motion control, a new video-to-video task where a reference video plus a target motion label (e.g., maintain frontal view of a subject) defines the desired subject-relative camera behavior without an explicit trajectory. The proposed SemCam method learns to realize these dynamic camera-subject relationships while preserving video content. This matters because it enables more intuitive, intent-level control of virtual cameras in generated or edited video.

entry.title: A Spatiotemporal Semantic Importance-Guided Unified Compression and Editing Framework for AI-Generated Videos

author.name: Xihua Sheng, Dong Liu, Chang Wen Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a compression framework tailored to AI-generated videos that preserves semantically important spatiotemporal information while allowing regenerable textures to be discarded, unified with prompt-based editing that maintains content consistency. This reframes codec design for generative content, where reconstruction fidelity to a specific sample matters less than semantic preservation.

entry.title: Bayesian Optimization in Sequence-to-Architecture Latent Space for Zero-Shot NAS

author.name: Ondrej Tybl, Lukas Neumann

entry.summary: The paper brings Bayesian optimization to zero-shot neural architecture search for large-scale networks by learning a VAE latent space over a novel prefix encoding of architectures. This replaces near-random evolutionary mutation with a principled, model-based search while avoiding the prohibitive cost of traditional NAS.

entry.title: Lens3D: Target-Conditioned Visual Foveation for Fine-Grained 3D Understanding

author.name: Junming Huang, Zini Chen, Shuaiying Hou, Chi Wang, Qiang Dai, Weiwei Xu

entry.summary: Lens3D improves fine-grained 3D object understanding through a foveation pipeline (LensUnd) that selects informative views for an external 2D VLM via 3D localization, and a distillation path (LensDistill) that transfers the knowledge into 3D LLMs without runtime VLM calls. It also contributes a held-out benchmark, LensBench.

entry.title: ChronoWorld: Camera-Controlled Consistent 4D World Generation via Spatiotemporal Cues and Geometric Reflections

author.name: Xiaoyu Zhou, Dingwei Xian, Zhenyu Wang, Yajiao Xiong, Yongtao Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: ChronoWorld proposes an Observation-State-Reflection framework for camera-controllable 4D scene generation that maintains spatiotemporal coherence. It introduces Spatiotemporal Epipolar Causal Attention to enforce multi-view constraints and a reconstruction-driven geometric reflection pipeline for self-correction of generated content.

entry.title: TACET: Context-Appropriate Acoustic-Social Navigation for Quadrupeds

author.name: Sungsan Park, Young-Sik Shin, Sanghyun Kim

entry.summary: TACET enables quadruped robots to modulate both walking path and locomotion noise based on inferred social context, using a slow fine-tuned vision-language reasoner coupled to a fast reactive controller through a compact behavior token. This addresses an overlooked social dimension of legged robot deployment in hospitals, care homes, and offices where footstep noise matters.

entry.title: Test-Time Training as Residual Memory for Robot Policies

author.name: Haoxuan Wang, Gengyu Zhang, Ramana Rao Kompella, Gaowen Liu, Yan Yan

entry.summary: Reframes test-time training as a residual memory mechanism for long-horizon robot manipulation, explicitly distinguishing information recoverable from the current context from information that must persist beyond it. This selective persistence makes memory-augmented policies more scalable than full-history storage or indiscriminate TTT compression.

entry.title: When to Switch: Reliable Action-Chunk Extension for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Seonghoon Yu, Dongwon Kim, HyungRok Jung, Yoonjae Baek, Byung-kwan Lee, Suha Kwak, Jeany Son

entry.summary: Analyzing error patterns in vision-language-action models, the paper finds that errors in long action chunks concentrate at transitions between manipulation subskills and grow with chunk length. Motivated by this, it introduces a mechanism for predicting transition timing to enable reliable action-chunk extension, reducing stop-and-go execution and speeding task completion.

entry.title: Beyond LLM Serving: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Workloads for Embodied AI System Design

author.name: Seonghun Jung, Sieun Moon, Jiyoung Jeong, Jimin Lee, Jaehyuk Huh

entry.summary: This systems paper characterizes the runtime behavior of four representative vision-language-action models under batch-1, deadline-constrained control settings, profiling on an edge GPU server and two onboard SoCs with single-inference profiling plus 43,200 closed-loop runs. It shows VLA workloads mix vision-language, autoregressive, and diffusion-style components whose behavior departs from LLM serving design points, informing embodied AI hardware and system design. Inference overruns translate directly into stale observations and reduced task success.

entry.title: Decoding-time Realignment of Language Models

author.name: Tianlin Liu, Shangmin Guo, Leonardo Bianco, Daniele Calandriello, Quentin Berthet, Felipe Llinares, Jessica Hoffmann, Lucas Dixon, Michal Valko, Mathieu Blondel

entry.summary: This paper proposes adjusting the regularization level of aligned language models at decoding time, avoiding the need to retrain multiple models at different RLHF regularization strengths. This is critical because too little regularization causes reward hacking while too much hinders alignment. The method substantially reduces the cost of tuning the alignment-capability trade-off in LLMs.

entry.title: Understanding the performance gap between online and offline alignment algorithms

author.name: Yunhao Tang, Daniel Zhaohan Guo, Zeyu Zheng, Daniele Calandriello, Yuan Cao, Eugene Tarassov, R\'emi Munos, Bernardo \'Avila Pires, Michal Valko, Yong Cheng, Will Dabney

entry.summary: This empirical study investigates why online RLHF methods outperform offline alignment algorithms such as DPO, using reward over-optimization experiments and careful ablations. It shows that offline data coverage and quality alone cannot explain the gap, and finds offline algorithms optimize the policy differently than expected. This is an important diagnostic for alignment methodology choices.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Comparative Evidence for Social Intelligence

author.name: Keane Ong, Yuriel Ryan, Sabri Boughorbel, Vladimir Necula, Jack Wei Lun Shi, Rui Mao, Roy Ka-Wei Lee, Adriel Kuek, Nancy F. Chen, Erik Cambria, Gianmarco Mengaldo, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: RLCE is a reinforcement learning method that trains social understanding models from unlabeled data by using comparative evidence among plausible interpretations of ambiguous social signals like affect, intent, and preference, bypassing the need for verification oracles. It addresses the dependence of social AI on costly human annotation.

entry.title: MOIRA: Mass-Oriented Indexing with Ragged Attention for Long-Context Decoding

author.name: Dich Nhat Minh Nguyen, Tran Dang Duong Nguyen

entry.summary: MOIRA improves long-context LLM decoding by using adaptive per-head, per-layer KV-cache page budgets with mass-oriented indexing and a ragged attention kernel, since fixed sparse-attention budgets waste memory bandwidth and existing kernels like FlashAttention-3 handle ragged page lists poorly. The system-level design avoids the padding and load-imbalance losses of prior sparse decoding. This targets the memory-bandwidth bottleneck of long-context inference.

entry.title: When Debate Helps: Proposal Supply and Verification-Aware Readout in Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Zihao Zhao, Tunyu Zhang, Haizhou Shi, Yusong Zhao, Xinxi Zhang, Hao Wang

entry.summary: The paper argues multi-agent debate fails to beat majority voting when two mechanisms are conflated: proposal supply (a correct answer must be surfaced) and readout (the correct answer must be identified). It formalizes recoverable headroom, introduces Latent Verification Debate where proposals receive answer-specific verification evidence, and uses controlled interventions to show correct evidence shifts answer selection.

entry.title: SpecFold: Folding Multi-Branch Redundancy for Faster Speculative Decoding in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Chung-En Ho (Celine), Weiyu Sun (Celine), Cheng-Jhih Shih (Celine), He Li (Celine), Yong Liu (Celine), Yingyan (Celine), Lin

entry.summary: SpecFold accelerates diffusion language models by exploiting multi-branch computational redundancy within speculative verification steps, where draft branches inherit most tokens from parents so hidden states remain highly similar across branches. It is an algorithm-system co-design that folds this redundancy to reduce the cost of verifying multiple draft branches in one forward pass.

entry.title: Do Time-Series QA Systems Read the Time Series? Evidence Use and Reasoning Reliability

author.name: Zhuomin Chen, Jingchao Ni, Xu Zheng, Janki Bhimani, Mo Sha, Wei Cheng, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: This evaluation study probes whether time-series QA systems actually rely on the supplied numerical series, reproducing results for four systems (TimeOmni-1, ChatTS, TimeOmni-VL, Time-MQA) and testing sensitivity to input changes and grounding of numerical claims in rationales. The work exposes reliability gaps between answer accuracy and genuine evidence use.

entry.title: DPNL: A DPLL-based Algorithm for Probabilistic Neurosymbolic Learning

author.name: Thomas Jean-Michel Valentin (ENS Paris Saclay, TYREX), Pierre Genev{\`e}s (LIG, TYREX), Luisa Sophie Werner (LIG, TYREX), Sarah Chlyah (TYREX), Nabil Laya{\"i}da (TYREX), Nils Gesbert (Grenoble INP ENSIMAG, TYREX)

entry.summary: DPNL is an oracle-guided framework for probabilistic neurosymbolic learning that avoids materializing the complete logical provenance of a query, lazily exploring intermediate assignments while oracles certify whole regions that produce or exclude the target output. The authors establish conditions under which the approach is sound and improve on the provenance-materialization bottleneck of state-of-the-art PNL methods.

entry.title: Mind the Execution Gap: Action-Semantic Mismatch in World-Model Control

author.name: Shengtao Wen, Xiang Chen, Yu Tian, Lingbing Guo, Lina Gong, Sheng-Jun Huang

entry.summary: The paper studies how asynchronous execution (delay, packet loss, reordering, actuator buffering) changes the action semantics assumed by world-model controllers, identifying architecture-dependent failure modes: TD-MPC2 suffers from imagined-versus-executed timeline mismatch while DreamerV3 misattributes observed transitions to unapplied commands. It reframes asynchrony as a semantic problem, not merely a disturbance.

entry.title: Distribution Matching Evolutionary Algorithms for Rare Event Sampling

author.name: Yonatan Gideoni, Yarin Gal

entry.summary: The paper interprets evolutionary algorithms as approximate Markov Chain Monte Carlo and derives distribution-matching objectives for rare-event discovery, where a discovery is both surprising (low generation probability) and useful (high reward). This avoids expensive weight updates and works with closed-source models, addressing a limitation of gradient-based global optimization.

entry.title: XTurnix: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Turn Control through Two-State Binary Decisions

author.name: Zhanxun Liu, Yifan Duan, Hengtao Wu, Chen Yang, Qinyuan Cheng, Kun Wang, Xingyu Zeng, Xipeng Qiu, Chaochao Lu, Xie Chen

entry.summary: XTurnix is a compact text-based model for unified turn-taking control in real-time dialogue, formulating it as two binary decisions conditioned on the AI's listening or speaking state, predicted from complete dialogue history. It is pretrained on 5.5 million causal action examples derived automatically from time-stamped data, avoiding task-specific label spaces of prior turn detectors.

entry.title: ConEx: Human-Interpretable Saliency Maps via Concept-Aware Attribution

author.name: Yehonatan Elisha, Oren Barkan, Ziv Weiss Haddad, Noam Koenigstein

entry.summary: ConEx bridges saliency visualization and concept-based explanations by automatically discovering class-specific concepts as concept activation vectors learned without manual supervision, using a masking mechanism to improve concept purity. It generates saliency maps that show where each concept applies, aiming for both faithfulness and interpretability.

entry.title: Enhancing Long-Video VLM Embeddings with Query-Aware Streaming Latent Reasoning

author.name: Haozhe Chi, Song Jin, Yang Jin, Yadong Mu

entry.summary: QASLR is a post-training framework for long-video embedding that accumulates evidence across clips under a fixed visual-token budget, selecting frames, restoring temporal order, and processing clips sequentially with persistent think tokens and an embed token that reads out normalized representations. This captures sparse query-relevant events in videos spanning minutes or hours without blowing up memory.

entry.title: VAMPS: Visual and Motor Policies from Sampling-Based Planning

author.name: Mohamed Yassine Kabouri, Pietro Noah Crestaz, Quang-Nam Nguyen, Qilong Cheng, Ludovic Righetti, Nicolas Mansard

entry.summary: VAMPS uses MPPI sampling-based control to train reusable robot policies without human demonstrations, supporting iterative simulation training where the policy warm-starts MPPI and refined trajectories provide fresh supervision. It combines a learned terminal value for short-horizon planning with an Implicit Q-Learning critic guiding policy updates, and iterative refinement outperforms training on frozen MPPI data.

entry.title: Transfer-Stratified On-Policy Distillation for RL-Improved Reasoning Teachers

author.name: Xiaoyu Chen, Bo Shao, Tiangang Zhu, Bintao Wu, Linjun Shou, Fengge Wu, Feng Sun, Wenbiao Ding

entry.summary: The paper studies which reasoning improvements from RL-trained teachers actually transfer to smaller students under on-policy distillation, finding that transfer is structured and metric-dependent rather than scalar. It proposes Transfer-Stratified On-Policy Distillation (TS-OPD), which screens training problems by joint student-teacher sampled success to route data appropriately. Results inform when RL investment in teachers benefits distilled students.

entry.title: SO(3)-RoPE for Spherical Transformers

author.name: Christian Libner, Chase van de Geijn, Alexander S. Ecker, Maurice Weiler

entry.summary: The paper introduces SO(3)-RoPE, a relative positional embedding that incorporates spherical geometry into transformer attention via unitary SO(3) representations, remaining equivariant and compatible with FlashAttention. On shallow water dynamics over a rotating sphere, the resulting SO3ViT outperforms an S2 transformer baseline with lower error and reduced runtime. It elegantly connects rotational equivariance with efficient attention.

entry.title: GAMBIT: Learning to Plan Continuous Multi-Robot Trajectories

author.name: Rishabh Jain, Akmaral Moldagalieva, Lorenzo Magnino, Michael Amir, Keisuke Okumura, Ajay Shankar, Wolfgang H\"onig, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: GAMBIT learns coordinated motion-primitive selection for multi-robot trajectory planning with double-integrator continuous dynamics, capturing self-sacrificial team behaviors that manual heuristics miss. It trains via imitation learning and then fine-tunes the policy for overall team performance in dense, interaction-rich environments. The work comes from a recognized multi-robot planning group (Prorok, Honig, Okumura).

entry.title: Odyssey: A Closed-Loop Benchmark for Long-Horizon Real-World Driving with Explicit Navigation Routes

author.name: Jungho Kim, Hongjae Shin, Seunghoon Yu, Heecheol Yoo, Myeongjun Kim, Jiyong Oh, Donghyuk Kwak, Seunghyeop Nam, Haesung Oh, Hyunju Kim, Hyungchan Cho, Jaehyun Park, Soo Won Seo, Jun Won Choi

entry.summary: Odyssey is a closed-loop benchmark of 100 long-horizon driving scenarios reconstructed from 100-second nuPlan logs, replacing ambiguous directional commands with explicit SD-map routes to disambiguate navigation goals. It enables evaluation of how early decisions affect subsequent driving, addressing a key gap in end-to-end autonomous driving evaluation.

entry.title: Differentially Private Mixing of Public Datasets Improves Private Learning

author.name: Yufei Chen, Tejumade Afonja, Anvith Thudi, Nicolas Papernot

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first pipeline that privately learns a mixture over several public datasets to pretrain on before DP finetuning on sensitive data, keying on the insight that the best mixture can be found via a privately learned low-dimensional linear model. Tests on NIH chest X-ray data and other tasks show improved utility over single-dataset selection. This reduces the utility cost of differential privacy in a principled way.

entry.title: Integrated Imputation-Classification for Supervised Learning with Missing Data

author.name: Yue Liu, Ben Liang, Ali Tizghadam, Ilijc Albanese

entry.summary: IICN jointly trains an imputer and an (n+1)-class discriminator adversarially under a single supervised objective, where the discriminator distinguishes true classes from an additional imputed class. It proves that at the global optimum the pair implements marginalization over missing coordinates and yields a Bayes-optimal classifier. A principled alternative to decoupled impute-then-predict pipelines.

entry.title: Asymptotically Optimal Best Arm Identification with Fixed-Budget under Differential Privacy

author.name: Keqin Chen, Jie Bian, Yulian Wu, Vincent Y. F. Tan

entry.summary: The paper studies fixed-budget best arm identification in bandits under pure epsilon-differential privacy protecting the full transcript, proving the optimal error decay is governed by an instance-dependent privacy-aware transportation exponent distinct from the fixed-confidence analogue. Guided by this exponent, it proposes AO-Pri-BAI, an adaptive algorithm with asymptotic optimality guarantees. This resolves a theory gap at the intersection of bandits and privacy.

entry.title: From Pixels, Without Pre-training: Joint Generative and Self-Supervised Representation Learning in One Model

author.name: Vicente Balmaseda, Ching-Long Lin, Tianbao Yang

entry.summary: Studies joint generative and self-supervised representation learning in a single model, enabling self-conditioned image generation from pixels without labels, pretrained encoders, or autoencoders. The work tackles the objective mismatch between contrastive learning (invariant, coarse semantics on clean views) and flow matching (fine detail on noisy inputs).

entry.title: Training-Free Transformer Merging via Sequential Local Operator Alignment

author.name: Akansh Maurya, Ya-Wei Eileen Lin, Stefanie Jegelka, Sebastian U Stich, Rotem Mulayoff

entry.summary: This paper identifies that layer-wise merging of transformers ignores the composed-matrix structure of query-key and value-output operators and that downstream activations drift as earlier layers are merged. The proposed Sequential Local Operator Alignment method merges transformers along the execution path of the partially merged model using calibration data, without any further training. This improves training-free model merging quality.

entry.title: Representation-Aligned Auxiliary Supervision for Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Kyuyoung Kim, Peiyao Sheng, Ashwin Hebbar, Peiyang Xu, Yunfei Xie, Kevin Wang, Rui Xin, Chen Wei, Zhangyang Wang, Jinwoo Shin, Pramod Viswanath, Sewoong Oh

entry.summary: Using chess as a controlled testbed with symbolic (FEN) and spatial (ASCII) state representations, the authors identify representation compatibility as a key factor in adapting language models to structured domains. They show models process semantically equivalent inputs very differently, affecting learning and generalization, and propose representation-aligned auxiliary supervision to improve adaptation. The framework may transfer to other structured domains such as code and math.

entry.title: DV-Lens: Revealing the Functional Organization of Language Model Parameters

author.name: Chenhang Cui, Jian Yu, Shuyi Miao, Xiaohao Liu, Rui Huang, Fei Shen, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Introduces the downstream vocabulary lens (DV-Lens), a parameter-level interpretability framework linking native parameter directions in Q/K/V/O projections and FFNs to their downstream vocabulary responses via module-specific Jacobians. This connects parameters across modules to verifiable output effects and enables studying how functional organization relates to model capability. A novel mechanistic-interpretability tool operating at the parameter rather than neuron or circuit level.

entry.title: TrajLong: Co-Designing Agentic and Long-Context Supervision for Mid-Training

author.name: Miao Peng, Qintong Zhang, Nuo Chen, Yuhan Li, Guochen Yan, Xinran Gu, Hongqiu Wu, Hai Wang, Lydell Huang, Wentao Zhang, Jia Li

entry.summary: TrajLong compiles agent trajectories into long-context mid-training tasks with dense supervision targeting atomic capabilities like evidence grounding, cross-evidence aggregation, and related skills needed by coding and search agents. It systematically studies how to organize trajectory information into effective supervision rather than just dumping trajectories into training. Addresses a timely gap at the intersection of agent training and long-context learning.

entry.title: Towards Unbiased On-Policy Distillation for Block Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zaiquan Yang, Fei Wei, Yong Wang, Yudong Han, Yiyu Li, Zhuofan Zong, Gerhard Petrus Hancke, Xiangxiang Chu, Rynson WH Lau

entry.summary: This work studies on-policy distillation for block diffusion language models (BDLMs) with larger block sizes, revealing two optimization biases that cause training instability: context misalignment from mismatched teacher-student block boundaries, and an intrinsic bias where the student drifts toward convenient outputs. By identifying and correcting these biases, the paper extends a promising post-training paradigm to a regime (larger blocks) previously underexplored. It is relevant to the emerging diffusion-LM line of research.

entry.title: Shared Stopping Decisions Change Answers in HQQ Cache Quantization

author.name: Seunghui Jwa, Minsu Oh, Chanjun Park, Yeo-Chan Yoon

entry.summary: This paper reveals a determinism violation in batched inference with Half-Quadratic Quantization of the KV cache: a shared average-error stopping criterion means swapping an unrelated batched question changes a target question's four-bit answer in 170/384 comparisons, and replaying the other execution's update counts reproduces its answer exactly. It identifies and characterizes cross-request interference in quantized batched serving. This has implications for reproducibility and silent behavioral variation in production systems.

entry.title: Test-Time Adaptation of Reasoning Strategies with Bayesian Nonparametric Memory

author.name: Keshav Ramji, Tahira Naseem, Ram\'on Fernandez Astudillo

entry.summary: The paper introduces an HDP-Gaussian Mixture Model over behavior embeddings that maintains a growing, clustered cheatsheet of reasoning strategies, retrieved and updated at inference time as new insights emerge from self-reflection. This provides a principled Bayesian nonparametric mechanism for carrying forward test-time discoveries across problems. It aims to cut generation cost from suboptimal reasoning paths.

entry.title: When and What to Prune? Stage-Aware Visual Token Pruning for Efficient VLA

author.name: Tianjun Shi, Haotian Xiong, Ziyu Gong, Qi Lu, Li Li

entry.summary: This paper targets visual token pruning for vision-language-action (VLA) robot models, arguing that fixed pruning schedules are risky because tokens unimportant in early layers may become critical for action prediction later. It proposes stage-aware pruning that adapts both when and which tokens are pruned across layers. Efficient VLA inference is important for real-time robot control with limited compute.

entry.title: SPIN: Image Immunization Against Diffusion Editing via Single-Step Projection in Stochastic Neighborhoods

author.name: Fengming Gu, Jie Zhang, Zhongqi Wang, Qiankun Li, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: SPIN adds imperceptible perturbations to images to disrupt subsequent diffusion-based editing, using single-step projection in stochastic neighborhoods to avoid costly full-trajectory backpropagation while maintaining protection across unseen editing instructions. It addresses the risk of unauthorized image manipulation.

entry.title: ForeAct3D: Policy-Grounded Future World Modeling for VLA Policies

author.name: Zhe Tao, Feiran Wang, Gaowen Liu, Ramana Rao Kompella$, Yan Yan

entry.summary: ForeAct3D introduces policy-grounded future world modeling for VLA policies, decoding depth, segmentation, and camera pose into current and future semantic 3D scene states via learnable geometric queries. Crucially, future queries are conditioned on the policy's action chunks, coupling the forecast to the actions actually to be executed.

entry.title: DreamFormer: Dream Imitation with a Transformer World Model for Language-Conditioned Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Mostafa Kotb, Cornelius Weber, Muhammad Burhan Hafez, Stefan Wermter

entry.summary: DreamFormer is a model-based agent that learns a task-agnostic Transformer world model from unstructured play data, then acquires language-conditioned multi-task skills by optimizing an intrinsic reward aligning imagined rollouts with expert demonstrations in latent space. Training on-policy inside imagination mitigates offline behavioral cloning's covariate shift while compressing multi-view observations for affordable long-horizon imagination.

entry.title: $R^2$-WAM: Repair-and-Reject Post-Training for World Action Models

author.name: Ruiyan Xu, Haisheng Su, Sixu Lin, Zhaokun Yue, Chengming Hu, Xin Jin, Guiliang Liu

entry.summary: R2-WAM is a two-stage post-training framework for world action models: a repair stage aligns predicted video futures with input actions via a kinematic alignment score, then a reject stage uses repaired predictions to identify and negatively fine-tune on inferior action samples. This addresses the problem of visually plausible but action-inconsistent predictions misleading policy refinement.

entry.title: Teaching Agents to Code Reliably

author.name: Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Myeongsoo Kim, Kangrui Ruan, Shweta Garg, Varun Kumar, Murali Krishna Ramanathan

entry.summary: The paper argues that three behaviors limit autonomous coding agents: narrow location diversity, unexploited edit-method diversity, and self-deceptive verification where agent-written tests accept incorrect patches. It proposes teaching these behaviors into the policy itself rather than relying on external scaffolds and extra inference compute.

entry.title: Spec2Game: Can LLMs Generate Complete Playable Games from Detailed Specifications?

author.name: Yixue Cai, Yuzhe Zhao, Hanxiang Chao, Qingsen Ma, Ziheng Xiong, Jinhu Qi, Irwin King

entry.summary: Spec2Game is a benchmark requiring LLMs to generate complete executable Pygame projects from detailed natural-language game specifications, covering 15 game families with 150 tasks across three complexity levels. Evaluation uses source-code, runtime, and visual evidence across executability, specification realization, code quality, and additional dimensions. It targets a real gap between producing runnable code and correctly realizing behavioral requirements.

entry.title: Do Tool Calls Execute as Intended? Measuring and Repairing Intent-Execution Correspondence in LLM Agents

author.name: Boyang Yang, Zhenhao Li, Ziyao Yang, Kanghui Jia, Xin Yin, Mingmou Liu, Haoye Tian

entry.summary: This paper defines intent-execution correspondence (IEC): the property that an executed action matches what the emitted tool call denotes under the tool contract, noting that intermediate hops can silently alter calls. The proposed protocol observes what each hop received without executing, identifies the first hop that changed the call, and IntAct delivers calls in a form that repairs the mismatch. This exposes a previously invisible class of agent failures that waste retries, time, and money.

entry.title: MASBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration under Partial Observability

author.name: Qizhi Chu, Zekai Yu, Sijie Wen, Yang Liu, Chen Qian, Cheng Yang, Chuan Shi, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: MASBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM-based multi-agent systems under partial observability, where each agent accesses only partial environment information due to physical or privacy constraints, unlike most existing benchmarks that assume global observability. It enables systematic study of how collaboration mechanisms perform under realistic information asymmetry.

entry.title: When Is Enough Enough in Self-Evolving LLM Systems?

author.name: Enoch Yin, Bin Liu, Zhengling Qi

entry.summary: This paper addresses a principled stopping problem for self-evolving LLM systems, which iteratively propose and incorporate updates to prompts or skills but typically run under arbitrary budgets, risking wasted compute or late overfitting updates. It formulates stopping as an online sequential decision problem and provides criteria for when to stop and what artifact to output.

entry.title: From Memory to Guide: Spatio-Temporal Composer for Procedural Coding Memory

author.name: Zhixuan Tan, Pengjie Gu, Zhao Li, Yihan Hu, Xu He, Dong Li, Jianye Hao

entry.summary: This work argues that injecting retrieved skills as text prompts naively equates readable text with reliable execution, and proposes the Spatio-Temporal Composer, an active policy compiler that decides how and when retrieved procedural knowledge should be applied at inference time. It aligns historical knowledge with current environmental constraints and dictates applicability timing rather than treating skills as plug-and-play.

entry.title: SharpDraft: Accelerating Long-Context Speculative Decoding with Cardinality-Aware Query Scaling

author.name: Jeonghoon Park, Seongwoon Jo, Jongwon Lee, Taesik Gong

entry.summary: SharpDraft is a training-free method that counteracts attention-mass dilution in long-context speculative decoding via cardinality-aware query scaling, deriving an exact top-k mass correction and a closed-form fixed-slope approximation. It achieves 2.59-3.19x speedups on AIME-26, GPQA-Diamond, and LongGenBench Diary.

entry.title: AECG: Asymmetric Experience Consolidation and Governance In Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Ao Tian, Jialong Liu, Daqi Zheng, Xin Sun, Mengting Li, Zhizhao Xiao, Zijian Huang, Honglei Wang, Zijian Hei, Yukun Yan

entry.summary: The paper studies memory pollution and scope collapse in LLM multi-agent systems, where weakly supported or spuriously successful procedures become persistent components of future reasoning, or procedural knowledge escapes the coordination scope in which it was validated. AECG provides asymmetric consolidation and governance mechanisms to control how shared experience is reused across agents and decision levels.

entry.title: Sibyl: An Efficient Small-large Model Collaboration Framework for Long-horizon Tasks

author.name: Zhewei Fang, Yuxin Zhang, Zhenwei Shao, Mengze Li, Zheng Lin, Long Chen, Zhou Yu, Zhe Chen, Zhiwen Chen, Zhaode Wang, chengfei lv

entry.summary: Sibyl enables on-device small language models to collaborate step-by-step with larger cloud models on long-horizon tasks, learning which states warrant cloud assistance. It addresses credit assignment for individual cloud calls, which is only observable through final task outcomes, and balances task success against minimizing costly cloud calls.

entry.title: Have I Scene This Before? Spatially Grounded Conversational Memory for Complex Queries in Egocentric Assistants

author.name: Jiazhou Liang, Liam Gallagher, Kiko Chen, David Guo, Armin Toroghi, Yifan Simon Liu, Scott Sanner

entry.summary: The paper formalizes SpaCR, cross-scene recall-oriented and counterfactual spatial queries for egocentric assistants, and proposes SpaC-MEM, an object-centric working memory grounded in 3D reconstruction and segmentation. It compresses multimodal interaction histories while preserving geometric evidence, addressing context limits of direct VLM inference.

entry.title: Toward AI Trustworthiness: Finding Analytically Proven Forward-Invariant Sets for AI-Controlled Systems

author.name: Haoyang Song, Xikun Yang, Qixin Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes using an invertible neural network to transform a nonlinear AI-controlled system's state space into a latent space where a regular-shaped forward-invariant set can be found analytically, certifying safety for initial states within the set. This addresses verification challenges posed by neural-network controllers in safety-critical systems.

entry.title: Request Order Matters: Cache-History Sensitivity in Selective KV-Cache Reuse for Rolling Agents

author.name: Tiffany Gu, Annie Guan, Manshu Huang, Nitin Rao, Siddhant Shah, Margaret Capetz

entry.summary: The paper shows that persistent KV-cache reuse with selective recomputation in long-running rolling agents is history-dependent: an unchanged prompt can yield different answers depending on prior requests. A document-aligned recomputation policy reduces cross-order answer variation from 69.0% to 26.1% at a matched 5% recomputation budget compared to CacheBlend token top-k.

entry.title: Evolving in Thought Space: Training a Small Model at Test Time Unlocks Better Discoveries

author.name: Chonghe Jiang, Ao Qu, Siyuan Liu, Ruoyun Ma, Zijian Zhou, Dingyi Zhuang, Bo Liu, Han Zheng, Hanfei Yu, Baichuan Mo, Jinhua Zhao, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: The paper addresses the cost and credit-assignment problems of test-time training for scientific discovery by training a small model in latent thought space rather than repeatedly fine-tuning a large solution-generating LLM. This reduces gradient, optimizer, and long-output generation overheads while allowing outcome-level verifier feedback to better target high-level strategy versus low-level code.

entry.title: The Review Lottery: Calibrating an Observational Estimator of Peer-Review Noise (ICLR 2017-2025)

author.name: Feilian Huang

entry.summary: The paper builds a twice-calibrated observational estimator of how often accept/reject decisions would flip under a different reviewer set, applied to nine years of ICLR data (36,113 papers, 134,912 reviews) using a Bayesian ordered-probit decomposition and simulated independent committees. It offers a cheap alternative to the prohibitively expensive second-committee experiments done only at NeurIPS 2014 and 2021.

entry.title: AI Agent Pull Requests on GitHub: Frequency, Structure, and Merge Conflict Rates

author.name: George Xu, Arjun Subramanian, Nithilan Karthik

entry.summary: Using the AIDev-pop dataset of 33,596 agent-authored PRs across 2,807 repositories, this is the first empirical study of concurrent AI agent submissions to shared repositories. It finds 40.2% of repositories contain temporally co-active agent PR pairs accounting for 79.4% of agent PRs, rising to 53.4% and 95.0% within a one-week window, with analysis of merge conflict implications.

entry.title: Playing social deduction games with reinforcement fine-tuned large language models

author.name: Lingzhe Zhang, Yunpeng Zhai, Tong Jia, Kening Zheng, Chiming Duan, Minghua He, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding, Philip S. Yu, Ying Li

entry.summary: The study uses hidden-role social deduction games to examine how reinforcement fine-tuning changes LLM social behavior, covering hidden-state inference, social reading, and vote steering. It finds that optimizing terminal win-loss outcomes alone gives a sparse, noisy signal, while RFT substantially improves social reading abilities such as inferring hidden roles from public discussion.

entry.title: GrayShield: Bit-Level Sanitization for Transformer Model Supply-Chain Security

author.name: Armstrong Foundjem, Tsung-Hsien Chuang, Foutse Khomh, Mohamed Amine Merzouk

entry.summary: GrayShield defends the AI model supply chain against covert channels hidden in the least significant bits of 32-bit transformer weights, where malicious payloads can be concealed. It is a lightweight, post-training, zero-data sanitization method that overwrites the mantissa-LSB channel with a Gray-code-guided sequence, giving the channel zero payload capacity.

entry.title: Understanding Clustering in Slot Attention via Particle Dynamics

author.name: Vasudev Joy, Rajat Rasal, Avinash Kori, Anthea Monod, Ben Glocker

entry.summary: Introduces simplified slot attention (SSA), a parameter-free variant whose dynamics are connected to soft k-means clustering, providing a mechanistic explanation for how object-centric representations emerge from attention dynamics. On Pascal VOC, SSA achieves performance comparable to full slot attention.

entry.title: Coupling Noisy Pairwise Knowledge to the DAG Posterior for Causal Discovery

author.name: Guoliang Xu, James E Corter

entry.summary: Introduces HB-NoisyKG, a Bayesian framework combining observational data with repeated noisy causal reports from sources like LLMs for structure learning. A feature-conditioned Beta prior pools reliability estimates across sources, and alternating inference lets the graph posterior refine reliability and vice versa.

entry.title: RETRACE: From Entangled Repair Histories to Reusable Experience for CI Repair

author.name: Rabeya Khatun Muna, Muhammad Ahasanuzzaman, Nakhla Rafi, Yisen Xu, Jinqiu Yang, Tse-Hsun Chen

entry.summary: RETRACE reconstructs problem-level repair experience from messy CI histories, where pull requests mix multiple problems, failed attempts, and unrelated changes. It combines a backward endpoint view with a forward development view, reconciled by CI execution evidence, to produce reusable experience for LLM-agent repair systems.

entry.title: Knossos and Ariadne: Benchmarking and Learning Complete Diagram Topology Extraction with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Bangwei Guo, Xujiang Zhao, Shengyu Chen, Yanchi Liu, Wei Cheng, Xi Zhu, Guoning Zhang, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: The paper targets diagram-to-graph topology extraction, asking VLMs to recover all entities and complete relations in structural diagrams. It introduces Knossos, a 19,200-diagram benchmark across six domains with roughly 245K nodes and 440K edges generated symbolically, plus Ariadne, a learned approach for the task.

entry.title: Assembling Insights for Agentic Machine Learning Engineering Systems

author.name: Bihui Jin, Yinxi Li, Kaiyuan Wang, Pengyu Nie

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies how insights from related machine learning engineering tasks affect agentic MLE systems, a step toward recursive self-improvement, noting that current insight collection and injection are ad hoc and that uncontrolled insight sources create data leakage threats to validity. It analyzes how impact depends on insight provenance and assembly.

entry.title: Tracing a Sparse Emotion-Control Circuit in LLM-Based Text-to-Speech

author.name: Hongfei Du, Jiacheng Shi, Yanfu Zhang, Ye Gao

entry.summary: The paper introduces two emotion-sensitive metrics and uses activation patching to localize how reference emotion flows through LLM-based text-to-speech models. Under matched conditions it identifies a sparse circuit of 23-27 attention heads and MLPs per emotion, about 5% of components considered, that recover or suppress 74-88% of the late emotion-readout shift. The circuit combines a shared backbone with emotion-specific components, extending mechanistic interpretability from text models into speech generation.

entry.title: How Does Geometry Enter Generated Motion?

author.name: Weihan Li, Junhao Wu, Yuhan Song, Xiaofeng Lin, Xinlei Chen

entry.summary: The paper probes nine image-to-video models with paired interventions that vary scene geometry (a bump, barrier height, prompt wording, clip length) while fixing physical law and initial state, comparing generated trajectories to simulator predictions. It finds geometry is largely preserved and shapes motion, e.g., ball speed follows drawn track undulation, but generated motion diverges from physical behavior in specific ways where a persistent physical state would carry the response forward. This is a careful physics-grounded evaluation of video generator world modeling.

entry.title: Characterizing Parallelism Strategies in LLM Inference: Fundamental Compute-Communication Trade-offs

author.name: Javad Mirzaei, Jeebak Mitra

entry.summary: The paper provides an analytical characterization of tensor, pipeline, and hybrid parallelism strategies for multi-GPU LLM inference, modeling interactions among computation, communication, pipeline utilization, sequence length, batch size, and architecture. It aims to replace empirical strategy selection with fundamental compute-communication trade-off analysis under latency SLOs.

entry.title: Rethinking Tabular Foundation Models On Data Streams

author.name: Nilesh Verma, Daniel Nowak-Assis, Afonso Louren\c{c}o, Albert Bifet, Bernhard Pfahringer, Maroua Bahri, Nick Jin Sean Lim

entry.summary: This systematic study examines tabular foundation models on streaming data, where adaptation happens through context updates rather than parameter updates. Covering memory management, computational cost, concept drift, and delayed labels, the authors find TFMs achieve the highest predictive performance and that simply retaining the most recent examples is as effective as more sophisticated context-selection strategies.

entry.title: CIPHER-MoE: Balancing Efficiency and Routing Fidelity in Trillion-Scale MoE Training

author.name: Jing Li, Jian Meng, Yingmeng Gao, Suming Qiu, Linyuan Qiu, Dongfang Li, Baotian Hu, Binfan Zheng, Rongqian Zhao, Weijian Sun, Xin Chen

entry.summary: Tackles workload imbalance in trillion-scale Mixture-of-Experts training, where non-uniform token routing degrades hardware utilization and training stability. Rather than intricate parallelism or resource reallocation, CIPHER-MoE appears to balance system efficiency with routing fidelity, keeping expert assignments closer to the model's preferred routing. Systems-level contributions for MoE training at frontier scale are increasingly important.

entry.title: Incentive Alignment in Online Experimentation

author.name: {Ermis Soumalias, Richard Mudd, Abbas Zaidi

entry.summary: This paper reframes online A/B experimentation as a principal-agent incentive design problem, since decentralized experimenters are rewarded on average treatment effects that are prone to upward bias. The authors show this structural conflict can erode platform value in ways that conventional centralized levers like significance thresholds and traffic budgets cannot fix. They propose mechanisms to align experimenter incentives with platform goals.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Transferability of Training Data Extraction Attacks to Recover Memorized PII

author.name: Alexandru Nazare, Agnese Profico, Nicol\`o Vania, Elena Di Croce, Daria Caramanica, Davide Venditti, Elena Sofia Ruzzetti, Giancarlo A. Xompero, Fabio Massimo Zanzotto

entry.summary: The study evaluates training data extraction attacks for recovering memorized PII when prompts are translated into Italian, Spanish, French, and German, testing both English-centric and multilingual LLMs. It finds attacks transfer successfully across languages, revealing that English-only privacy evaluations underestimate extraction risk. This is an important warning for privacy auditing practices.

entry.title: VLA-ZO: Fast Zeroth-Order Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jaemin Kim, Jiahn Kim, Taesik Gong

entry.summary: VLA-ZO enables fast zeroth-order adaptation of vision-language-action models at deployment time, keeping the expensive vision-language prefix frozen and reusing its conditioning states across perturbation queries and optimizer steps. This achieves inference-level memory requirements while making naive ZO optimization practical for large VLAs. It addresses a real deployment constraint for robotic foundation models.

entry.title: MeSD: Multi-Evidence Self-Distillation for VideoLLM

author.name: Weijie Zhu, Han Fang, Hanyu Fu, Yuzhe Zhang, Xin Wei, Zhaoyan Pan, Feiran Liu, Xunjie Jin, Hongbo Sun, Zhiyu Lin, Tianyi Gao, Tianyi Ding, Ye Yuan, Zhongjiang He, Hao Sun, Zhiheng Wu

entry.summary: MeSD improves VideoLLM training beyond RL with verifiable rewards by building multiple evidence-conditioned self-teachers that provide dense token-level supervision, addressing how heterogeneous evidence agreements and conflicts should guide reward-based versus corrective updates. It targets the sparse sequence-level reward limitation in video reasoning models.

entry.title: MC-Sparse: Deconstructing and Closing the Dense-Sparse Attention Gap in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Jiarui Chen, Zeqiang Lai, Jiangshan Wang, Ziheng Ouyang, Ye Huang, Xiangyu Yue, Cewu Lu, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: The paper traces quality degradation in sparse attention for diffusion transformers to three causes: token-grouping constraints, inaccurate interaction selection, and lost attention contributions from discarded tokens. It proposes MC-Sparse, a training-free framework that selects individual KV tokens, groups similar queries into tile-aligned groups for GPU efficiency, and caches meta-information. This enables high-sparsity video and 3D generation without quality loss.

entry.title: Where Does Jagged Competence Come From?

author.name: Ioannis Tsiokos

entry.summary: Investigates the origins of jagged competence, the coexistence of low average error with failures on specific inputs, by training small recurrent networks on a task where an upper layer strictly extends a lower layer. The key finding is that learning the extension task yields a jagged, partial acquisition of the underlying layer: readable where the extension needs it and unreadable elsewhere.

entry.title: $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ Regret and Polylogarithmic Constraint Violation for COCO

author.name: Dhruv Sarkar, Abhishek Sinha

entry.summary: Studies constrained online convex optimization with adversarial convex losses and constraints, improving on prior algorithms that achieve root-T regret and root-T cumulative constraint violation. The paper shows an online policy achieving O(sqrt(T log T)) regret and O(log^2 T) cumulative constraint violation, a substantial tightening on the violation side.

entry.title: You May Be Running the Wrong Inception Crop

author.name: Jason Chuan-Chih Chou

entry.summary: Discovers that the standard TensorFlow/JAX Inception crop implementation samples crop scale with a 1/sqrt(A) density, unlike the PyTorch implementation which follows the original description. Training 522 ViT-S/16 models on ImageNet-1k across budgets and crop distributions reveals the discrepancy matters. A valuable reproducibility finding for the vision community.

entry.title: Length Generalization Needs Proper Regularization

author.name: Pavlo Vasylenko, Matthias Lindemann, Andr\'e F. T. Martins, Marcos Treviso

entry.summary: This work shows that length generalization in sequential models depends not only on architecture (positional encodings, attention) but also on training regularization: weight decay can hinder extrapolation, while carefully placed dropout improves it. The authors identify that standard dropout placement before layer normalization causes a systematic distributional mismatch, and moving dropout to just before the linear projection fixes this. A simple, actionable finding for building length-robust models.

entry.title: Backward-Consistent Diffusion Sampling for Sparsely Observed PDE Inverse Problems

author.name: Yida Pan, Muhammad H. Ashiq, Chanyong Jung, Yixuan Jia, Jonah M. Miller, Qing Qu, Ismail Alkhouri

entry.summary: The paper proves that state-of-the-art function-space diffusion solvers can fail to minimize unobserved error in discontinuous PDE coefficient recovery, then proposes FunBCS, an input-space optimization approach enforcing backward consistency with the physics during sampling. This targets severely ill-posed PDE inverse problems from extremely sparse observations, where diffusion priors are the leading method. The negative result plus fix is valuable for scientific diffusion-model users.

entry.title: CURIO: Curiosity-Driven Test-Time Learning for Open-Ended Discovery

author.name: Tao Feng, Fangxu Yu, Zijie Lei, Jiaru Zou, Changjiang Jiang, Yi Yan, Jiaxuan You, Pan Lu

entry.summary: CURIO is a curiosity-driven test-time learning framework that supplements task reward with an Intrinsic Curiosity World Model operating in the policy's hidden-state representation, providing prediction-error bonuses to avoid prematurely abandoning low-reward but promising directions. It targets open-ended discovery where a frozen LLM cannot adapt from experience and greedy RL may over-exploit.

entry.title: Pessimistic Minimax Learning for Public-Private Information Games under Unilateral Coverage

author.name: Shuze Daniel Liu, Claire Chen, Jiuqi Wang, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: This work studies offline learning in two-player zero-sum contextual games with public and private information, motivated by auctions and negotiations. It introduces unilateral prescriptive concentrability, a pessimistic algorithm with near-optimal exploitability rates, and a policy mirror descent framework (PPA-PMD) for function approximation.

entry.title: A Unified Scaling Law for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Xilin Dai, Yiding Liu, Zewei Dong, Jiang-Ming Yang, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: The paper derives a unified five-parameter scaling law and theory of time series learning from 18,768 experimental cells across 21 checkpoints on 23 dataset-frequency tasks. The law captures capacity-history interactions, saturating context gains, and horizon shifts, and predicts held-out scaling curves (e.g., Toto 2.0) with about 1-1.5 percent error.

entry.title: Robust Parameter-Efficient LLM Adaptation on Analog Hardware

author.name: Jindan Li, Zhaoxian Wu, Tianyi Chen

entry.summary: The paper develops a LoRA-based, optimizer-agnostic adaptation method for running LLMs on analog in-memory computing hardware, keeping pretrained weights fixed on analog arrays while adapting to hardware non-idealities like limited DAC precision and input noise. It handles errors in both forward and backward matrix-vector multiplications.

entry.title: Poisson-GENERIC Neural Operators: Exact Metriplectic Structure in Function Space via Casimir Entropies

author.name: Jason Sulskis, Sathya Ravi

entry.summary: Proposes neural operators that satisfy the GENERIC degeneracy conditions exactly by using a latent entropy density whose integral is a Casimir of a Lie-Poisson operator, avoiding state-dependent projections that break the Jacobi identity. This yields thermodynamically consistent, metriplectic structure in function space for physics modeling.

entry.title: TurboPairFormer: Fast and Stable Protein Folding Model Training with an Optimized Triangle Attention Kernel

author.name: Yide Ran, Chelsea Lowman, Jan Doma\'nski, David Hartmann, Jenke Scheen, Jennifer Wei, Chuan Li, Jianwen Xie, Zhaozhuo Xu

entry.summary: TurboPairFormer is a triangular attention implementation for NVIDIA Hopper GPUs targeting AlphaFold3-style biomolecular models, addressing the cubic cost of pair attention and its extra gradient reductions. The method uses a key-tile-parallel backward algorithm that recomputes each probability tile once for all gradient types, avoiding repeated recomputation, atomics, or full score-gradient storage, and handles BF16 precision loss in the softmax backward correction. This enables faster and more stable training of protein folding models.

entry.title: Dynamic Minimax Regret Optimization for Robust LLM Post-Training

author.name: Chengbo Zang, Haoyu Dong, Mehmet Kerem Turkcan, Gil Zussman, Zoran Kostic, Javad Ghaderi

entry.summary: The paper formulates group-distributionally robust LLM post-training as a two-player sampler-optimizer game under mini-batch-only bandit feedback, where a sampler adaptively selects among heterogeneous data sources tracking instantaneous worst sources from stale partial information. This matches the practical constraint that historical losses are not re-evaluated as the model trains. The dynamic minimax regret framework targets robustness across domains, tasks, preference distributions, and difficulty levels during post-training.

entry.title: Conditional Flow Matching for Single-Neuron Electrophysiology: Capturing Multimodal Responses Across Stimuli

author.name: Cameron Schofield, Luca Ghafourpour, Philip H. Wong, Costas A. Anastassiou, Richard E. Turner

entry.summary: The authors train a conditional generative model for single-neuron electrophysiology using flow matching with a velocity field conditioned on input current, capturing the multimodal voltage responses a single cell can produce for repeated stimuli. This replaces costly ensembles of deterministic biophysical parametrizations that require hundreds of thousands of CPU hours. Demonstrated on biophysically detailed models of two human cortical interneuron types.

entry.title: LinearPFN: Amortized Variable Selection for Linear Models with Interactions

author.name: Louis Schiekiera, Max Zimmer, Christophe Roux, Manuel Arnold, Sebastian Pokutta, Fritz G\"unther

entry.summary: LinearPFN is a prior-data fitted transformer that amortizes spike-and-slab Bayesian variable selection for linear models with interactions, replacing exponentially costly exact posterior enumeration or MCMC with a single forward pass that returns inclusion probabilities per candidate effect. This makes principled Bayesian variable selection scalable to larger predictor sets. It extends the PFN paradigm to a classical statistical inference task.

entry.title: Private online learning and prediction for Littlestone classes

author.name: Amartya Sanyal

entry.summary: The paper proves novel lower bounds for differentially private online learning and upper bounds for private online prediction, showing the sample complexities of the two problems are separated by a factor growing with the time horizon for every class of finite Littlestone dimension. This establishes a fundamental separation between releasing hypotheses and merely predicting.

entry.title: Targeted Active Learning for Preference-Based Treatment Effects on Multivariate Outcomes

author.name: Lola Giordani, Mathieu Even, Chlo\'e Geoffroy, Jean-Christophe Corvol, Rapha\"el Porcher, Federico Pavone

entry.summary: This paper proposes an active learning framework for estimating preference-based treatment effects over multiple clinical outcomes, selecting which pairwise expert comparisons to query when the preference rule itself must be learned. It connects ML methodology to realistic clinical decision-making where patients weight benefits and risks differently. The theory-driven approach could reduce costly expert annotation in personalized medicine.

entry.title: What Gradients Add to Text Leakage in Split Language Models, Counted per Token and per Document

author.name: Georgios Politis, Evangelos Pappas

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate that an observer at the split point in split learning can reconstruct most of a client's text from activations and gradients: on GPT-2, 94.20% of tokens from activations alone and 97.38% with gradients, with document-level exact recovery jumping substantially when gradients are available. This quantifies how much the gradient stream worsens privacy leakage in split training. The findings challenge the assumption that not sending raw text protects client data.

entry.title: Local Fisher Information Enables Sparse Causal Discovery

author.name: Byeongguk Kang, Donghyeon Lee, Euijong Song, Gunwoong Park

entry.summary: Introduces Fisher Information Completion Search (FiCS), a source-first causal discovery algorithm for additive noise models that uses a single local Fisher score for both causal ordering and parent selection. It proves that a node's local Fisher information equals its noise Fisher information exactly when the conditioning set contains all parents, enabling sample-efficient discovery with bounded conditioning size. This avoids estimating high-dimensional densities.

entry.title: From Transformers to Weighted Automata: Towards the Verification of Large Language Models

author.name: Smayan Agarwal, Aslah Ahmad Faizi, Shobhit Singh, Aalok Thakkar

entry.summary: Establishes a formal correspondence between transformer architectures and weighted automata over formal languages, enabling verification tools from automata theory to be applied to LLM analysis. This offers a principled route beyond empirical probing toward rigorous guarantees about transformer behavior in safety-critical deployments. An early step toward formal verification of general-purpose language models.

entry.title: Flow Policies as Actions of Skill-Level World Models: Learned and Symbolic Abstractions for Long-Horizon Planning

author.name: Andreu Matoses Gimenez, Andrei-Carlo Papuc, Chris Pek, Javier Alonso-Mora

entry.summary: The paper constructs skill-level actions from a flow-matching policy trained on skill-segmented demonstrations, so that one skill execution equals one world-model transition, and proposes four action abstractions of increasing task knowledge. This shortens planning horizons for long-horizon robotic tasks without requiring a hand-designed symbolic skill vocabulary.

entry.title: Lend Me Your Eyes: Instruction-Aware Text Embeddings via Attention Relay

author.name: Yiyuan Luo, Vaggos Chatziafratis

entry.summary: The paper introduces Attention Relay, a training-free method that transfers instruction-following ability from an instruction-tuned LLM to a text embedding model by passing LLM attention weights into the embedder's attention. Experiments across six LLMs and ten embedding models show nearly all combinations become instruction-aware. This is a simple, broadly applicable trick for improving embedding models without training.

entry.title: When Evidence Changes: Evaluating Memory Repair and Re-reading in Language-Model Agents

author.name: Wenhui Chu (University at Albany, State University of New York)

entry.summary: The paper introduces an evidence-revision evaluation on medication and problem-list tasks from ICU records, testing how LLM agents should handle revoked or replaced supporting documents: memory repair (caching, rebuilding, graph-local repair) versus full or filtered re-reading. Across two 7B models, local repair cuts revision tokens 5-10x versus rebuilding, but every memory pipeline costs at least twice full re-reading in held-out conditions.

entry.title: Stance Drift: How AI-mediated Communication Distorts Our Message

author.name: Lingchong Liu, Yanfei Zhou, Jacob Bien, Y. X. Rachel Wang, Lucy Xia, Xin Tong

entry.summary: The authors model AI-mediated communication as a generate-then-extract pipeline over five stance categories and define a stance preservation rate, finding that none of nine LLMs exceeded 0.7 SPR across 112 debate propositions. This quantifies how LLM mediation subtly shifts the positions a speaker is conveying, with implications for trust and faithful communication. Statistically careful and societally relevant.

entry.title: Dataset Signatures in Human-LLM Interactions and User Modeling

author.name: Joseph Suh, Serina Chang

entry.summary: The authors study seven human-LLM interaction datasets, spanning in-the-wild chat logs and human preference data, and show via a Torralba-Efros-style classification experiment that classifiers can identify a conversation's source dataset from user messages alone well above chance. This indicates datasets carry distinct signatures that affect downstream user modeling and research built on them. The work raises important concerns about generalization and representativeness in human-LLM interaction research.

entry.title: Plan Canvas: Fixed Reasoning Regions for Continuous Language Flows

author.name: Miaohe Niu, Pengxiang Li, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: Plan Canvas addresses how to add chain-of-thought reasoning to continuous/diffusion-style language models that denoise an entire canvas at once, by fixing a fixed-capacity plan region boundary between reasoning trace and answer, with supervised padding and separate denoising clocks for plan and answer. This removes the need for the model to jointly decide trace length, trace placement, and answer content. Relevant to the growing area of diffusion and non-autoregressive text generation.

entry.title: AECP: Artifact-Exclusive Communication Protocol for Multi-Agent Code Generation

author.name: Jiaqi Xue, Yanjun Wang, Xiangci Li, Lingbo Mo, Aritra Sengupta, Shweta Garg, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Myeongsoo Kim

entry.summary: AECP moves part of multi-agent code-generation coordination from individual agents into the execution harness by making shared artifacts interface-enforced, so shared findings are actually used and deviations from agreed interfaces are detected automatically. This addresses the problem that context-only communication in agent teams often goes unused or unverified. Relevant to scaling coding agents on repository-level tasks.

entry.title: SAFE-MR: Evidence Sufficiency Learning for Selective Multimodal Rumor Detection

author.name: Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: SAFE-MR separates claim veracity from evidence sufficiency in multimodal rumor detection, decomposing image-text posts into verifiable claims and building a relation-aware claim-evidence graph with provenance weighting. Separate veracity and sufficiency heads enable selective prediction, abstaining when retrieved evidence is relevant but insufficient.

entry.title: COMPASS 2.0: psychometric representational similarity analysis distinguishes symptom structure from personal signal

author.name: Baihan Lin

entry.summary: COMPASS 2.0 introduces psychometric representational similarity analysis to test whether speech-derived psychiatric questionnaire scores reflect the person or merely item wording. In pre-registered analyses of 275 clinical interviews, language-derived symptom geometry resembled item wording more than self-report, with no structure beyond wording detected by registered tests - a cautionary negative result.

entry.title: FADE: Frame-Aware Diffusion-Transformer-based Multi-Concept Erasure for Video Unlearning

author.name: Yuchen Li, Kaiyuan Deng, Chaoran Feng, Zhenyu Tang, Li Yuan

entry.summary: FADE is a multi-concept unlearning framework for text-to-video diffusion models that identifies and fixes frame-reactivation gaps where erased concepts resurface in isolated frames. It combines a closed-form key/value edit suppressing all target concepts with per-concept frame-aware low-rank adapters, and evaluates multi-concept erasure that prior work ignored.

entry.title: Rethinking Long-Video Efficiency: A Joint Allocation Perspective on Frames, Pixels, and Front-End Latency

author.name: Sixun Dong, Wei Li, Andong Deng, Qi Qian, Victor Zhu, Zhengping Ji, Chen Chen

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that for long-video VLMs, dense low-resolution sampling beats sparse native-resolution sampling at matched token budgets, resolution-sensitive tasks benefit from selected high-resolution frames, and front-end decoding dominates wall-clock time for hour-long videos. Based on these findings it introduces LoHi, a training-free joint allocation method across frames, pixels, and decoding.

entry.title: LoCoSplat: Real-Time Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Minimal 3D Reasoning

author.name: Sinan Wang, Jinjin He, Yuchen Sun, Duowen Chen, Shenyifan Lu, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: LoCoSplat argues that Gaussian parameters beyond depth can be derived from a fixed local average of neighboring point features rather than a heavy learned 3D network. It uses a 0.14M-parameter pointwise MLP reading coarse and fine grids, achieving real-time feed-forward 3DGS without learned 3D networks or dynamic sparse computation.

entry.title: DriftSR: One-Step Real-World Image Super-Resolution via Distribution Drifting

author.name: Wei Zhu, Kai Zhang, Yu Zheng, Zhaopeng Yang, Lei Luo, Yong Guo, Jian Yang

entry.summary: DriftSR is a one-step real-world image super-resolution framework that exploits pretrained diffusion priors through distribution drifting in a frozen intermediate representation space, avoiding score distillation, adversarial losses, and extra task-specific encoders. Spatial Feature Drifting treats spatial features as distributional samples to enable better detail recovery. It targets the practical goal of efficient, perceptually rich Real-ISR with simpler optimization.

entry.title: PixReenact: Pixel-Conditioned Causal Video Diffusion for Streaming Head-Avatar Reenactment

author.name: Gavriel Habib, Dvir Samuel, Or Shimshi, Rami Ben-Ari

entry.summary: PixReenact is a streaming head-avatar reenactment framework built on causal video diffusion that conditions directly on VAE-encoded reference pixels, avoiding lossy identity/motion extractors while providing robust motion transfer, long-term identity stability, and low latency. It moves past offline clip-based diffusion generation toward continuous streaming output. Relevant to real-time avatars for telepresence, VR, and video conferencing.

entry.title: Learning Conditional Source Distribution via Flow Reversal for Temporal Flow Matching

author.name: Kuan-Hsun Tu, Hsuan-Chi Liu, Jia-Wei Liao, Chien-Sheng Chiang, Tsung-Wei Ke

entry.summary: CNP-Flow introduces a flow matching framework for temporal generation in which a conditional noise predictor produces an isotropic Gaussian source per condition, supervised by source samples recovered through flow reversal of a pretrained FM model, within a three-stage training pipeline that preserves the FM backbone. Standard conditional flow matching instead draws sources from an unconditional Gaussian. Evaluated across video prediction and related tasks, this offers a new conditioning mechanism for generative flow models.

entry.title: Robust Local Optimization Done Right

author.name: James Pritts, Kevin K\"oser

entry.summary: Systematically separates hypothesis selection from refinement in RANSAC-based geometry estimation, isolating the effects of robust-loss shape, mis-specified inlier scales, and optimization strategy for essential/fundamental matrix and homography estimation. Introduces a profile-marginal score that marginalizes nuisance inlier scale and analyzes optimizer behavior on currently-rejected correspondences.

entry.title: FairRSFM: A Biome-Aware Benchmark and Debiasing Framework for Remote Sensing Foundation Models

author.name: Md Aminur Hossain, Omkumar Vaghasiya, Rajeev Ranjan Dwivedi, Vinod Kurmi, Biplab Banerjee

entry.summary: FairRSFM introduces a biome-aware benchmark mapping georeferenced samples from 14 terrestrial biome classes into six ecological macro-groups to reveal disparities hidden by aggregate metrics in remote sensing foundation models. Evaluating Prithvi-EO-2.0, SatMAE, and DOFA under a unified frozen-backbone protocol, it shows consistent biome-dependent performance gaps and proposes a debiasing framework.

entry.title: AnchorGen: Anchored Optimization for Customizable Generative 3D Design

author.name: Hantao Zhang, Oliver Heinimann, Jieke Wu, Yingxuan You, Emilien Seiler, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: AnchorGen introduces a rectified-flow framework trained on joint shape-sketch latents so that 3D shape generation stays consistent with a user-supplied 2D sketch, unlike generic generative priors that drift toward high-density training regions. Constraining the sketch component restricts optimization to the sub-manifold of sketch-consistent shapes.

entry.title: MTOR: Generalizable AI-Generated Video Detection with Multimodal Semantics and Temporal Over-Regularity

author.name: Hang Wang, Chao Shen, Lei Zhang, Zhi-Qi Cheng

entry.summary: MTOR detects AI-generated videos by combining caption-derived textual semantics with visual cues, and by exploiting temporal over-regularity—the finding that generated videos show stronger temporal persistence and lower variability than real footage. This targets generalizable detection as video generation quality improves.

entry.title: VGGT-Bridge: Beyond Sequential Pose Graphs via Coarse-Stride Skip Edges

author.name: Sungjae Choi, Hanna Bae, Sunghyun Baek, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: VGGT-Bridge extends chunk-and-align frameworks for feed-forward visual geometry transformers by adding long-range skip edges between non-adjacent chunks without retraining VGGT, curbing the drift that accumulates through purely sequential pose graphs. This mitigates quadratic attention limits when scaling to thousands of frames.

entry.title: Grounded in Time: A Multi-Source Dataset and Benchmark for Temporal Grounding in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yi Wang, Yang Yang, Guangqi Xu, Sumin Lin, Ning Kang, Pengxiang Lu, Xiaotong Chen, Zeyu Xue, Ping Deng, Xing Liu, Chenguang Yang, Zhenyu Lu

entry.summary: GiT introduces a dataset and benchmark for temporal grounding in robotic manipulation, requiring policies to infer task-relevant states from past interactions across biolaboratory, household, and industrial scenarios. It includes real-robot and UMI demonstrations of 18 bimanual tasks, simulation data, and a ManiSkill-based evaluation suite of nine tasks with fine-grained temporal annotations.

entry.title: MOSAIC-SV: Real-Time Adaptive Identification of Vessel Dynamics for the Control and Deployment of Aquatic Robots

author.name: Wensen Liu, Jerry Peng, Shravani Vedagiri, Aaron M. Johnson

entry.summary: MOSAIC-SV is a real-time adaptive system identification and control system for aquatic robots that builds a control-sufficient hydrodynamic model from a spec-sheet prior without dedicated identification trials, re-estimating parameters at every control step. A physically admissible unscented Kalman filter with command-dependent consider projection identifies hydrodynamic, disturbance, and actuator parameters while the controller plans on the evolving model.

entry.title: TacOT: Learning Contact-Rich Dexterous Manipulation from Human Demonstrations via Tactile-Guided Optimal Transport

author.name: Xingting Li, Yifan Han, Zijian Lin, Wei Hou, Chuqiao Lyu, Shoujie Li, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: TacOT is a human-to-robot transfer framework for contact-rich dexterous manipulation that uses tactile dynamics rather than visual or motion similarity to establish human-robot correspondence, employing action-tactile dynamic time warping and optimal transport to match demonstrations with consistent contact states and force patterns.

entry.title: Tackling Sim-to-Real Mismatch Through Sampling-Based Disturbance Observers: From Analytical Models to Learned World Models

author.name: Tianqi Zhu, Jun Yang, Jianliang Mao, Cong Li, Shihua Li

entry.summary: Introduces the sampling-based disturbance observer (SDOB), extending classical disturbance observers beyond explicit plant models to simulators, cost-query interfaces, and learned world models by separating observable state and cost channels. This provides a unified mechanism to estimate unmodeled disturbances and close the sim-to-real gap across model types.

entry.title: FOCUS: Fine-Grained Open-Vocabulary Change Detection for Uncertainty-Aware Semi-Static Scenes

author.name: Can Xu, Mingfeng Yuan, Mahan Mohammadi, Steven L. Waslander

entry.summary: FOCUS formulates long-term map maintenance in semi-static environments as probabilistic inference, fusing geometric likelihood with appearance likelihood from a 3D Gaussian map to detect object-level changes such as in-place replacement of similar objects. A recursive three-state estimator tracks whether each mapped object persisted, was replaced, or was removed.

entry.title: Arm-wise Compositional Generalization in Dual-Arm Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zaibin Zhang, Binghao Ran, Yuhan Wu, Zhongbo Zhang, Yifan Wang, Junwei Jiang, Junlan Xiao, Wangcheng Shi, Li Kang, Yiran Qin, Zhenfei Yin, Lijun Wang, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: ACG-Bench provides a standardized testbed for studying whether dual-arm vision-language-action policies can recompose familiar per-arm atomic skills into new coordination patterns, with 23 task-condition pairs across 8 task families covering reordering, synchronization, and cross-task composition. All methods receive identical per-arm prompts, isolating generalization ability. This systematically probes an underexamined axis of VLA generalization.

entry.title: Exploration-Preserving Policy Optimization

author.name: Hangzhan jin, Mohammad Hamdaqa, Doina Precup

entry.summary: ExPPO is a lightweight advantage-shaping rule for RL with verifiable rewards that redistributes credit using response surprisal and prompt pass rate, aiming to keep diverse solutions accessible under repeated sampling where group-relative objectives favor majority modes. The paper includes theoretical analysis of response-level credit.

entry.title: Asynchronous Is Nearly Free for Evolution Strategies on Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: William Hoy, Jingxuan Fan, Nurcin Celik, Xu Pan

entry.summary: This short paper introduces bounded-staleness asynchronous evolution strategies for LLM post-training on long-horizon agentic tasks, where synchronous rollout barriers waste compute waiting for stragglers. Because ES is population-based and backpropagation-free, asynchronous consumption of trajectories avoids much of the off-policy cost that plagues asynchronous RL. The result is a near-free efficiency gain demonstrated on the Endless Terminal benchmark-style setting.

entry.title: LMBuild: Evaluating LLM Agents for Generating Buildable and Functional Structures

author.name: Jiateng Liu, Rushi Wang, Cheng Qian, Xuejun Zhang, Sun Li, Jiayu Liu, Yifan Shen, Xu Cao, Jiarui Yao, Bingxuan Li, Ruhi Sarikaya, Heng Ji

entry.summary: LMBuild is a new benchmark that evaluates LLM agents on generating 3D structures that are not just geometrically elegant but physically buildable and functional. It represents objects as assembled structures with part decompositions, joints, materials, and assembly sequences, and provides a unified reproducible evaluation framework with an interactive environment.
